children.text: paramakāruṇikarāṉa periyavāccāṉ piḷḷai aruḷicceyta vyākhyānam
children.translated_text: The commentary composed by the supremely compassionate <s>Periyavāccāṉ Piḷḷai</s>

children.text: avatārikai - śriyaḥpatiyāy jñānānandaikasvarūpaṉāy, samastakalyāṇa-guṇātmakaṉāy, ubhayavibhūtiyuktaṉāy, sarvasmātparaṉāṉa sarveśvaraṉ aṭiyāka perumāḷ peṟṟatu bhaktirūpāpannajñānam-ākaiyālē, kramattālē kāṇkiṟōm eṉṟu āṟi irukkal āvatu tan talaiyālē vantat’ ākiliṟē, avaṉ tāṉē kāṭṭa kāṇkiṟavar-ākaiyālē appōtē kāṇa vēṇṭumpaṭi viṭāy piṟantatu. paramapadattilum anubhavippatu guṇānubhavam-ākaiyālē anta śīlādi-guṇaṅkaḷ pūrṇamāṉa kōyililē anubhavikka prārthikkiṟār. iṅku anubhavikka kuṟai eṉ? prārthanai eṉ? eṉṉil - svātantryam piṟappē uṭaiyar-ākaiyālē, manuṣyar nirodhippār palarum uṇṭākaiyālē, iṅku vant’ anubhavikka māṭṭātē
aṭiyārkaḷ kuḻāṅkaḷai uṭaṉ kūṭuvat’ eṉṟu-kolō
children.translated_text: "When will I join the assemblies of devotees?"

children.text: eṉṟum,
children.translated_text: thus,

children.text: am tamil pēr iṉpatt’ aṭiyārōṭ’ iruntamai
children.translated_text: "Being together with the devotees in the great bliss of beautiful Tamil"

children.text: eṉṟum nammāḻvār prārthittu peṟṟa pēṟṟai iṅkē anubhavikka ācaippaṭukiṟār.
children.translated_text: thus, he desires to experience here itself the fruit that <s>Nammāḻvār</s> prayed for and obtained.

Introduction — Since <s>Perumāḷ</s> (the Lord), who is the consort of <s>Śrī</s>, whose essential nature is knowledge and bliss alone, who possesses all auspicious qualities, who is endowed with both <s>vibhūtis</s> (dominions), and who is the Supreme Lord, the highest of all, obtained <s>bhakti-rūpāpanna-jñāna</s> (knowledge transformed into devotion), we might say 'we shall see Him gradually and wait patiently' — but since it came by His own initiative, and since He Himself shows and we are the ones who see, the urgency arose to see Him immediately. Since what is experienced even in <s>Paramapadam</s> (the supreme abode) is the experience of His qualities, he prays to experience those qualities of <s>śīla</s> (graciousness) and others in their fullness at the temple. What is the deficiency in experiencing here? Why the prayer? — Because He inherently possesses <s>svātantrya</s> (independence), because there are many humans who obstruct, one cannot come here and experience,

children.text: paryaṅkavidyaiyil collukiṟapaṭiyēyiṟē mumukṣu manorathippatu; attai iṅkē tiru anantāḻvāṉ-mēlē cāyntu kiṭakkiṟa iṭattilē anubhavikka manorathikkiṟār. saṃsāri muktaṉāy ceṉṟāl
children.translated_text: What a <s>mumukṣu</s> (seeker of liberation) desires is as described in the <s>Paryaṅka-vidyā</s>; here he desires to experience that same thing at the place where the Lord reclines upon <s>Tiru Anantāḻvāṉ</s> (Ādiśeṣa). When a <s>saṃsārī</s> (worldly being) becomes liberated and goes,

children.text: pāde-nādhyārohati
children.translated_text: "He ascends to the couch" —

children.text: ityādippaṭiyē, eḻuntaruḷi irukkiṟa paryaṅkattilē mititt’ ēṟiṉāl nī yār eṉṟāl, nāṉ rājaputraṉ eṉpārai pōlē, ahaṃ brahmāsmi eṉṟiṟē ivaṉ colluvatu.
children.translated_text: according to this, when he steps up onto the couch where the Lord is graciously seated, if asked 'Who are you?', just as one would say 'I am a prince,' what he says is '<s>ahaṃ brahmāsmi</s>' (I am Brahman).

children.translated_text: Rows of <s>tutti</s> (ornamental crests); that is, having hoods numbering a thousand that possess what are called the two joined foot-marks, fully endowed,

children.text: arav’ araca perum cōti
children.translated_text: The serpent king of great splendor —

children.text: nāgarājā eṉṉum mahātejassai uṭaiyavaṉāy
children.translated_text: He who possesses the great radiance called <s>Nāgarāja</s> (king of serpents),

children.text: aṉantaṉ eṉṉum
children.translated_text: Called <s>Ananta</s> —

children.text: ellāvaṟṟaiyum vyāpittu niṟkiṟa sarveśvaraṉai viḷākkulai koḷḷukiṟa svarūpa-guṇaṅkaḷai uṭaiyaṉākaiyālē anantaṉ eṉṟu collappaṭukiṟa
children.translated_text: Because he possesses the essential nature and qualities that serve as a lamp to the Lord who pervades all and stands as <s>Sarveśvara</s> (the Lord of all), he is called <s>Ananta</s> (the endless one),

children.text: eṉṉum
children.translated_text: called —

children.text: sumukhaṉ, vāsuki, takṣakaṉ eṉṟum uṇṭiṟē; avarkaḷiṉ kāṭṭil bhaga-vatpratyāsattiyai uṭaiyaṉ eṉṉum prasiddhiyai uṭaiyavaṉ
children.translated_text: There are also <s>Sumukha</s>, <s>Vāsuki</s>, <s>Takṣaka</s> and others; compared to them, he has the renown of being close to the Lord,

children.text: aṇi viḷaṅkum uyar veḷḷai aṇaiyai mēvi
children.translated_text: Reclining upon that lofty white couch resplendent with beauty —

children.text: aḻaku mikku ōkkattai uṭaittāy maṟu aṟṟa veḷḷai paṭukkaiākiṟa tiru anantāḻvāṉai mēvi
children.translated_text: Reclining upon <s>Tiru Anantāḻvāṉ</s> who is the flawless white couch of great beauty and eminence,

children.text: tiruvaraṅka peru
m

In the great city of <s>Tiru Araṅkam</s>

children.text: vaikuṇṭhe tu pare loke eṉṟu collumatuvum iṅkē kāṇum ivarkku i- tiruvaraṅkam-ākiṟa mahānagarattilē
children.translated_text: That which is described as "<s>vaikuṇṭhe tu pare loke</s>" (in the supreme abode Vaikuṇṭha) — for those who see it here itself, in this great city that is <s>Tiru Araṅkam</s>,

children.text: teḷ nīr poṉṉi tirai kaiyāl aṭi varuṭa
children.translated_text: With the clear waters of <s>Poṉṉi</s> caressing His feet with its waves as hands —

children.text: teḷinta nīrai uṭaiya kāveri, tiraikaḷ-ākiṟa kaikaḷālē tiruvaṭikaḷai varuṭa
children.translated_text: The <s>Kāverī</s> with clear waters, caressing His sacred feet with hands that are its waves,

He who reclines — the dark

children.translated_text: Like a blue sapphire reclining upon <s>Tiru Anantāḻvāṉ</s>, He who graciously sleeps,

children.text: kōmaḷattai
children.translated_text: The tender and beautiful one —

children.text: kaṇṇāl tukaikka oṇṇāta saukumāryam uṭaiyavaṉai

children.translated_text: Having beheld —

children.text: kaliyar cōṟṟai kaṇṭukoṇṭu eṉṉumā pōlē
children.translated_text: Like saying 'having found food for the hungry,'

children.text: eṉ kaṇ iṇaikaḷ
children.translated_text: My two eyes —

children.text: paṭṭiṉi viṭṭa eṉ kaṇkaḷ
children.translated_text: My eyes that have been kept starving,

children.text: eṉṟu-kolō kaḷikkum nāḷē

children.text: eṉṟu kaḷikkum kaḷippai iṅkē kaṇṭu kaḷippat’ eṉṟō?
children.translated_text: The joy of seeing there and rejoicing — when will that be experienced here by seeing and rejoicing?

children.text: vāy ōr īr ai nūṟu tutaṅkaḷ ārnta
children.translated_text: With mouths numbering twice five hundred, fully endowed with fangs —

children.text: yaśodai pirāṭṭi kṛṣṇasparśattāl vanta sukhattukku pōkkuviṭṭ’ ēttumā pōlē, bhagavadanubhavaharṣaprakarṣattālē vanta prītikku pōkkuviṭṭu ēttukaikkāka āyiram vāyaiyum; tutaṅkaḷ āvatu - stotrādikaḷai puṟappaṭa viṭukai stutamiṟē.
children.translated_text: Just as <s>Yaśodā Pirāṭṭi</s> would release the joy that came from the touch of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> through praise, releasing the delight arising from the intensity of joy in experiencing the Lord through praise — a thousand mouths for that; <s>tutti</s> (fangs/crests) means the emission of hymns and praises, which constitutes <s>stuti</s> (praise).

children.text: vaḷai uṭampiṉ aḻal nākam
children.translated_text: From the curving body, the fiery tongues —

children.text: veḷutta niṟattai uṭaiyaṉumāy, pratipakṣattukku vant’ aṇuka oṇṇātapaṭi anabhibhavanīyaṉāy irukkiṟa tiru anantāḻvāṉ
children.translated_text: <s>Tiru Anantāḻvāṉ</s> who has a white complexion and who is so invincible that adversaries cannot approach,

children.text: umiḻnta cem tī vīyāta malar ceṉṉi vitāṉamē pōl mēl-mēlum mika eṅkum parant’ ataṉ kīḻ
children.translated_text: Spewing red flames, like an unfading flower-crowned canopy spreading more and more everywhere above, and beneath it —

children.text: avaṉ vāyālē iṭaiviṭātē umiḻkiṟa agnijvālaikaḷiṉ jyotisākiṟa mēṟkaṭṭiyiṉ-kīḻē
children.translated_text: Beneath the canopy formed by the brilliance of the fire-flames continuously emitted from his mouths,

children.text: vīyāta malar ceṉṉi
children.translated_text: The unfading flower-crowned head —

children.text: pū māṟāta tiru muṭiyai uṭaiyaṉumāy
children.translated_text: Having a divine crown whose flowers never wither,

m

children.translated_text: blossoming radiance — wearing such a garland —
Like the <s>kāyā</s> flower

children.text: kāyāviṉ aḻakiya pūvālē ceyyappaṭṭa mālai pōlē irukkiṟa sarveśvaraṉai
children.translated_text: The Lord of all who appears like a garland made of beautiful <s>kāyā</s> flowers,

children.text: kaṭi araṅkatt’ arav’ aṇaiyil
children.translated_text: In the fortified <s>Araṅkam</s>, upon the serpent-couch —

children.text: araṇāka pōrum matiḷai uṭaiya kōyililē appaṭi parivaṉāṉa tiru anantāḻvāṉ-mēlē kaṇvaḷarnt’ aruḷukiṟa
children.translated_text: In the temple with walls strong enough to serve as a fortress, upon that affectionate <s>Tiru Anantāḻvāṉ</s>, He who graciously sleeps,

children.text: māyōṉai
children.translated_text: The wondrous one —

children.text: sa mayā bodhitaḥ śrīmān
children.translated_text: "<s>sa mayā bodhitaḥ śrīmān</s>" (that glorious one was awakened by me) —

children.text: eṉṉumpaṭi kaṇvaḷarnt’ aruḷukiṟa āścarya-bhūtaṉai
children.translated_text: The wonder-embodied one who graciously sleeps as described thus,

children.text: maṇa tūṇē paṟṟi niṉṟu
children.translated_text: Holding onto the fragrant pillar, standing —

children.text: amodastambhadvayaṅkaḷai paṟṟi niṉṟu; aḻakilē akappaṭṭa harṣattālē taḷḷuṇṇāmē iraṇṭu stambhaṅkaḷai paṟṟi niṉṟu
children.translated_text: Holding onto the two fragrant pillars; gripping two pillars so as not to be swept away by the ecstasy born of beholding His beauty,

children.text: vāy āra eṉṟu-kolō vāḻttum nāḷē
children.translated_text: When will my mouth fully praise Him?

children.text: kaṇṭāl koḷvatu vēṟ’ oru prayojanam illaiyiṟē;
children.translated_text: Upon seeing Him, there is no other purpose to seek;

children.text: pallāṇṭu pallāṇṭu
children.translated_text: "<s>Pallāṇṭu Pallāṇṭu</s>" (Long live! Long live!) —

children.text: eṉṉum ittaṉaiyiṟē.
children.translated_text: It is just this much.

children.text: e- māṇpiṉ ayaṉ nāṉku nāviṉālum
children.translated_text: The glorious <s>Ayaṉ</s> (Brahmā), with his four tongues,

children.text: eṭutt’ ētti īr iraṇṭu mukamum koṇṭ’
children.translated_text: lifting up and praising, with his twice-two faces,

children.text: e- māṭum eḻil kaṇkaḷ eṭṭiṉōṭum
children.translated_text: and with his beautiful eight radiant eyes,

children.text: toḻut’ ētti iṉit’ iṟaiñca niṉṟa cem poṉ
children.translated_text: worshipping, praising, sweetly bowing, standing — the golden

children.text: ammāṉ taṉ malar kamala koppūḻ tōṉṟa
children.translated_text: Lord, from whose lotus-like <s>nābhi</s> (navel) appears,

children.text: aṇi araṅkatt’ arav’ aṇaiyil paḷḷikoḷḷum
children.translated_text: upon the serpent-couch in beautiful <s>Araṅkam</s>, He who reclines —

children.text: ammāṉ taṉ aṭi iṇai kīḻ alarkaḷ iṭṭ’ aṅk’
children.translated_text: beneath His pair of feet, placing flowers there,

children.text: aṭiyavarōṭ’ eṉṟu-kolō aṇukum nāḷē
children.translated_text: when will I join with His devotees?

children.text: e- māṇpiṉ ayaṉ
children.translated_text: The glorious <s>Ayaṉ</s> (Brahmā) —

children.text: eppaṭippaṭṭa māṭcimai uṭaiya brahmā. atāvatu – stotrādikaḷai paṇṇum taṉmai kuṟaivaṟṟirukkai
children.translated_text: How great in glory is <s>Brahmā</s>! That is — his capacity for composing hymns and praises is complete and unsurpassed,

children.text: nāṉku nāviṉālum
children.translated_text: With his four tongues —

children.text: stotrādikaḷukku parikaramāṉa nālu nākkālum
children.translated_text: With four tongues that serve as instruments for hymns and praises,

children.text: eṭutt’ ētti
children.translated_text: Lifting up and praising —

children.text: taṉ śraddhaikku takkapaṭi eṭutt’ ētti
children.translated_text: Lifting up and praising in accordance with his devotion,

children.text: īr iraṇṭu mukamum koṇṭu -
children.translated_text: With his twice-two faces —

children.text: nālu vedattukku camainta nālu mukamum koṇṭu
children.translated_text: With four faces suited to the four <s>Vedas</s>,

children.text: e- māṭum
children.translated_text: All around —

children.text: piṉṉum muṉṉum maṭṭaṅkaḷum-ākiṟa paryantaṅkaḷ eṅkum
children.translated_text: On all sides, front and back, to the very limits,

children.text: eḻil kaṇkaḷ eṭṭiṉōṭum
children.translated_text: With his beautiful eight eyes —

children.text: aḻakai anubhavikkaikku pala kaṇ paṭaitta prayojanam peṟṟāṉ.
children.translated_text: He obtained the fruit of having been given many eyes for experiencing that beauty.

children.text: toḻut’ ētti iṉit’ iṟaiñca niṉṟa
children.translated_text: Worshipping, praising, sweetly bowing, standing —

children.text: prītipreritaṉāy koṇṭu toḻutu stotrādikaḷai paṇṇuvatu taṇṭaṉiṭuvatāmpaṭi niṉṟa
children.translated_text: Impelled by love, he worshipped and performed hymns — standing in such a way that the prostrations became like praise,

children.text: cem poṉ ammāṉ taṉ malar kamala koppūḻ tōṉṟa
children.translated_text: The golden Lord, from whose lotus-like navel appears —

children.text: spṛhaṇīyamāy i- aruk’ uṇṭāṉa kāryavargattukk’ ellām kāraṇam eṉṉum mahatvam tōṟṟumpaṭiyāy irukkiṟa tāmarai pūvai uṭaiya taṉ tiru nābhi tōṉṟa
children.translated_text: Appearing in a manner that displays the greatness of being the cause of the entire created world, which is desirable — from His <s>tiru nābhi</s> (sacred navel) having the lotus,

children.text: aṇi araṅkatt’ arav’ aṇaiyil paḷḷikoḷḷum
children.translated_text: Upon the serpent-couch in beautiful <s>Araṅkam</s>, He who reclines —

children.text: saṃsārattiṟku ābharaṇamāṉa kōyililē tiru anantāḻvāṉ-mēlē kaṇvaḷarnt’ aruḷukiṟa sarveśvaraṉuṭaiya
children.translated_text: In the temple that is the ornament of <s>saṃsāra</s> (the world), the Lord of all who graciously sleeps upon <s>Tiru Anantāḻvāṉ</s>,

children.text: aṭi iṇai kīḻ alarkaḷ iṭṭu
children.translated_text: Beneath His pair of feet, placing flowers —

children.text: avaṉ tiruvaṭikaḷiṉ-kīḻē puṣpādyupakaraṇaṅkaḷai paṇimāṟi
children.translated_text: Offering floral and other accessories beneath His sacred feet,

children.text: aṅk’ aṭiyavarōṭ’ eṉṟu-kolō aṇukum nāḷē -
children.translated_text: When will I join with His devotees there? —

children.text: aṅku antaraṅgavṛtti ceyyumavarkaḷōṭē sajātīyaṉāy nāṉum kiṭṭuvatu eṉṟō?
children.translated_text: When will I, becoming of the same kind, draw near to those who perform intimate service there?

children.text: aṭiyār kuḻāṅkaḷ
children.translated_text: "The assemblies of devotees" —

children.text: ityādi.
children.translated_text: and so forth.

children.text: māviṉai vāy piḷant’ ukanta mālai vēlai
children.translated_text: The <s>Māl</s> (Viṣṇu) who joyfully split open the mouth of the horse-demon,

children.text: vaṇṇaṉai eṉ kaṇṇaṉai val kuṉṟam ēnti
children.translated_text: the ocean-hued one, my <s>Kaṇṇaṉ</s> (Kṛṣṇa), who lifted the strong mountain,

children.text: āviṉai aṉṟ’ uyya koṇṭa āyar ēṟṟai
children.translated_text: the chief of cowherds who saved the cattle that day,

children.text: amararkaḷ tam talaivaṉai am tamiḻiṉ iṉpa
children.translated_text: the leader of the immortals, the joyous verse of beautiful Tamil,

children.text: pāviṉai am vaṭa moḻiyai paṟṟ’ aṟṟārkaḷ
children.translated_text: the beautiful northern language — in <s>Araṅkam</s> frequented by those free from attachment,

children.text: payil araṅkatt’ arav’ aṇaiyil paḷḷikoḷḷum
children.translated_text: upon the serpent-couch, He who reclines —

children.text: kōviṉai nāv’ uṟa vaḻutti eṉ taṉ kaikaḷ
children.translated_text: the king — praising Him with my tongue fully engaged, when will my hands scatter choice flowers and fold in worship?

children.text: koy malar tūy eṉṟu-kolō kūppum nāḷē
children.translated_text: When will my hands scatter choice flowers and join in worship?

children.text: māviṉai vāy piḷant’ ukanta mālai
children.translated_text: The <s>Māl</s> who joyfully split open the mouth of the horse-demon —

children.text: keśiyai anāyāsena piḷantu, āśritavirodhi pōka peṟṟōm eṉṟu ukanta āśritavyāmugdhaṉai
children.translated_text: He who effortlessly split <s>Keśī</s> and, being devoted to His devotees, rejoiced that the enemy of His devotees was destroyed,

children.text: vēlai vaṇṇaṉai
children.translated_text: The ocean-hued one —

children.text: āśritavirodhikaḷai vaḷarttālum viṭa oṇṇāta vaṭiv’ aḻakai uṭaiyavaṉai
children.translated_text: He who possesses a bodily beauty that cannot be abandoned even if one nourishes enmity toward His devotees,

children.text: eṉ kaṇṇaṉai
children.translated_text: My <s>Kaṇṇaṉ</s> —

children.text: veṟum vaṭiv’ aḻakē aṉṟiyē eṉakku bhavyaṉ-āṉavaṉai
children.translated_text: Not merely of beautiful form, but one who is gracious to me,

children.text: val kuṉṟam ēnti āviṉai aṉṟ’ uyya koṇṭa āyar ēṟṟai
children.translated_text: Who lifted the strong mountain and saved the cattle that day — the chief of cowherds —

children.text: indraṉ varṣikkiṟa kalvarṣattukku caliyāta malaiyai eṉṉutal; śrama-haramāṉa kuṉṟam eṉṉutal
children.translated_text: Either referring to the mountain that did not waver against the stone-rain sent by <s>Indra</s>; or the mountain that removes weariness,

children.text: āviṉai aṉṟ’ uyya koṇṭa
children.translated_text: Who saved the cattle that day —

children.text: upakārasmṛtiyum illāta pacukkaḷai rakṣitta
children.translated_text: He who protected the cows that had no memory of gratitude,

children.text: āyar ēṟṟai
children.translated_text: The chief of cowherds —

children.text: taṉ paruvattil piḷḷaikaḷai kāṭṭil tāṉ mēṉāṇipp’ uṭaiyavaṉai
children.translated_text: Among the boys of His age, He who possessed the greatest manliness,

children.text: amararkaḷ tam talaivaṉai
children.translated_text: The leader of the immortals —

children.text: taṉṉōṭu sāmyāpatti peṟṟ’ irukkiṟa nityasūrikaḷai kāṭṭil talaivaṉ-āṉavaṉai
children.translated_text: He who is the chief among the <s>Nityasūris</s> (eternal attendants) who have attained equality with Him,

children.text: am tamiḻiṉ iṉpa pāviṉai
children.translated_text: The joyous verse of beautiful Tamil —

children.text: iruḷ iriya cuṭar maṇikaḷ imaikkum neṟṟi
children.translated_text: "Whose forehead sparkles with radiant gems that dispel darkness" —

children.text: pōlē iṉiyavaṉai
children.translated_text: similarly delightful,

children.text: am vaṭa moḻiyai
children.translated_text: The beautiful northern language —

children.text: śrīrāmāyaṇam pōlē iṉiyavaṉai
children.translated_text: Delightful like the <s>Śrī Rāmāyaṇam</s>,

children.text: paṟṟ’ aṟṟārkaḷ payil araṅkatt’ arav’ aṇaiyil paḷḷikoḷḷum kōviṉai
children.translated_text: In <s>Araṅkam</s> frequented by those free from attachment, upon the serpent-couch, the king who reclines —

children.text: taṉṉaiyē paṟṟi puṟamp’ uḷḷavaṟṟai viṭṭa ananyaprayojanar nityavāsam paṇṇukiṟa kōyililē tiru anantāḻvāṉ-mēlē kaṇvaḷarnt’ aruḷukiṟa nāthaṉai
children.translated_text: In the temple where those who have abandoned all else, clinging only to Him, having no other purpose, dwell eternally — the Lord who graciously sleeps upon <s>Tiru Anantāḻvāṉ</s>,

children.text: nāv’ uṟa vaḻutti
children.translated_text: Praising with the tongue fully —

children.text: nāttaḻumpēṟumpaṭi stotraṅkaḷai paṇṇi
children.translated_text: Performing hymns until calluses form on the tongue,

children.text: eṉ taṉ kaikaḷ koy malar tūy eṉṟu-kolō kūppum nāḷē
children.translated_text: When will my hands scatter choice flowers and fold in worship?

children.text: kai taḻumpēṟumpaṭi puṣpādyupakaraṇaṅkaḷai paṇimāṟi añjali paṇṇa peṟuvat’ eṉṟō?
children.translated_text: When will I offer floral and other accessories until calluses form on the hands and perform <s>añjali</s> (salutation)?

children.text: iṇai illā iṉ icai yāḻ keḻumi iṉpa
children.translated_text: With the matchless sweet-sounding <s>yāḻ</s> (lute) resounding,

children.text: tumpuruvum nārataṉum iṟaiñci ētta
children.translated_text: <s>Tumburu</s> and <s>Nārada</s> bowing and praising with joy,

children.text: tuṇai illā tol maṟai-nūl tōttirattāl
children.translated_text: With the incomparable ancient <s>Maṟai</s> (Vedic) scriptures as hymns,

children.text: tol malar kaṇ ayaṉ vaṇaṅki ōvāt’ ētta
children.translated_text: The ancient lotus-eyed <s>Ayaṉ</s> (Brahmā) worshipping and ceaselessly praising,

children.text: maṇi māṭa
m
children.translated_text: and

children.text: māḷikaikaḷ malku celva
children.translated_text: palaces abounding in wealth,
With jeweled mansions

children.text: matiḷ araṅkatt’ arav’ aṇaiyil paḷḷi-koḷḷum
children.translated_text: upon the serpent-couch in walled <s>Araṅkam</s>, He who reclines —

children.text: maṇi-vaṇṇaṉ ammāṉai kaṇṭukoṇṭ’ eṉ
children.translated_text: the sapphire-hued Lord — having beheld Him, when will

children.text: malar ceṉṉi eṉṟu-kolō vaṇaṅkum nāḷē
children.translated_text: my flower-like head bow in worship?

children.text: iṇai illā iṉ icai yāḻ keḻumi
children.translated_text: With the matchless sweet-sounding <s>yāḻ</s> resounding —

children.text: upamānarahitamāṉa iṉiya icaiyai uṭaiya yāḻai neruṅki
children.translated_text: Drawing near the lute that possesses incomparably sweet music,

children.text: iṉpa tumpuruvum nārataṉum iṟaiñci ētta
children.translated_text: <s>Tumburu</s> and <s>Nārada</s> bowing and praising with joy —

children.text: pāṭṭāl vanta ānandattai uṭaiya tumburuvum nāradaṉum tiruvaṭikaḷilē viḻuntu stotraṅkaḷai paṇṇa
children.translated_text: <s>Tumburu</s> and <s>Nārada</s>, possessing the bliss born of song, falling at His sacred feet and performing hymns,

children.text: tuṇai illā tol maṟai-nūl tōttirattāl
children.translated_text: With the incomparable ancient Vedic scriptures as hymns —

children.text: opp’ ilāta paḻaiya vedaśāstram-ākiṟa stotrattālē
children.translated_text: With the hymn that is the matchless ancient <s>Veda-śāstra</s>,

children.text: tol malar kaṇ ayaṉ vaṇaṅki ōvāt’ ētta
children.translated_text: The ancient lotus-eyed <s>Ayaṉ</s> worshipping and ceaselessly praising —

children.text: tiru nābhīkamalattiṉ iṭattilē irukkiṟa brahmā, tiruvaṭikaḷilē praṇāmam paṇṇi viṭātē stotram paṇṇa
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s>, who resides in the <s>tiru nābhī-kamalam</s> (sacred navel-lotus), performing prostrations at His sacred feet and praising without cease,

children.text: maṇi māṭa
m
children.translated_text: and

children.text: māḷikaikaḷ malku celvam
children.translated_text: palaces abounding in wealth —
With jeweled mansions

children.text: maṇimayamāṉa māṭaṅkaḷaiyum mikka aiśvaryattaiyum uṭaiya
children.translated_text: Having mansions made of gems and abundant prosperity,

children.text: matiḷ araṅkatt’ arav’ aṇaiyil paḷḷikoḷḷum
children.translated_text: Upon the serpent-couch in walled <s>Araṅkam</s>, He who reclines —

children.text: mikka araṇāṉa periya matiḷai uṭaiya periya kōyililē tiru anantāḻvāṉ-mēlē paḷḷikoṇṭ’ aruḷum
children.translated_text: In the great temple with mighty fortress walls, He who graciously reclines upon <s>Tiru Anantāḻvāṉ</s>,

children.text: maṇi-vaṇṇaṉ ammāṉai kaṇṭukoṇṭu
children.translated_text: The sapphire-hued Lord — having beheld Him —

children.text: aḻakiya vaṭivai uṭaiya sarveśvaraṉai kaṇṭukoṇṭu
children.translated_text: Having beheld the Lord of all who possesses a beautiful form

children.text: eṉ malar ceṉṉi eṉṟu-kolō vaṇaṅkum nāḷē
children.translated_text: When, I wonder, will I bow down saying 'my flower-crowned head'?

children.text: nāṉ pū muṭi cūṭiṉa talai eṉṟō avaṉ tiruvaṭikaḷilē vaṇaṅkuvatu
children.translated_text: When will I, with my flower-adorned head, bow down at His sacred feet?

children.text: aḷi malar mēl ayaṉ araṉ intiraṉōṭu ēṉai amararkaḷ tam kuḻuvum arampai-yarum maṟṟum
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> on the bee-laden flower, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and the hosts of other immortals, along with the <s>apsaras</s> and others,

children.text: teḷi mati cēr muṉivarkaḷ tam kuḻuvum unti ticai ticaiyil malar tūvi ceṉṟu cērum
children.translated_text: The hosts of sages endowed with clear wisdom, pushing each other, scattering flowers in every direction, come and gather,

children.text: kaḷi malar cēr poḻil araṅkatt’ urakam ēṟi kaṇvaḷarum kaṭal-vaṇṇar kamala kaṇṇum
children.translated_text: In <s>Araṅkam</s> (Śrīraṅgam) with groves full of joyous flowers, ascending the serpent-couch, the lotus eyes of the ocean-hued Lord who reclines,

children.text: oḷi mati cēr tiru mukamum kaṇṭukoṇṭ’ eṉ uḷḷam mika eṉṟu-kolō urukum nāḷē
children.translated_text: And His radiant moonlike sacred face — when, I wonder, will my heart melt upon beholding them?

children.text: aḷi malar mēl ayaṉ araṉ intiraṉōṭu
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> on the bee-laden flower, <s>Rudra</s>, and with <s>Indra</s> —

children.text: vaṇṭukaḷ paṭinta aravindattiṉ-mēlē irukkiṟa brahmāvum, avaṉ makaṉāṉa rudraṉum, avarkaḷōṭē sahapaṭhikkappaṭṭa indraṉum; ivarkaḷuṭaṉē
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> who sits on the lotus filled with bees, his son <s>Rudra</s>, and <s>Indra</s> who is mentioned along with them; together with these —

children.text: ēṉai amararkaḷ tam kuḻuvum
children.translated_text: The hosts of other immortals,

children.text: avarkaḷ mūvaraiyum oḻinta devarkaḷ tiraḷum
children.translated_text: The multitude of <s>devas</s> (gods) other than those three,

children.text: arampaiyarum
children.translated_text: And the <s>apsaras</s> (celestial nymphs),

children.text: rambhai mutalāṉa apsarassukkaḷum
children.translated_text: <s>Rambhā</s> and the other <s>apsaras</s>,

children.text: maṟṟum teḷi mati cēr muṉivarkaḷ tam kuḻuvum
children.translated_text: And also the hosts of sages endowed with clear wisdom,

children.text: brahmabhāvanaiyāy cellum sanakādikaḷ tiraḷum
children.translated_text: The multitude of <s>Sanaka</s> and others who have attained <s>brahmabhāvanā</s> (realization of Brahman),

children.text: unti
children.translated_text: Pushing —

children.text: oruvarukk’ oruvar nerukki taḷḷi
children.translated_text: Pressing and pushing one another,

children.text: ticai ticaiyil malar tūvi ceṉṟu cērum
children.translated_text: Scattering flowers in every direction, they come and gather,

children.text: pārtta pārtta iṭam ellām puṣpavṛṣṭiyai paṇṇikkoṇṭu ceṉṟu kiṭṭum
children.translated_text: Showering a rain of flowers everywhere they look, they come and draw near,

children.text: kaḷi malar cēr poḻil araṅkatt’ urakam ēṟi
children.translated_text: Ascending the serpent-couch in <s>Araṅkam</s> with groves full of joyous flowers —

children.text: matu malarai uṭaittāṉa poḻilai uṭaiya araṅkattilē tiru anantāḻvāṉ-mēlē ēṟi
children.translated_text: In <s>Araṅkam</s> which has groves bursting with honey-laden flowers, ascending upon <s>Tiruvanantāḻvāṉ</s> (the sacred serpent <s>Ananta</s>),

children.text: kaṇvaḷarum kaṭal-vaṇṇar kamala kaṇṇum
children.translated_text: The lotus eyes of the ocean-hued Lord who reclines —

children.text: paḷḷikoḷḷukiṟa nīrvaṇṇar kamalakkaṇṇum
children.translated_text: The lotus eyes of the water-hued Lord who reclines in sacred sleep,

children.text: oḷi mati cēr tiru mukamum kaṇṭukoṇṭu
children.translated_text: And His radiant moonlike sacred face — having beheld them,

children.text: kuḷirtti mikku pukarai uṭaiya candraṉai oppu collalāṉa aḻakiya tiru mukattaiyum kaṇṭukoṇṭu
children.translated_text: Having beheld the beautiful sacred face that can be compared to the cool and lustrous moon,

children.text: eṉ uḷḷam mika eṉṟu-kolō urukum nāḷē
children.translated_text: When, I wonder, will my heart melt with overwhelming joy?

children.text: eṉ neñcu kuḷirntu urukuvat’ eṉṟō?
children.translated_text: When will my heart become refreshed and melt?

children.text: maṟam tikaḻum maṉam oḻittu vañcam māṟṟi
children.translated_text: Having abandoned the mind blazing with hostility, having removed deceit,

children.text: ai
m
pulaṉkaḷ aṭakki iṭar pāra tuṉpam
children.translated_text: Having subdued the senses, the suffering of the burden of affliction,
The five

children.text: tuṟant’ iru mu poḻut’ ētti ellai illā
children.translated_text: Having renounced, worshipping at the three times, the boundless

children.text: tol neṟikkaṇ nilai niṉṟa toṇṭar āṉa
children.translated_text: Devotees who stood firm on the ancient path —

children.text: aṟam tikaḻum maṉattavar tam katiyai poṉṉi
children.translated_text: The supreme goal of those whose hearts shine with righteousness,

children.text: aṇi araṅkatt’ arav’ aṇaiyil paḷḷikoḷḷum
children.translated_text: Who reclines on the serpent-couch in <s>Araṅkam</s> adorned by the <s>Poṉṉi</s> (Kāverī),

children.text: niṟam tikaḻum māyōṉai kaṇṭ’ eṉ kaṇkaḷ
children.translated_text: Having beheld the wondrous One whose form is resplendent — when will my eyes

children.text: nīr malka eṉṟu-kolō niṟkum nāḷē
children.translated_text: Fill with tears, I wonder, and stand transfixed?

children.text: maṟam tikaḻum maṉam oḻittu
children.translated_text: Having abandoned the mind blazing with hostility —

children.text: maṟam - kolaiyum, ciṉamum, koṭumaiyum. ivaṟṟāl viḷaṅkā-niṉṟa manassai vāsanaiyōṭē pōkki
children.translated_text: <s>Maṟam</s> (hostility) — killing, anger, and cruelty. Having removed, along with its residual impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), the mind that was illumined by these,

children.text: vañcam māṟṟi
children.translated_text: Having removed deceit —

children.text: poyyai pōkki
children.translated_text: Having removed falsehood,

children.text: ai
m
pulaṉkaḷ aṭakki
children.translated_text: Having subdued the senses —
The five

children.text: vaṉ pula cēkkaḷai paṭṭi-pukāmē kaṭṭi
children.translated_text: Having restrained the strong, unruly senses so they do not enter the field of sense objects,

children.text: iṭar pāra tuṉpam tuṟantu
children.translated_text: Having renounced the suffering of the burden of affliction —

children.text: mikka duḥkhattai viḷaippatāṉa
children.translated_text: That which produces great suffering,

children.text: pāram āya paḻaviṉaiyai paṟṟ’ aṟuttu
children.translated_text: Having cut off attachment to the heavy ancient <s>karma</s> (past actions),

children.text: iru mu poḻut’ ētti
children.translated_text: Worshipping at the three times —

children.text: pañcakālam eṉṉutal; periya mu poḻut’ eṉṉutal. i- kālaṅkaḷilē ētti
children.translated_text: This means the five times (<s>pañcakāla</s>); or the great three times. Worshipping at these times,

children.text: ellai illā tol neṟikkaṇ nilai niṉṟa toṇṭar āṉa
children.translated_text: Devotees who stood firm on the boundless ancient path —

children.text: aḷav’ iṟanta paḻaiya maryādaiyilē, cilavarāl kalakka oṇṇātapaṭi nilainiṉṟa vaiṣṇavarkaḷāṉa
children.translated_text: <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s> who stood firm, undisturbed by anyone, in the immeasurable ancient tradition,

children.text: aṟam tikaḻum maṉattavar tam katiyai
children.translated_text: The supreme goal of those whose hearts shine with righteousness —

children.text: ānṛśaṃsyapradhānarāy irukkumavarkaḷukku paramaprāpyaṉ āṉavaṉai
children.translated_text: He who is the supreme attainment (<s>paramaprāpya</s>) for those who are foremost in compassion (<s>ānṛśaṃsya</s>),

children.text: poṉṉi aṇi araṅkatt’ arav’ aṇaiyil paḷḷikoḷḷum
children.translated_text: Who reclines on the serpent-couch in <s>Araṅkam</s> adorned by the <s>Poṉṉi</s> —

children.text: poṉṉi cūḻ araṅkattilē
children.translated_text: In <s>Araṅkam</s> surrounded by the <s>Poṉṉi</s> (Kāverī),

children.text: tiru anantāḻvāṉ-ākiṟa paṭukkaiyilē kaṇvaḷarnt’ aruḷum
children.translated_text: Who graciously reclines on the bed that is <s>Tiruvanantāḻvāṉ</s> (the sacred serpent <s>Ananta</s>),

children.text: poṉṉi aṇi araṅkam
children.translated_text: <s>Poṉṉi</s>-adorned <s>Araṅkam</s> —

children.text: līlāvibhūtikku ābharaṇamāṉa kōyil
children.translated_text: The temple that is the ornament of <s>līlāvibhūti</s> (the realm of divine play),

children.text: niṟam tikaḻum māyōṉai kaṇṭu
children.translated_text: Having beheld the wondrous One whose form is resplendent —

children.text: aḻaku viḷaṅkā-niṉṟa āścaryabhūtaṉai kaṇṭu
children.translated_text: Having beheld the wondrous being (<s>āścaryabhūta</s>) whose beauty is radiant,

children.text: eṉ kaṇkaḷ nīr malka eṉṟu-kolō niṟkum nāḷē
children.translated_text: When, I wonder, will my eyes stand brimming with tears?

children.text: avaṉuṭaiya vaṭiv’ aḻakai kaṇṭu kaḷittu ānandāśru pravahikka niṟkum nāḷ eṉṟō?
children.translated_text: When will I stand with tears of joy (<s>ānandāśru</s>) flowing, having beheld and rejoiced in His beautiful form?

children.text: kōl ārnta neṭum cārṅkam kūṉ nal caṅkam
children.translated_text: The great <s>Śārṅga</s> bow fitted with arrows, the curved noble conch,

children.text: kolai āḻi koṭum taṇṭu koṟṟa
m
oḷ vāḷ
children.translated_text: The bright sword,
The deadly discus, the fierce mace,

children.text: kāl ārnta kati karuṭaṉ eṉṉum veṉṟi
children.translated_text: The victorious <s>Garuḍa</s> of wind-like speed, called

children.text: kaṭum paṟavai ivai aṉaittum puṟam cūḻ kāppa
children.translated_text: The fierce bird — all these surround and protect Him,

children.text: cēl ārnta neṭum kaḻaṉi cōlai cūḻnta
children.translated_text: In <s>Tiru Araṅkam</s> surrounded by groves and fertile fields teeming with fish,

children.text: tiruvaraṅkatt’ arav’ aṇaiyil paḷḷikoḷḷum
children.translated_text: He who reclines on the serpent-couch in <s>Tiru Araṅkam</s>,

children.text: mālōṉai kaṇṭ’ iṉpa kalavi eyti
children.translated_text: Having beheld the Lord (<s>Māl</s>) and attaining the joy of union,

children.text: val viṉaiyēṉ eṉṟu-kolō vāḻum nāḷē
children.translated_text: When, I wonder, will I, of heavy sins, live?

children.text: kōl ārnta neṭum cārṅkam
children.translated_text: The great <s>Śārṅga</s> bow fitted with arrows —

children.text: tiru caraṅkaḷōṭē kūṭiṉa śrīśārṅgam.
children.translated_text: <s>Śrīśārṅga</s>, united with the sacred arrows.

children.text: eppōtum kai kaḻalā nēmiyāṉ
children.translated_text: "The one whose discus never leaves His hand" —

children.text: eṉṉumā pōlē, eppōtu viṉai uṇṭām eṉṟu aṟiyāmaiyālē tiru caraṅkaḷai toṭuttapaṭiyē āyttu śrīśārṅgam iruppatu
children.translated_text: Just as it is said, because He does not know when enemies may arise, He keeps the sacred arrows strung; such is the state of <s>Śrīśārṅga</s>,

children.text: kūṉ nal caṅkam
children.translated_text: The curved noble conch —

children.text: bhagavadanubhavattāl vanta cerukkālē kūṉi āyttu śrīpāñcajanyam iruppatu
children.translated_text: <s>Śrīpāñcajanya</s> is curved due to the pride arising from the experience of the Lord,

children.text: kolai āḻi
children.translated_text: The deadly discus —

children.text: ivarkaḷ anubhavattil iḻiya pōt’ iṉṟiyē pratipakṣattai iru tuṇṭamāka viṭukai paṇipōrum āyttu tiru āḻiyāḻvāṉukku
children.translated_text: When devotees are about to lose their experience, the sacred <s>Āḻiyāḻvāṉ</s> (the discus) takes it upon himself to cut the adversary in two,

children.text: koṭum taṇṭu
children.translated_text: The fierce mace —

children.text: piṭitta piṭiyilē ukavātār maṇṇuṇṇumpaṭiyāy irukkiṟa gadai
children.translated_text: The <s>gadā</s> (mace) which makes those who do not yield at first grip eat the dust,

children.text: koṟṟa
m
oḷ vāḷ
children.translated_text: bright sword —
The victorious

children.text: aiśvaryaprakāśakamāṉa tiru koṟṟa vāḷ. koṟṟam - veṟṟi.
children.translated_text: The sacred victorious sword that manifests sovereignty (<s>aiśvarya</s>). <s>Koṟṟam</s> means victory.

children.text: kāl ārnta kati karuṭaṉ eṉṉum veṉṟi kaṭum paṟavai
children.translated_text: <s>Garuḍa</s> of wind-like speed, called the victorious fierce bird —

children.text: kāṟṟiṉuṭaiya mikka vegam pōlē irukkiṟa gatiyai uṭaiyaṉāy, periyatiruvaṭi eṉkiṟa pēraiyum uṭaiyaṉāy irukkiṟa kaṭum paṟavai
children.translated_text: Having speed like that of the wind, bearing the name <s>Periyatiruvaṭi</s> — such is the fierce bird,

children.text: ivai aṉaittum puṟam cūḻ kāppa
children.translated_text: All these surround and protect Him —

children.text: rāmalakṣmaṇaguptā sā
children.translated_text: "<s>Rāma-Lakṣmaṇa-guptā sā</s>" —

children.text: eṉṉumā pōlē kaṭaṟkarai veḷiyilē śrīsenai ellām kuḻaiccarakk’ āy, tāmum tampiyārum kākkumā pōlē, periyaperumāḷ kaṇvaḷarnt’ aruḷukaiyālē periyatiruvaṭi mutalāka śrīpañcāyudhāḻvārkaḷ cuṟṟum kāttukkoṇṭ’ āyttu niṟpatu.
children.translated_text: Just as on the seashore the entire army of <s>Śrī</s> formed a protective circle, and <s>Rāma</s> with His brother stood guard, so too because <s>Periya Perumāḷ</s> (the great Lord) graciously reclines, <s>Periyatiruvaṭi</s> (Garuḍa) along with the <s>Śrī Pañcāyudhāḻvārkaḷ</s> (the five sacred weapons) stand guard all around.

children.text: cēl ārnta neṭum kaḻaṉi cōlai cūḻnta tiruvaraṅkatt’ arav’ aṇaiyil paḷḷikoḷḷum mālōṉai
children.translated_text: The Lord (<s>Māl</s>) who reclines on the serpent-couch in <s>Tiru Araṅkam</s>, surrounded by groves and fertile fields teeming with fish —

children.text: cēlālē nirampiṉa kaḻaṉikaḷum cōlaikaḷum cūḻnta kōyililē tiru anantāḻvāṉ-mēlē kaṇvaḷarnt’ aruḷukiṟa sarvādhikaṉai
children.translated_text: The supreme one (<s>Sarvādhika</s>) who graciously reclines upon <s>Tiruvanantāḻvāṉ</s> in the temple surrounded by fields full of fish and groves,

children.text: kaṇṭ’ iṉpa kalavi eyti
children.translated_text: Having beheld and attaining the joy of union —

children.text: kaṇṭu niratiśayānandayuktaṉ āmpaṭi saṃśleṣittu
children.translated_text: Having beheld and embraced (<s>saṃśleṣa</s>) so as to attain unsurpassed bliss (<s>niratiśayānanda</s>),

children.text: val viṉaiyēṉ eṉṟu-kolō vāḻum nāḷē
children.translated_text: When, I wonder, will I, of heavy sins, live?

children.text: lokāntarattilē pōy kāṇa vēṇṭum vastu iṅkē sannihitamāy irukka ceytē anubhavikka oṇṇātē mahāpāpattai paṇṇiṉa nāṉ anubhavittu vāḻa peṟuvatu eṉṟō? bhagavadanubhavattukku virodhiyāy uḷḷavai ellām pāpamāy irukkumiṟē.
children.translated_text: The very object that one must go to another world to see is present here; yet I have committed the great sin of not experiencing it — when will I experience it and live? Everything that opposes the experience of the Lord is indeed sin.

children.text: tūrāta maṉa kātal toṇṭar taṅkaḷ
children.translated_text: The devotees whose heart-love is insatiable,

children.text: kuḻām kuḻumi tiruppukaḻkaḷ palavum pāṭi
children.translated_text: Gathering in crowds, singing many sacred praises,

children.text: ārāta maṉa kaḷippōṭ’ aḻuta kaṇṇīr
children.translated_text: With insatiable joy of heart, with tears that flow from weeping —

children.text: maḻai cōra niṉaint’ uruki ētti nāḷum
children.translated_text: Raining down, contemplating and melting, praising daily,

children.text: cīr ārnta muḻav’ ōcai paravai kāṭṭum
children.translated_text: In <s>Tiru Araṅkam</s> where splendid drum-music evokes the ocean's sound,

children.text: tiruvaraṅkatt’ arav’ aṇaiyil paḷḷikoḷḷum
children.translated_text: He who reclines on the serpent-couch in <s>Tiru Araṅkam</s>,

children.text: pōr āḻi ammāṉai kaṇṭu tuḷḷi
children.translated_text: Having beheld the Lord of the battle-discus, leaping with joy —

children.text: pūtalattil eṉṟu-kolō puraḷum nāḷē
children.translated_text: When, I wonder, will I roll upon this earth?

children.text: tūrāta maṉa kātal toṇṭar taṅkaḷ kuḻām kuḻumi
children.translated_text: The devotees whose heart-love is insatiable, gathering in crowds —

children.text: tūrā kuḻi tūrtt’ eṉai nāḷ akaṉṟ’ iruppaṉ
children.translated_text: "How many days will I remain, having departed, filling the unfillable pit?" —

children.text: eṉṟu saṃsārikaḷ śabdādiviṣayaṅkaḷai pala nāḷ anubhavittālum indriyaṅkaḷai tṛpti ākka pōkātā pōlē, bhagavadanubhavam orukālum ārāt’ irukkum śrīvaiṣṇavarkaḷ kuḻāttil eṉṉaiyum kūṭa kalaci
children.translated_text: Just as worldly people (<s>saṃsārins</s>) can never satisfy their senses even after enjoying sense-objects for many days, the <s>Śrī Vaiṣṇavas</s> whose experience of the Lord is never satiated — mixing me too into their assembly,

children.text: tiru-p-pukaḻkaḷ palavum pāṭi
children.translated_text: Singing many sacred praises —

children.text: avaṉuṭaiya kalyāṇaguṇaṅkaḷukku vācakamāṉa tirunāmaṅkaḷ palavaṟ-ṟaiyum pāṭi
children.translated_text: Singing many sacred names (<s>tirunāma</s>) that express His auspicious qualities (<s>kalyāṇaguṇa</s>),

children.text: ārāta maṉa kaḷippōṭ’ aḻuta kaṇṇīr maḻai cōra
children.translated_text: With insatiable joy of heart, tears flowing from weeping —

children.text: tirunāmaṅkaḷai coṉṉapaṭiyālē manassukku ārāmaiyālē hṛṣṭaṉāy attālē ānandāśru pravahikka
children.translated_text: Because of uttering the sacred names, the heart remains insatiable, and being delighted thereby, tears of joy (<s>ānandāśru</s>) flow,

children.text: niṉaint’ uruki ētti
children.translated_text: Contemplating and melting, praising —

children.text: ivarkaḷ tiraḷilē kūṭi tirunāmattai coṉṉapaṭiyālē tirunāmadvārā viṣayattai niṉaittu attālē uruki, uruki vaḻintu puṟappaṭṭa col eṉṉumpaṭi stotraṅkaḷai paṇṇi
children.translated_text: Having joined their assembly and uttered the sacred names, contemplating the object through the sacred names, thereby melting, and from that melting, words flowing forth — thus composing hymns of praise (<s>stotra</s>),

children.text: nāḷumcīr ārnta ityādi
children.translated_text: Daily, with splendid etc. —

children.text: aiśvaryaprakāśakamāṉa vādhyaghoṣaṅkaḷ samudraghoṣattai kāṭṭā-niṟkiṟa kōyililē tiru anantāḻvāṉ-mēlē nityavāsam paṇṇukiṟa yuddhonmukhamāṉa tiruvāḻiyai kaiyilē uṭaiya sarveśvaraṉai
children.translated_text: In the temple where the drum-sounds manifesting sovereignty rival the roar of the ocean, the Lord of all (<s>Sarveśvara</s>) who eternally resides upon <s>Tiruvanantāḻvāṉ</s>, holding in His hand the sacred discus ready for battle,

children.text: tuḷḷi
children.translated_text: Leaping —

children.text: sasambhramanṛttam paṇṇi
children.translated_text: Performing a dance of ecstasy (<s>sasambhrama-nṛtta</s>),

children.text: pūtalattil eṉṟu-kolō puraḷum nāḷē
children.translated_text: When, I wonder, will I roll upon this earth?

children.text: siṃhāsanattilē iṟumānt’ irukkum iruppu oḻintu hṛṣṭaṉāy bhūmiyilē puraḷuvatu eṉṟu-kolō?
children.translated_text: When will I abandon the proud posture of sitting on a throne and, filled with joy, roll upon the ground?

m
vāṉakam uyya amarar uyya
children.translated_text: That the heavenly world may thrive, that the immortals may thrive,
The great mighty

children.text: maṇ uyya maṇṇulakil maṉicar uyya
children.translated_text: That the earth may thrive, that humans in the earthly world may thrive,

Happiness may grow, and

children.translated_text: He who graciously reclines facing the southern direction with love,

children.translated_text: In the sacred courtyard of the beautiful <s>Araṅkaṉ</s> (Lord of Śrīraṅgam), the devotees'

children.translated_text: Great assembly, having beheld it — I too,
Joyous

children.text: icaint’ uṭaṉē eṉṟu-kolō irukkum nāḷē
children.translated_text: When, I wonder, will I dwell there in agreement?

children.text: val peru
m
vāṉakam uyya amarar uyya
children.translated_text: That the heavenly world may thrive, that the immortals may thrive —
The great mighty

children.text: naimittikapraḷayāpad-t-ukku iḷaiyāta brahmalokam mutalāka mēl uṇṭāṉa lokaṅkaḷ uyya; aṅk’ uṇṭāṉa brahmādikaḷ ujjīvikka āyttu brahmalokattil kōyilāḻvār eḻuntaruḷi iruntapaṭi
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmaloka</s> and the worlds above, which are not destroyed by incidental cosmic dissolution (<s>naimittikapralaya</s>), may thrive; that <s>Brahmā</s> and others there may be uplifted — such is the state of the Lord's presence in <s>Brahmaloka</s>,

children.text: maṇ uyya maṇṇulakil maṉicar uyya
children.translated_text: That the earth may thrive, that humans in the earthly world may thrive —

children.text: śrīvibhīṣaṇāḻvāṉukkāka aṅkuniṉṟum iṅk’ ēṟa eḻuntaruḷukaiyālē bhūmi-yum bhūmiyil uṇṭāṉa cetanarum ujjīvikka
children.translated_text: Because He graciously descended from there to here for the sake of <s>Śrī Vibhīṣaṇāḻvāṉ</s>, the earth and the sentient beings on earth may be uplifted,

children.text: tuṉpa
m
miku tuyar akala
children.translated_text: And great sorrow may depart —
That suffering

children.text: nityaduḥkhattai viḷaivippatāṉa pāpaṅkaḷ akala
children.translated_text: That the sins which produce eternal suffering may depart,

children.text: ayarv’ oṉṟ’ illā cukam vaḷara
children.translated_text: That unmixed tireless happiness may grow —

children.text: duḥkha
children.translated_text: Suffering

children.text: m
miśriyāta nityamāṉa sukham vaḷara
children.translated_text: That eternal happiness, unmixed with sorrow, may grow,

children.text: aka
m
makiḻum toṇṭar vāḻa
children.translated_text: The rejoicing devotees may flourish —
And

children.text: bhagavadanubhavattālē niratiśayānandayuktarāṉa śrīvaiṣṇavarkaḷ vāḻa
children.translated_text: That the <s>Śrī Vaiṣṇavas</s>, filled with unsurpassed bliss from the experience of the Lord, may flourish,

children.text: aṉpoṭu teṉ ticai nōkki paḷḷikoḷḷum aṇi araṅkaṉ tiru muṟṟattu
children.translated_text: In the sacred courtyard of the beautiful <s>Araṅkaṉ</s> who graciously reclines facing the southern direction with love —

children.text: śrīvibhīṣaṇāḻvāṉukku rājyattai koṭuttu a- dikkai pārttu kaṇvaḷarnt’ aruḷukiṟa periyaperumāḷiṉ uḷḷil tirumuṟṟattilē
children.translated_text: In the inner sacred courtyard of <s>Periya Perumāḷ</s> who, having given the kingdom to <s>Śrī Vibhīṣaṇāḻvāṉ</s>, graciously reclines facing that direction,

children.text: aṇi araṅkaṉ
children.translated_text: The beautiful <s>Araṅkaṉ</s> —

children.text: aḻakiya araṅkattai taṉakku vāsasthānamāka uṭaiyavaṉ
children.translated_text: He who has beautiful <s>Araṅkam</s> as His abode,

children.text: aṭiyār taṅkaḷ iṉpa
m
miku perum kuḻuvu kaṇṭu
children.translated_text: Great assembly, having beheld —
The devotees' joyous

children.text: niratiśayānandayuktarāy irukkiṟa śrīvaiṣṇavarkaḷ tiraḷai kaṇṭu
children.translated_text: Having beheld the assembly of <s>Śrī Vaiṣṇavas</s> filled with unsurpassed bliss,

children.text: yāṉum icaintu
children.translated_text: I too, having agreed —

children.text: abhiṣiktakṣatriyaṉ eṉṟu eṉṉai niṉaiyātē avarkaḷilē oruvaṉāka icaintu
children.translated_text: Not considering myself as an anointed king (<s>abhiṣikta-kṣatriya</s>), having agreed to become one among them,

children.text: uṭaṉē eṉṟu-kolō irukkum nāḷē
children.translated_text: When, I wonder, will I dwell there?

children.text: eṉṉai cilar sevikka nāṉ niyāmakaṉāy irukkum iruppai oḻintu śrī-vaiṣṇavarkaḷ tiraḷilē sevitt’ iruppatu eṉṟō?
children.translated_text: When will I abandon the position where some serve me and I am the ruler, and instead serve among the assembly of <s>Śrī Vaiṣṇavas</s>?

children.text: tiṭar viḷaṅku karai poṉṉi naṭuvupāṭṭu
children.translated_text: Amidst the <s>Poṉṉi</s> (Kāverī) with its gleaming banks,

children.text: tiruvaraṅkatt’ arav’ aṇaiyil paḷḷikoḷḷum
children.translated_text: He who reclines on the serpent-couch in <s>Tiru Araṅkam</s>,

children.text: kaṭal viḷaṅku karu
m
mēṉi ammāṉ taṉṉai
children.translated_text: Form gleams like the ocean —
The Lord whose dark

children.text: kaṇ āra kaṇṭ’ ukakkum kātal taṉṉāl
children.translated_text: With a love that desires to behold Him to the full satisfaction of the eyes,

children.text: kuṭai viḷaṅku viṟal tāṉai koṟṟa
m
children.translated_text: Victorious

children.text: oḷ vāḷ
children.translated_text: bright sword —
With parasol gleaming, with victorious mighty army,

children.text: kūṭalar kōṉ koṭai kulacēkaraṉ col ceyta
children.translated_text: <s>Kulacēkaraṉ</s>, king of the <s>Kūṭalar</s> (Madurai), of great generosity, composed these words,

children.text: naṭai viḷaṅku tamiḻ mālai pattum vallār
children.translated_text: Those who master this garland of ten verses in flowing Tamil,

children.text: nalam tikaḻ nāraṇaṉ aṭi kīḻ naṇṇuvārē
children.translated_text: Will attain the feet of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> who shines with all goodness.

children.text: tiṭar viḷaṅku karai poṉṉi naṭuvupāṭṭu
children.translated_text: Amidst the <s>Poṉṉi</s> with its gleaming banks —

children.text: viḷaṅkā-niṉṟa tiru kuṟaiyai uṭaittāy karaiyaiyum uṭaittāṉa kāveri cūḻnta
children.translated_text: The <s>Kāverī</s>, which has resplendent bends and banks, surrounding it,

children.text: tiruvaraṅkatt’ arav’ aṇaiyil paḷḷikoḷḷum kaṭal viḷaṅku karu
m
mēṉi ammāṉ taṉṉai
children.translated_text: Form gleams like the ocean —
He who reclines on the serpent-couch in <s>Tiru Araṅkam</s>, whose dark

children.text: kōyililē tiru anantāḻvāṉ-mēlē kaṇvaḷarnt’ aruḷukiṟa kaṭal pōlē śramaharamāṉa tirumēṉi niṟattai uṭaiya sarveśvaraṉai
children.translated_text: The Lord of all (<s>Sarveśvara</s>) who graciously reclines upon <s>Tiruvanantāḻvāṉ</s> in the temple, whose sacred form has the fatigue-removing hue of the ocean,

children.text: kaṇ āra kaṇṭ’ ukakkum kātal taṉṉāl
children.translated_text: With a love that desires to behold Him to the full satisfaction of the eyes —

children.text: kaṇṇālē kaṇṭ’ aṉubhavikka vēṇum eṉṉum ācaippāṭṭōṭē
children.translated_text: With the yearning to experience Him by seeing with one's own eyes,

children.text: kuṭai viḷaṅku viṟal tāṉai koṟṟa
m
children.translated_text: Victorious

children.text: oḷ vāḷ kūṭalar kōṉ
children.translated_text: bright sword — the king of <s>Kūṭalar</s> (Madurai),
With parasol gleaming, with victorious mighty army,

children.text: viḷaṅkukiṟa veṇkoṟṟakkuṭaiyaiyum veṟṟiyai uṭaiya senaiyaiyum, aiśvaryaprakāśakamāṉa vāḷaiyum uṭaiyavarāy maturaikku nirvāhakarumāṉa
children.translated_text: Possessing the gleaming white royal parasol, the victorious army, and the sword manifesting sovereignty — the ruler of Madurai,

children.text: koṭai kulacēkaraṉ col ceyta
children.translated_text: <s>Kulacēkaraṉ</s> of great generosity composed these —

children.text: koṭai māṟātē koṭukkum perumāḷ aruḷicceyta
children.translated_text: <s>Perumāḷ</s> (the king) who gives without cease, graciously composed these,

children.text: naṭai viḷaṅku tamiḻ mālai pattum vallār
children.translated_text: Those who master this garland of ten verses in flowing Tamil

children.text: uḷḷil arthattil iḻiya vēṇṭātē, padaṅkaḷ cērnta cērttikaḷ pārkkavum vēṇṭātē, itu tāṉē ākarṣakamāy irukkiṟa tamiḻ toṭai pattum vallār
children.translated_text: Without needing to delve into the inner meaning, without needing to examine the combinations formed by the words, these ten Tamil verses that are attractive in themselves—those who master them

children.text: nalam tikaḻ nāraṇaṉ aṭi kīḻ naṇṇuvārē
children.translated_text: will reach the feet of <s>Nāraṇaṉ</s> (Nārāyaṇa) who shines with goodness.

children.text: śīlādiguṇapūrṇarāy, sarvasvāmiyāy, vatsalarāy irukkum periyaperumāḷ tiruvaṭikaḷiṉ-kīḻē anubhavikka ācaippaṭṭā pōlē kiṭṭa peṟuvarkaḷ.
children.translated_text: They will attain proximity to the divine feet of <s>Periya Perumāḷ</s> (Lord Raṅganātha), who is full of qualities such as <s>śīla</s> (gracious condescension), who is the Lord of all, and who is <s>vatsala</s> (tender like a mother cow to her calf), just as they desired to experience.

children.text: bhagavadviṣayattilē kaivaittārkku saṃbhavippaṉa cila svabhāvaṅkaḷ uṇṭu; ānukūlyasaṅkalpādikaḷ.
ānukūlyasya saṅkalpaḥ prātikūlyasya varjanam
children.translated_text: The resolve toward what is favorable, the avoidance of what is adverse—

children.text: ānukūlyam āvatu - bhāgavataviṣayattilum, bhagavadviṣayattilum paṇṇum ānukūlyam. bhagavadviṣayam pūrṇam-ākaiyālē ivaṉukku ānukūlyam paṇṇukaikku tuṟai illaiyiṟē. ippaṭi tuṟai illai eṉṟu ivaṉ kaivāṅkāmaikkiṟē ivaṉ ukanta dravyamē taṉakku tirumēṉiyākavum, ivaṉ tirumañcaṉam paṇṇiṉapōtu tirumañcaṉam paṇṇiyum, amutu ceyya paṇṇiṉapōtu amutu ceytum, allātapōtu paṭṭiṉiyum āmpaṭiyiṟē avarkaḷukku taṉṉai amaittu vaippatu; ippaṭi āyttat’ illaiākil paripūrṇaviṣayattil ivaṉukku kiñcitkarikkaikku tuṟai illaiyiṟē.
children.translated_text: <s>Ānukūlya</s> (favorableness) means the favorableness one shows toward <s>bhāgavata</s>-s (devotees) and toward the Lord. Since the Lord is complete and perfect, there is no occasion for this person to render service to Him. Because there is no such occasion, the Lord, so that this person does not withdraw, makes the very substance dear to Him into His divine body; when He performs His sacred ablution, they perform ablution; when He partakes of food, they partake; and when He does not, they fast—thus He arranges Himself for them. If it were not so, there would be no occasion for rendering even the slightest service to the perfect Lord.

children.text: jñānī tvātmaiva me matam
children.translated_text: "The <s>jñānī</s> (knower) is My very self—this is My view,"

children.text: eṉṟum,
children.translated_text: and,

children.text: mama prāṇā hi pāṇḍavāḥ
children.translated_text: "The <s>Pāṇḍava</s>-s are My very life-breath,"

children.text: eṉṟum, pattar āvi eṉṟum irukkumavaṉ-ākaiyālē, tadīyaviṣayattilē paṇṇum ānukūlyamum bhagavadviṣayattilē paṇṇiṟṟāmiṟē. ākaiyālē, ivarum tamakku ivai iraṇṭum piṟantat’ eṉkiṟār. bhaga-vadviṣayattilē piṟanta ānukūlyam coṉṉār kīḻil tirumoḻiyil; tadīyaviṣayattil ānukūlyam piṟanta paṭi collukiṟār i- tirumoḻiyil.
children.translated_text: and since He is one who considers His devotees as His very life, the favorableness shown toward His devotees (<s>tadīya</s>) is itself favorableness shown toward the Lord. Therefore, these <s>Āḻvār</s>-s say that both of these have arisen in them. The favorableness born in <s>bhagavadviṣaya</s> was spoken of in the previous <s>Tirumoḻi</s>; the favorableness born toward the devotees is being spoken of in this <s>Tirumoḻi</s>.
For those who have placed themselves in <s>bhagavadviṣaya</s> (the matter of the Lord), certain dispositions naturally arise—the resolve toward what is favorable and so forth.

children.text: tēṭṭ’ arum tiṟal tēṉiṉai teṉ araṅkaṉai tiru-mātu vāḻ
children.translated_text: Him who is honey of rare and mighty power, the Lord of beautiful <s>Araṅkam</s> (Śrīraṅgam), where <s>Tiru</s> (<s>Śrī</s>, <s>Lakṣmī</s>) dwells—

children.text: vāṭṭam il vaṉamālai mārvaṉai vāḻtti māl koḷ cintaiyar āy
children.translated_text: Him who bears on His chest the unfading, beautiful <s>vanamālā</s> (forest garland)—having praised Him and become those whose minds are seized by love,

children.text: āṭṭam mēvi alant’ aḻaitt’ ayarv’ eytum mey aṭiyārkaḷ tam
children.translated_text: the true devotees who, engaging in dance, cry out with outstretched arms and grow weary—

children.text: īṭṭam kaṇṭ’ iṭa kūṭumēl atu kāṇum kaṇ payaṉ āvatē
children.translated_text: if one could see their assembly, that seeing would be the true fruit of having eyes.

children.text: avatārikai -
tēṭṭarum ityādi
children.translated_text: "<s>Tēṭṭarum</s>" and so forth.

children.text: muṭiya bhāgavataviṣayam uddeśyam ākiṟatu bhagavadguṇaṅkaḷilē avagāhittār eṉṉumatiṟē. iṉṉāṉ arthamuṭaiyaṉ, kṣetramuṭaiyaṉ eṉṟu āśrayippārai pōlē, bhagavadpratyāsatti uṭaiyār eṉṟiṟē ivarkaḷai paṟṟukiṟatu. bhagavadviṣayattilē stotram paṇṇa iḻintavar ācārya-viṣayattai stotram paṇṇa pukku avarkku niṟamāka colliṟṟu bhagavad-viṣayattil jñānabhaktikaḷaiyiṟē;
children.translated_text: Ultimately, the devotees (<s>bhāgavata</s>-s) become the goal because they have immersed themselves in the Lord's qualities. Just as people seek refuge saying 'this person has wealth, this person has land,' so too it is because of their proximity to the Lord that one takes refuge in these devotees. Those who descended to compose hymns about the Lord, when they entered into praising the <s>ācārya</s>-s (preceptors), what they expressed as a measure of the <s>ācārya</s>-s' greatness was indeed the knowledge and devotion directed toward the Lord;

children.text: jñānavairāgyarāśaye.
children.translated_text: "To Him who is a treasure-house of <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) and <s>vairāgya</s> (renunciation)."

children.text: tēṭṭ’ arum
children.translated_text: "Of rare"—

children.text: tāmē vantu sulabhar ām ittaṉai allatu svayatnattāl kāṇa oṇṇāt’ eṉkai
children.translated_text: means that unless He Himself comes and makes Himself accessible, He cannot be found through one's own effort.

children.text: tiṟal tēṉiṉai
children.translated_text: "Of mighty honey"—

children.text: ya ātmadā baladā
children.translated_text: "He who gives the self, who gives strength"—

children.text: eṉṉumā pōlē taṉṉaiyum koṭuttu taṉṉai anubhavikkaikk’ īṭāṉa balattaiyum koṭukkum tēṉ
children.translated_text: just as that verse says, He is the honey who gives Himself and also gives the strength needed to experience Him.

children.text: tēṉiṉai teṉ araṅkaṉai ityādi
children.translated_text: "The honey, the Lord of beautiful <s>Araṅkam</s>" and so forth—

children.text: spṛhaṇīyamāṉa tiruvaraṅkattilē nityavāsam paṇṇumavaṉāy. tirumēṉiyiṉ sparśattālē oru kālaikk’ orukāl cevvi peṟum-āyttu iṭṭa tiru mālai
children.translated_text: He who makes His permanent abode in the desirable <s>Tiru Araṅkam</s> (Śrīraṅgam). The garland placed upon Him gains ever greater beauty through the touch of His divine form.

children.text: vāḻtti
children.translated_text: "Having praised"—

children.text: vaṭiv’ āy niṉ vala
m
mārpiṉil vāḻkiṉṟa maṅkaiyum pallāṇṭu
children.translated_text: "chest where the Lady dwells—long live!"
"In the form of Your mighty"

children.text: eṉkiṟapaṭiyē avaḷum ivaṉum cērnta cērttikku maṅgaḷāśāsanam paṇṇi
children.translated_text: As that verse says, performing <s>maṅgaḷāśāsana</s> (benedictory praise) for the union of Her and Him,

children.text: māl koḷ cintaiyar āy
children.translated_text: "those whose minds are seized by love"—

children.text: pittēṟiṉa manassai uṭaiyarāy
children.translated_text: those who have minds maddened with love,

children.text: āṭṭam mēvi
children.translated_text: "engaging in dance"—

children.text: āṭavēṇum eṉṉum kāryabuddhyā aṉṟiyilē premam oṭṭāmaiyālē āṭṭa
children.translated_text: not out of any calculated purpose to dance, but because love compels them, they dance—

children.text: m
mēvi
children.translated_text: "engaging"—

children.text: alant’ aḻaittu
children.translated_text: "crying out with outstretched arms"—

children.text: alamantu kāryappāṭ’ aṟa kūppiṭṭu
children.translated_text: being overwhelmed and crying out helplessly, having lost all sense of purpose,

children.text: ayarv’ eytum mey aṭiyārkaḷ tam
children.translated_text: "the true devotees who grow weary"—

children.text: kramaprāpti poṟāmaiyālē aṟivu kuṭipōy, paravaśarāṉa ananyaprayojana-ruṭaiya
children.translated_text: those who are exclusive devotees (<s>ananyaprayojana</s>), who, unable to endure the gradual path (<s>kramaprapti</s>), lose their senses and become completely absorbed,

children.text: īṭṭam -
children.translated_text: "assembly"—

children.text: ippaṭi iruppār umakku ettaṉai pēr vēṇum eṉṉa; aṭiyārkaḷ kuḻāṅkaḷai kāṇa peṟil
children.translated_text: as if to say, 'How many such people do you need?'—if one could see the assemblies of devotees,

children.text: kūṭumēl atu kāṇum kaṇ payaṉ āvatē
children.translated_text: "if one could gather them, that seeing would be the fruit of having eyes"—

children.text: itu kūṭiṟṟ’ ākil prayojanam kaṇṇukku it’ allat’ illai. dṛṣṭaprayojanam itu.
children.translated_text: if this gathering were to happen, the reward for the eyes would be nothing other than this. This is the visible reward.
Introduction—

children.text: tōṭ’ ulām malar maṅkai tōḷ iṇai tōyntatum cuṭar vāḷiyāl
children.translated_text: Him who embraced the shoulders of the Lady of the flower with abundant petals, Him who by His radiant discus

children.text: nīṭu mā maram ceṟṟatum nirai mēyttatum ivaiyē niṉaintu
children.translated_text: felled the tall great trees, Him who herded the cattle—thinking only of these deeds,

children.text: āṭi pāṭi araṅka ō eṉṟ’ aḻaikkum toṇṭar aṭi poṭi
children.translated_text: the devotees who dance and sing crying out 'O <s>Araṅkā</s>!'—the dust of their feet,

children.text: āṭa nām peṟil kaṅkai nīr kuṭaint’ āṭum vēṭkai eṉ āvatē
children.translated_text: if we could receive it and bathe in it, what need would there be for the desire to plunge and bathe in the waters of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>?

children.text: tōṭ’ ulām malar maṅkai tōḷ iṇai tōyntatum
children.translated_text: "Him who embraced the shoulders of the Lady of the flower with abundant petals"—

children.text: itaḻ mikk’ irunta tāmarai pūvai vāsasthānamāka uṭaiya periya-pirāṭṭiyār tiru tōḷkaḷ iraṇṭaiyum tōyntatum; taṉiyaṉ peru veḷḷattilē iḻintu anubhavikka tēṭiṉā pōlē tōyntatum
children.translated_text: The two divine shoulders of <s>Periya Pirāṭṭi</s> (Mahālakṣmī), who has as Her abode the lotus flower rich with petals—He embraced them; just as one who has plunged into a singular great flood seeks to experience it fully, He embraced them.

children.text: cuṭar vāḷiyāl
children.translated_text: "by His radiant discus"—

children.text: pukarai uṭaiya ampālē
children.translated_text: by the arrow possessing splendor,

children.text: nīṭu mā maram ceṟṟatum
children.translated_text: "felled the tall great trees"—

children.text: ōkkattai uṭaittāṉa marā maraṅkaḷ ēḻaiyum eytatum, paṇṭē tuḷai āṉavaṟṟilē ōṭṭiṉā pōlēāyttu – anantamāy balavattaramāṉa saptasālattai nirasittatum; āśritarai viśvasippikkum ceyaliṟē.
children.translated_text: He shot through all seven of the mighty <s>marā</s> trees that had strength—as though piercing through what was already hollowed—He destroyed the seven <s>sāla</s> trees that were immense and exceedingly powerful; this is the deed that inspires trust in those who take refuge.

children.text: nirai mēyttatum
children.translated_text: "herded the cattle"—

children.text: ubhayavibhūtināyakaṉāy iruntu-vaittu kaiyilē oru kōlai koṇṭu pacu mēyttatum
children.translated_text: though being the Lord of both realms (<s>ubhayavibhūti</s>), He held a staff in His hand and herded cows.

children.text: ivaiyē niṉaintu
children.translated_text: "thinking only of these"—

children.text: inta śīlādiguṇaṅkaḷaiyē niṉaintu; ivaṟṟai niṉaikkumat’ oḻiya vēṟ’ oru prayojanattaiyum kaṇiciyātē
children.translated_text: thinking only of these qualities of <s>śīla</s> (gracious condescension) and the like; not seeking any other reward besides contemplating these,

children.text: āṭi pāṭi
children.translated_text: "dancing and singing"—

children.text: prītiprakarṣattālē irukka māṭṭātē āṭi pāṭi
children.translated_text: out of the intensity of love, unable to remain still, dancing and singing,

children.text: araṅka ō eṉṟ’ aḻaikkum
children.translated_text: "crying out 'O <s>Araṅkā</s>!'"—

children.text: perumāḷ tirunāmattai colli āṟṟa māṭṭātē kūppiṭum
children.translated_text: calling out the divine name of <s>Perumāḷ</s> (the Lord), unable to contain themselves,

children.text: toṇṭar aṭi poṭi āṭa nām peṟil
children.translated_text: "if we could receive the dust of the feet of such devotees"—

children.text: bhagavadguṇaviddharāṉa śrīvaiṣṇavarkaḷuṭaiya pādareṇukkaḷilē ava-gāhikka peṟil; eppōtum okka bhagavadsambandham uṭaiyar-ākaiyālē tīrthabhūtarāṉa śrīvaiṣṇavarkaḷuṭaiya pādareṇukkaḷilē avagāhikka peṟil
children.translated_text: if we could immerse ourselves in the foot-dust of the <s>Śrīvaiṣṇava</s>-s who are pierced by the Lord's qualities; if we could immerse ourselves in the foot-dust of those <s>Śrīvaiṣṇava</s>-s who are sacred like <s>tīrtha</s> (holy waters) because they always possess connection with the Lord,

children.text: kaṅkai nīr kuṭaint’ āṭum vēṭkai eṉ āvatē
children.translated_text: "what need would there be for the desire to bathe in the waters of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>?"—

children.text: kādācitkasambandhamē āy pala cikku talaikaḷilē pukku upahatippaṭṭa gaṅgai āṭiṉāl eṉṉa prayojanam uṇṭu?
children.translated_text: What benefit would there be in bathing in the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, whose connection is only occasional and which, having entered into many complicated channels, has become contaminated?

children.text: nalam tikaḻ caṭaiyāṉ
children.translated_text: "The one with matted locks shining with goodness"—

children.text: ityādi. potu āṉatiṟē atu.
children.translated_text: and so forth. That is common to all.

children.text: ēṟ’ aṭarttatum ēṉam āy nilam kīṇṭatum muṉ irāmaṉ āy
children.translated_text: Him who subdued the bulls, Him who as the Boar dug up the earth, Him who previously as <s>Rāma</s>

children.text: māṟ’ aṭarttatum maṇ aḷantatum colli pāṭi vaḷ poṉṉi pēr
children.translated_text: vanquished the enemies, Him who measured the earth—singing and praising these deeds, with tears flowing like the great river of abundant <s>Poṉṉi</s> (Kāvēri),

children.text: āṟu pōl varum kaṇṇa nīr koṇṭ’ araṅkaṉ kōyil tiru muṟṟam
children.translated_text: the devotees who make the sacred courtyard of <s>Araṅkaṉ</s>'s (Raṅganātha's) temple into mud—

children.text: cēṟu cey toṇṭar cē aṭi ceḻum cēṟ’ eṉ ceṉṉikk’ aṇivaṉē
children.translated_text: the beautiful, rich mud from their red feet I shall adorn upon my head.

children.text: ēṟ’ aṭarttatum
children.translated_text: "Him who subdued the bulls"—

children.text: nappiṉṉai pirāṭṭiyōṭṭai saṃśleṣattukku iṭaiccuvarāṉa ṛṣabhaṅkaḷ ēḻaiyum aṭarttatum
children.translated_text: He subdued the seven bulls that stood as a wall between Him and union with <s>Nappiṉṉai Pirāṭṭi</s> (Nīḷādevī).

children.text: ēṉam āy nilam kīṇṭatum
children.translated_text: "Him who as the Boar dug up the earth"—

children.text: śrībhūmi pirāṭṭiyōṭṭai saṃśleṣattukku virodhi āmpaṭi avaḷukku prakāramāṉa bhūmiyai praḷayam koḷḷa utaviṟṟ’ alaṉ eṉṉum avadyam vārātapaṭi mahāvarāhamāy aṇḍabhittiyilē pukku oṭṭiṉa bhūmiyai oṭṭu viṭuvittatum
children.translated_text: In order to remove the obstacle to union with <s>Śrī Bhūmi Pirāṭṭi</s> (the Earth Goddess), lest the fault of having allowed the earth—which is Her very form—to be swallowed by the deluge be attributed to Him, He became the great <s>Varāha</s> (Boar) and entered the shell of the cosmic egg and released the earth that was stuck there.

children.text: muṉ irāmaṉ āy māṟ’ aṭarttatum
children.translated_text: "Him who previously as <s>Rāma</s> vanquished the enemies"—

children.text: pirāṭṭiyai piritta payalai etiri ākki koṉṟatum
children.translated_text: He made the wretch who had separated Him from <s>Pirāṭṭi</s> (Sītā) into an adversary and slew him.

children.text: maṇ aḷantatum
children.translated_text: "Him who measured the earth"—

children.text: pirāṭṭimārōṭṭai saṃśleṣavirodhikaḷai pōkkiṉā pōlē indraṉōṭu virodhitta mahābali kaikkoṇṭa bhūmiyai mīṭṭu ellai naṭantu koṭuttatum
children.translated_text: Just as He removed the obstacles to union with the divine consorts, He recovered the earth that <s>Mahābali</s>, who opposed <s>Indra</s>, had seized, and walked its boundaries and gave it back.

children.text: colli pāṭi
children.translated_text: "singing and praising"—

children.text: i- apadānaṅkaḷai colli prītiprakarṣattālē pāṭi
children.translated_text: recounting these deeds and singing with the intensity of love,

children.text: vaṇ poṉṉi pēr āṟu pōl varum kaṇṇa nīr koṇṭu
children.translated_text: "with tears flowing like the great river of abundant <s>Poṉṉi</s> (Kāvēri)"—

children.text: kāveri peru veḷḷamāy malaippaṇṭam koṇṭu varumā pōlē amaikka nillātē veḷḷam iṭukiṟa kaṇṇīrai koṇṭu
children.translated_text: just as the <s>Kāvēri</s> comes in a great flood carrying mountain treasures, with tears that flow ceaselessly like a flood,

children.text: araṅkaṉ kōyil tiru muṟṟam cēṟu cey toṇṭar
children.translated_text: "the devotees who make the sacred courtyard of <s>Araṅkaṉ</s>'s temple into mud"—

children.text: aṅku pāṅkāka tiruvalaku tiruppaṇi ceytu vaittāl ivarkaḷ attai kaṇṇanīrālē cēṟ’ ākkuvarkaḷ-āyttu
children.translated_text: there, having lovingly performed the sacred service of sweeping and cleaning, these devotees would turn it into mud with their tears.

children.text: cē aṭi ceḻum cēṟ’ eṉ ceṉṉikk’ aṇivaṉē
children.translated_text: "the beautiful, rich mud from their red feet I shall adorn upon my head"—

children.text: amaṅgaḷamāṉa puḻuku neyyālē alaṅkaritt’ uḷḷa doṣaṃ tīra maṅgaḷārthamāṉa śrīvaiṣṇavarkaḷiṉ tiruvaṭikaḷil aḻakiya cēṟṟai aṇivaṉ.
children.translated_text: To remove the fault of having adorned oneself with inauspicious musk oil, I shall adorn the beautiful mud from the sacred feet of the <s>Śrīvaiṣṇava</s>-s, which is auspicious.

children.text: tōytta taṇ tayir veṇṇey pāl uṭaṉ uṇṭalum uṭaṉṟ’ āycci kaṇṭu
children.translated_text: Him who ate together the cool curd that was stirred, the butter, and the milk—when the cowherdess saw this and

children.text: ārtta tōḷ uṭai em pirāṉ eṉ araṅkaṉukk’ aṭiyārkaḷ āy
children.translated_text: our Lord with mighty arms who embraced—for those who have become devotees of my <s>Araṅkaṉ</s> (Raṅganātha),

children.text: nā taḻump’ eḻa nāraṇā eṉṟ’ aḻaittu mey taḻumpa toḻut’
children.translated_text: calling out '<s>Nārāṇā</s>!' until their tongues develop calluses, worshipping with their bodies trembling,

children.text: ētti iṉp’ uṟum toṇṭar cē aṭi ētti vāḻttum eṉ neñcamē
children.translated_text: praising—the red feet of those devotees who experience bliss, my heart praises and blesses them.

children.text: tōytta taṇ tayir veṇṇey pāl
children.translated_text: "the cool curd that was stirred, the butter, the milk"—

children.text: kaṭaintu piritta veṇṇey, atukku uṟuppāka tōytta tayir, atukk’ aṭiyāṉa pāl
children.translated_text: the butter that was churned and separated, the curd that was stirred as the basis for it, and the milk that was the source of that,

children.text: uṭaṉ uṇṭalum
children.translated_text: "ate together"—

children.text: ivai aṭaṅkalum niḥśeṣamāka orukālē amutu ceytavāṟē
children.translated_text: He consumed all of these completely at once.

children.text: uṭaṉṟu
children.translated_text: "was angered"—

children.text: aṭaiya kāṇā-viṭṭa āṟē kopittāḷ.
children.translated_text: The moment she found everything gone, she became angry.

children.text: tīrā vekuḷiyaḷ āy’ snehattukku avadhi uṇṭ
children.translated_text: "She became one of unceasing anger"—since love has a limit,

children.text: ākiliṟē kopattukku avadhi uṇṭāvatu.
children.translated_text: anger too must have a limit.

children.text: āycci kaṇṭu
children.translated_text: "the cowherdess saw"—

children.text: vāy atu kai atuvāka koṇṭiyōṭē kaṇṭu piṭittāḷ-āyttu.
children.translated_text: with His mouth and hands still showing the evidence, she saw and caught Him.

children.text: ārtta tōḷ uṭai em pirāṉ
children.translated_text: "our Lord with mighty arms who embraced"—

children.text: kaṇṭavāṟē kaiyai piṭittu kaṭṭiṉāḷ.
children.translated_text: the moment she saw Him, she seized His hand and bound it.

children.text: em pirāṉ
children.translated_text: "our Lord"—

children.text: āśritasparśam uḷḷa dravyattāl allatu cellāmaiyai kāṭṭi eṉṉai ananyārhaṉ ākkiṉavaṉ
children.translated_text: He who, by showing that He cannot bear anything except what has been touched by His devotees, has made me exclusively His own.

children.text: eṉ araṅkaṉukk’ aṭiyārkaḷ āy
children.translated_text: "for those who have become devotees of my <s>Araṅkaṉ</s>"—

children.text: avatārakālattil iḻantār iḻavu tīra vantu sulabharāṉa periyaperumāḷuṭaiya ceyalālē eḻuti koṭuttavarkaḷ-āyttu.
children.translated_text: those who have been claimed by the deeds of <s>Periya Perumāḷ</s>, who came and made Himself accessible so that the loss suffered by those who missed the incarnation period might be remedied.

children.text: nā taḻump’ eḻa
children.translated_text: "until their tongues develop calluses"—

children.text: nāvāṉatu taḻumpēṟumpaṭi
children.translated_text: to the point where the tongue develops calluses,

children.text: nāraṇā eṉṟ’ aḻaittu
children.translated_text: "calling out '<s>Nārāṇā</s>!'"—

children.text: ammē eṉpārai pōlē tirunāmattai aṭaivu keṭa colli
children.translated_text: calling out the divine name helplessly, like those who cry 'Mother!',

children.text: mey taḻumpa toḻut’
children.translated_text: "with their bodies trembling"—

children.text: praṇāmam paṇṇiṉapaṭi tōṉṟa uṭamp’ ellām taḻumpāka; ciṟiyāttāṉai pōlē.
children.translated_text: the entire body becoming covered in bumps from the act of prostration, becoming visible; like <s>Ciṟiyāttāṉ</s> (a devotee).

children.text: ētti
children.translated_text: "praising"—

children.text: ippaṭippaṭṭa ceyalkaḷai colli ētti
children.translated_text: recounting and praising such deeds,

children.text: iṉp’ uṟum toṇṭar cē aṭi
children.translated_text: "the red feet of those devotees who experience bliss"—

children.text: manassilē vaittu ēttukaiyālē, viṣayattai kiṭṭiṉāl piṟakkum niratiśayānandayuktarāy irukkum śrīvaiṣṇavarkaḷ śrīpādaṅkaḷai
children.translated_text: the sacred feet of those <s>Śrīvaiṣṇava</s>-s who, because they hold this in their hearts and praise it, are filled with unsurpassed bliss when they approach the object of their devotion,

children.text: toṇṭar cē aṭi ētti vāḻttum eṉ neñcamē
children.translated_text: "my heart praises and blesses the red feet of such devotees"—

children.text: avarkaḷ tāṅkaḷ akappaṭṭa navanītacauryattil pōkātu eṉ neñcu. atilē akappaṭṭavarkaḷ taṅkaḷai ētti vāḻttum ittaṉai.
children.translated_text: my heart does not go toward the butter-theft in which they are absorbed. It only praises and blesses those who are absorbed in it—that is all.

children.text: ētti vāḻttum
children.translated_text: "praises and blesses"—

children.text: i- ceyalukku ivarkaḷ nilavar āvatē eṉṟu stotrattai paṇṇi, itu nityam āka vēṇum eṉṟu maṅgaḷāśāsanam paṇṇā-niṟkum eṉ neñcu.
children.translated_text: performing a hymn saying that these devotees are the proper ground for this deed, and my heart stands performing <s>maṅgaḷāśāsana</s> (benediction), wishing that this may be eternal.

children.text: poy cilai kural ēṟṟ’ eruttam iṟuttu pōr arav’ īrtta kōṉ
children.translated_text: The king who subdued the bulls with false rage and fierce bellowing, and who tore apart the serpent in battle,

children.text: cey cilai cuṭar cūḻ oḷi tiṇṇa mā matiḷ teṉ araṅkaṉ ām
children.translated_text: He who is the Lord of beautiful <s>Araṅkam</s> with its brilliant, radiant, strong and mighty ramparts,

children.text: mey cilai karu mēkam oṉṟu tam neñcil niṉṟu tikaḻa pōy
children.translated_text: like a dark rain-cloud of true form shining in their hearts, those who go

children.text: meycilirppavar tammaiyē niṉaint’ eṉ maṉam meycilirkkumē
children.translated_text: experiencing true ecstatic trembling—thinking of them alone, my heart too trembles with ecstasy.

children.text: poy cilai kural ēṟṟ’ eruttam iṟuttu
children.translated_text: "the bulls with false rage, fierce bellowing, He subdued"—

children.text: poy = kṛtrimam. cilai = kopam. asurāveśattālē kṛtrimamāy, kopattaiyum uṭaittāy iruntuḷḷa ēṟum iṟāya porutu. nappiṉṉai pirāṭṭiyōṭṭai saṃśleṣattukku virodhi āṉavaiyumāy, porukiṟavaiyumāy cilai pōlē ghoramāṉa dhvaniyai uṭaittāy iruntuḷḷa ṛṣabhaṅkaḷiṉ kakuttai muṟittu
children.translated_text: "False" means artificial. "Rage" means anger. The bulls that were possessed by <s>asura</s>-s (demons) and thus had artificial, wrathful dispositions—He fought them to the death. The bulls that were obstacles to union with <s>Nappiṉṉai Pirāṭṭi</s> (Nīḷādevī), that were combative, that had a terrifying sound like a bow, whose necks He broke—those <s>ṛṣabha</s>-s (bulls),

children.text: pōr arav’ īrtta kōṉ
children.translated_text: "the king who tore apart the serpent in battle"—

children.text: tiruvāyppāṭiyil pacukkaḷum iṭaiyarum taṇṇīr kuṭikka oṇṇātapaṭi jalattai dūṣittu kiṭanta kāḷiyaṉ, yuddhonmukhaṉāy puṟappaṭumpaṭi kalakki poykaiyil niṉṟum pōkaviṭṭu, attālē tiruvāyppāṭiyil uḷḷārkku nāthaṉ-āṉavaṉai
children.translated_text: In <s>Tiruvāyppāṭi</s>, <s>Kāḷiyaṉ</s> who had polluted the water so that the cattle and cowherds could not drink, was provoked to come forth for battle and expelled from the pond, and thereby the one who became the protector of those in <s>Tiruvāyppāṭi</s>

children.text: cey cilai cuṭar cūḻ oḷi tiṇṇa mā matiḷ teṉ araṅkaṉ-ām
children.translated_text: is <s>Teṉ Araṅkaṉ</s> (the Lord of Southern <s>Raṅgam</s>) surrounded by the radiance of beautiful bows and bright, blazing light, and strong, great walls

children.text: kallālē ceyyappaṭṭu piṟarāl abhibhavikka oṇṇāta paṭiyāṉa matippai uṭaittāy tiṇmaiyaiyum ōkkattaiyum uṭaittāṉa tiru matiḷkaḷ palavum cūḻnt’ irukkiṟa kōyililē kaṇvaḷarnt’ aruḷukiṟa
children.translated_text: Made of stone, with walls so strong that they cannot be overcome by others, possessing firmness and greatness, surrounded by many such sacred walls, in that temple where He graciously reclines

children.text: mey cilai karu mēkam
children.translated_text: a true-bodied dark cloud

children.text: uṭampilē villaiyuṭaiya megham eṉṉutal. meyyē villōṭē kūṭiṉa megham tāṉ eṉṉutal.
children.translated_text: This means either 'one whose body bears a bow like a cloud,' or 'He is indeed a cloud united with a bow.'

children.text: oṉṟu tam neñcil niṉṟu tikaḻa
children.translated_text: one stands shining in their heart

children.text: śobhayat daṇḍakāraṇyam
children.translated_text: <s>śobhayat daṇḍakāraṇyam</s> (He who beautified the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest)

children.text: eṉṉumā pōlē māṇikkam kuppiyil uḷḷu niṉṟa nilai puṟampē teriyumā pōlē periyaperumāḷai taṅkaḷ neñcilē eḻuntaruḷuvittu vaikkaiyālē niḻaliṭā-niṟkumiṟē.
children.translated_text: Just as stated thus, just as a gem placed inside a flask reveals its brilliance externally, by having <s>Periya Perumāḷ</s> enshrined and seated in their hearts, His radiance shines forth like a shadow cast.

children.text: meycilirppavar
children.translated_text: those whose bodies tremble

children.text: uḷḷē eḻuntaruḷi irukkiṟa paṭiyai anusandhittu puḷakitagātrarāy irukkum śrīvaiṣṇavarkaḷ
children.translated_text: The <s>Śrīvaiṣṇavas</s> who contemplate His gracious presence within and become <s>pulakitagātra</s> (having bodies thrilling with horripilation)

children.text: tammaiyē niṉaint’ eṉ maṉam meycilirkkumē
children.translated_text: my heart truly trembles thinking of them

children.text: periyaperumāḷai anubhavittu avarkaḷ uṭampu paṭum pāṭṭai, avarkaḷai anubhavittu eṉ neñcu paṭāniṉṟatu. sparśadravyam paṭṭat’ ellām paṭā-niṉṟatu amūrtadravyam.
children.translated_text: The bodily states that they undergo while experiencing <s>Periya Perumāḷ</s> — my heart undergoes the same while experiencing them. What the <s>sparśadravya</s> (tangible substance) undergoes, the <s>amūrtadravya</s> (intangible substance) also undergoes.

children.text: āti antam aṉantam aṟputam āṉa vāṉavar tam pirāṉ
children.translated_text: The Lord of the celestials who is the beginning, the end, infinite, and wondrous

children.text: pāta mā malar cūṭum patti ilāta pāvikaḷ uynt’ iṭa
children.translated_text: so that the sinners who lack the devotion to wear the great flowers of His feet may be saved

children.text: tīt’ il nal neṟi kāṭṭi eṅkum tirint’ araṅkaṉ emmāṉukkē
children.translated_text: showing the faultless, good path, wandering everywhere, for our Lord <s>Araṅkaṉ</s> alone
