children.text: kātal cey toṇṭarkk’ e- piṟappilum kātal ceyyum eṉ neñcamē
children.translated_text: my heart loves in every birth those devotees who perform loving service

children.text: āti
children.translated_text: <s>āti</s> (beginning)

children.text: jagatkāraṇabhūtaṉ
children.translated_text: He who is the cause of the universe

children.text: antam
children.translated_text: <s>antam</s> (end)

children.text: praḷayakālattilum sadavasthaṉāy niṟkumavaṉ
children.translated_text: He who remains as the eternal reality even at the time of <s>pralaya</s> (cosmic dissolution)

children.text: aṉantam
children.translated_text: <s>aṉantam</s> (infinite)

children.text: kāraṇāvasthaiyilum kāryāvasthaiyilum okka vyāpittu niṟkumavaṉ
children.translated_text: He who pervades equally in both the causal state and the effected state

children.text: aṟputam
children.translated_text: <s>aṟputam</s> (wondrous)

children.text: kāryāvasthaiyōṭu sadavasthaṉāy niṟkumattōṭu vāciyaṟa niṟkum nilaikaḷ vēṟ’ ōr iṭattil kāṇa oṇṇāt’ eṉṉumpaṭi irukkum āścaryabhūtaṉ
children.translated_text: He who is a wonder, such that the states of remaining eternal alongside the effected state cannot be seen elsewhere in such indistinguishable manner

children.text: āṉa vāṉavar tam pirāṉ
children.translated_text: the Lord of the celestials who is such

children.text: āṉapōtum amiḻntapōtum eppōtum okka uḷarāy irukkum nityasūrikaḷukku nāthaṉ. ubhayavibhūtināthaṉ.
children.translated_text: The Lord of the <s>Nityasūris</s> (eternal beings) who remain ever-present whether He rises or descends. The Lord of both <s>vibhūtis</s> (realms).

children.text: pāta mā malar cūṭum patti ilāta
children.translated_text: who lack the devotion to wear the great flowers of His feet

children.text: avaṉ tiruvaṭikaḷ-ākiṟa cevvi tāmaraiyai cūṭum bhaktiyai uṭaiyarāy irukkaiāyttu kartavyam; at’ illāta
children.translated_text: The proper duty is to possess <s>bhakti</s> (devotion) to wear on one's head the beautiful lotus that is His sacred feet; those who lack that

children.text: pāvikaḷ uynt’ iṭa
children.translated_text: the sinners may be saved

children.text: bhakti illātapaṭi mahāpāpattai paṇṇi,
children.translated_text: Having committed great sin by being without <s>bhakti</s> (devotion),

children.text: asanneva
children.translated_text: <s>asanneva</s> (as if non-existent)

children.text: eṉṉumpaṭi irukkiṟa deśam eṅkum pukku sañcarittu avarkaḷai bhakti uṇṭākki ujjīvippikkaikkāka
children.translated_text: entering and wandering through every land where such people exist, in order to create <s>bhakti</s> in them and bring about their salvation

children.text: tīt’ il nal neṟi
children.translated_text: the faultless, good path

children.text: tīmaiyōṭē kūṭiṉa neṟi aṉṟikkē, cetanar nalvaḻi pōmpaṭi tāṅkaḷ ācarittu kāṭṭi
children.translated_text: Not a path mixed with evil, but one where they themselves practice and demonstrate so that sentient beings may walk the good path

children.text: eṅkum tirintu
children.translated_text: wandering everywhere

children.text: puka kaṭava deśam eṅkum pukku sañcarittu
children.translated_text: entering and wandering through every land that should be visited

children.text: araṅkaṉ emmāṉukkē kātal cey
children.translated_text: performing loving service to <s>Araṅkaṉ</s> our Lord

children.text: eṉṉai ananyārham ākkiṉa periyaperumāḷ tiruvaṭikaḷē bhakti uṇṭāy irukkum śrīvaiṣṇavarkaḷukku
children.translated_text: for the <s>Śrīvaiṣṇavas</s> who possess devotion solely to the sacred feet of <s>Periya Perumāḷ</s> who made me exclusively His own

children.text: e- piṟappilum kātal ceyyum eṉ neñcamē
children.translated_text: my heart loves them in every birth

children.text: anekajanmaṅkaḷ piṟantu avarkaḷukku aṭimai ceyya vēṇum eṉṟu ācaippaṭā-niṉṟatu eṉ neñcu.
children.translated_text: My heart desires to be born through many births and perform service to them.

children.text: kār iṉam purai mēṉi nal katir mutta
m
veḷ nakai ceyya vāy
children.translated_text: with white smile, with a beautiful mouth
The one with a form like a cluster of dark rain clouds, with good rays, with pearls

children.text: āra
m
mārvaṉ araṅkaṉ eṉṉum arum perum cuṭar oṉṟiṉai
children.translated_text: He who is called <s>Araṅkaṉ</s>, the one with a chest bearing a garland — that rare, great effulgence
with a garland

children.text: cērum neñciṉar āki cērntu kacint’ iḻinta kaṇṇīrkaḷāl
children.translated_text: those who become united in heart, and having approached, shed tears melting with emotion

children.text: vāra niṟpavar tāḷ iṇaikk’ oru vāram ākum eṉ neñcamē
children.translated_text: my heart becomes devoted to the pair of feet of those who stand streaming (with love)

children.text: kār iṉam purai mēṉi
children.translated_text: the one with a form like a cluster of dark rain clouds

children.text: tokka mēka pal kuḻāṅkaḷ kār tiraḷ aṉaiya mēṉi
children.translated_text: As it is said, 'a form like the gathering of many dark cloud masses'

children.text: eṉkiṟapaṭiyē aḻakiya tirumēṉiyaiyum uṭaiyarāy
children.translated_text: having such a beautiful sacred form, and also

children.text: nal katir mutta
m
veḷ nakai ceyya vāy
children.translated_text: white smile, beautiful mouth
good rays, pearls

children.text: kaṇṭārai pōkāmal tuvakka valla veṇmaiyaiyuṭaiya muttu nirai pōlē irukkum dantapaṅktiyaiyum, itukku parabhāgamāṉa tiru adharattil paḻuppaiyum uṭaiyavarāy
children.translated_text: rows of teeth like strands of pearls with a whiteness that captivates those who see them and does not let them go, and the redness of the sacred lower lip which surpasses even this

children.text: āra mārvaṉ
children.translated_text: the one with a garland on his chest

children.text: periya varai mārvil pēr āram pūṇṭu
children.translated_text: As it is said, 'wearing a great garland on his mountain-like chest'

children.text: eṉṟu aiśvaryaprakāśakamāmpaṭi iṭṭu pūṇa vēṇumpaṭi uḷḷa hārattaiyum tiru mārpilē uṭaiyarāy irukkiṟa
children.translated_text: having a <s>hāra</s> (necklace) that must be worn to manifest <s>aiśvarya</s> (sovereignty), on the sacred chest

children.text: araṅkaṉ eṉṉum arum perum cuṭar oṉṟiṉai
children.translated_text: <s>Araṅkaṉ</s>, that rare, great effulgence

children.text: periyaperumāḷ eṉṟu ubhayavibhūtiyilum prasiddharāy niravadhika-tejorūparāy advitīyarāṉavarai
children.translated_text: He who is known as <s>Periya Perumāḷ</s>, famous in both <s>vibhūtis</s> (realms), of unlimited radiant form, and without a second

children.text: cērum neñciṉar āki
children.translated_text: those who become united in heart

children.text: avar vantu kiṭṭumpōtu vilakkāmai aṭiyāka piṟanta bhaktiyai uṭaiyarāy
children.translated_text: possessing innate <s>bhakti</s> (devotion) that does not push away when He comes near

children.text: cērntu kacint’ iḻinta kaṇṇīrkaḷāl vāra niṟpavar tāḷ iṇaikku
children.translated_text: having approached, melting, shedding tears, standing streaming

children.text: avaṉai kiṭṭi niratiśayabhaktiyuktarāy kaṇṇum kaṇṇīrumāy niṟkumavar-kaḷukku, bhaktipāravaśyattālēyiṟē eṉṟu aṅkuttaikkum ivarkaḷukkumāy nillātē ivarkaḷuṭaiya tiruvaṭikaḷukku
children.translated_text: for those who, having approached Him, stand with unsurpassed devotion, with eyes and tears — through the overflow of devotion — not stopping there with Him but flowing to the sacred feet of these devotees

children.text: oru vāram ākum eṉ neñcamē
children.translated_text: my heart becomes devoted

children.text: ananyaprayojanamāy nillā-niṉṟatu eṉ neñcu.
children.translated_text: My heart stands ceaselessly with no other purpose.

children.text: mālai uṟṟa kaṭal kiṭantavaṉ vaṇṭu kiṇṭu naṟum tuḻāy
children.translated_text: He who reclines on the ocean garlanded with waves, bearing the fragrant <s>Tuḻāy</s> (holy basil) garland swarming with bees

children.text: mālai uṟṟa varai perum tiru mārvaṉai malar kaṇṇaṉai
children.translated_text: the one with a great sacred chest bearing a garland, on the mountain, the lotus-eyed one

children.text: mālai uṟṟ’ eḻunt’ āṭi pāṭi tirint’ araṅkaṉ emmāṉukkē
children.translated_text: rising with love, dancing, singing, wandering, for our Lord <s>Araṅkaṉ</s> alone

children.text: mālai uṟṟ’ iṭum toṇṭar vāḻvukku mālai uṟṟat’ eṉ neñcamē
children.translated_text: my heart has become love-mad toward the blessed life of those devotees who offer garlands of love

children.text: mālai uṟṟa kaṭal kiṭantavaṉ
children.translated_text: He who reclines on the ocean garlanded with waves

children.text: svasparśattālē alaiyeṟikiṟa tiruppāṟkaṭalilē kaṇvaḷarnt’ aruḷukiṟavaṉ
children.translated_text: He who graciously reclines in the Milk Ocean whose waves rise at His touch

children.text: vaṇṭu kiṇṭu naṟum tuḻāy mālai uṟṟa varai perum tiru mārvaṉai
children.translated_text: the one with a great sacred chest bearing a mountain-like form, wearing the fragrant sacred <s>Tuḻāy</s> garland thronged with bees

children.text: vaṇṭukaḷ neruṅki irukkiṟa cevvi tiruttuḻāy mālai cērntu, varaipōlē irukkiṟa perum tiru mārvai uṭaiyavarai;
children.translated_text: having bees crowding upon the beautiful sacred <s>Tuḻāy</s> garland, possessing the great sacred chest that is like a mountain;

children.text: mai pōl neṭu
m
varaivāy tāḻum aruvi pōl tār kiṭappa
children.translated_text: with garlands hanging like waterfalls cascading down the mountainside
dark, long, like collyrium

children.text: eṉṉa kaṭavatiṟē.
children.translated_text: as it should be said.

children.text: malar kaṇṇaṉai
children.translated_text: the lotus-eyed one

children.text: cevvi tāmarai pū pōlē malarnta tiru kaṇkaḷai uṭaiyavarai
children.translated_text: the one possessing sacred eyes blooming like beautiful lotus flowers

children.text: mālai uṟṟ’ eḻunt’ āṭi pāṭi tirint’
children.translated_text: rising with love, dancing, singing, wandering

children.text: bhaktiyai uṭaiyavarāy irunta iṭattil irukka oṭṭāmaiyālē eḻunt’ āṭuvatu pāṭuvatu, prīti prerikka irukka māṭṭātē sañcarittu
children.translated_text: being possessed of devotion and unable to remain still, rising and dancing and singing, and driven by love, unable to sit still, wandering about

children.text: araṅkaṉ emmāṉukkē mālai uṟṟiṭum toṇṭar vāḻvukku
children.translated_text: for our Lord <s>Araṅkaṉ</s> alone, the devotees who offer love

children.text: kōyililē sulabharāṉa paṭiyai kāṭṭi eṉṉai eḻutikkoṇṭa periyaperumāḷukkē bhaktikāryamāṉa pittēṟi tiriyum śrīvaiṣṇavarkaḷuṭaiya vaiṣṇavalakṣmikku
children.translated_text: for the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> splendor of the <s>Śrīvaiṣṇavas</s> who wander mad with devotion to <s>Periya Perumāḷ</s> who, having shown His accessibility in the temple, claimed me as His own

children.text: mālai uṟṟat’ eṉ neñcamē
children.translated_text: my heart has become love-mad

children.text: pittēṟā-niṉṟatu eṉ neñcu.
children.translated_text: My heart has gone mad with devotion.

children.text: moyttu kaṇ paṉi cōra meykaḷ cilirppa ēṅki iḷaittu niṉṟ’
children.translated_text: tears streaming from eyes, bodies trembling, sighing, growing faint, and standing thus

children.text: eyttu kumpiṭu naṭṭam iṭṭ’ eḻunt’ āṭi pāṭi iṟaiñci eṉ
children.translated_text: exhausted, prostrating, dancing wildly, rising, dancing, singing, and worshipping

children.text: attaṉ accaṉ araṅkaṉukk’ aṭiyārkaḷ āki avaṉukkē
children.translated_text: becoming servants of my father, my lord, <s>Araṅkaṉ</s>, and to Him alone

children.text: pittar ām avar pittar allarkaḷ maṟṟaiyār muṟṟum pittarē
children.translated_text: those who are mad for Him are not the mad ones; all others are truly mad

children.text: avatārikai - oṉpatām pāṭṭu. pittēṟi tirivārkkō nīr pittēṟuvatu? eṉṉa - prāptaviṣayattil pittēṟumavarkaḷ pittar aṉṟu eṉkiṟār.
moyttu kaṇ paṉi cōra
children.translated_text: tears streaming from eyes

children.text: iraṇṭu kaṇṇālē varṣadhārai pōlē coriya
children.translated_text: streaming like torrents of rain from both eyes

children.text: meykaḷ cilirppa
children.translated_text: bodies trembling

children.text: puḷakitagātrarāy
children.translated_text: being <s>pulakitagātra</s> (having bodies thrilling with horripilation)

children.text: ēṅki iḷaittu niṉṟ’ eyttu kumpiṭu naṭṭam iṭṭ’ eḻunt’ āṭi pāṭi iṟaiñci
children.translated_text: sighing, growing faint, standing exhausted, prostrating, dancing wildly, rising, dancing, singing, and worshipping

children.text: viṣayattai niṉaitt’ ēṅki iḷaittu śithilarāy, a- aḷav’ aṉṟiyilē stabdharāy niṉṟu, a- nilaiyum nillātē
children.translated_text: thinking of the object, sighing, growing faint, becoming weakened, and beyond that standing motionless, and not remaining even in that state

children.text: kumpiṭu naṭṭam iṭṭ’
children.translated_text: prostrating, dancing wildly

children.text: sasambhramanṛttam paṇṇi
children.translated_text: performing <s>sasambhrama-nṛtta</s> (ecstatic dance)

children.text: iṟaiñci
children.translated_text: worshipping

children.text: dīrghapraṇāmattai paṇṇi
children.translated_text: performing <s>dīrghapraṇāma</s> (long prostration)

children.text: eṉ attaṉ accaṉ
children.translated_text: my father, my lord

children.text: eṉakku janakaṉumāy svāmiyum āṉavaṉ
children.translated_text: He who is both my progenitor and my master

children.text: araṅkaṉukk’ aṭiyārkaḷ āki
children.translated_text: becoming servants of <s>Araṅkaṉ</s>

children.text: periyaperumāḷukku ananyaprayojanarāy irukkum śrīvaiṣṇavarkaḷukku aṭiyār āki
children.translated_text: becoming servants of the <s>Śrīvaiṣṇavas</s> who exist as <s>ananyaprayojana</s> (having no other purpose) for <s>Periya Perumāḷ</s>

children.text: avaṉukkē pittar ām avar pittar allarkaḷ
children.translated_text: those who are mad for Him are not the mad ones

children.text: avarkku bhaktimāṉkaḷāy bhaktikāryamāṉa pittēṟi tirikiṟavarkaḷ pittar allarkaḷ
children.translated_text: those who wander mad with devotion as an expression of <s>bhakti</s> toward them are not the mad ones

children.text: maṟṟaiyār muṟṟum pittarē
children.translated_text: all others are truly mad

children.text: inta bhaktikāryamāṉa pitt’ illātavarkaḷ aṭaiya pittarē. i- kalakkam ilātē teḷint’ irukkumavar sanakādikaḷēākilum avarkaḷ pittar.
children.translated_text: All those who lack this madness of devotion are indeed mad. Even if those who appear clear and composed are like <s>Sanaka</s> and the other sages, they are mad.
Introduction — Ninth verse. You are going mad for those who wander mad with devotion? To this, he says: those who are mad about the proper object are not mad.

children.text: alli mā malar maṅkai nātaṉ araṅkaṉ mey aṭiyārkaḷ tam
children.translated_text: <s>Maṅkai</s> (Lakṣmī), seated on the beautiful great lotus, Her Lord, <s>Araṅkaṉ</s>'s true servants'

children.text: ellai il aṭimai tiṟattiṉil eṉṟum mēvu maṉattaṉ ām
children.translated_text: one whose heart always dwells in the limitless modes of service

children.text: kolli kāvalaṉ kūṭal nāyakaṉ kōḻi kōṉ kulacēkaraṉ
children.translated_text: <s>Kulacēkaraṉ</s>, the guardian of <s>Kolli</s>, the lord of <s>Kūṭal</s>, the king of <s>Kōḻi</s>

children.text: collil iṉ tamiḻ mālai vallavar toṇṭar toṇṭarkaḷ āvarē
children.translated_text: those who master this sweet Tamil garland of words will become servants of servants

children.text: alli mā malar maṅkai nātaṉ araṅkaṉ
children.translated_text: the Lord of <s>Maṅkai</s> (Lakṣmī) seated on the beautiful great lotus, <s>Araṅkaṉ</s>

children.text: śriyaḥpatiyāṉa periyaperumāḷuṭaiya
children.translated_text: of <s>Periya Perumāḷ</s> who is the consort of <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī)

children.text: mey aṭiyārkaḷ tam
children.translated_text: the true servants

children.text: ananyaprayojanarāy irukkum śrīvaiṣṇavarkaḷuṭaiya
children.translated_text: of the <s>Śrīvaiṣṇavas</s> who exist as <s>ananyaprayojana</s> (having no other purpose)

children.text: ellai il aṭimai tiṟattiṉil eṉṟum mēvu maṉattaṉ ām
children.translated_text: one whose heart always dwells in the limitless modes of service

children.text: ātmadāsya
children.translated_text: <s>ātmadāsya</s> (servitude of the self)

children.text: ttilē eṉṟum okka poruntiṉa tiruvuḷḷattai uṭaiyarām
children.translated_text: one who has a sacred will that is always equally engaged in that

children.text: kolli kāvalaṉ kūṭal nāyakaṉ kōḻi kōṉ
children.translated_text: the guardian of <s>Kolli</s>, the lord of <s>Kūṭal</s>, the king of <s>Kōḻi</s>

children.text: kollikkum maturaikkum uṟaiyūrkkum nāyakarāṉa perumāḷ; periyavuṭaiyāruṭaiya iḻavāl vanta veṟuppālē,
children.translated_text: <s>Perumāḷ</s> who was lord of <s>Kolli</s>, <s>Maturai</s>, and <s>Uṟaiyūr</s>; due to the renunciation born from the loss of <s>Periya Uṭaiyār</s>,

children.text: vanavāso mahodayaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>vanavāso mahodayaḥ</s> (the great fortune of dwelling in the forest)

children.text: eṉṟu vanattukku pōntatu priyamāy iruntavarkku
children.translated_text: for him who found delight in going to the forest as stated thus,

children.text: rājyād bhraṃśo vane vāsaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>rājyād bhraṃśo vane vāsaḥ</s> (loss of kingdom, dwelling in the forest)

children.text: eṉṟu i- iḻavālē aṭiyil pōntavaiyum ellām tamakku veṟuppukk’ uṭal āṉāpōlē;
children.translated_text: just as all the losses that originally came through this deprivation became causes for his renunciation;

children.text: ūṉ ēṟu celvatt’ uṭal piṟavi yāṉ vēṇṭēṉ
children.translated_text: 'I do not desire bodily birth amid the wealth of growing flesh'

children.text: eṉṟum,
children.translated_text: thus, and

children.text: i- aracum yāṉ vēṇṭēṉ
children.translated_text: 'I do not desire this kingdom either'

children.text: eṉṟum collukiṟa ivarkku tadīyaśeṣatvattai tanta janmam eṉṟu rājajanmam taṉṉaiyum koṇṭāṭukiṟāriṟē.
children.translated_text: thus says he, yet he celebrates even the royal birth as the one that granted him servitude to the Lord's devotees.

children.text: collil iṉ tamiḻ mālai vallavar
children.translated_text: those who master this sweet Tamil garland of words

children.text: iṉitāṉa śabdaṅkaḷai uṭaiya tamiḻ toṭai vallavarkaḷ
children.translated_text: those who master this Tamil composition of sweet words

children.text: toṇṭar toṇṭarkaḷ āvarē
children.translated_text: they will become servants of servants

children.text: ivar ācaippaṭṭu pōnta bhāgavataśeṣatvaparyantam-ākiṟa puruṣārthattai labhipparkaḷ.
children.translated_text: they will attain the <s>puruṣārtha</s> (supreme goal) that extends to <s>bhāgavataśeṣatva</s> (servitude to the devotees of the Lord) which he desired.

children.text: avatārikai -
pērāḷaṉ pēr ōtum periyōrai orukālum pirikilēṉ
children.translated_text: 'I will never be separated from the great ones who chant the names of the Supreme Lord'

children.text: eṉṟu, bhagavadprāvaṇyam tadīyaśeṣatvaparyantamāy, avarkaḷ allatu cellāmai piṟakkum-aḷavum uṇṭāṉatu colliṟṟu, kīḻil tirumoḻiyil.
children.translated_text: Thus, in the previous <s>Tirumoḻi</s>, it was stated that devotion to the Lord culminated in servitude to His devotees, and that inseparability from them arose to the point of rebirth.

children.text: eṇṇāta māṉiṭattai eṇṇāta pōt’ ellām iṉiya āṟē
children.translated_text: 'whenever I do not think of those unworthy humans, it is sweet indeed'

children.text: eṉṟum,
children.translated_text: thus, and

children.text: māṉiṭavar allar eṉṟ
children.translated_text: 'they are not mere humans'

children.text: eṉ maṉattē vaittēṉē’ eṉṟum,
children.translated_text: thus 'I have placed them in my heart,' and

children.text: pittaṉ eṉṟē piṟar kūṟa
children.translated_text: 'let others call me mad'

children.text: eṉṟum piṟakkum avasthai uṇṭu bhagavadprāvaṇyattālē; muṉpil-atukku saṅkalpamātramēāyttu vēṇṭuvatu; aṭimai avarkaḷ koḷḷa koḷḷaviṟē ceyvatu. prātikūlyattil varjittē niṟka vēṇum. bhagavadguṇaṅkaḷ ōpāti vibhūtiyum tadīyatvākārattālē anubhāvyam eṉṟu coṉṉa śāstram tāṉēyiṟē ittai tyājyam eṉṟatum. jñānakāryamāyiṟē tadīyar uddeśyam ākiṟatum; tamoguṇapracurarōṭu sahavāsam poruntiṟṟ’ākil ajñānakāryamāyiṟē.
children.translated_text: such states arise through devotion to the Lord; previously, what was needed was merely the resolve for it; service is to be done as the devotees accept it. One must simply refrain from antagonism. The same <s>śāstra</s> that declared the Lord's <s>vibhūti</s> (glory) along with His qualities to be enjoyable in the mode of belonging to His devotees, also declared this to be renounced. Servitude to His devotees arises as a product of <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge); association with those dominated by <s>tamoguṇa</s> (quality of darkness) is a product of <s>ajñāna</s> (ignorance).

children.text: mattas sarvam aham
children.translated_text: <s>mattas sarvam aham</s> (from me is everything, I)

children.text: eṉṟu sāmānyabuddhi paṇṇiṉa śrī prahlādāḻvāṉ pūrvāvasthaiyil,
children.translated_text: When <s>Śrī Prahlāda Āḻvāṉ</s> in his earlier state regarded all with equal vision,

children.text: matpituḥ
children.translated_text: <s>matpituḥ</s> (of my father)

children.text: eṉṟu avaṉai rakṣikka pārttavaṉ prātikūlyattilē viñciṉavāṟē avaṉai viṭṭu kāṭṭi koṭuttāṉiṟē. śrīvibhīṣaṇāḻvāṉ āntaṉaiyum hitam colli pārttu taṉ hitattukku mīḷāta avasthai āṉavāṟē neruppu paṭṭa iṭattil vilakka oṇṇātapōtu taṉṉai koṇṭu tāṉ tappuvārai pōlē, prātikūlyam acaliṭṭu taṉaḷavum varum eṉṟu taṉṉai koṇṭu tāṉ tappiṉāṉiṟē. prātikūlyam ākiṟatu - dehātmābhimānikaḷ ākaiyum, viṣayapravaṇarāy irukkaiyum, dehātvyatiriktam veṟ’ oru vastu uṇṭ’ eṉṟ’ aṟiyāt’ irukkaiyumiṟē. ippaṭi iruppārōṭu eṉakku poruntāt’ eṉkiṟār i- tirumoḻiyil.
children.translated_text: he who had tried to protect him — when the antagonism intensified, he pointed him out and handed him over. <s>Śrī Vibhīṣaṇa Āḻvāṉ</s>, having tried to advise well up to the limit, when the state became irredeemable — like one who saves himself when the fire reaches a point where it cannot be extinguished — knowing that the antagonism would reach him too, he saved himself. Antagonism consists of: identifying the self with the body, being attached to sense objects, and not knowing that there is a reality beyond the body. 'I cannot associate with those who are like this,' says the author in this <s>Tirumoḻi</s>.
Introduction —

children.text: mey il vāḻkkaiyai mey eṉa koḷḷum i-
children.translated_text: 'this world which takes the false life as true'

children.text: vaiyam taṉṉoṭum kūṭuvat’ illai yāṉ
children.translated_text: 'I shall not associate with this world'

children.text: aiyaṉē araṅkā eṉṟ’ aḻaikkiṉṟēṉ
children.translated_text: O Lord! I call out 'O <s>Araṅkā</s> (Lord of Śrīraṅgam)!'

children.text: maiyal koṇṭ’ oḻintēṉ eṉ taṉ mālukkē
children.translated_text: I have become infatuated with my <s>Māl</s> (the Lord who is bewilderingly great)

children.text: mey il vāḻkkaiyai mey eṉa koḷḷum
children.translated_text: Taking the unreal life as real

children.text: mey eṉṟum poy eṉṟum nilai illāmaiyaiyum, nilainiṟkumattaiyum collukiṟatu. nilainillātatilē, nityamāṉa ātmavastuvil paṇṇum pratipattiyai paṇṇum eṉṉutal, meyyilē uṇṭāṉa vāḻkkai eṉṉutal; atākiṟatu – prakṛtiyai paṟṟivarum prākṛtabhogaṅkaḷiṟē.
children.translated_text: It speaks of the instability of what is called 'real' and 'false,' and of what is permanent. That is, making toward the impermanent the same commitment one should make toward the eternal <s>ātman</s> (self) — calling it 'life that exists in reality'; that amounts to the material pleasures (<s>prākṛtabhogaṅkaḷ</s>) that arise from attachment to <s>Prakṛti</s> (material nature).

children.text: i- vaiyam taṉṉoṭum kūṭuvat’ illai yāṉ
children.translated_text: I have no association with this world

children.text: dehātmābhimānikaḷāy iruppārōṭu eṉakk’ oru cērtti illai.
children.translated_text: I have no connection with those who identify themselves with the body (<s>dehātmābhimānikaḷ</s>).

children.text: aiyaṉ ityādi
children.translated_text: '<s>aiyaṉ</s>' etc. —

children.text: dehātvyatiriktam vēṟ’ oruvar uṇṭ’ eṉṟu aṟintavaṉ eṉkiṟār.
children.translated_text: He says: 'One who has realized that there exists someone other than the body.'

children.text: aiyaṉē
children.translated_text: O Lord! (<s>aiyaṉē</s>)

children.text: nirupādhikabandhuvē
children.translated_text: The unconditional kinsman (<s>nirupādhikabandhuvē</s>)

children.text: araṅkā
children.translated_text: O <s>Araṅkā</s>!

children.text: anuṣṭhānaparyantam ākkiṉa mūtalittā pōlē kōyililē vantu sulabhaṉ-āṉavaṉē
children.translated_text: Like the capital that has been brought to the point of practice (<s>anuṣṭhānaparyantam</s>), He who has become easily accessible (<s>sulabhaṉ</s>) by coming to the temple

children.text: eṉṟ’ aḻaikkiṉṟēṉ
children.translated_text: 'Calling out' (<s>eṉṟ' aḻaikkiṉṟēṉ</s>)

children.text: kāriyappāṭ’ aṟa kūppiṭā-niṉṟēṉ.
children.translated_text: I stood crying out without any ulterior motive.

children.text: maiyal koṇṭ’ oḻintēṉ eṉ taṉ mālukkē
children.translated_text: I have become infatuated with my <s>Māl</s>

children.text: avaṉ eṉakku pittēṟiṉa paṭiyai kaṇṭu nāṉum avaṉukku pittaṉ āṉēṉ.
children.translated_text: Seeing how He became mad about me, I too became mad about Him.

children.text: nūliṉ nēr iṭaiyār tiṟattē niṟkum
children.translated_text: In the manner of those women with waists as slender as a thread

children.text: ñālam taṉṉoṭum kūṭuvat’ illai yāṉ
children.translated_text: I have no association with this world

children.text: āliyā aḻaiyā araṅkā eṉṟu
children.translated_text: Crying out ceaselessly 'O <s>Araṅkā</s>!'

children.text: māl eḻunt’ oḻintēṉ eṉ taṉ mālukkē
children.translated_text: I have become overwhelmed with passion for my <s>Māl</s>

children.text: nūliṉ nēr iṭaiyār tiṟattē
children.translated_text: 'In the manner of those with waists as slender as a thread' —

children.text: nūl pōlē nuṇṇiya iṭaiyai uṭaiyarāy irukkum strīkaḷ tiṟattilē niṟkum. oru avayavattai anubhavikka pukkāl maṟṟaiya avayavattil pōka māṭṭātē niṟkum.
children.translated_text: Standing in the way of women who have waists as slender as a thread. When one begins to experience one limb, one cannot move on to another limb — one stands fixed.

children.text: ñālam taṉṉoṭum kūṭuvat’ illai yāṉ
children.translated_text: I have no association with this world

children.text: prāptaviṣayattil irukka kaṭava iruppai aprāptaviṣayattē irukkumavar-kaḷōṭu eṉakku oru sambandham illai.
children.translated_text: I have no connection with those who remain in what is not the proper object, when one should remain in the proper object (<s>prāptaviṣaya</s>).

children.text: āliyā ityādi
children.translated_text: '<s>āliyā</s>' etc. —

children.text: ivarkaḷ aprāptaviṣayattilē paṭum pāṭ’ ellām prāptaviṣayattē paṭumavaṉ nāṉ eṉkiṟār.
children.translated_text: He says: 'I am the one who undergoes in the proper object all the suffering that they undergo in the improper object.'

children.text: āliyā aḻaiyā araṅkā eṉṟu
children.translated_text: Crying out ceaselessly 'O <s>Araṅkā</s>!'

children.text: prītiprakarṣattālē irukka māṭṭātē āliyā, periyaperumāḷ tirunāmattai colli, aṭaivu keṭa kūppiṭṭu
children.translated_text: Unable to remain still due to the intensity of love (<s>prītiprakarṣa</s>), crying out ceaselessly, calling out the divine name of <s>Periyaperumāḷ</s>, shouting without restraint

children.text: māl eḻunt’ oḻintēṉ eṉ taṉ mālukkē
children.translated_text: I have become overwhelmed with passion for my <s>Māl</s>

children.text: tena te tam anuvratāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>tena te tam anuvratāḥ</s> (Therefore they follow Him devotedly)

children.text: eṉṉumā pōlē avaṉ eṉ pakkal vyāmugdhaṉ āṉapaṭi kaṇṭu nāṉum pittēṟiṉēṉ.
children.translated_text: Just as it is said, seeing how He became enchanted (<s>vyāmugdhaṉ</s>) with me, I too became mad.

children.text: māraṉār vari vem cilaikk’ āṭceyyum
children.translated_text: Under the command of <s>Māraṉ</s> (Kāma, the god of love) and his mighty, striped bow

children.text: pāriṉāroṭum kūṭuvat’ illai yāṉ
children.translated_text: I have no association with anyone on this earth

children.text: āra
m
children.translated_text: m

children.text: mārvaṉ araṅkaṉ aṉantaṉ nal
children.translated_text: <s>Mārvaṉ</s> (the broad-chested one), <s>Araṅkaṉ</s> (Lord of Śrīraṅgam), <s>Anantaṉ</s> (the infinite one), the good
Āra-

children.text: nāraṇaṉ narakāntakaṉ pittaṉē
children.translated_text: <s>Nāraṇaṉ</s> (Nārāyaṇa), <s>Narakāntakaṉ</s> (the destroyer of Naraka) — His madman am I!

children.text: māraṉār vari vem cilaikk’ āṭceyyum
children.translated_text: Under the command of <s>Māraṉ</s> and his mighty, striped bow

children.text: kāmaṉuṭaiya darśanīyamāy tappa oṇṇātapaṭi koṭitāy irukkiṟa villukku kuṭimakaṉāy tiriyum pāriṉāroṭum kūṭuvat’ illai yāṉ eṉṉutal; pāril āroṭum kūṭuvatillai yāṉ eṉṉutal;
children.translated_text: Either: I have no association with those on this earth who serve as subjects to the bow of <s>Kāma</s> (the god of love) — which is beautiful to behold and impossible to evade and cruel; or: I have no association with anyone on earth.

children.text: cārṅkam eṉṉum villāṇṭāṉ
children.translated_text: He who wielded the bow called <s>Cārṅkam</s> (Śārṅga)

children.text: taṉakku āṭceyyumavaṉ nāṉ.
children.translated_text: I am the one who serves Him.

children.text: āra
m
children.translated_text: m

children.text: mārvaṉ araṅkaṉ
children.translated_text: <s>Mārvaṉ</s>, <s>Araṅkaṉ</s> —
Āra-

children.text: ākarṣakamāṉa oppaṉaiyai uṭaiya periyaperumāḷ
children.translated_text: <s>Periyaperumāḷ</s> (the great Lord) who possesses an attractive ornament

children.text: aṉantaṉ
children.translated_text: <s>Anantaṉ</s> (the infinite one) —

children.text: manuṣyatve paratvam pōlē iṅkē vantu sulabharāy kiṭakka ceytē, paricchedikka oṇṇātapaṭi irukkiṟavar.
children.translated_text: Just as His supremacy (<s>paratva</s>) is manifest in His human incarnation (<s>manuṣyatva</s>), here too He has come and become easily accessible (<s>sulabha</s>), reclining in such a way that He cannot be fully comprehended.

children.text: nal nāraṇaṉ
children.translated_text: 'The good <s>Nāraṇaṉ</s>' —

children.text: taṉ uṭaimaiyai viṭa māṭṭāmaiyālē aḻukkai virumpumavaṉ.
children.translated_text: One who loves intimacy because He will not let go of His property.

children.text: narakāntakaṉ pittaṉē
children.translated_text: '<s>Narakāntakaṉ</s> — His madman!' —

children.text: avaṉ taṉ vātsalyattālē mēl viḻā-niṟka naṭuvē virodhiyum pōykkoṭu niṟkumiṟē. ippaṭi irukkiṟavaṉukku pittaṉē.
children.translated_text: While He falls upon one due to His <s>vātsalya</s> (parental affection), the obstacle also departs of its own accord in between. For such a one, I am a madman!

children.text: uṇṭiyē uṭaiyē ukant’ ōṭum i-
children.translated_text: Those who run eagerly after food and clothing —

children.text: maṇṭalattoṭum kūṭuvat’ illai yāṉ
children.translated_text: I have no association with this world

children.text: aṇṭa
m
children.translated_text: m

children.text: vāṇaṉ araṅkaṉ val pēy mulai
children.translated_text: <s>Vāṇaṉ</s> (the Lord of all), <s>Araṅkaṉ</s>, He who drank the breast of the fierce demoness (<s>pēy</s>) —
Aṇṭa-

children.text: uṇṭa vāyaṉ taṉ uṉmattaṉ kāṇmiṉē
children.translated_text: He with the mouth that drank the breast of the mighty demoness — I am His madman, behold!

children.text: uṇṭiyē uṭaiyē ukant’ ōṭum
children.translated_text: 'Those who run eagerly after food and clothing' —

children.text: upāsanattukku śarīram vēṇṭukaiyālē atu dharikka vēṇṭum-aḷav’ aṉṟiyilē ellāvaṟṟaiyum aḻiyamāṟi uṇṭiyum uṭaiyum ākkum.
children.translated_text: Since the body is needed for <s>upāsana</s> (worship), one must sustain it to that extent only; beyond that, they convert everything into just food and clothing, destroying all else.

children.text: i- maṇṭalattoṭum kūṭuvat’ illai yāṉ
children.translated_text: I have no association with this world

children.text: uṇṇum cōṟu paruku nīr tiṉṉum veṟṟilaiyum ellām kaṇṇaṉ
children.translated_text: 'The rice one eats, the water one drinks, the betel one chews — all are <s>Kaṇṇaṉ</s> (Kṛṣṇa)' —

children.text: eṉṟirukka oru vibhūti uṇṭāṉā pōlē prākṛtabhogaṅkaḷai virumpukaikk’ oru vibhūtiyiṟē ituvum.
children.translated_text: While it should be thus, just as there exists a realm for material pleasures (<s>prākṛtabhogaṅkaḷ</s>), this too is such a realm for desiring them.

children.text: aṇṭa
m
children.translated_text: m

children.text: vāṇaṉ
children.translated_text: <s>Vāṇaṉ</s> —
Aṇṭa-

children.text: aṇḍāntarvartikaḷukku nirvāhakaṉ.
children.translated_text: The ruler (<s>nirvāhaka</s>) of those within the cosmic egg (<s>aṇḍa</s>).

children.text: araṅkaṉ
children.translated_text: <s>Araṅkaṉ</s> —

children.text: itukku nirvāhakaṉāy irukkum irupp’ oḻiya itiṉ-uḷḷē pukuntu sulabhaṉāy kōyililē sannihitaṉ āṉavaṉ.
children.translated_text: Rather than merely being the ruler of this, He entered within it and became easily accessible (<s>sulabha</s>), being present in the temple.

children.text: val pēy mulai uṇṭa vāyaṉ taṉ uṉmattaṉ kāṇmiṉē
children.translated_text: 'He with the mouth that drank the breast of the mighty demoness — His madman, behold!' —

children.text: iṅkē vantu avatarittu pratibandhaṅkaḷai tāṉē pōkkumavaṉukku pittaṉ nāṉ.
children.translated_text: I am a madman for the one who incarnated here and Himself removed all obstacles (<s>pratibandhaṅkaḷ</s>).

children.text: taṉ uṉmattaṉ kāṇmiṉē
children.translated_text: 'His own madman, behold!' —

children.text: auṣadhasevai paṇṇiṉārai mīṭka oṇṇātā pōlē avaṉuṭaiya guṇaceṣṭi-taṅkaḷilē akappaṭṭu pittaṉ āṉa eṉṉai kevalaśarīrapararōṭē cēra viṭa oṇṇumō?
children.translated_text: Just as one who has taken medicine cannot be retrieved, can I — who have become mad being caught in His qualities and deeds (<s>guṇaceṣṭitaṅkaḷ</s>) — be made to associate with those who are merely concerned with the body?

children.text: tīt’ il nal neṟi niṟka allātu cey
children.translated_text: Standing in the faultless, good path, rather than with those who follow

children.text: nītiyāroṭum kūṭuvat’ illai yāṉ
children.translated_text: wrong ways — I have no association with them

children.text: āti āyaṉ araṅkaṉ am tāmarai
children.translated_text: <s>Āti</s> (the primordial one), <s>Āyaṉ</s> (the cowherd), <s>Araṅkaṉ</s>, the beautiful lotus —

children.text: pētai mā maṇavāḷaṉ taṉ pittaṉē
children.translated_text: The great bridegroom of the innocent <s>Lakṣmī</s> — His madman am I!

children.text: tītu il nal neṟi niṟka
children.translated_text: 'Standing in the faultless, good path' —

children.text: tīmaiyōṭu viravāta nalvaḻi niṟka; ivaṉai oḻinta phalaṅkaḷukku sādhanānuṣṭhānam paṇṇi peṟum pēṟṟil iḻavē naṉṟ’ eṉṉumpaṭiyiṟē iruppatu.
children.translated_text: Standing in the good path that is unmixed with evil; performing means (<s>sādhanānuṣṭhāna</s>) for fruits other than Him — the loss in such attainment is itself better, such is its nature.

children.text: allātu cey nītiyāroṭum kūṭuvat’ illai yāṉ
children.translated_text: 'Rather than with those who follow wrong ways — I have no association' —

children.text: itarapuruṣārthaṅkaḷai ācaippaṭukaiyē yātraiyāy iruppārōṭu kūṭuvat’ illai yāṉ.
children.translated_text: I have no association with those whose entire journey consists of desiring other goals (<s>itarapuruṣārthaṅkaḷ</s>).

children.text: āti
pramāṇaṅkaḷāl upāsyavastu eṉṟu collappaṭukiṟavaṉ
children.translated_text: The one who is declared by the <s>pramāṇas</s> (authoritative scriptures) as the object of worship (<s>upāsyavastu</s>)

children.text: āyaṉ
children.translated_text: '<s>Āyaṉ</s>' —

children.text: upāsyavastu tāṉ arit’ eṉṉa oṇṇātapaṭi avatarittu sulabhaṉ-āṉavaṉ
children.translated_text: The object of worship itself incarnated and became easily accessible so that one cannot say 'it is difficult to attain'

children.text: araṅkaṉ
children.translated_text: '<s>Araṅkaṉ</s>' —

children.text: avatāram pōlē tīrtham prasādittu piṟpāṭar iḻavāmē kōyililē vantu sannihitar āṉavar.
children.translated_text: Unlike the incarnations that end, He came to the temple so that later generations would not suffer loss, and became present (<s>sannihita</s>) there.

children.text: am tāmarai pētai mā maṇavāḷaṉ taṉ pittaṉē
children.translated_text: 'The great bridegroom of the beautiful lotus maiden — His madman!' —

children.text: aḻakiya tāmarai pūvai taṉakk’ iruppiṭamāka uṭaiya periya-pirāṭṭiyārukku vallabhar āṉavarkku pittaṉāṉēṉ nāṉ. ōr aṭi ivaṉ pukura niṉṟāl attai kuvāl ākki, avaṉ neñcilē puṇpaṭumpaṭi ivaṉ paṇṇiṉa aparādhattai avaṉ kāṇātapaṭi irukkiṟa puruṣakārabhūtai.
children.translated_text: I became a madman for the consort of <s>Periya Pirāṭṭiyār</s> (Śrī Mahālakṣmī) who has the beautiful lotus as her abode. When a devotee stands ready to enter, she makes it into an embrace; she is the mediatrix (<s>puruṣakārabhūtai</s>) who ensures that He does not see the offense the devotee committed that would wound His heart.

children.text: mā maṇavāḷaṉ
children.translated_text: 'The great bridegroom' —

children.text: aprameyaṃ hi tattejaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>aprameyaṃ hi tat tejaḥ</s> (For that splendor is immeasurable)

children.text: ivaḷukku vallabhaṉ-ākaiyālē vanta perumaiyai uṭaiyavaṉ viṣayattil pittaṉ nāṉ.
children.translated_text: I am a madman for the one whose greatness comes from being the beloved of Her — His consort.

children.text: em parattar allāroṭum kūṭalaṉ
children.translated_text: I do not associate with anyone other than my Supreme Lord

children.text: umpar vāḻvai oṉṟ’ āka karutilaṉ
children.translated_text: I do not consider the life of the celestials (<s>umpar</s>) as anything of value

children.text: tampirāṉ amararkk’ araṅka
m
children.translated_text: m

children.text: nakar
children.translated_text: <s>nakar</s> (the city of Śrīraṅgam)
<s>Tampirāṉ</s> (the Supreme Lord) of the immortals, at <s>Araṅka-</s>

children.text: em pirāṉukk’ eḻumaiyum pittaṉē
children.translated_text: For my Lord, I am forever a madman!

children.text: em parattar allāroṭum kūṭalaṉ
children.translated_text: 'I do not associate with anyone other than my Supreme Lord' —

children.text: eṉ yātraiyē yātraiyāy irātārai nākkuvaḷaittiruppaṉ.
children.translated_text: I turn my tongue away from those who do not make my way their own way.

children.text: i niṉṟa nīrmai iṉi yām uṟāmai
children.translated_text: 'This state of standing in water we shall no longer endure' —

children.text: eṉṟum,
children.translated_text: thus,

children.text: vaḻuv’ ilā aṭimai ceyya vēṇṭum nām
children.translated_text: 'We must perform faultless service' —

children.text: eṉṟum irātāroṭu sambandham illai.
children.translated_text: thus — I have no connection with those who do not hold these.

children.text: umpar vāḻvai oṉṟ’ āka karutilaṉ
children.translated_text: 'I do not consider the life of the celestials as anything' —

children.text: saṃsārattil aruciyum kaiṅkaryattil ruciyum illaiākil, brahmādikaḷ sampattē ākilum tṛṇavatkarippaṉ.
children.translated_text: If there is no distaste for <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) and no relish for service (<s>kaiṅkarya</s>), I would regard even the wealth of <s>Brahmā</s> and others as a blade of grass.

children.text: tampirāṉ amararkku
children.translated_text: '<s>Tampirāṉ</s> of the immortals' —

children.text: ayarv’ aṟum amararkaḷ atipati
children.translated_text: The chief of the ever-wakeful immortals (<s>ayarv' aṟum amararkaḷ atipati</s>)

children.text: araṅka
m
children.translated_text: m

children.text: nakar em pirāṉukku
children.translated_text: '<s>nakar</s>, for my Lord' —
<s>Araṅka-</s>

children.text: nityasūrikaḷ ellām anubhavikkumā pōlē saṃsārikaḷ ellām iḻavātapaṭi kōyililē vantu sulabhar-āṉavar
children.translated_text: So that all those in <s>saṃsāra</s> may not suffer loss — just as the eternal attendants (<s>nityasūrikaḷ</s>) enjoy Him — He became easily accessible by coming to the temple.

children.text: eḻumaiyum pittaṉē
children.translated_text: 'Forever a madman!' —

children.text: i- ceyalukk’ eṉṟum pittaṉāy tiriyumavaṉ.
children.translated_text: One who wanders always as a madman for this purpose.

children.text: e- tiṟattilum yāroṭum kūṭum a-
children.translated_text: In every way, with anyone who would join, that

children.text: cittam taṉṉai tavirttaṉaṉ cem kaṇ māl
children.translated_text: mind He has removed — the red-eyed <s>Māl</s> (the great Lord)

children.text: attaṉē araṅkā eṉṟ’ aḻaikkiṉṟēṉ
children.translated_text: O Lord! O <s>Araṅkā</s>! — thus I call out

children.text: pittaṉ āy oḻintēṉ em pirāṉukkē
children.translated_text: I have become a madman for my Lord!

children.text: avatārikai - ēḻām pāṭṭu. itararōṭu kūṭāta naṉmai umakku vanta paṭiyeṉ? eṉṉa - nāṉ aṭiyāka vantat’ alla, sarveśvaraṉ aṭiyāka vantatu eṉkiṟār.
e- tiṟattilum
children.translated_text: 'In every way' —

children.text: abhāgavataṉōṭu sambhāṣikka abhimatapuruṣārthaṅkaḷai ellām labhikkalām eṉṉilum attaiyum nākkuvaḷaippaṉ.
children.translated_text: Even if one could obtain all desired goals (<s>abhimatapuruṣārthaṅkaḷ</s>) by conversing with a non-devotee (<s>abhāgavata</s>), I would turn my tongue away from that too.

children.text: yāroṭum kūṭum
children.translated_text: 'With anyone who would join' —

children.text: puruṣārthaṅkaḷai labhiyāt’ oḻintālum avaṉōṭṭai cērttiyālē ellā mēṉmai uṇṭām eṉṉilum attaiyum kāṟkaṭai koḷḷumpaṭi āṉēṉ.
children.translated_text: Even if by associating with Him one could gain all greatness though failing to obtain the desired goals — I became such that I would kick even that aside.

children.text: a- cittam taṉṉai tavirttaṉaṉ cem kaṇ māl
children.translated_text: 'That mind He has removed — the red-eyed <s>Māl</s>' —

children.text: kaṇṇālē kuḷira nōkki taṉ vyāmohattai kāṭṭi piṟarōṭu manassu poruntātapaṭi paṇṇiṉāṉ.
children.translated_text: Looking with His eyes to cool the heart, showing His own infatuation (<s>vyāmoha</s>), He made it so that the mind would not be compatible with others.

children.text: attaṉē
children.translated_text: '<s>Attaṉē</s>' —

children.text: eṉakku svāmi āṉavaṉē
children.translated_text: He who became my master (<s>svāmi</s>)!

children.text: araṅkā eṉṟ’ aḻaikkiṉṟēṉ
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Araṅkā</s>! — thus I call out' —

children.text: anta svāmitvattai nirvahittu koṭukkaikkāka kōyililē vantu sulabhaṉ-āṉavaṉē eṉṟu kūppiṭā-niṉṟēṉ.
children.translated_text: I stood crying out: 'O You who became easily accessible (<s>sulabhaṉ</s>) by coming to the temple to fulfill that lordship (<s>svāmitva</s>)!'

children.text: pittaṉ āy oḻintēṉ em pirāṉukkē
children.translated_text: 'I have become a madman for my Lord!' —

children.text: itaraviṣayaprāvaṇyattōṭu poruntātapaṭi paṇṇiṉa upakāraṉukku pittaṉ āṉēṉ.
children.translated_text: I became a madman for the benefactor (<s>upakāra</s>) who made me incompatible with attachment to other objects.

Introduction to the seventh verse: 'How did this good fortune of not associating with others come to you?' — 'It did not come through my own effort; it came through the <s>Sarveśvaraṉ</s> (Supreme Lord),' he says.

children.text: pēyarē eṉakku yāvarum yāṉum ōr
children.translated_text: Madmen are all people to me, and I too am a

children.text: pēyaṉē evarkkum itu pēci eṉ
children.translated_text: madman to everyone — what is the use of saying this?

children.text: āyaṉē araṅkā eṉṟ’ aḻaikkiṉṟēṉ
children.translated_text: O <s>Āyaṉ</s> (the cowherd Lord)! O <s>Araṅkā</s>! — thus I call out

children.text: pēyaṉ āy oḻintēṉ em pirāṉukkē
children.translated_text: I have become a madman for my Lord!

children.text: avatārikai - eṭṭām pāṭṭu. ellārum viṭṭālum, oruvar allā oruvar paṟṟuvarkaḷiṟē, avarkaḷ ellārum viṭumpaṭi āṉēṉ eṉkiṟār.
pēyarē eṉakku yāvarum
children.translated_text: 'Madmen are all people to me' —

children.text: nilainiṉṟa puruṣārthattai viṭṭu asthiramāṉa prākṛtabhogaṅkaḷai virumpuvatē! pēyarāy iruntārkaḷ eṉṟu viṭṭēṉ nāṉ.
children.translated_text: Abandoning the permanent goal (<s>puruṣārtha</s>) and desiring impermanent material pleasures (<s>prākṛtabhogaṅkaḷ</s>)! I gave them up as madmen.

children.text: yāṉum ōr pēyaṉē evarkkum
children.translated_text: 'And I too am a madman to everyone' —

children.text: kaṇṇāl kāṇkiṟat’ oḻiya vēṟē oṉṟ’ uṇṭ eṉṟu bhramiyā-niṉṟāṉ pittaṉāy iruntāṉ’ eṉṟu viṭṭārkaḷ ivarkaḷum eṉṉai.
children.translated_text: Apart from what is seen by the eyes, 'he stands deluded saying there exists something else — he has gone mad' — thus they too gave me up.

children.text: itu pēci eṉ
children.translated_text: 'What is the use of saying this?' —

children.text: ittai parakka collukiṟat’ eṉ?
children.translated_text: What is the use of speaking about this at length?

children.text: āyaṉē
children.translated_text: '<s>Āyaṉē</s>' —

children.text: kaṇṇāl kāṇkiṟatu poy eṉṟirātapaṭi vantu avatarittu taṉ paṭikaḷai eṉakku kāṭṭiṉavaṉ
children.translated_text: He who incarnated so that what is seen by the eyes would not be dismissed as false, and showed me His true nature

children.text: araṅkā eṉṟ’ aḻaikkiṉṟēṉ
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Araṅkā</s>! — thus I call out' —

children.text: avatārattukku piṟpāṭar iḻavōṭē talaikkaṭṭātapaṭi kōyililē kaṇvaḷarnt’ aruḷiṉa periyaperumāḷ tirunāmattai colli aṭaivu keṭa kūppiṭā-niṉṟēṉ.
children.translated_text: So that later generations would not end in loss as with the incarnations, I stood crying out without restraint the divine name of <s>Periyaperumāḷ</s> who graciously reclines in the temple.

children.text: pēyaṉ āy oḻintēṉ em pirāṉukkē
children.translated_text: 'I have become a madman for my Lord!' —

children.text: oru viṣayattilē pittēṟiṉavaṉ namakku iṉi ākāṉ kāṇ, viṭāy eṉṟu itarar eṉṉai upekṣikkumpaṭi āṉēṉ.’
children.translated_text: 'One who has become mad about a single object is no longer useful to us — leave him!' — thus others came to disregard me.
Introduction to the eighth verse: 'Even if everyone else abandons, at least one or two would hold on — but I have become such that even all of them abandon me,' he says.

children.text: am kai āḻi araṅkaṉ aṭi iṇai
children.translated_text: The feet of <s>Araṅkaṉ</s> who holds the beautiful discus (<s>āḻi</s>) in His hand,

children.text: taṅku cintai taṉi perum pittaṉ āy
children.translated_text: with a mind that stays fixed there — the one great solitary madman,

children.text: koṅkar kōṉ kulacēkaraṉ coṉṉa col
children.translated_text: the words spoken by <s>Kulacēkaraṉ</s>, king of the <s>Koṅkar</s> (Cēra) people —

children.text: iṅku vallavarkk’ ētam oṉṟ’ illaiyē
children.translated_text: for those who master them here, there will be no sorrow whatsoever!

children.text: am kai āḻi araṅkaṉ aṭi iṇai
children.translated_text: 'The feet of <s>Araṅkaṉ</s> who holds the beautiful discus in His hand' —

children.text: aḻakiyamaṇavāḷapperumāḷ tiruvaṭikaḷilē
children.translated_text: At the divine feet of <s>Aḻakiyamaṇavāḷa Perumāḷ</s> (the beautiful bridegroom Lord)

children.text: taṅku cintai
children.translated_text: 'With a mind that stays' —

children.text: perumāḷ tiruvaṭikaḷukku a- aruku gantavyabhūmi illāmaiyālē aṅkē taṅkum cintaiyai uṭaiya
children.translated_text: Since there is no further destination beyond the Lord's divine feet, one with a mind that stays fixed there

children.text: taṉi perum pittaṉ āy
children.translated_text: 'The one great solitary madman' —

children.text: bhagavadviṣayattil ivar ōpāti pittēṟiṉār vēṟ’ oruvar illāmaiyum, cilarāl mīṭka oṇṇāmaiyumāṉa pittaṉāy
children.translated_text: There being no one else who became as mad in matters of the Lord (<s>bhagavadviṣaya</s>) as he, and being such a madman that no one could retrieve him

children.text: koṅkar kōṉ kulacēkaraṉ coṉṉa col
children.translated_text: 'The words spoken by <s>Kulacēkaraṉ</s>, king of the <s>Koṅkar</s>' —

children.text: mēlai tikkukku nirvāhakarāṉa śrīkulaśekhara perumāḷ aruḷicceyta
children.translated_text: The gracious words of <s>Śrī Kulaśekhara Perumāḷ</s>, the ruler of the western region

children.text: iṅku vallavarkk’ ētam oṉṟ’ illaiyē
children.translated_text: 'For those who master them here, there will be no sorrow whatsoever!' —

children.text: ivaṟṟai vallavarkaḷukku iṅku ētam oṉṟu illaiyē. ētam āvatu - abhāgavatasparśam ātal, bhagavadprāvaṇyattil kuṟai ātal; ivaṟṟāl varum duḥkham oṉṟum i- saṃsārattil irukkum nāḷil illai. i- duḥkhaprasaṅgam uḷḷatu i- iṭattēyiṟē. ivai kaṟṟavarkaḷukku i- prasaṅgam uḷḷa deśattilē illai.
children.translated_text: For those who master these, there will be no sorrow here. Sorrow means: contact with non-devotees (<s>abhāgavatasparśa</s>), or deficiency in devotion to the Lord (<s>bhagavadprāvaṇya</s>); the suffering that comes from these will not exist during the days one lives in this <s>saṃsāra</s>. This prospect of suffering exists only in this place. For those who have learned these, this prospect does not exist in such a place.

children.text: avatārikai - bhagavadjñānamum piṟantu, itaraviṣayatyāgamum piṟantu, guṇādhikaviṣayattai anubhavikka vēṇum eṉṉum ruciyum piṟantu, anta guṇam pūrṇamāka anubhavikkalām iṭattē anubhavikka vēṇum eṉṉum ācaiyum piṟantu,
aṭiyārkaḷ kuḻāṅkaḷai uṭaṉ kūṭuvatu eṉṟu-kolō
children.translated_text: 'When will I join the assemblies of devotees (<s>aṭiyārkaḷ kuḻāṅkaḷ</s>)?'

children.text: eṉṉumā pōlē,
children.translated_text: Just as it is said,

children.text: aṭiyārkaḷ tam īṭṭam kaṇṭiṭa kūṭumēl
children.translated_text: 'If only I could see the gathering of devotees!'

children.text: eṉṉumatuvum piṟantu, ippaṭi bhagavadviṣayattilum, bhāgavataviṣayattilum ānukūlyamum, itaraviṣaya-tyāgapūrvakamāka kaṇṇaḻiv’ aṟa piṟakka ceytē, virodhiyum pōy anantaram bhagavallābham ākavum kāṇāmaiyālē,
children.translated_text: This too having been born — thus, with affinity for both the Lord's domain (<s>bhagavadviṣaya</s>) and the devotees' domain (<s>bhāgavataviṣaya</s>), and with complete renunciation of other objects born mercilessly — yet since the obstacle has departed and still the attainment of the Lord (<s>bhagavallābha</s>) is not seen,

children.text: yadi vā rāvaṇaḥ svayam
children.translated_text: <s>yadi vā rāvaṇaḥ svayam</s> (even if it be Rāvaṇa himself)

children.text: eṉṟum,
children.translated_text: thus,

children.text: āḷ pārtt’ uḻi taruvāy
children.translated_text: 'O You who grant the right person at the right time!'

children.text: eṉṟum mēl viḻa kaṭava avaṉ pakkal kuṟai illai; itukku vēṟē oru hṛdayam uṇṭāka vēṇum eṉṟu pārttu, śarīrasamanantaram bhagavallābham ākil parigrahitta śarīram kṣatriyaśarīramāy bhogaṅkaḷil kuṟaiv’ aṟṟ’ irunta piṉpu śarīrāvasānatt’ aḷavum bhogaṅkaḷai bhujittu, piṉṉai kramattilē bhagavadprāpti paṇṇukiṟōm eṉṟu niṉaittirukkiṟēṉ eṉṟu niṉaittu āṟi iruntāṉ āka vēṇum eṉṉumattai tiruvuḷḷattilē koṇṭum tamakku kramaprāpti poṟāmai tōṉṟa
children.translated_text: There is no deficiency on the part of Him who always rushes toward us; thinking that a different disposition is needed for this, and that if attainment of the Lord follows immediately after death but the body assumed is a <s>kṣatriya</s> (warrior) body, then after enjoying pleasures without any lack, one might think 'I shall enjoy pleasures until the end of the body and then gradually attain the Lord' — keeping this thought in his sacred mind, and with impatience toward gradual attainment becoming manifest,

children.text: oṉṟi yākkai pukāmai uyyakoḷvāṉ niṉṟa vēṅkaṭam
children.translated_text: "<s>Vēṅkaṭam</s>, where He stands to save, so that one does not enter a body again"

children.text: eṉṟum,
children.translated_text: thus, and

children.text: manti pāy vaṭa
m
children.translated_text: He

children.text: veṅkaṭa mā malai vāṉavarkaḷ canti ceyya niṉṟāṉ
children.translated_text: stood for the celestials to worship" —
"On the great mountain of the northern <s>Vēṅkaṭam</s> where monkeys leap,

children.text: eṉṟum, kīḻ anubhavitta periyaperumāḷ tāmē saṃsārasambandham aṟuttu koṭukkaikkum, kaiṅkaryam koḷḷukaikkum tirumalaiyilē niṟkiṟār-ākaiyālē tiruvēṅkaṭamuṭaiyāṉ tiruvaṭikaḷē viḻuntu virodhiyil aruciyum kaiṅkaryattil ruciyum piṟanta tvaraiyum āviṣkarikkiṟār.
children.translated_text: thus, since <s>Periya Perumāḷ</s> whom he experienced earlier Himself stands at <s>Tirumalai</s> to sever the bond of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) and to accept service, he falls at the feet of <s>Tiruvēṅkaṭamuṭaiyāṉ</s> (the Lord of Tiruvēṅkaṭam) and manifests his distaste for obstacles, his relish for service, and his urgency.

Introduction — Having been born knowledge of the Lord (<s>bhagavadjñāna</s>), having been born renunciation of other objects (<s>itaraviṣayatyāga</s>), having been born the desire to experience the object of supreme qualities (<s>guṇādhikaviṣaya</s>), having been born the longing to experience that quality fully in the place where it can be fully experienced,

children.text: ūṉ ēṟu celvatt’ uṭal piṟavi yāṉ vēṇṭēṉ
children.translated_text: I do not desire bodily birth amid the wealth of growing flesh,

children.text: āṉēṟ’ ēḻ veṉṟāṉ aṭimai tiṟam allāl
children.translated_text: except the manner of servitude to Him who conquered the seven bulls,

children.text: kūṉ ēṟu caṅkam iṭattāṉ taṉ vēṅkaṭattu
children.translated_text: He who holds the curved conch in His left hand — at His <s>Vēṅkaṭam</s>,

children.text: kōṉēri vāḻum kuruk’ āy piṟappēṉē
children.translated_text: I would be born as a crane living at <s>Kōṉ Ēri</s> (the king's tank)!

children.text: avatārikai – mutal pāṭṭu.
ūṉēṟ’ ityādi
children.translated_text: "<s>ūṉ ēṟu</s>" etc.

children.text: prakṛtipuruṣavivekam paṇṇukaikku yogyatai uḷḷa manuṣyajanmamāy, atilē pararakṣaṇattukk’ uṟuppāṉa kṣatriyajanmam vēṇṭā; kaiṅkaryattil ellai nilattukk’ uṟuppāṉa tiryakkāy piṟakka amaiyum nāṉ eṉkiṟār.
children.translated_text: He says: I do not need a human birth which is fit for discriminating between <s>Prakṛti</s> (matter) and <s>Puruṣa</s> (self), nor within that a <s>kṣatriya</s> birth which is suited for protecting others; it suffices for me to be born as an animal that is fit for the ultimate limit of service.

children.text: ūṉ ēṟu celvatt’ uṭal piṟavi yāṉ vēṇṭēṉ
children.translated_text: I do not desire bodily birth amid the wealth of growing flesh —

children.text: inta śarīrattukku collukiṟa kuṟṟam eṉ? eṉṉa - nāḷ cella nāḷ cella māṃsapracuramāy varukaiyālē śarīram taṭittu ātmā iḷaikkum ittaṉai; attālē vēṇṭēṉ eṉkiṟār. dharmamuṭaiya svarūpamum nityamāy irukka ceytē
children.translated_text: What is the fault attributed to this body? — As days pass, the body grows fat with increasing flesh while the soul becomes emaciated; that is all. Therefore he says 'I do not desire.' Even though the essential nature of <s>dharma</s> is eternal,

children.text: asann eva
children.translated_text: "<s>asann eva</s>" (as if non-existent) —

children.text: eṉkiṟatu jñānasaṅkocattai paṟṟaviṟē; appaṭiyē jñānasaṅkocattai piṟappikkumatuākaiyālē vēṇṭēṉ eṉkiṟār.
children.translated_text: this is said with reference to the contraction of knowledge; since the body similarly produces contraction of knowledge, he says 'I do not desire.'

children.text: yāṉ vēṇṭēṉ
children.translated_text: I do not desire —

children.text: talai aṟuttu koḷḷumavarkaḷ candanam pūci tiriyumā pōlē viḻukkāṭ’ aṟiyātāṉ vēṇumē eṉṟ’ iruntāṉām attaṉai; vivekajñānamuṭaiya nāṉ vēṇṭēṉ. śarīrattiṉuṭaiya heyataiyum, ātmāviṉuṭaiya vailakṣaṇyattaiyum, itutāṉ taṉakkē śeṣam eṉṉum iṭattaiyum avaṉ tāṉē aṟivikka aṟinta nāṉ vēṇṭēṉ.
children.translated_text: Just as those who cut off heads wander around having applied sandalwood paste — one who does not know what is fit remained content with that; I, who possess discriminative knowledge, do not desire it. Having been made to know by Him Himself the despicableness of the body, the distinctiveness of the soul, and that this soul belongs exclusively to Him — I do not desire it.

children.text: āṉ ēṟ’ ēḻ veṉṟāṉ aṭimai tiṟam allāl
children.translated_text: Except the manner of servitude to Him who conquered the seven bulls —

children.text: avaṉ tāṉē virodhiyai pōkki kaiṅkaryattilē anvayippikkumavaṉ āṉāṉ.
children.translated_text: He Himself became one who removes the obstacle and engages one in service.

children.text: āṉēṟ’ ēḻ veṉṟāṉ
children.translated_text: He who conquered the seven bulls —

children.text: nappiṉṉai pirāṭṭiyōṭṭai saṃśleṣattukku iṭaiccuvarāṉa ṛṣabhaṅkaḷ ēḻaiyum veṉṟavaṉ. mātāviṉ pakkalilē snehattai paṇṇiṉa pitāvai anuvartikkum putraṉai pōlē
children.translated_text: He who conquered the seven bulls that stood as a wall between Him and union with <s>Nappiṉṉai Pirāṭṭi</s>. Just as a son follows a father who showed affection to his mother,

children.text: aṭimai tiṟam allāl
children.translated_text: the manner of servitude —

children.text: aṭimaiyiṭaiyāṭṭam eṉṉutal;
children.translated_text: either meaning the way of servitude;

children.text: ahaṃ sarvam
children.translated_text: "<s>ahaṃ sarvam</s>" (I am everything) —

children.text: eṉṟum,
children.translated_text: thus, and

children.text: vaḻuv’ ilā aṭimai
children.translated_text: "flawless servitude" —

children.text: eṉṟum collukiṟapaṭiyē aṭimai tiṟam eṉṉutal
children.translated_text: as stated thus, meaning the mode of servitude,

children.text: kūṉ ēṟu caṅkam iṭattāṉ
children.translated_text: He who holds the curved conch in His left hand —

children.text: kaiṅkaryaruci uṭaiyārai nityakaiṅkaryam koḷḷumavaṉ
children.translated_text: He who accepts eternal service from those who have the taste for service,

children.text: kūṉ ēṟu caṅkam iṭattāṉ
children.translated_text: He who holds the curved conch in His left hand —

children.text: prāñjaliṃ prahvam āsīnam
children.translated_text: "<s>prāñjaliṃ prahvam āsīnam</s>" (seated with folded hands and bowed) —

children.text: eṉṉumā pōlē bhagavadanubhavacerukkālē iḷaiyaperumāḷai pōlē kāṭcikku nōkkāy irukkiṟa śrīpāñcajanyāḻvāṉ
children.translated_text: just as <s>Śrī Pāñcajanya Āḻvāṉ</s> (the divine conch), in the pride of experiencing the Lord, stands like <s>Iḷaiya Perumāḷ</s> (Lakṣmaṇa) focused on beholding,

children.text: caṅkam iṭattāṉ
children.translated_text: The conch in His left hand —

children.text: iṭa kaiyilē kāṇil caṅkam iṭattāṉ eṉkiṟār; valakkaiyilē tiruvāḻiyāḻvāṉai kaṇṭavar-ākaiyālē
children.translated_text: Seeing it in the left hand, he says 'the conch in His left hand'; since he has already seen <s>Tiruvāḻi Āḻvāṉ</s> (the divine discus) in the right hand,

children.text: vala kai āḻi
children.translated_text: "the discus in the right hand" —

children.text: eṉkiṟār; tiru mārvilē pirāṭṭiyai kaṇṭavāṟē
children.translated_text: he says; upon seeing <s>Pirāṭṭi</s> (Lakṣmī) on His sacred chest,

children.text: niṉ vala
m
children.translated_text: right

children.text: mārpiṉil vāḻkiṉṟa maṅkai
children.translated_text: chest" —
"the maiden who dwells on Your

children.text: eṉkiṟār. ivar paṭi itiṟē.
children.translated_text: he says. This is his manner.

children.text: taṉ vēṅkaṭattu
children.translated_text: At His <s>Vēṅkaṭam</s> —

children.text: aṅkē aṭimai koḷḷukaikku pāṅkāṉa deśam-ākaiyālē eṉṉat’ eṉṟu avaṉ virumpiṉa tirumalaiyil
children.translated_text: Since it is the fitting place for accepting service there, at <s>Tirumalai</s> which He cherishes, saying 'what is mine,'

children.text: kōṉ ēri vāḻum kuruk’ āy piṟappēṉē
children.translated_text: I would be born as a crane living at <s>Kōṉ Ēri</s>! —

children.text: virajaiyai paṟṟi amānava vaśattilē vartikkumā pōlē, tiru kōṉēriyai paṟṟi vartikkum kurukāy piṟappēṉ eṉkiṟār.
children.translated_text: Just as one would dwell at the <s>Virajā</s> (river) in the domain of the non-human (divine), he says he would be born as a crane dwelling by <s>Tiru Kōṉ Ēri</s>.

children.text: vāḻum
children.translated_text: Living —

children.text: kōyil vāsam pōlē kāṇum tiru kōṉēriyil. vartikkum eṉkiṟa iṭattukku vēṟē vācakaśabdaṅkaḷ uṇṭāyirukka ceytē vāḻum eṉkiṟa śabdattai iṭṭapaṭiyālē aṅkuttai vāsam tāṉē bhogarūpamāy irukkum eṉkai.
children.translated_text: At <s>Tiru Kōṉ Ēri</s> which is like dwelling in the temple. Though there are other words to express 'dwelling,' by using the word 'living' (<s>vāḻum</s>), it means that dwelling there itself is a form of enjoyment.

children.text: kuruk’ āy piṟappēṉē
children.translated_text: I would be born as a crane! —

children.text: prakṛtipuruṣavivekam paṇṇukaikk’ uṟuppāṉa manuṣyajanmamumāy, atilē pararakṣaṇattukk’ uṟuppum-ākaiyālē puṇyaśarīramāṉa kṣatriya-janmam vēṇṭā eṉkiṟār. atu durmādahetuākaiyālē; prakṛtipuruṣavivekam paṇṇavum māṭṭātē pararakṣaṇattukk’ uṟuppum iṉṟikkē pāpayoniyumāy irukkiṟa tiryakkāy piṟakka amaiyumē tirumalai ellaikk’ uḷḷē piṟakka peṟil eṉkiṟār. uṭal piṟavi yāṉ vēṇṭēṉ eṉkiṟār; kurukāy piṟappēṉē eṉkiṟār. piṟavi aṉṟu pōlē kāṇum aṅkē piṟakkai.
children.translated_text: He says he does not want a human birth suited for discriminating between <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, nor within that a <s>kṣatriya</s> birth which, being suited for protecting others, is a meritorious body — because it causes false pride. It suffices to be born as an animal which can neither discriminate between <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> nor serve as an instrument for protecting others, and which is of lowly birth — if only one can be born within the precincts of <s>Tirumalai</s>. He says 'I do not desire bodily birth'; he says 'I would be born as a crane!' Being born there is not like birth elsewhere, it seems.
Introduction — First verse.

children.text: āṉāta celvatt’ arampaiyarkaḷ tam cūḻa
children.translated_text: Surrounded by <s>apsaras</s> (celestial maidens) of inexhaustible beauty,

children.text: vāṉ āḷum celvamum maṇ aracum yāṉ vēṇṭēṉ
children.translated_text: I do not desire the wealth of ruling heaven or earthly kingship,

children.text: tēṉ ār pūm cōlai tiru vēṅkaṭa cuṉaiyil
children.translated_text: In the pools of <s>Tiru Vēṅkaṭam</s> with honey-filled flower groves,

children.text: mīṉ āy piṟakkum viti uṭaiyēṉ āvēṉē
children.translated_text: May I have the fortune of being born as a fish!

children.text: avatārikai - iraṇṭām pāṭṭu. iṅkuttai bhogaṅkaḷiṉ kāṭṭil nilainiṉṟa bhogaṅkaḷumāy itu pōlē sāvadhi aṉṟiyē niravadhiyumāy irukkumiṟē svargattil bhogam; avai peṟṟāl ceyvat’ eṉ nīr? eṉṉa - avaiyum kīḻil kaḻitta bhūmiyil bhogamum iraṇṭum kūṭa kiṭaikkilum vēṇṭā eṉkiṟār.
āṉāta
children.translated_text: Inexhaustible —

children.text: keṭāta sampat. atāvatu - aḻiyāta yauvanaśrīyaiuṭaiya apsarassukkaḷ
children.translated_text: Imperishable wealth. That is — <s>apsaras</s> (celestial maidens) possessing unfading youthful beauty,

children.text: tam cūḻa
children.translated_text: surrounding him —

children.text: ivaṉ tāṉ tappa niṉaittālum tappa oṇṇātapaṭi avarkaḷ mēl viḻa
children.translated_text: Even if he himself thought of escaping, they would fall upon him in such a way that he cannot escape,

children.text: vāṉ āḷum celvamum maṇ aracum yāṉ vēṇṭēṉ
children.translated_text: I do not desire the wealth of ruling heaven or earthly kingship —

children.text: svargādikaḷ anubhavikkum sampattōṭē kūṭa kīḻil kaḻinta rājyaśrīyaiyum kūṭṭiṉālum vēṇṭēṉ. vēṇṭēṉ eṉkiṟatu - ivaṟṟukku kuṟai uṇṭāy aṉṟu; tām niṉaitta puruṣārtham allāmaiyālē vēṇṭēṉ eṉkiṟār. nīr vēṇṭiyiruppat’ eṉ? eṉṉa -
children.translated_text: Even if the wealth of enjoying heavenly realms and the glory of the earthly kingdom previously rejected were combined, I do not want them. His saying 'I do not desire' is not because they are deficient; since they are not the <s>puruṣārtha</s> (goal) he has in mind, he says 'I do not desire.' 'What is it that you desire?' —

children.text: tēṉ ār pūm cōlai tiru vēṅkaṭa cuṉaiyil
children.translated_text: In the pools of <s>Tiru Vēṅkaṭam</s> with honey-filled flower groves —

children.text: tēṉ mikk’ irunt’ uḷḷa poḻil eṉṉutal; vaṇṭukaḷ mikka poḻil eṉṉutal; poḻil cūḻappaṭṭ’ irukkiṟa tirumalaiyil cuṉaikaḷilē
children.translated_text: Either meaning a grove overflowing with honey; or a grove full of bees; in the mountain pools of <s>Tirumalai</s> surrounded by such groves,

children.text: mīṉ āy piṟakkum viti uṭaiyēṉ āvēṉē
children.translated_text: May I have the fortune of being born as a fish! —

children.text: kīḻ coṉṉa kurukāy piṟakkil atukku ciṟak’ uṇṭākaiyālē tirumalaiyil ellaiyai kaḻiya paṟakkaikku yogyatai uṇṭiṟē; appaṭiyum oṉṟ’ aṉṟiyē utpattisthitilayaṅkaḷum tirumalaiyilē ām mīṉāy piṟappēṉ eṉkiṟār.
children.translated_text: If born as a crane as said before, since it has wings, it would be fit to fly beyond the boundaries of <s>Tirumalai</s>; not even that — he says he would be born as a fish whose birth, existence, and death all occur within <s>Tirumalai</s>.

children.text: piṟakkum viti uṭaiyēṉ āvēṉē
children.translated_text: May I have the fortune of being born! —

children.text: ippōtu mīṉāy piṟakkavum vēṇṭā; oru sukṛtattālē anta janmam mēl varum eṉṉum tiṇmai peṟa amaiyum eṉkiṟār.
children.translated_text: He need not even be born as a fish right now; it suffices to gain the firm conviction that by some <s>sukṛta</s> (meritorious act), that birth will come in the future, he says.

Introduction — Second verse. Compared to the pleasures here, the pleasures in heaven are enduring, and unlike these which are limited, they are unlimited. 'If you obtained those, what would you do?' — He says even if both those and the earthly pleasures previously rejected were offered together, he would not want them.

children.text: piṉṉ’ iṭṭa caṭaiyāṉum piramaṉum intiraṉum
children.translated_text: <s>Śiva</s> with matted locks placed behind, and <s>Brahmā</s>, and <s>Indra</s>,

children.text: tuṉṉiṭṭu pukal ariya vaikunta
m
children.translated_text: long

children.text: nīḷ vācal
children.translated_text: gateway,
crowding together, can hardly enter — <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>'s

children.text: miṉ vaṭṭa cuṭar āḻi vēṅkaṭa kōṉ tāṉ umiḻum
children.translated_text: the Lord of <s>Vēṅkaṭam</s>, with His lightning-circled radiant discus, the golden plate He offers —

children.text: poṉ vaṭṭil piṭitt’ uṭaṉē puka peṟuvēṉ āvēṉē
children.translated_text: grasping it, may I enter along with them!

children.text: avatārikai - mūṉṟām pāṭṭu. pāratantryattukk’ uṟupp’ āka peṟil kīḻil kaḻinta manuṣyajanmamē ākilum amaiyum eṉkiṟār.
piṉṉ’ iṭṭa caṭaiyāṉum
children.translated_text: <s>Śiva</s> with matted locks placed behind —

children.text: piṉṉappaṭṭa caṭaiyāṉ eṉṉutal; piṉṉē nālappaṭṭa caṭaiyāṉ eṉṉutal; piṉṉē vartikka kaṭavaṉiṟē putraṉ; appaṭiyē brahmāviṉ piṉṉē niṟkum caṭaiyāṉ eṉṉutal.
children.translated_text: Either meaning the one with braided matted locks; or the one with matted locks hanging behind; since a son should follow behind his father, similarly the one with matted locks who stands behind <s>Brahmā</s>,

children.text: piramaṉum
children.translated_text: and <s>Brahmā</s> —

children.text: ivaṉukku janakaṉāṉa brahmāvum
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> who is his progenitor,

children.text: intiraṉum
children.translated_text: and <s>Indra</s> —

children.text: sa brahmā sa śivaḥ
children.translated_text: "<s>sa brahmā sa śivaḥ</s>" (he is Brahmā, he is Śiva) —

children.text: eṉṟāl ivarkaḷōṭ’ okka,
children.translated_text: on par with these,

children.text: sendraḥ
children.translated_text: "<s>sendraḥ</s>" (along with Indra) —

children.text: eṉṉumpaṭiyāṉa indraṉum;
children.translated_text: as stated, <s>Indra</s>;

children.text: tuṉṉiṭṭu pukal ariya vaikunta
m
children.translated_text: long

children.text: nīḷ vācal
children.translated_text: gateway —
crowding together, can hardly enter — <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>'s

children.text: oruvarkk’ oruvar muṉpu pōka vēṇṭi nerukkukaiyālē puka aritāy irukkiṟa vaikunta nīḷ vācal
children.translated_text: The long gateway of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> which is difficult to enter because they crowd against each other, each wanting to go before the other,

children.text: miṉ vaṭṭa cuṭar āḻi
children.translated_text: the lightning-circled radiant discus —

children.text: miṉṉai vaḷaittā pōlē jyotissaiyum uṭaittāy, cuṟṟum vāyaiyum uṭaittāy irukkiṟa tiruvāḻiyāḻvāṉuṭaiya
children.translated_text: <s>Tiruvāḻi Āḻvāṉ</s> (the divine discus) who possesses brilliance as if lightning were coiled around, and has a circular edge,

children.text: vēṅkaṭa
m
children.translated_text: His

children.text: kōṉ tāṉ umiḻum poṉ vaṭṭil piṭittu uṭaṉē puka peṟuvēṉ āvēṉē
children.translated_text: golden plate — grasping it, may I enter along with them! —
the Lord of <s>Vēṅkaṭam</s>,

children.text: brahmarudrādikaḷ nerukki puka peṟātē niṟka, paṇikku kaṭavaṉ, ivaṉai pukura viṭu eṉṟu uḷḷē antaraṅgavṛddhikku kaṭava avarkaḷōṭē nāṉum sajātīyaṉāy puka vēṇum.
children.translated_text: While <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Rudra</s> and others stand unable to crowd in and enter, being one fit for service, 'let him enter' — I too should enter as one of the same kind along with those who are fit for intimate service within.
Introduction — Third verse. He says that if one could obtain the state of complete dependence, even the human birth previously rejected would suffice.

children.text: oḷ pavaḷa vēlai ulavu taṇ pāl kaṭal uḷ
children.translated_text: In the cool milk ocean where bright coral waves roll,

children.text: kaṇṭuyilum māyōṉ kaḻal iṇaikaḷ kāṇpataṟku
children.translated_text: to behold the pair of feet of the wondrous one who sleeps there,

children.text: paṇ pakarum vaṇṭ’ iṉaṅkaḷ paṇ pāṭum vēṅkaṭattu
children.translated_text: at <s>Vēṅkaṭam</s> where swarms of bees sing melodies that share their music,

children.text: ceṇpakam āy niṟkum tiru uṭaiyēṉ āvēṉē
children.translated_text: may I have the fortune of standing as a <s>ceṇpakam</s> (champak) tree!

children.text: avatārikai - nālām pāṭṭu. manuṣyaśarīram rājāvākaikkum potuākaiyālē atu vēṇṭā, tiruvēṅkaṭamuṭaiyāṉukku uṟupp’ āmpaṭi tirumalaiyilē niṟpat’ oru sthāvaramāka amaiyum nāṉ eṉkiṟār.
oḷ pavaḷa vēlai ulavu taṇ pāl kaṭal uḷ
children.translated_text: In the cool milk ocean where bright coral waves roll —

children.text: oḷḷiya pavaḷattai karaiyilē koṭuvantu koḻikkiṟa pāṟkaṭal eṉṉutal; oḷḷiya pavaḷaṅkaḷai koṇṭu ulāvukiṟa tiraikaḷai uṭaiya śramaharamāṉa tiruppāṟkaṭalilē eṉṉutal.
children.translated_text: Either meaning the milk ocean that brings bright corals to the shore and deposits them; or meaning in the weariness-removing sacred milk ocean with waves that carry bright corals,

children.text: kaṇtuyilum māyōṉ
children.translated_text: the wondrous one who sleeps there —

children.text: tiruppāṟkaṭalilē
children.translated_text: in the sacred milk ocean,

children.text: kiṭantat’ ōr kiṭakkai
children.translated_text: "a reclining that is a reclining" —

children.text: eṉṟu collumpaṭi kaṇvaḷarnt’ aruḷukiṟa āścaryabhūtaṉ-āṉavaṉ
children.translated_text: as described thus, the wonder-embodied one who graciously sleeps,

children.text: kaḻal iṇaikaḷ kāṇpataṟku
children.translated_text: to behold His pair of feet —

children.text: aṅku ceṉṟu kiṭṭi kāṇa oṇṇāta arumai tīra kāṇalām deśattilē kāṇkaikkāka
children.translated_text: Since one cannot go there and approach and see, for the purpose of seeing in a land where one can see without that difficulty,

children.text: paṇ pakarum
children.translated_text: sharing melodies —

children.text: iyalai kaṟṟu śikṣābalattālē icai varum at’ aṉṟiyē vārttai collumpōtum paṇṇāy irukkai
children.translated_text: Not merely that music comes through learning techniques and practice of scales, but even when simply speaking, it comes out as melody,

children.text: vaṇṭ’ iṉaṅkaḷ paṇ pāṭum vēṅkaṭattu
children.translated_text: at <s>Vēṅkaṭam</s> where swarms of bees sing melodies —

children.text: tāṅkaḷ pāṭukiṟa pāṭṭukku icaintu vaṇṭ’ iṉaṅkaḷ-āṉavai paṇpāṭukiṟa tirumalaiyilē
children.translated_text: At <s>Tirumalai</s> where swarms of bees sing melodies in harmony with the songs being sung,

children.text: ceṇpakam āy niṟkum tiru uṭaiyēṉ āvēṉē
children.translated_text: may I have the fortune of standing as a <s>ceṇpakam</s> (champak) tree! —

children.text: tirumalaiyilē ceṇpakamāy niṟkum sampatt’ uṇṭāka vēṇum - atāvatu bhagavadpratyāsattiyiṟē prāpyam; atu kiṭṭum atāṉa piṉpu sthāvaramāy niṟkavum amaiyum; mēlē ēṟiṉa caitanyattālē kāryam illai eṉkiṟār.
children.translated_text: May I have the wealth of standing as a champak tree at <s>Tirumalai</s> — that is, proximity to the Lord is itself the goal; once that is obtained, it suffices even to stand as a stationary being; there is no need for the higher consciousness, he says.

Introduction — Fourth verse. Since a human body is common to being a king as well, he does not want that; he says it suffices for him to stand as a stationary being (<s>sthāvara</s>) at <s>Tirumalai</s> in a way that serves the Lord of <s>Tiruvēṅkaṭam</s>.

children.text: kampa
m
children.translated_text: and

children.text: mata
children.translated_text: proud

children.text: m
children.translated_text: temperament

children.translated_text: — riding atop its neck,
An elephant of fearsome

children.text: iṉp’ amarum celvamum i- aracum yāṉ vēṇṭēṉ
children.translated_text: I do not desire that pleasurable wealth or this kingship,

children.text: emperumāṉ īcaṉ eḻil vēṅkaṭam malai mēl
children.translated_text: upon the beautiful <s>Vēṅkaṭam</s> mountain of my lord, the Supreme One,

children.text: tampakam āy niṟkum tavam uṭaiyēṉ āvēṉē
children.translated_text: may I have the <s>tavam</s> (merit) of standing as a <s>tampakam</s> (copper-leaf tree)!

children.text: avatārikai – añcām pāṭṭu. ceṇpakam āṉāl parimaḷattukkāka uḷḷē koṇṭu pukuvarkaḷ eṉṟu oru prayojanattai kaṇicittatāmiṟē; appaṭiyum oṉṟum illāta tampakam ākavum amaiyum eṉkiṟār.
kampa
m
children.translated_text: and

children.translated_text: proud
