children.translated_text: — riding atop its neck —
An elephant of fearsome

children.text: kaṇṭār ellām naṭuṅkumpaṭi matippai uṭaiya āṉai eṉṉutal; matattālē kampattiṉiṉṟum viṭa oṇṇātapaṭi niṟkum yāṉai eṉṉutal; oruvarālum mēṟkoḷḷa oṇṇāt’ ākilum rājākkaḷai mēṟkoḷḷa oṭṭumiṟē yāṉaikaḷ. ellārkkum bhayāvahamāṉa yāṉaiyai mēṟkoṇṭu taṉ karuttilē naṭatti
children.translated_text: Either meaning an elephant with pride that makes all who see it tremble; or an elephant that stands immovable at its post due to its rut; though no one else can mount them, elephants allow kings to mount them. Having mounted the elephant fearsome to all and directing it by his will,

children.text: iṉp’ amarum celvamum i- aracum yāṉ vēṇṭēṉ
children.translated_text: I do not desire that pleasurable wealth or this kingship —

children.text: aṅkē iruntu ellā bhogaṅkaḷum bhujikkum sampattum atukk’ aṭiyāṉa rājadharmamum yāṉ vēṇṭēṉ. nīr vēṇṭuvat’ eṉ? eṉṉil -
children.translated_text: The wealth of enjoying all pleasures there and the royal duty that is the basis for it — I do not desire them. 'What is it that you desire?' —

children.text: emperumāṉ īcaṉ
children.translated_text: My Lord, the Supreme One —

children.text: akhilajagatsvāmi asmat svāmi
children.translated_text: "<s>akhila-jagat-svāmī asmat-svāmī</s>" (the master of the entire universe, our master) —

children.text: eḻil vēṅkaṭa
m
children.translated_text: mountain

children.text: malai mēl
children.translated_text: upon
the beautiful <s>Vēṅkaṭa</s>

children.text: ellārkkum svāmiyāy iruntu vaittu eṉ pakkalilē viśeṣakaṭākṣattai paṇṇiṉa eṉ nāyaṉatāṉa eḻil uṭaiya tirumalaiyilē
children.translated_text: Being the Lord of all, yet bestowing special grace upon me — on the beautiful sacred hill of my master

children.text: tampakam āy niṟkum tavam uṭaiyēṉ āvēṉē
children.translated_text: I would become a plant standing there, possessing such <s>tapas</s> (penance)

children.text: oru prayojanattukk’ ākātē aṅkē muḷaittu tīyntu pōvat’ oru sthāvaram āvēṉ.
children.translated_text: I would become a stationary being that sprouts there and withers away without serving any purpose.

children.text: tavam uṭaiyēṉ āvēṉē
children.translated_text: I would become one possessing such <s>tapas</s>

children.text: anekajanmasādhyatapaḥphalam eṉṟ’ irukkiṟār kāṇum itu taṉṉai.
children.translated_text: He regards this itself as the fruit of <s>tapas</s> (penance) cultivated over many births.

Introduction — Fifth verse. If one became a champak tree, since people would pluck it and bring it inside for its fragrance, he had envisioned some purpose in that; he says it suffices to be even a <s>tampakam</s> (copper-leaf tree) which has nothing of that sort.

children.text: miṉ aṉaiya nuṇ iṭaiyār uruppaciyum mēṉakaiyum
children.translated_text: <s>Urvacī</s> and <s>Mēṉakā</s>, women with waists slender as lightning

children.text: aṉṉavar tam pāṭaloṭum āṭal avai ātariyēṉ
children.translated_text: I do not care for their songs and dances

children.text: teṉṉa eṉa vaṇṭ’ iṉaṅkaḷ paṇ pāṭum vēṅkaṭatt’ uḷ
children.translated_text: On <s>Vēṅkaṭam</s> where swarms of bees sing melodious tunes humming 'teṉṉa'

children.text: aṉ aṉaiya poṉ kuvaṭ’ ām arum tavattaṉ āvēṉē
children.translated_text: I would become the rare penance of being like a golden peak

children.text: avatārikai - āṟām pāṭṭu. sthāvaram āṉāl oru nāḷ uṇṭāy oru nāḷ iṉṟiyē pōmiṟē; aṅṅaṉ aṉṟiyē eṉṟum okka uṇṭāy irunta tirumalaiyil ekadeśamāka vēṇum nāṉ eṉkiṟār.
miṉ aṉaiya nuṇ iṭaiyār, etc.
children.translated_text: 'Women with waists slender as lightning,' etc.

children.text: miṉ pōlē nuṇṇiya iṭaiyai uṭaiyarāṉa devastrīkaḷai pōlē aḻakiyarāy irukkiṟa strīkaḷuṭaiya āṭal pāṭalkaḷil eṉakku ādaram illai.
children.translated_text: I have no interest in the songs and dances of beautiful women who are like the celestial women (<s>devastrī</s>) with waists slender as lightning.

children.text: teṉṉa eṉa vaṇṭ’ iṉaṅkaḷ paṇ pāṭum vēṅkaṭatt’ uḷ
children.translated_text: On <s>Vēṅkaṭam</s> where swarms of bees sing melodious tunes humming 'teṉṉa'

children.text: teṉa teṉa eṉṟu āḷatti vaittu vaṇṭ’ iṉaṅkaḷ paṇpāṭukiṟa tirumalaiyilē
children.translated_text: On the sacred hill where swarms of bees sing tunes buzzing 'teṉa teṉa'

children.text: aṉ aṉaiya poṉ kuvaṭ’ ām arum tavattaṉ āvēṉē
children.translated_text: I would become the rare penance of being like a golden peak

children.text: appaṭippaṭṭa poṟkuvaṭ’ eṉṉum attaṉai; vēṟu upamānam illai.
children.translated_text: Such a golden peak is itself the analogy; there is no other comparison.

children.text: arum tavattaṉ āvēṉē
children.translated_text: I would become one of rare penance

children.text: tiruvēṅkaṭamuṭaiyāṉ taṉakku a- aruk’ ākiṟatiṟē; ākaiyālē, arum tavattaṉ eṉṉa kuṟai illaiyiṟē.
children.translated_text: It becomes rare precisely because it belongs to <s>Tiruvēṅkaṭamuṭaiyāṉ</s> (the Lord of <s>Tiruvēṅkaṭam</s>); therefore, there is no deficiency in calling it rare penance.
Introduction — Sixth verse. If one becomes a plant, one day it exists and another day it perishes; unlike that, 'I wish to become a part of the eternal sacred hill,' he says.

children.text: vāṉ āḷum mā mati pōl veṇ kuṭai kīḻ maṉṉavar tam
children.translated_text: Under the white parasol like the great moon ruling the sky, of kings

children.text: kōṉ āki vīṟṟiruntu koṇṭāṭum celv’ aṟiyēṉ
children.translated_text: I do not know the wealth of being their sovereign, sitting exalted and being celebrated

children.text: tēṉ ār pūm cōlai tiru vēṅkaṭam malai mēl
children.translated_text: On the sacred <s>Vēṅkaṭam</s> hill with honey-filled flower groves

children.text: kāṉ āṟ’ āy pāyum karutt’ uṭaiyēṉ āvēṉē
children.translated_text: I would become one with the intention to flow as a forest stream

children.text: avatārikai - ēḻām pāṭṭu. tirumalaiyil śikharam āṉāl ēṟa vallār anubhavittu, māṭṭātār iḻakkumatāy irukkumiṟē; appaṭi iṉṟiyē ellārkkum anubhava-yogyamāy irukkum kāṉāṟāka vēṇum nāṉ eṉkiṟār.
vāṉ āḷum mā mati pōl veḷ kuṭai kīḻ
children.translated_text: Under the white parasol like the great moon ruling the sky

children.text: ākāśa parappukk’ ellām candraṉ oruvaṉumē āṉā pōlē, lokam ellām taṉ veṇkoṟṟakkuṭai kīḻē otuṅkumpaṭiyāka
children.translated_text: Just as the moon alone suffices for the entire expanse of the sky, under the single pearl parasol so that the whole world comes under it

children.text: maṉṉavar tam kōṉ āki
children.translated_text: being the king of kings

children.text: nakṣatratārāgaṇaṅkaḷ candraṉai sevittirukkumā pōlē; rājākkaḷ ellām vantu sevittirukkumpaṭi rājarājaṉāy
children.translated_text: Just as the constellations and stars attend upon the moon, being the king of kings with all rulers coming to serve

children.text: vīṟṟiruntu koṇṭāṭum celv’ aṟiyēṉ
children.translated_text: I do not know the wealth of sitting exalted and being celebrated

children.text: vēṟupaṭa iruntu koṇṭāṭum sampat eṉakku pratipattiviṣayam ākiṟat’ illai.
children.translated_text: The prosperity of sitting distinguished and being celebrated is not an object of my regard.

children.text: tēṉ ār pūm cōlai tiru vēṅkaṭam malai mēl
children.translated_text: On the sacred <s>Vēṅkaṭam</s> hill with honey-filled flower groves

children.text: tēṉ mikk’ iruntuḷḷa cōlaiyai uṭaiya tirumalai-mēl
children.translated_text: On the sacred hill that has groves overflowing with honey

children.text: kāṉ āṟ’ āy pāyum karutt’ uṭaiyēṉ āvēṉē
children.translated_text: I would become one with the intention to flow as a forest stream

children.text: sahyam paṟṟiṉat’ ākil kīḻē pōmiṟē; aṅkē cuvaṟi pōm kāṭṭāṟukaḷ ām abhisandhiyai uṭaiyēṉ āka vēṇum.
children.translated_text: If it originates from <s>Sahya</s>, it would flow downward; I wish to become those forest streams that flow along the walls there.

Introduction — Seventh verse. If it is a peak on the sacred hill, those who can climb will experience it, but those who cannot will miss it; unlike that, 'I wish to become a forest stream accessible for everyone's experience,' he says.

children.text: piṟai ēṟu caṭaiyāṉum piramaṉum intiraṉum
children.translated_text: <s>Śiva</s> who bears the crescent moon on his matted locks, and <s>Brahmā</s>, and <s>Indra</s>

children.text: muṟai āya peru vēḷvi kuṟai muṭippāṉ maṟai āṉāṉ
children.translated_text: He who became the <s>Veda</s> to complete the deficiencies in their great, ordained <s>yajñas</s> (sacrifices)

children.text: veṟi ār taṇ cōlai tiru vēṅkaṭam malai mēl
children.translated_text: On the sacred <s>Vēṅkaṭam</s> hill with cool, fragrant groves

children.text: neṟi āy kiṭakkum nilai uṭaiyēṉ āvēṉē
children.translated_text: I would become one with the state of lying there as a path

children.text: piṟai ēṟu caṭaiyāṉum
children.translated_text: <s>Śiva</s> who bears the crescent moon on his matted locks

children.text: sādhakaveṣam tōṟṟumpaṭi jaṭaiyōṭē irukka ceytē sukhapradhānaṉ eṉṟu tōṟṟumpaṭi piṟaiyai dharittukkoṇṭ’ irukkiṟa haraṉum
children.translated_text: <s>Hara</s> who, while appearing in the guise of an ascetic with matted locks, bears the crescent moon to show that he is one who gives pleasure

children.text: piramaṉum
children.translated_text: and <s>Brahmā</s>

children.text: avaṉukku janakaṉāṉa brahmāvum
children.translated_text: and <s>Brahmā</s> who is his progenitor

children.text: intiraṉum
children.translated_text: and <s>Indra</s>

children.text: sendraḥ
children.translated_text: <s>sendraḥ</s> (with <s>Indra</s>)

children.text: eṉṉumpaṭiyāṉa indraṉum
children.translated_text: and <s>Indra</s> as described thus

children.text: muṟai āya peru vēḷvi kuṟai muṭippāṉ
children.translated_text: He who completes the deficiencies in the great, ordained sacrifices

children.text: tam tāmuṭaiya adhikārānuguṇamāka paṇṇum yajñaphalamāṉa adhikāraṅkaḷai koṭukkumavaṉ
children.translated_text: He who grants the positions that are the fruits of the <s>yajñas</s> (sacrifices) they perform according to their respective qualifications

children.text: maṟai āṉāṉ
children.translated_text: He who became the <s>Veda</s>

children.text: brahmādikaḷukku āśrayaṇīyaṉ eṉṉum vedaikasamadhigamyaṉ āṉavaṉ
children.translated_text: He who is known only through the <s>Vedas</s> as the one worthy of refuge for <s>Brahmā</s> and others

children.text: veṟi ār taṇ cōlai tiru vēṅkaṭam malai mēl neṟi āy kiṭakkum nilai uṭaiyēṉ āvēṉē
children.translated_text: On the sacred <s>Vēṅkaṭam</s> hill with cool, fragrant groves, I would become one with the state of lying there as a path

children.text: parimaḷa
children.translated_text: fragrance

children.text: m

mikku kuḷirttiyai uṭaiya tirumalai-mēlē; āṟ’ āṉāl orukāl perukiṉāl viniyogappaṭṭu, vaṟṟiṉāl viniyogappaṭātiṟē; aṅṅaṉ aṉṟiyē, eppōtum okka śrīvaiṣṇavarkaḷ sañcarikkaiyālē avarkaḷ pādareṇu paṭumpaṭi vaḻiyāy kiṭakkum tuṇiv’ uṭaiyaṉ āvēṉē.
children.translated_text: On the sacred hill that has abundant coolness; if it were a river, it would be useful when flooding but useless when it dries up; unlike that, because <s>Śrīvaiṣṇavas</s> constantly traverse here, I would become one with the resolve to lie as a path where their foot-dust falls upon me.

children.text: toṇṭar aṭi poṭi āṭa nām peṟil
children.translated_text: 'If only we could bathe in the foot-dust of the devotees'

children.text: eṉṟ’ irukkumavariṟē.
children.translated_text: thus speaks one who holds this sentiment.

children.text: ceṭi āya val viṉaikaḷ tīrkkum tirumālē

avatārikai – taru tuyaram - tirumantrattāl colliṟṟ’āyttu ananyārha-śeṣatvamiṟē; inta ananyārhaśeṣatvapratipattikku virodhi tāṉ nāṉ eṉṉatu eṉṟ’ irukkum ahaṅkāramamakāramiṟē. anātmanyātmabuddhiyum, asve-svatvabuddhiyumiṟē saṃsāram-ākiṟa vṛkṣattukku bījam eṉṟu pra-māṇaṅkaḷ collukiṉṟaṉa; atu cetanarkku potuvāṉat’ iṟē. appaṭi aṉṟiyē, rājākkaḷ-ākaiyālē ahaṅkāramamakāravaśyarāyiṟē iruppatu. nilā, teṉṟal, cantaṉam eṉṟu collukiṟa ivai parārtham ākātapōtu svarūpasiddhi illaiyāmiṟē. appaṭiyēyiṟē parārthamāṉa vastuvukkum; ahaṅkāramamakārattālē svarūpa-siddhi aḻiyumiṟē.

eṉṟum ōtukaiyālē ivaṉ oṉṟukkum kaṭavaṉ allaṉ; uṭaiyavaṉāṉa avaṉ ellāvaṟṟukkum kaṭavaṉ eṉṟatiṟē; appaṭi pramāṇaṅkaḷāl coṉṉa śeṣatvapratipatti āvatu tadīyaśeṣatvaparyantamāṉa ananyārhaśeṣatvamiṟē. appaṭi tamakku piṟant’ irukka ceytē atu phalapradamāka kaṇṭilar; tāṉ taṉ karmam ceykiṟāṉ eṉṟ’ ātal; nām kramattālē ceykiṟōm eṉṟu āṟi iruntāṉ ātalāl; nammuṭaiya tvaraikk’ aṭiyāṉa ruciyum aṟiyumavaṉ-ākaiyālē ruci pākam āṉāl ceykiṟōm eṉṟu āṟi iruntāṉām ittaṉai.
	  nammai pōl aṉṟiyē, ceytatu aṟint’ irukkum sarvajñaṉāyum, niṉaittatu talaikkaṭṭa valla sarvaśaktiyāyum iruntu-vaittu āṟi irukkumpōtu cila hetukkaḷ uṇṭāka vēṇumiṟē eṉṟu pārttu eṉakku nāṉum illai, piṟarum illai, pēṟṟil tvaraiyālē tuṭikkiṟēṉ ittaṉai allatu sādhanānuṣṭhānakṣamaṉum allēṉ eṉṉum iṭattai ananyagatikaḷāy irukkum padārthaṅkaḷai nidarśanamāka iṭṭu tammuṭaiya ananyagatitvattai tiru vittuvakkōṭṭu nāyaṉār tiruvaṭikaḷilē viṇṇappam ceykiṟār.
children.translated_text: thus reciting — this means this being owes nothing to anyone; He who is the owner is the one responsible for everything. The realization of <s>śeṣatva</s> (servitude) stated thus by the <s>pramāṇas</s> is exclusive servitude extending to <s>tadīyaśeṣatva</s> (servitude to His devotees). Even though this had arisen in him, he did not see it bear fruit; either thinking 'he is performing his own <s>karma</s>,' or being patient thinking 'we shall do it in due course'; since He who knows the <s>ruci</s> (taste/inclination) that is the basis of our urgency waits until the taste matures, He remained patient — that is all. Unlike us, being the omniscient one who knows what has been done, and the omnipotent one capable of accomplishing what He wills — yet when He waits patiently, there must be certain reasons — thinking thus, 'I have neither myself nor anyone else; I merely struggle due to my urgency for the goal and am not even capable of practicing the means' — using objects that have no other refuge as illustrations, he presents his own state of having no other refuge at the sacred feet of the Lord of <s>Tiruvittuvakkōṭu</s>.

Introduction — '<s>taru tuyaram</s>' — What was stated through the <s>Tirumantra</s> (sacred mantra) is <s>ananyārhaśeṣatva</s> (exclusive servitude to none other); the obstacle to this realization of exclusive servitude is <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego) and <s>mamakāra</s> (possessiveness) which constitute 'I' and 'mine.' The <s>pramāṇas</s> (authoritative texts) declare that <s>anātmanyātmabuddhi</s> (mistaking the non-self for the self) and <s>asve-svatvabuddhi</s> (mistaking another's property for one's own) are the seed of the tree of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence); this is common to all sentient beings. Moreover, being kings, they are especially subject to <s>ahaṅkāra</s> and <s>mamakāra</s>. Just as moonlight, breeze, and sandalwood have no <s>svarūpasiddhi</s> (fulfillment of essential nature) unless they serve others, so too for any entity that exists for another's sake — through <s>ahaṅkāra</s> and <s>mamakāra</s>, the fulfillment of essential nature is destroyed. Is there <s>pramāṇa</s> (authoritative evidence) for saying 'exists for another's sake'? — Regarding the self,

nīyē tarukiṟa duḥkhattai nīyē māṟṟāy ākil; taṉṉālē taṉakku virodhi vantat’ eṉṟum tāṉē sādhanānuṣṭhānattālē atu pōkki koḷvāṉ eṉṟum śāstraṅkaḷ colli kiṭakka ceytē, ivar avaṉē tuyar tantāṉ eṉpāṉ eṉ? eṉṉil - prāptāprāptavivekam paṇṇi iruppār oruvar-ākaiyālē collukiṟār. tāṉē karmam paṇṇiṉavaṉ, tāṉē sādhanānuṣṭhānam paṇṇi tavirttu koḷḷukiṟāṉ eṉṟu nammai paḻi iṭṭu taḷḷa niṉaittāṉ-ākilum, nāṉum taṉṉai kuṟittu paratantraṉ, nāṉ ceyta karmamum paratantram, nāṉ paṇṇum sādhanānuṣṭhānattukku phalapradaṉ tāṉ ākaiyālē atuvum taṉṉai kuṟittu paratantram ākaiyālē taru tuyaram eṉkiṟār.
	  mutalikaḷ ellārum kūṭa periya tiru-maṇa maṇṭapattukku kīḻāka iruntu rahasyārthaṅkaḷ vicārittu eḻuntiruppārkaḷ-āyttu; oru nāḷ nityasaṃsāriyāy pōntavaṉukku bhagavadviṣayattil ruci piṟakkaikku aṭi eṉ? eṉṟu vicārikka ceytē, yādṛcchikasukṛtam, ajñātasukṛtam eṉṉa piṟantatu; a- aḷavil kiṭāmpipperumāḷ-iruntavaṉ, namakku bhagavadsamāśrayaṇam pōlē sukṛtadevar eṉṟ oruvar uṇṭō āśrayaṇīyaṉ? eṉṟāṉ; piḷḷai tirunaṟaiyūraraiyar, sukṛtam eṉṟu collukiṟa nīr tām niṉaitt’ irukkiṟatu ettai kāṇ? eṉṟār. atāvatu - oṉṟai ārāya pukkāl atukk’ a- aruku vēṟ’ oṉṟu iṉṟi iruppatiṟē aṭi āvatu; yāt’ oṉṟu phalapradamāṉatiṟē upāyam āvatu; allatu naṭuvē anekāvasthai piṟantāl avaṟṟiṉ aḷavil paryavasiyātiṟē. iḷaippāṟuvatu itilē ceṉṟiṟē; naṭuvu iḷaippāṟātiṟē; attālē taru tuyaram eṉṉalāmiṟē.
children.translated_text:
If You who inflict the suffering do not Yourself remove it—though the scriptures (<s>śāstra</s>-s) say that one's obstacle comes from oneself and that one must remove it through one's own practice of means (<s>sādhanānuṣṭhāna</s>), why does this <s>Āḻvār</s> say 'He Himself gave the suffering'? Because he is one who discerns what is proper and what is not (<s>prāptāprāptaviveka</s>). Even if the Lord intends to blame us and push us away saying 'He who performed the <s>karma</s> must himself perform the means and remove it,' I too am subordinate (<s>paratantra</s>) to Him, my <s>karma</s> too is subordinate, and since He alone grants the fruit of whatever means I practice, that too is subordinate to Him—hence he says 'the suffering You give.'
	All the senior disciples (<s>mutalikaḷ</s>) would sit together beneath the great wedding hall and deliberate on the esoteric meanings (<s>rahasyārtha</s>-s) and then rise; one day they were inquiring: 'What is the basis for a taste (<s>ruci</s>) for the Lord to arise in one who has been an eternal <s>saṃsārī</s> (worldly being)?' The answer arose: '<s>yādṛcchikasukṛta</s> (accidental merit), <s>ajñātasukṛta</s> (unknowing merit).' At that point, <s>Kiṭāmbi Perumāḷ</s> who was present asked: 'Just as for us there is taking refuge in the Lord (<s>bhagavadsamāśrayaṇa</s>), is there a certain '<s>Sukṛtadevar</s>' (Lord of Merit) whom one must take refuge in?' <s>Piḷḷai Tirunaṟaiyūr Araiyar</s> said: 'You who speak of merit—what exactly do you think it is?' That is to say—when one investigates anything, the basis is that there is nothing else close to it; what grants the fruit is what constitutes the means; otherwise, if many intermediate states arise, it does not terminate at their level. The resting point is only at this ultimate end; it does not rest at any intermediate point; therefore it can be called 'the suffering You give.'

children.translated_text: "If You would"—

children.translated_text: "My <s>māyā</s> is exceedingly difficult to cross"—

children.translated_text: and,

children.text:
eṉṟum nammuṭaiya māyai oruvarāl kaṭakka oṇṇātu kāṇ eṉṟum, itu kaṭakka vēṇṭi iruntavaṉ nammai paṟṟi kaḻittu koḷvāṉ eṉṟum nīyē colli vaikkayālē nīyē tuyar tantāy eṉṉumpaṭi tōṟṟukiṟatiṟē. duḥkhattai viḷaivippāṉ oruvaṉum pōkkuvāṉ oruvaṉumāy aṉṟiṟē iruppatu. paṇṇiṉavaṉ tāṉē pōkkum ittaṉaiyiṟē; piḷḷai tirunaṟaiyūraraiyar, oru kuruvi piṇaitta piṇaiyal oruvarāl aviḻkka oṇkiṟat’ illai; oru sarvaśakti piṇaitta piṇaiyai eliyelumpaṉāṉa ivaṉ aviḻkka eṉṟu oru kāryam illaiyiṟē; avaṉ taṉṉaiyē kālkaṭṭi pōkkum ittaṉaiyiṟē eṉṟār.
	  i- aḷavāka viḷaittukkoṇṭa nāṉ eṉakk’ illai; piṟar rakṣakar uṇṭākilum nāṉ avarai rakṣakarāka koḷḷa māṭṭāmaiyālē avarkaḷum illai; nāṉ paṇṇum sādhanānuṣṭhānamum eṉakku kaḻuttukkaṭṭiākaiyālē devarīr tiruvaṭikaḷ allatu vēṟu upāyam illai.
children.translated_text:
Since You Yourself have declared that 'Our <s>māyā</s> cannot be crossed by anyone' and that 'One who wishes to cross it must take hold of Us and extricate himself,' it appears that You Yourself have given the suffering. It is not that one person creates the suffering and another removes it. The one who created it Himself removes it—that is all. <s>Piḷḷai Tirunaṟaiyūr Araiyar</s> said: 'A knot tied by a little sparrow cannot be untied by anyone; there is no question of this insignificant being untying a knot tied by One who is omnipotent (<s>sarvaśakti</s>); He Himself must bind our feet and send us—that is all.'
	I who have caused this much trouble am of no use to myself; even if other protectors exist, since I am unable to accept them as protectors, they too are of no avail; since the means I practice become a noose around my own neck, there is no means other than Your divine feet.

children.text: virai kuḻuvu malar poḻil cūḻ viṟṟuvakkōṭṭ’ ammāṉē
children.translated_text: "O Lord of <s>Viṟṟuvakkōṭu</s> (Tiruvittuvakkōṭu), surrounded by flower-groves fragrant with perfume!"—

children.text: parimaḷapracuramāṉa cōlaiyai uṭaittāṉa tiru vittuvakkōṭṭilē eḻuntaruḷi irukkiṟa sarveśvaraṉē!
children.translated_text: O <s>Sarveśvara</s> (Lord of all) who graciously resides in <s>Tiru Vittuvakkōṭu</s> which possesses groves abundant with fragrance!

children.text: virai kuḻuvu malar poḻil cūḻ
children.translated_text: "surrounded by flower-groves fragrant with perfume"—

children.text: sarvagandhaḥ
children.translated_text: "<s>sarvagandhaḥ</s>" (He who is all fragrances)—

children.text: eṉkiṟa prāpyavastu vantu kiṭṭiṉa iṭam eṉṟu tōṉṟi irukkum-āyttu
children.translated_text: it appears as the place where the object to be attained (<s>prāpyavastu</s>), who is described thus, has come and made Himself accessible.

children.text: viṟṟuvakkōṭṭ’ ammāṉē
children.translated_text: "O Lord of <s>Viṟṟuvakkōṭu</s>"—

children.text: vēṇumiṟē
children.translated_text: it is necessary indeed—

children.text: ammāṉē
children.translated_text: "O Lord!"—

children.text: prajai uṟaṅkukiṟa toṭṭil-kīḻē kiṭakkum tāyai pōlē iṅkē vantu kiṭṭiṉavaṉē! tammuṭaiya pāratantryattālē tammuṭaiya rakṣaṇattukku tamakku ananvayam coṉṉār. śeṣiākaiyālē tammuṭaiya rakṣaṇattukku prāptaṉ avaṉ eṉkiṟār. ippōtu oruvaṉ pēṟṟukku oruvaṉ sādhanam āmpōtu ittaṉai prāpti uṇṭāṉāl-allatu ākātiṟē. prajai uṭaiya nōykku tāyiṟē kuṭinīr kuṭippāḷ. mēl tāyai nidarśanamāka colla pukukiṟavar-ākaiyālē ippōtu ammāṉē eṉṟu prāpti tōṉṟa collukiṟār.
children.translated_text: Like a mother who lies beneath the cradle where her child sleeps, He who has come here and made Himself accessible! By their own subordination (<s>pāratantrya</s>) they declared their own non-involvement in their own protection. Since He is the Master (<s>śeṣī</s>), they say He is the one entitled to their protection. Now, when one person's attainment requires another as the means, such entitlement (<s>prāpti</s>) must exist for it to work. It is the mother who drinks the medicinal water for the child's illness. Since the <s>Āḻvār</s> is about to use the mother as an illustration in what follows, he now says 'O Lord!' (<s>ammāṉē</s>) to indicate this entitlement.

children.text: ari ciṉattāl, ityādi
children.translated_text: "With discerning anger" and so forth—

children.text: avaṉē rakṣakaṉ eṉṉum adhyavasāyam uṇṭāṉālum pēṟu tāḻttāl avaṉai veṟukka vēṇṭum prāpti uṇṭiṟē cetanaṉ-ākaiyālē.
children.translated_text: Even when the conviction arises that He alone is the protector, if the attainment is delayed, there is entitlement to be angry with Him, since one is a conscious being (<s>cetana</s>).

children.text: taṉakkē āka eṉai koḷḷum ītē
children.translated_text: "Exclusively for Himself He takes me—this alone"—

children.text: eṉṟu acitsamānamāka pāratantryattai collivaittu,
children.translated_text: having stated the subordination (<s>pāratantrya</s>) as equal to that of insentient matter (<s>acit</s>),

children.text: eṉakkē kaṇṇaṉai yāṉ koḷ ciṟappu
children.translated_text: "The special privilege that I take <s>Kaṇṇaṉ</s> (Kṛṣṇa) exclusively for myself"—

children.text: eṉkiṟatu puruṣārthasiddhi cetanaṉukkāka vēṇṭiyiṟē. avaṉai kuṟittu cetanācetanaṅkaḷ iraṇṭukkum pāratantryam aviśiṣṭamāy irukka ceytē puruṣārthasiddhi ivaṉukku uṇṭākiṟatu cetanaṉ-ākaiyāliṟē.
children.translated_text: the attainment of the supreme goal (<s>puruṣārthasiddhi</s>) must be for the sake of the conscious being. Though subordination to Him is equal for both sentient and insentient beings, the attainment of the goal occurs for this one because he is a conscious being.

children.text: ari ciṉattāl
children.translated_text: "with discerning anger"—

children.text: arintu pokaṭa vēṇṭum ciṉattai uṭaiyavaḷāy koṇṭu
children.translated_text: possessing an anger that knows and must strike,

children.text: īṉṟa tāy
children.translated_text: "the birth-mother"—

children.text: vaḷartta tāy eṉṉātē īṉṟa tāy eṉṟattālē prāpti colliṟṟu.
children.translated_text: by saying 'birth-mother' rather than 'foster-mother,' the entitlement (<s>prāpti</s>) is indicated.

children.text: akaṟṟ’ iṭiṉum
children.translated_text: "even if she pushes away"—

children.text: akaṟṟiṭiṉum eṉkaiyālē akaṟṟukai asambhāvitam eṉkiṟatu. īṉṟa tāy eṉkaiyālē, peṟukaikku nōṉpu nōṟkaiyum pattu māsam cumakkaiyum prasavavedanai paṭukaiyum eṉkiṟa ivai ellām uṭaiyavaḷ eṉkai.
children.translated_text: by saying 'even if she pushes away,' it indicates that pushing away is inconceivable. By saying 'birth-mother,' it means she is one who underwent the austerity of desiring offspring, carried the child for ten months, and endured the pain of childbirth—all this she possesses.

children.text: akaṟṟ’ iṭiṉum
children.translated_text: "even if she pushes away"—

children.text: ippaṭi peṟuvataṟku muṉp’ uḷḷa ellā duḥkhamum paṭṭavaḷ-ākaiyālē varukiṟattai niṉaikkum at’ oḻiya akaṟṟa niṉaiyāḷiṟē; avaḷ tāṉē akala viṭiṉum; ittāl colliṟṟ’ āyttu - nirupādhikabandhuvāṉa devarīr kaiviṭilum vēṟu eṉakku pukal illai eṉkiṟār.
children.translated_text: since she has endured all the suffering prior to giving birth, she would only think of what is coming and would never think of pushing away; even if she herself were to let go—by this it is said: even if You, who are my unconditional kinsman (<s>nirupādhikabandhu</s>), were to abandon me, there is no other refuge for me.

children.text: maṟṟ’ avaḷ taṉ aruḷ niṉaintē aḻum kuḻavi
children.translated_text: "the infant that cries thinking only of her grace"—

children.text:
ivaḷ kopittu viṭṭālum vēṟ’ oruvaruṭaiya aruḷai apekṣiyātiṟē prajai. atukk’ aṭiyāṉa premattukku avadhi uṇṭākiliṟē kopattukku avadhi uḷḷatu; sneham illāmaiyālē kopam illaiyiṟē piṟarkku.
	  nampi tiruvaḻuti vaḷanāṭu dāsarai mutaliyāṇṭāṉ kopittu, kaiyālum kālālum tukaittu iḻuttavāṟē tiṇṇaiyil paṭṭiṉiyē oru nāḷ pōkātē kiṭantār; āṇṭāṉ maṟṟai nāḷ amutu ceyya pukukiṟār; avaṉ ceytat eṉ’ eṉṟu kēṭṭavāṟē, paṭṭiṉiyē vācalilē kiṭantāṉ eṉṟu kēṭṭu aḻaittu, nī pōkātē kiṭantat eṉ?’ eṉṉa; oru nāḷ oru piṭi cōṟ’ iṭṭavaṉ ellā paṭiyālum nintittālum vācal viṭṭu pōkiṟat’ illai nāy; nāṉ eṅkē pōvatu? eṉṟār.
children.translated_text:
even if she becomes angry and lets go, the child does not seek the grace of anyone else. Since the love that underlies it has a limit, anger too has a limit; for others, since there is no love, there is no anger either.
	<s>Mutaliyāṇṭāṉ</s> once became angry with <s>Nampi Tiruvaḻuti Vaḷanāṭu Dāsar</s> and beat him with hands and feet and dragged him out; he lay on the veranda fasting for a whole day without leaving; the next day when <s>Āṇṭāṉ</s> was about to eat, he asked 'What did he do?'; hearing that 'he is lying at the doorstep fasting,' he called him and asked 'Why didn't you leave?' He replied: 'A dog that has been given even one handful of rice by someone will not leave the doorstep no matter how much he is reviled in every way; where would I go?'

children.text: aḻum kuḻavi atuvē pōṉṟ’ iruntēṉē
children.translated_text: "I remained just like that crying infant"—

children.text: vēṟu cilarāl āṟṟa oṇṇātiṟē; muṉṉāḷ mulai koṭutta upakārattai niṉaitt’ irukkumat’ākaiyālē avaḷ tāṉē āṟṟa vēṇumē.
children.translated_text: no one else can console it; since it keeps remembering the earlier kindness of being given the breast, she herself must console it.

children.text: śiśuḥ stanandhayaḥ
children.translated_text: "<s>śiśuḥ stanandhayaḥ</s>" (the infant at the breast)—

children.text: aḷav’ il piḷḷaimai
children.translated_text: "the state of utter infancy"—

children.text: eṉṟu collukiṟapaṭiyē. atāvatu – raktasparśam uṭaiyār ellāraiyum aṟiyātē mātā oruttiyaiyum aṟiyum-aḷavē āyttu atibālyam; appaṭiyē emperumāṉai kuṟittu i- ātmavastu nityastanandhayamāy-āyttu iruppatākaiyāliṟē ivaṉ pēṟṟukku avaṉ upāyam ākiṟatu.
children.translated_text: as it is said. That is—extreme infancy is when, not knowing anyone else among blood-relations, one knows only the mother alone; just so, since the soul (<s>ātman</s>) eternally remains like an infant at the breast with respect to the Lord (<s>Emperumāṉ</s>), He becomes the means for this one's attainment.

children.text: kaṇṭār ikaḻvaṉavē kātalaṉ tāṉ ceyt’ iṭiṉum
children.translated_text: "Even if the beloved does things that onlookers would despise,"

children.text: koṇṭāṉai allāl aṟiyā kulamakaḷ pōl
children.translated_text: "like a woman of noble family (<s>kulamakaḷ</s>) who knows no one but the one who married her,"

children.text: viṇ tōy matiḷ puṭai cūḻ viṟṟuvakkōṭṭ’ ammā
children.translated_text: "O Lord of <s>Viṟṟuvakkōṭu</s> surrounded by sky-touching ramparts,"

children.text: koṇṭ’ āḷāy ākilum uṉ kurai kaḻalē kūṟuvaṉē
children.translated_text: "even if You take me as Your servant, I shall speak only of Your ringing feet!"

children.text: kaṇṭār ikaḻvaṉavē kātalaṉ tāṉ ceyt’ iṭiṉum
children.translated_text: "Even if the beloved does things that onlookers would despise"—

children.text: tāṉum avaṉum aṟintatāka piṟakkum praṇayakalahaṅkaḷukkum parihāraṅkaḷukkum ōr avadhi illaiyiṟē. appaṭi aṉṟiyē, ivarkaḷ kāryam koṇṭu kāryam illāta udāsīnarum ikaḻumpaṭikk’ īṭāṉa asahyaṅkaḷai avaṉ paṇṇiṉālum
children.translated_text: the lovers' quarrels (<s>praṇayakalaha</s>-s) and reconciliations that arise when both she and he are aware of them have no limit. But beyond that, even if he commits unbearable acts that cause even disinterested onlookers to despise him—

children.text: kātalaṉ
children.translated_text: "the beloved"—

children.text: premattai iṭṭu nirūpikka vēṇṭi irukkumavaṉ.
children.translated_text: one whose identity must be defined by his love,

children.text: koṇṭāṉai allāl aṟiyā kulamakaḷ pōl
children.translated_text: "like a woman of noble family who knows no one but the one who married her"—

children.text: i- aruku avaṉ paṇṇum apakāraṅkaḷai kāṟkaṭaikkoṇṭu sambandhattil mutal aṭiyilē niṉaitt’ irukkumavaḷai pōlē
children.translated_text: like one who brushes aside the injuries he inflicts at such close quarters and stands firm remembering only the very first moment of their bond,

children.text: koṇṭāṉai allāl aṟiyā kulamakaḷ pōl
children.translated_text: "like a woman of noble family who knows no one but the one who married her"—

children.text: agnikku antaryāmiyāṉa sarveśvaraṉai sākṣiyāka koṇṭavaṉaiallatu aṟiyātavaḷai pōlē. koṇṭāṉai allāl aṟiyā eṉkaiyālē, pātivratyam colliṟṟu; kulamakaḷ eṉkaiyālē ābhijātyam colliṟṟu.
children.translated_text: like one who knows no one other than the one who took her hand with <s>Sarveśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord) dwelling within <s>Agni</s> (fire) as witness. By saying 'knows no one but the one who married her,' <s>pātivratya</s> (wifely fidelity) is expressed; by saying '<s>kulamakaḷ</s>' (woman of noble family), noble birth (<s>ābhijātya</s>) is expressed.

children.text: viṇ tōy matiḷ puṭai cūḻ viṟṟuvakkōṭṭ’ ammā
children.translated_text: "O Lord of <s>Viṟṟuvakkōṭu</s> surrounded by sky-touching ramparts"—

children.text: pirāṭṭi svayaṃvarattukku śrīmithilaiyil puṟa cōlaiyilē viṭṭ’ iruntā pōlē, ivarai svayaṃvarikkaikkākaviṟē tiru vittuvakkōṭṭilē vantu niṟkiṟatu.
children.translated_text: just as <s>Pirāṭṭi</s> (Sītā) was kept in the outer grove of <s>Śrī Mithilā</s> for her <s>svayaṃvara</s> (self-choice marriage), it is for the purpose of choosing these devotees that He comes and stands at <s>Tiru Vittuvakkōṭu</s>.

children.text: nī koṇṭ’ āḷāy ākilum
children.translated_text: "even if You take me as Your servant"—

children.text: i- aḷavāka upakārakaṉāṉa nī kuṟaiyum talaikkaṭṭātē upekṣittālum
children.translated_text: even if You who have been thus far the benefactor neglect me without even completing the deficiency,

children.text: uṉ kurai kaḻalē kūṟuvaṉē
children.translated_text: "I shall speak only of Your ringing feet!"—

children.text: uṉ tiruvaṭikaḷ allatu eṉakku vēṟu pukal illai. upakārakaṉāṉa nī upekṣittāy eṉṟu kaivāṅkumavaṉ aṉṟu nāṉ; eṉat’ āvi yār yāṉ ār eṉṟu nī paṇṇiṉa upakārattukku talaicīykkumavaṉ nāṉ eṉkiṟār.
children.translated_text: I have no other refuge except Your divine feet. I am not one who would withdraw saying 'You the benefactor have neglected me.' 'Whose is my soul? Who am I?'—I am one who surrenders completely to the benefaction You have bestowed, he says.

children.text: mīṉ nōkkum nīḷ vayal cūḻ viṟṟuvakkōṭṭ’ ammā eṉ
children.translated_text: "O Lord of <s>Viṟṟuvakkōṭu</s> surrounded by long fields where fish gaze, even if You"

children.text: pāl nōkkāy ākilum uṉ paṟṟ’ allāl paṟṟ’ illēṉ
children.translated_text: "do not look upon me, I have no hold other than holding onto You!"

children.text: tāṉ nōkkāt’ e- tuyaram ceyt’ iṭiṉum tār vēntaṉ
children.translated_text: "Even if the king who does not look upon them inflicts every kind of suffering,"

children.text: kōl nōkki vāḻum kuṭi pōṉṟ’ iruntēṉē
children.translated_text: "I remained like a people who live looking to the king's scepter."

children.text: mīṉ nōkkum nīḷ vayal cūḻ
children.translated_text: "long fields where fish gaze"—

children.text: matsyam eṉṟu pēr peṟṟavai aṭaiya kaṭākṣikkum deśam-āyttu; kaṭalil matsyam, kaṭal vaṟṟiṉāl namakku pukaliṭam eṉṟu niṉaittirukkum deśam-āyttu.
children.translated_text: it is a land where everything called fish looks on with longing; it is a land where even sea-fish think 'if the sea dries up, this is our place of refuge.'

children.text: viṟṟuvakkōṭṭ’ ammā
children.translated_text: "O Lord of <s>Viṟṟuvakkōṭu</s>"—

children.text: paramapadattil uḷḷārum śīlaguṇam anubhavikkum deśam-āyttu. utkarṣam dharmiprayuktam eṉṟu pramāṇattālē nām kēṭṭ’ aṟiyumā pōlē śīlādikaḷ dharmiprayuktam eṉṟ’ irukkum ittaṉai iṟē paramapadattil; kaṇṭu anubhavikkal āvatu iṅkēyiṟē.
children.translated_text: it is a place where even those in <s>Paramapadam</s> (the supreme abode) can experience the quality of <s>śīla</s> (gracious condescension). Just as we learn from scripture (<s>pramāṇa</s>) that excellence belongs to the substance (<s>dharmi</s>), in <s>Paramapadam</s> one merely knows that <s>śīla</s> and such qualities belong to the substance; but to see and experience them directly is possible only here.

children.text: viṟṟuvakkōṭṭ’ ammā eṉ pāl nōkkāy ākilum
children.translated_text: "O Lord of <s>Viṟṟuvakkōṭu</s>, even if You do not look upon me"—

children.text: paramapadam-ākiṟatu oru nāṭāka nī nōkkukiṟa nōkkai eṉṉai oruvaṉaiyum nōkki vant’ iruntu ippōtu eṉṉai kaṭākṣiyāt’ iruntāy ākilum
children.translated_text: even if You who have been casting Your gaze upon <s>Paramapadam</s> as an entire realm, and who came to gaze upon me individually, now do not bestow Your grace upon me,

children.text: uṉ paṟṟ’ allāl paṟṟ’ illēṉ
children.translated_text: "I have no hold other than holding onto You"—

children.text: eṉṉuṭaiya rakṣaiyil udyuktaṉāṉa uṉṉai viṭṭu bādhakarāka samprati-pannar-āṉārai paṟṟuvēṉō? nityasaṃsāriyāy i- aḷavāka cūḻttukkoṇṭa eṉṉai paṟṟavō? eṉṉuṭaiya rakṣaṇattil eṉ ōpātiyum prāpti illāta piṟarai paṟṟavō?
children.translated_text: would I hold onto those who, though claiming to be engaged in my protection, have turned out to be harmful? Would I hold onto myself who, as an eternal <s>saṃsārī</s>, have become thus entangled? Would I hold onto others who have not even as much entitlement to my protection as I myself have?

children.text: tāṉ nōkkāt’ e- tuyaram ceyt’ iṭiṉum tār vēntaṉ
children.translated_text: "Even if the king who does not look upon them inflicts every kind of suffering"—

children.text: prajaikaḷuṭaiya rakṣaṇattilē dīkṣittu taṉimālai iṭṭirukkiṟa rājāvāṉavaṉ, rakṣaṇattilē nekiḻa niṟkum-aḷav’ aṉṟikkē, ellā duḥkhaṅkaḷaiyum viḷaikkilum
children.translated_text: even if the king who has taken the vow (<s>dīkṣā</s>) of protecting his subjects by wearing the garland of sovereignty, far from merely being lax in his protection, actually inflicts every kind of suffering,

children.text: tār vēntaṉ kōl nōkki vāḻum kuṭi pōṉṟ’ iruntēṉē
children.translated_text: "I remained like a people who live looking to the king's scepter"—

children.text: rakṣakaṉāy iruntuvaittu bādhakaṉ āṉālum avaṉuṭaiya ājñānuvartanam paṇṇum kuṭi pōlē iruntēṉ. ciṟiyattai periyatu tiṉṉāmal kākka tāṉ māṭṭāṉ; ceṅkaṟcīraikaṭṭi rakṣippittukkoḷḷum prāpti avaṉukk’ uṇṭu; eṉ rakṣaṇattil eṉakku anvayam illātā pōlē, sambandhamuṭaiya nīyē rakṣikkum ittaṉai. nāṉ ceyyal-āvatum illai. nī māṭṭātatum illai.
children.translated_text: even though the protector has become the persecutor, I remained like the subjects who obey his commands. He cannot protect the small from being devoured by the great by himself alone; he has the entitlement to appoint a guardian and get protection arranged. Just as I have no part in my own protection, You who have the relationship must protect—that is all. There is nothing I can do. There is nothing You cannot do.

children.text: vāḷāl aṟuttu cuṭiṉum maruttuvaṉ pāl
children.translated_text: "Even if the physician cuts with a knife and cauterizes,"

children.text: māḷāta kātal nōyāḷaṉ pōl māyattāl
children.translated_text: "like a patient with an undying love-sickness,"

children.text: mīḷā tuyar tariṉum viṟṟuvakkōṭṭ’ ammā nī
children.translated_text: "even if I bear irremediable suffering through <s>māyā</s>, O Lord of <s>Viṟṟuvakkōṭu</s>,"

children.text: āḷā uṉat’ aruḷē pārppaṉ aṭiyēṉē
children.translated_text: "this servant shall look only to Your grace for being claimed as Your own."

children.text: avatārikai - nālām pāṭṭu. oruvaṉālē hitam eṉṟum, phalattilē anvayam oru talaikkē eṉṟum adhyavasittāl, ahitaṅkaḷaiyē pravartiyā-niṉṟāṉ eṉṟu tōṟṟiṉālum avaṉai rakṣakaṉ eṉṟu kiṭakkaviṟē kaṭavatu. piḷḷai tirunaṟaiyūr araiyarai, piḷḷaikaḷ pukai cūḻntapaṭi sahikka pōkiṟat’ illai eṉṉa, caṟṟu pōt’ aṉṟō vyasana paṭuvatu, śrīvaikuṇṭhanāthaṉ tiruvaṭikaḷilē sukhamē irukka aṉṟō pukukiṟatu eṉṟāriṟē. tāṉ tañcamāka paṟṟiṉa viṣayattukku anyathāsiddhi piṟantatō eṉṟu mīḷumpaṭi irukkiṟa daśaiyilē, hetvantaram atu; a- arukil pēṟṟil kuṟai illai eṉṉum adhyavasāyam irunta paṭiyiṟē; itiṟē mahāviśvāsam ākiṟatu; tōṟṟukiṟa āpātapratītiyai kaṇṭu mīḷātē irukkumatiṟē.
vāḷāl aṟuttu cuṭiṉum
children.translated_text: Even if He cuts with a blade and burns —

children.text: hiṃsāsādhanattai koṇṭu aṟuppatu cuṭuvat’ āṉālum
children.translated_text: Even if He cuts and burns with instruments of harm,

children.text: maruttuvaṉ pāl māḷāta kātal nōyāḷaṉ pōl
children.translated_text: Like a patient with an undying love for the physician —

children.text: ahitaṅkaḷai mēl mēlaṉa pravartippikka ceytēyum bhiṣak, avaṉ namakku hitakāmaṉ eṉṟu avaṉukku taṉ sarvasvattaiyum koṭuttu avaṉ pakkalilē snehattai paṇṇum vyādhiyāḷarai pōlē
children.translated_text: Just as a sick person who, even though the doctor inflicts more and more harmful treatments, gives his entire possession to the doctor thinking 'he desires my welfare,' and maintains affection toward him,

children.text: māyattāl mīḷā tuyar tariṉum
children.translated_text: Even if He inflicts inescapable suffering through <s>māyā</s> (illusion) —

children.text: mama māyā
children.translated_text: '<s>Mama māyā</s>' (My illusion) —

children.text: eṉṉumpaṭiyē uṉṉuṭaiyatāṉa prakṛtisambandhattālē apunarāvṛttilakṣaṇamē duḥkhattai viḷaikkilum
children.translated_text: As it is said, through the connection with <s>prakṛti</s> (material nature) which is Yours, even if He produces suffering of the nature of non-return,

children.text: viṟṟuvakkōṭṭ’ ammā nī mīḷā tuyar tariṉum
children.translated_text: O Lord of <s>Viṟṟuvakkōṭṭu</s>! Even if You inflict inescapable suffering —

children.text: eṉakku tyājyamāṉa saṃsārattilē rakṣaṇattukkāka kuṭiyēṟi irukkiṟa nī nityaduḥkhattai viḷaikkilum. peṟṟa tāy prajaikku ahitam ceyyiliṟē nī ceyvatu; appaṭi irukkiṟa nī ceyyilum
children.translated_text: Even if You who have taken residence in this <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) that is to be abandoned by me, for the sake of protection, produce eternal suffering. A mother who bore the child would do harm to the child — what You do is like that; even if You who are like that do so,

children.text: āḷāy
children.translated_text: As Your servant —

children.text: svarūpānurūpamāṉa vṛttiyai peṟukaikkāka
children.translated_text: For the sake of obtaining the conduct befitting one's essential nature (<s>svarūpa</s>),

children.text: uṉat’ aruḷē pārppaṉ
children.translated_text: I shall look only to Your grace —

children.text: ippōtu tōṟṟukiṟa vyasanaṅkaḷai buddhi paṇṇātē uṉ kṛpaiyaiyē buddhi paṇṇi iruppaṉ. ippaṭi irukkaikku nibandhanam eṉ? eṉṉil -
children.translated_text: Without paying heed to the sufferings that appear now, I shall contemplate only Your compassion (<s>kṛpā</s>). What is the basis for being thus? If you ask —

children.text: aṭiyēṉē
children.translated_text: Because I am Your servant —

children.text: aṭiyēṉ-ākaiyālē. eṉ svarūpattaiyum uṉ svarūpattaiyum nērāka aṟintavaṉ-ākaiyālē.
children.translated_text: Because I am a servant. Because I am one who has correctly understood both my essential nature and Your essential nature.

children.text: asau
children.translated_text: '<s>Asau</s>' (That one) —

children.text: - aṉṟu kaṇṭā pōlē kaiyum villumāy niṟpar; avaṉukku accattālē; taṉakku uruvu veḷippāṭṭālē muṉṉē niṟpar; tīra kaḻiya aparādham ceyta eṉakku avar kṛpai paṇṇuvārō eṉṟu avaṉukku niṉaivāka koṇṭu - puruṣarṣabhaḥ - nī anukūlaṉāy ōr aṭi vara niṉṟāl attaiyē niṉaittu nī paṇṇiṉa apakāram ellām buddhi paṇṇuvārō? avar puruṣōttamaṉ kāṇ.
children.translated_text: Just as on that day, He would stand with His hand and bow; due to fear, he; due to the manifestation of His form, he would stand before Him; thinking 'will He show grace to me who has committed grievous offenses?' — <s>puruṣarṣabhaḥ</s> (O best of men) — 'if you stand having come as a well-wisher even one step, would He think about all the offenses you committed? He is <s>Puruṣōttama</s> (the Supreme Person), you see.'

children.text: muṉp’ ūḻi kāṇāṉ
children.translated_text: 'He does not look at former eons' —

children.text: - kuṟṟattai maṟakkum at’ aṉṟiyē, kuṟṟam ceyta nāḷai niṉaikkil kuṟṟam tōṟṟum eṉṟu a- nāḷaiyum maṟakkumavar kāṇ eṉṟu pirāṭṭi rāvaṇaṉukku aruḷicceytapaṭiyē iṉi nīr-allatu pukal illai eṉkiṟār.
children.translated_text: Not only does He forget offenses, but thinking that if He remembers the day the offense was committed the offense would appear again, He forgets even that day — thus <s>Pirāṭṭi</s> (Sītā) graciously told <s>Rāvaṇa</s>; accordingly he says 'henceforth there is no refuge other than You.'

Introduction — Fourth verse. If one has firmly resolved that benefit comes from one person alone, and that the fruit belongs only to one side, then even if it appears that He is causing only harm, one must remain accepting Him as the protector. When <s>Piḷḷai Tirunaṟaiyūr Araiyar</s> said to <s>Piḷḷaikaḷ</s> that it was unbearable to see the smoke surrounding them, he replied: 'The suffering is only for a short while, is it not? They are entering to dwell happily at the feet of <s>Śrīvaikuṇṭhanātha</s>.' In a situation where one might turn back thinking the object one has taken refuge in has turned out otherwise — the reasoning is different; the firm conviction that 'there is no deficiency in the attainment nearby' was present. This indeed constitutes <s>mahāviśvāsa</s> (great faith) — not turning back upon seeing the superficial appearance.

children.text: vem kaṇ tiṇ kaḷiṟ’ aṭarttāy viṟṟuvakkōṭṭ’ ammāṉē
children.translated_text: O Lord of <s>Viṟṟuvakkōṭṭu</s> who subdued the fierce-eyed, strong elephant!

children.text: eṅku pōy uykēṉ uṉ iṇai aṭiyē aṭaiyal allāl
children.translated_text: Where can I go and survive, other than taking refuge at Your twin feet?

children.text: eṅkum pōy karai kāṇāt’ eṟi kaṭalvāy mīṇṭ’ ēyum
children.translated_text: Like a great bird that, having flown everywhere without finding shore over the surging sea, returns

children.text: vaṅkattiṉ kūmp’ ēṟum mā paṟavai pōṉṟēṉē
children.translated_text: And climbs the mast of the ship — so am I.

children.text: vem kaṇ tiṇ kaḷiṟ’ aṭarttāy
children.translated_text: 'Who subdued the fierce-eyed, strong elephant' —

children.text: vevviya kaṇṇaiyum tiṇṇiya neñcaiyum uṭaittāṉa kuvalayāpīḍattai koṉṟavaṉē! prabalapratibandhakaṅkaḷ uṇṭ’ eṉṟ’ irukka vēṇumō devarīr uḷḷīrāy irukka?
children.translated_text: O You who killed <s>Kuvalayāpīḍa</s>, the elephant with fierce eyes and a strong heart! Should one think there are powerful obstacles when You are present?

children.text: viṟṟuvakkōṭṭ’
children.translated_text: 'Of <s>Viṟṟuvakkōṭṭu</s>' —

children.text: pratibandhakam pōkkiṟṟu avatārakālattilēyiṟē; atu tīrtham prasādittatiṟē eṉṟu piṟpāṭaṟku iḻakka vēṇṭātapaṭi tiru vittuvakkōṭṭilē vantu sannihitaṉ āṉavaṉē! paramapadam kalavirukkaiyāka svāmyattai nirvahikkaikkāka aṉṟō iṅku vantu eḻuntaruḷi irukkiṟatu.
children.translated_text: Removing obstacles was during the time of incarnation; that has become sacred water (<s>tīrtha</s>) — so that later generations need not suffer loss, He came and became present at <s>Tiru Viṭṭuvakkōṭṭu</s>! Is it not to fulfill His lordship (<s>svāmitva</s>) and to provide the experience of union (<s>kalavirkkai</s>) as in <s>Paramapadam</s> that He has come and graciously taken residence here?

children.text: viṟṟuvakkōṭṭ’ ammāṉē eṅku pōy uykēṉ
children.translated_text: 'O Lord of <s>Viṟṟuvakkōṭṭu</s>! Where can I go and survive?' —

children.text: prāptaṉumāy paciyaṉum-āṉavaṉ, vācalilē vantu cōṟu cōṟu eṉṉā-ṉiṟka, anyarāy nirapekṣar-āṉavarkaḷai uṇṇa aḻaippārai pōlē, uṉṉai viṭṭu parama-padattilē irukkiṟa avāptasamastakāmaṉai paṟṟavō?
children.translated_text: When one who has the right and is hungry comes to the doorstep crying 'food, food!' — like those who, being strangers and indifferent, call others to eat — shall I leave You and take refuge in the one of fulfilled desires (<s>avāptasamastakāma</s>) in <s>Paramapadam</s>?

children.text: eṅku pōy uykēṉ
children.translated_text: 'Where can I go and survive?' —

children.text: ujjīvanahetuvāka pōm iṭam illai. vināśahetuvāka pōkil pōm ittaṉaiyiṟē. ukant’ aruḷiṉa deśaṅkaḷai viṭṭu devatāntaraṅkaḷai paṟṟukai āvatu, vināśaparyāyamiṟē.
children.translated_text: There is no place to go for the sake of upliftment (<s>ujjīvana</s>). If one goes for destruction, one may go — that is all. Leaving the places He has chosen with love (<s>ukantaruḷiṉa deśaṅkaḷ</s>) and resorting to other deities is synonymous with destruction.

children.text: uṉ iṇai aṭiyē aṭaiyal allāl
children.translated_text: 'Other than taking refuge at Your twin feet' —

children.text: adhyavasāyam āvatu buddhyarthamiṟē. gatyarthāḥ buddhyarthāḥ eṉṟa nyāyattai niṉaikkiṟār. avaṉ tāṉē vantu kiṭṭa ceytē, iḻakkiṟār; iḻakkiṟatum, peṟukiṟatum apratipattiyālum pratipattiyālumiṟē.
children.translated_text: Firm conviction (<s>adhyavasāya</s>) is intellectual understanding. He reflects on the principle that 'words of motion (<s>gatyarthāḥ</s>) have the meaning of cognition (<s>buddhyarthāḥ</s>).' Even when He Himself comes near, they lose Him; and both the losing and the gaining are through non-recognition and recognition respectively.

children.text: eṟi kaṭal ityādi
children.translated_text: 'Over the surging sea' etc. —

children.text: periya kṣobhattai uṭaiya kaṭalilē oru marakkalam āvatu; atiṉ kompilē iruntat’ oru pakṣi nālu tikkilum pōkkiṭam tēṭi paṟantālum, karai kāṇa oṇṇātiṟē; mīṇṭu vantu kālpāval āvatu i- marakkalattilēyiṟē. appaṭiyē saṃsārasāgarattai kaṭakkumpōtu ukant’ aruḷiṉa deśamāṉa tiru vittuvak-kōṭṭai paṟṟi kaṭakkal ām attaṉaiallatu vēṟu upāyam illaiyiṟē kaṭakkaikku; ukant’ aruḷiṉa deśattai oḻintat’ ellām a- kaṭal pōlēyiṟē.
children.translated_text: A ship in the greatly agitated ocean; a bird that was perched on its mast, even if it flies in all four directions seeking land, cannot find the shore; returning, its foothold is only this ship. Similarly, when crossing the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>, one can cross only by holding on to <s>Tiru Viṭṭuvakkōṭṭu</s>, the place He has chosen with love; there is no other means to cross; everything other than the place He has chosen is like that ocean.

children.text: mā paṟavai
children.translated_text: 'The great bird' —

children.text: tāṉ ēṟiṭṭukkoṇṭa akalam ellām nīrilē āḻukaikku uṭalām ittaṉaiyiṟē; avaṉ kai nekiḻntāṉ eṉṟu tōṟṟa aṭimaṭṭaiyai uṟakka paṟṟum ittaṉaiyiṟē.
children.translated_text: The entire expanse it rides upon is such that it would drown in water; when it appears that He has loosened His grip, it firmly grasps the base — that is all.

children.text: cem taḻalē vant’ aḻalai ceytiṭiṉum cem kamalam
children.translated_text: Even if the red fire itself comes and scorches, the red lotus

children.text: antaram cēr vem katirōṟk’ allāl alarā āl
children.translated_text: Will not bloom except for the hot-rayed one (the sun) dwelling in the sky —

children.text: vem tuyar vīṭṭā iṭiṉum viṟṟuvakkōṭṭ’ ammā uṉ
children.translated_text: Even if You do not remove fierce suffering, O Lord of <s>Viṟṟuvakkōṭṭu</s>, for Your

children.text: antam il cīrkk’ allāl akam kuḻaiya māṭṭēṉē
children.translated_text: Boundless auspicious qualities alone — my heart will not melt for anything else!

children.text: cem taḻalē vant’ aḻalai ceyt’ iṭiṉum
children.translated_text: 'Even if the red fire itself comes and scorches' —

children.text: dāhakamāṉa agni kiṭṭi uṣṇattai paṇṇiṉālum
children.translated_text: Even if the burning fire approaches and produces heat,

children.text: cem kamalam ityādi
children.translated_text: 'The red lotus' etc. —

children.text: tāmaraiyāṉatu ādityaṉ dūrasthaṉ āṉāṉē ākilum avaṉuṭaiya kiraṇattukku alarum attaṉaiallatu agni kiṭṭiṟṟ’ eṉṟu atiṉuṭaiya uṣṇattukku alarātu.
children.translated_text: The lotus, even though the sun (<s>Āditya</s>) is distant, blooms only for his rays — it does not bloom for the heat of fire even when fire approaches.

children.text: vem tuyar vīṭṭā iṭiṉum viṟṟuvakkōṭṭ’ ammā
children.translated_text: 'Even if You do not remove fierce suffering, O Lord of <s>Viṟṟuvakkōṭṭu</s>' —

children.text: anubhavavināśyamāṉa pāpaṅkaḷai pōkki itukku vikāsattai viḷaippikka vant’ irukkiṟa nī upekṣittāyākilum
children.translated_text: Even if You, who have come to remove the sins destroyable through experience and to produce blossoming for this, show neglect,

children.text: uṉ antam il cīrkk’ allāl
children.translated_text: 'For Your boundless auspicious qualities alone' —

children.text: kalyāṇaguṇayuktaṉāṉa uṉ guṇaṅkaḷukk’ allatu
children.translated_text: Only for the qualities of You who are endowed with auspicious qualities (<s>kalyāṇaguṇa</s>),

children.text: akam kuḻaiya māṭṭēṉē
children.translated_text: 'My heart will not melt for anything else' —

children.text: eṉṉeñcu nekiḻātu.
children.translated_text: My heart will not soften for anything else.

children.text: ettaṉaiyum vāṉ maṟanta kālattum paim kūḻkaḷ
children.translated_text: Even when the sky has withheld rain for ever so long, the green shoots

children.text: maitt’ eḻunta mā mukilē pārtt’ irukkum maṟṟ’ avai pōl
children.translated_text: Keep looking only at the dark cloud that has risen with moisture — like those,

children.text: mey tuyar vīṭṭā iṭiṉum viṟṟuvakkōṭṭ’ ammā eṉ
children.translated_text: Even if You do not remove true suffering, O Lord of <s>Viṟṟuvakkōṭṭu</s>, my

children.text: citta
m
mika uṉ pālē vaippaṉ aṭiyēṉē
children.translated_text: I shall place entirely in You alone, for I am Your servant.
Mind

children.text: ettaṉaiyum vāṉ maṟanta kālattum
children.translated_text: 'Even when the sky has withheld rain for ever so long' —

children.text: kārkālattil varṣiyātē meghaṅkaḷ maṟutta kālattilum; paiṅkūḻkaḷ-uṇṭu - payirkaḷ
children.translated_text: Even when, during the rainy season, the clouds have withheld rain; the green shoots — the crops,

children.text: maitt’ eḻunta ityādi
children.translated_text: 'That has risen with moisture' etc. —

children.text: ākāśattilē kaṟutta meghaṅkaḷai pārtt’ irukkum attaṉaiallatu nīrnilam tēṭi pōka aṟiyātā pōlē
children.translated_text: Just as they keep looking at the dark clouds in the sky, not knowing to seek water-land elsewhere,

children.text: mey tuyar vīṭṭā iṭiṉum viṟṟuvakkōṭṭ’ ammā
children.translated_text: 'Even if You do not remove true suffering, O Lord of <s>Viṟṟuvakkōṭṭu</s>' —

children.text: avaśyaṃ anubhoktavyam eṉkiṟa pāpattai pōkki saṃsārasaṃbandham aṟuttu koṭukka vant’ irukkiṟa nī atu ceytilaiākilum
children.translated_text: Even if You who have come to remove the sin described as '<s>avaśyam anubhoktavyam</s>' (that which must necessarily be experienced) and to sever the bond of <s>saṃsāra</s>, do not do so,

children.text: eṉ citta
m
mika uṉ pālē vaippaṉ aṭiyēṉē
children.translated_text: 'I shall place entirely in You alone, for I am Your servant' —
'My mind' —

children.text: eṉ rakṣaṇattilē nekiḻntāy eṉṟu tōṟṟa orukālukku orukāl uṉ pakkalilē neñcu pravaṇamākā-niṉṟatu.
children.translated_text: Even when it appears that He has become lax in my protection, my heart increasingly inclines toward Him more and more.

children.text: tokk’ ilaṅku āṟ’ ellām parant’ ōṭi toṭu kaṭalē
children.translated_text: All the gleaming rivers, spreading and rushing,

children.text: pukk’ aṉṟi puṟam niṟka māṭṭāta maṟṟ’ avai pōl
children.translated_text: Cannot stand outside without entering the vast sea — like them,

children.text: mikk’ ilaṅku mukil niṟattāy viṟṟuvakkōṭṭ’ ammā uṉ
children.translated_text: O Lord of <s>Viṟṟuvakkōṭṭu</s> of brilliantly shining cloud-hue!

children.text: pukk’ ilaṅku cīr allāl pukkilaṉ kāṇ puṇṇiyaṉē
children.translated_text: I have entered nowhere but into Your radiant auspicious qualities, O holy one!

children.text: tokk’ ilaṅku āṟ’ ellām parant’ ōṭi
children.translated_text: 'All the gleaming rivers, spreading and rushing' —

children.text: jalarāśi ellām tiraṇṭu oḷiyai uṭaittāy, pārtta iṭam eṅkum parant’ ōṭi
children.translated_text: All the bodies of water, gathered and luminous, spreading and rushing everywhere one looks,

children.text: toṭu kaṭal ityādi
children.translated_text: 'The vast sea' etc. —

children.text: āḻnta kaṭalilē ceṉṟu pukk’allatu puṟampu niṟka māṭṭāta āṟukaḷ pōlē;
children.translated_text: Like rivers that cannot stand outside without entering the deep sea;

children.text: samudra iva sindhubhiḥ
children.translated_text: '<s>Samudra iva sindhubhiḥ</s>' (like the ocean with its rivers) —

children.text: eṉṉumā pōlē, ivai pukkāl kaṭal niṟaiyumatum, illai ākil kuṟaipaṭukiṟatum aṉṟiṟē; ivaṟṟukku puṟampu dharippatu aritāyiṟē pukukiṟaṉa.
children.translated_text: Just as the ocean is neither filled when they enter nor diminished if they don't — for the rivers, it is difficult to hold themselves outside, so they enter.

children.text: mikk’ ilaṅku mukil niṟattāy
children.translated_text: 'Of brilliantly shining cloud-hue' —

children.text: mikku ujjvalamāṉa kāḷamegham pōlē irukkiṟa niṟattai uṭaiyavaṉē!
children.translated_text: O You whose complexion is like a supremely radiant dark cloud (<s>kāḷamegha</s>)!

children.text: viṟṟuvakkōṭṭ’ ammā
children.translated_text: 'Lord of <s>Viṟṟuvakkōṭṭu</s>' —

children.text: a- mēgham paṭinta malai
children.translated_text: The mountain upon which that cloud has settled,

children.text: uṉ pukk’ ilaṅku cīr allāl pukk’ ilaṉ kāṇ
children.translated_text: 'I have entered nowhere but into Your radiant auspicious qualities' —

children.text: uḷpuka uḷpuka ujjvalamāṉa kalyāṇaguṇaṅkaḷilēallatu, uḷpuka uḷpuka masṛṇamāy irukkum guṇaṅkaḷilē avagāhittilēṉ kāṇ. itukku nibandhanam eṉ eṉṉil
children.translated_text: I have immersed myself only in the auspicious qualities (<s>kalyāṇaguṇa</s>) that become more and more radiant the deeper one enters, in the qualities that become more and more soft and smooth the deeper one enters — nowhere else have I immersed. If you ask what the basis for this is —

children.text: puṇṇiyaṉē
children.translated_text: 'O holy one!' —

children.text: prathamasukṛtam nīākaiyālē.
children.translated_text: Because You are the first good fortune (<s>prathamasukṛta</s>).

children.text: niṉṉaiyē tāṉ vēṇṭi nīḷ celvam vēṇṭātāṉ
children.translated_text: One who desires You alone and does not desire vast wealth —

children.text: taṉṉaiyē tāṉ vēṇṭum celvam pōl māyattāl
children.translated_text: Like the wealth that itself desires such a person —

children.text: miṉṉaiyē cēr tikiri viṟṟuvakkōṭṭ’ ammāṉē
children.translated_text: O Lord of <s>Viṟṟuvakkōṭṭu</s> with the lightning-like discus through <s>māyā</s>!

children.text: niṉṉaiyē tāṉ vēṇṭi niṟpaṉ aṭiyēṉē
children.translated_text: I shall stand desiring You alone, for I am Your servant.

children.text: niṉṉaiyē tāṉ vēṇṭi nīḷ celvam vēṇṭātāṉ taṉṉaiyē tāṉ vēṇṭum celvam pōl
children.translated_text: 'One who desires You alone and does not desire vast wealth — like the wealth that itself desires such a person' —

children.text: uṉṉaiyē vēṇṭi niravadhikasampattai kāṟkaṭai koṇṭavaṉ taṉṉaiyē avasarapratīkṣamāy pārttu niṟkum aiśvaryam pōlē eṉṉutal; mokṣalakṣmiyai pōlē eṉṉutal.
children.translated_text: Like the boundless wealth that, when one desires You alone and kicks aside limitless prosperity, waits looking for an opportunity to approach that person; or like <s>mokṣalakṣmī</s> (the goddess of liberation).

children.text: māyattāl miṉṉaiyē cēr tikiri viṟṟuvakkōṭṭ’ ammā
children.translated_text: 'Through <s>māyā</s>, the lightning-like discus, O Lord of <s>Viṟṟuvakkōṭṭu</s>' —

children.text: miṉ pōlē paḷapaḷatt’ iruntuḷḷa tiruvāḻiyai
children.translated_text: The sacred discus (<s>tiruvāḻi</s>) that gleams like lightning,

children.text: eppōtum kaikaḻalā nēmiyāṉ
children.translated_text: 'The one whose discus never leaves His hand' —

children.text: ’āy, ācilē vaitta kaiyum nīyumāy eṉṉuṭaiya rakṣaṇattukkāka iṅkē vant iruntu-vaittu kāṟkaṭai koṇṭāy-ākilum
children.translated_text: Being such, with the discus placed on Your hand, You and it together have come here for my protection — yet even if You have kicked me aside,

children.text: niṉṉaiyē tāṉ vēṇṭi niṟpaṉ aṭiyēṉē
children.translated_text: 'I shall stand desiring You alone, for I am Your servant' —

children.text: taṉṉai kāṟkaṭai koṇṭavaṉai aiśvaryam viṭātā pōlē nī eṉṉai upekṣikka upekṣikka uṉṉaiyē paṟṟā-niṉṟēṉ.
children.translated_text: Just as wealth does not abandon the one who has kicked it aside, the more You neglect me, the more I cling to You alone.

children.text: viṟṟuvakkōṭṭ’ ammā nī vēṇṭāyē āyiṭiṉum
children.translated_text: O Lord of <s>Viṟṟuvakkōṭṭu</s>! Even if You do not desire me,

children.text: maṟṟ’ ārum paṟṟ’ illēṉ eṉṟ’ avaṉai tāḷ nayanta
children.translated_text: I have no other refuge — thus, longing for His feet,

children.text: koṟṟa
m
vēl tāṉai kulacēkaraṉ coṉṉa
children.translated_text: <s>Kulacēkaraṉ</s> of the spear-bearing army spoke these —
Victorious

children.text: nal tamiḻ pattum vallār naṇṇār narakamē
children.translated_text: Those who master these ten good Tamil verses shall never approach hell.

children.text: viṟṟuvakkōṭṭ’ ammā nī vēṇṭāyē āyiṭiṉum
children.translated_text: 'O Lord of <s>Viṟṟuvakkōṭṭu</s>! Even if You do not desire me' —

children.text: itukk’ eṉṟu vant’ irukkiṟa nī eṉṉai upekṣittāy ākilum
children.translated_text: Even if You who have come for this very purpose neglect me,

children.text: maṟṟ’ ārum paṟṟ’ ilēṉ eṉṟ’ avaṉai tāḷ nayanta
children.translated_text: 'I have no other refuge — thus, longing for His feet' —

children.text: vēṟ’ oru pukal illai. nāṉ ananyagati
children.translated_text: There is no other refuge. I am one with no other recourse (<s>ananyagati</s>),

children.text: eṉṟu avaṉ tiruvaṭikaḷai ācaippaṭṭu
children.translated_text: Thus longing for His sacred feet,

children.text: koṟṟa
m
vēl tāṉai kulacēkaraṉ coṉṉa
children.translated_text: '<s>Kulacēkaraṉ</s> of the spear-bearing army spoke these' —
Victorious

children.text: pratipakṣattai pakkavērōṭē vāṅkavaṟṟāṉa veṟṟiyai uṭaiya vēlaiyum senaiyaiyum uṭaiya perumāḷ coṉṉavai; pratipakṣattai vellukaikk’ īṭāṉa parikaramuṭaiyarāṉā pōlēāyttu bhagavatprāptikku parikaramāka iva-ruṭaiya ananyagatitvam
children.translated_text: These were spoken by <s>Perumāḷ</s> who has the victorious spear capable of uprooting adversaries along with their roots, and the army; just as having the equipment to conquer adversaries — so too is his <s>ananyagatitva</s> (having no other recourse) as the equipment for attaining the Lord.

children.text: nal tamiḻ pattum vallār
children.translated_text: 'Those who master these ten good Tamil verses' —

children.text: kaṭal pēr āḻamāy irukka ceytē uḷ uḷḷa padārthaṅkaḷ tōṟṟumpaṭiyāy irukkumā pōlē artham mikku irukkum āyttu i- tirumoḻi; ivai vallavarkaḷ
children.translated_text: Just as the ocean, while being enormously deep, is such that the objects within it are visible — so too this <s>Tirumoḻi</s> (sacred verse-garland) is replete with meaning; those who master these,

children.text: naṇṇār narakamē
children.translated_text: 'Shall never approach hell' —

children.text: saṃsārasaṃbandhattukku aṭiyāṉa pāpattai paṇṇiṉārkaḷ ākilum i- saṃsārattilē vantu praveśiyārkaḷ.
children.translated_text: Even though they may have committed sins that are the root of bondage to <s>saṃsāra</s>, they shall not enter this <s>saṃsāra</s>.

children.text: avatārikai -
ukantaruḷiṉa deśattai anubhavittār kīḻ; a- anubhavam avatāraṅkaḷil anubhavāpekṣaiyai piṟappittatu; atil tōḷ tīṇṭiyatāṉa kṛṣṇā-vatārattai anubhavittavarkaḷuṭaiya pācurattālē anubhavikkiṟār
children.translated_text: Below, he experienced the place chosen with love by the Lord; that experience gave rise to the desire to experience the incarnations; among those, he experiences through the verses of those who experienced the <s>Kṛṣṇāvatāra</s> (incarnation as Kṛṣṇa), the incarnation of intimate embrace.

children.text:
i- talaiyāl vēṟu ceyyal-āvat’ illāmaiyālē, kilāykka toṭaṅkiṉār. bhagavadviṣayattil bhāvabandhattil ūṟṟam iruntapaṭi pirāṭṭimār daśaiyai prāptarāy, kūṭuvatu pirivatu ūṭuvatāmpaṭi āṉār.
	  nammāḻvārukku
children.translated_text:
Since nothing else could be done at this juncture, he began to melt. The intensity of emotional attachment (<s>bhāvabandha</s>) in matters of the Lord led him to attain the state of the consorts (<s>pirāṭṭimār</s>), becoming one who unites, separates, and quarrels in love.
	For <s>Nammāḻvār</s>,

children.text: miṉ iṭai maṭavārum,
children.translated_text: 'the women with lightning-like waists' (<s>miṉ iṭai maṭavār</s>),

children.text: tirumaṅkaiyāḻvārkku
children.translated_text: for <s>Tirumaṅkaiyāḻvār</s>,

children.text: kātil kaṭippum,
children.translated_text: 'the ear-ornament' (<s>kātil kaṭippu</s>),

children.text:
pōlē irukkiṟat’āyttu perumāḷukku i- tirumoḻi; nammāḻvār bhagavadviṣayattil niṉṟa ūṟṟam ellām tōṟṟa vaṉmai uṭaittāy irukkum miṉ iṭai maṭavār; tirumaṅkaiyāḻvār tam mārdavam ellām tōṟṟa meṉmaiyai uṭaittāy irukkum kātil kaṭippu. ivar tammuṭaiya rājakulam ellām tōṟṟa irukkum i- tirumoḻi.
	  kṛṣṇāvatāram tōḷtīṇṭiākaiyālē oru cevvāykkiḻamai muṟpaṭa peṟṟilōm, pallilē paṭṭu teṟittatu eṉṟu pañcalakṣam kuṭiyil peṇkaḷukku kṛṣṇaṉ pakkal uḷḷa viṭāy ellām tamakk’ oruvarkkum uṇṭākaiyālē tiruvāyppāṭiyil peṇkaḷ pēccāl pēcukiṟār.
children.translated_text:
similarly for <s>Perumāḷ</s> it is this <s>Tirumoḻi</s>; for <s>Nammāḻvār</s>, the 'women with lightning-like waists' has the strength that reveals all the intensity of his devotion to the Lord; for <s>Tirumaṅkaiyāḻvār</s>, the 'ear-ornament' has the tenderness that reveals all his softness. For this one, it is this <s>Tirumoḻi</s> that reveals all the glory of his royal lineage.
	Since the <s>Kṛṣṇāvatāra</s> (incarnation of Kṛṣṇa) is one of direct contact, he speaks in the voice of the women of <s>Tiruvāyppāṭi</s> (Vṛndāvana), since all the longing that the women of five hundred thousand households had toward <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — 'we did not even get a Tuesday to begin with, it bounced off the teeth' — was entirely present in him alone.
Introduction —

children.text: ēr malar pūm kuḻal āyar mātar eṉai palar uḷḷa  i- ūril uṉ taṉ
children.translated_text: O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>! Among the many cowherd women (<s>āyar mātar</s>) with beautiful flower-adorned tresses in this town,

children.text: mārvu taḻuvutaṟk’ ācai iṉmai aṟint’ aṟintē uṉ taṉ poyyai kēṭṭu
children.translated_text: knowing well that there is no possibility of embracing Your chest, yet hearing Your lies,

children.text: kūr maḻai pōl paṉi kūtal eyti kūci naṭuṅki yamuṉai āṟṟil
children.translated_text: caught in the cold that came with dew falling like sharp rain, shivering and trembling,

children.text: vār maṇal kuṉṟil pulara niṉṟēṉ vācutēvā uṉ varavu pārttē
children.translated_text: I stood on the long sandy hill by the <s>Yamunā</s> river until dawn, O <s>Vāsudeva</s>, watching for Your arrival!

children.text: avatārikai – mutal pāṭṭu. oru pirāṭṭi, yamunaiyil maṇalilē pōy nillu, nāṉ aṅkē varukiṟēṉ eṉṟu colliviṭa; avaḷ aṅkē pōy viṭiyum-aḷavum niṉṟu avaṉ vara kāṇāmaiyālē avaṉai kaṇṭapōtu ūṭi collukiṟa vārttaiyāy irukkiṟatu.
ēr malar pūm kuḻal āyar mātar
children.translated_text: 'Beautiful flower-adorned tresses, cowherd women' —

children.text: aḻakiya malarai uṭaittāy malarukkum kūṭa nāṟṟattai koṭukkum mayir muṭiyai uṭaiya iṭai peṇkaḷ
children.translated_text: The cowherd women with hair that is beautiful, flower-laden, and gives fragrance even to the flowers themselves

children.text: eṉai palar uḷḷa i- ūril
children.translated_text: 'The many who are in this town' —

children.text: anekam pēr tiraḷāṉa i- ūril - tiruvāyppāṭiyil
children.translated_text: In this town where multitudes gather — in <s>Tiruvāyppāṭi</s> (Vṛndāvana)

children.text: uṉ taṉ mārvu taḻuvutaṟk’ ācai iṉmai aṟint’ aṟintē
children.translated_text: 'Knowing well that there is no possibility of embracing Your chest' —

children.text: anekam peṇkaḷ uḷḷa ūrumāy nīyum sarvasādhāraṇaṉum āṉāl uṉ mārvai ācaippaṭa kaṭavat’ aṉṟu eṉṟu aṟintuvaittu
children.translated_text: When the town is full of many women and You are common to all, knowing that one should not desire Your chest,

children.text: uṉ taṉ poyyai kēṭṭu
children.translated_text: 'Yet hearing Your lies' —

children.text: uṉ svarūpattai uṇara oṭṭātiṟē uṉ vārttai. nī allatu pukal uṇṭō? uṉṉai allatu nāṉ aṟivēṉō? eṉṟu tāḻcci tōṉṟa nī collum vārttaiyai kēṭṭu
children.translated_text: Your words do not allow one to know Your true nature. 'Is there any refuge other than You? Do I know anyone other than You?' — hearing the words You speak so as to appear humble,

children.text: kūr maḻai pōl paṉi kūtal eyti
children.translated_text: 'Caught in the cold with dew falling like sharp rain' —

children.text: mikka maḻai pōlē peykiṟa paṉiyāl vanta kuḷirilē akappaṭṭu
children.translated_text: Caught in the cold that came from dew falling like heavy rain

children.text: kūci
children.translated_text: 'Shivering' —

children.text: ār kāṇkiṟārkaḷō eṉṟu kūci
children.translated_text: Shivering, thinking 'who might be watching?'

children.text: naṭuṅki
children.translated_text: 'Trembling' —

children.text: accattālum kuḷirālum naṭuṅki
children.translated_text: Trembling from both fear and cold

children.text: yamuṉai āṟṟil
children.translated_text: 'By the <s>Yamunā</s> river' —

children.text: atu tāṉ ekāntasthalattilēyō? sarvasādhāraṇamāṉa deśattilē aṉṟō?
children.translated_text: Was that even a secluded spot? Was it not a place common to all?

children.text: vār maṇal kuṉṟil pulara niṉṟēṉ
children.translated_text: 'I stood on the long sandy hill until dawn' —

children.text: niṉṟatu tāṉ taṉiyē niṟkalām deśattilē niṉṟēṉō? bhogattukku ekāntasthale aṉṟō? ellārum vantu sañcarittu kāṇumpōtu sarvasādhāraṇamāṉa deśattilē vantāḷ eṉṟirāmē bhogattukku ekāntamāṉa maṇal kuṉṟilē viṭiyum-aḷavum niṉṟāḷ eṉṉumpaṭi tōṟṟa niṉṟēṉ.
children.translated_text: Did I stand in a place where one could stand alone? Was it not a spot meant for romantic enjoyment? Rather than people saying 'she came to a public place where everyone walks about,' I stood in such a way that it would appear I was standing until dawn on the sandy hill meant for enjoyment.

children.text: vācutēvā
children.translated_text: '<s>Vāsudeva</s>!' —

children.text: nī iṅku niṟkiṟat’ eṉ? eṉṉil - uṉṉai viśvasitt’ aṉṟu; uṉ pitāvai viśvasittu; oru vārttai allatu aṟiyāta śrīvasudevar piḷḷai eṉṉumattai viśvasittu niṉṟēṉ.
children.translated_text: If You ask 'why are you standing here?' — it was not trusting You; it was trusting Your father; I stood trusting that You are the son of <s>Śrī Vasudeva</s> who knows nothing but truthful words.

children.text: uṉ varavu pārttē
children.translated_text: 'Watching for Your arrival' —

children.text: uṉṉuṭaiya aḻaku kāṇa vēṇum eṉṉum nacaiyālē.
children.translated_text: Out of longing to see Your beauty.

Introduction to the first verse: A consort (<s>pirāṭṭi</s>) — <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> told her 'Go and stand in the sands by the <s>Yamunā</s>, I will come there.' She went there and stood until dawn, and not seeing Him come, these are the words of reproach she speaks when she finally sees Him.

children.text: keṇṭai oḷ kaṇ maṭavāḷ orutti kīḻai akattu tayir kaṭaiya
children.translated_text: Seeing a young woman with bright eyes like the <s>keṇṭai</s> fish churning curds in the eastern house,

children.text: viḻiyai viḻittu pukku
children.translated_text: He cast His deceitful eyes and entered
'I too will churn quickly!' — saying this, with thieving

children.text: vaṇṭ’ amar pūm kuḻal tāḻnt’ ulāva vāḷ mukam vērppa ce
