While His bee-frequented flower-adorned tresses hung swaying, His bright face perspiring, His red

children.text: taṇ tayir nī kaṭaint’ iṭṭa vaṇṇam tāmōtarā mey aṟivaṉ nāṉē
children.translated_text: the manner in which You churned the cool curds — O <s>Dāmodara</s>, I know the truth of it!

children.text: avatārikai - iraṇṭām pāṭṭu. vēṟ’ oru pirāṭṭi vārttai.
keṇṭai oḷ kaṇ maṭavāḷ orutti
children.translated_text: 'A young woman with bright eyes like the <s>keṇṭai</s> fish' —

children.text: mugdhamāṉa nōkkai uṭaiyavaḷāy, colliṟṟ’ ellām mey eṉṟirukkum paruvattai uṭaiyāḷ orutti
children.translated_text: One with an innocent gaze, of an age where she would believe everything said to be true

children.text: kīḻai akattu
children.translated_text: 'In the eastern house' —

children.text: bhāvanāprakarṣattālē tiruvāyppāṭiyil oru akamum uṇṭāy atukku kīḻai akamumāy cellukiṟatu kāṇum ivarkku. nī tāṉ mūlaiyaṭiyē naṭantatu vēṟ’ ōr iṭattēyō? eṉ akattukku kīḻai akattē aṉṟō?
children.translated_text: Due to the intensity of his imagination (<s>bhāvanāprakarṣa</s>), it seems to him that there is a house in <s>Tiruvāyppāṭi</s> and an eastern house next to it. 'Was it some other place You walked to stealthily? Was it not the eastern house next to my own house?'

children.text: tayir kaṭaiya kaṇṭu
children.translated_text: 'Seeing her churning curds' —

children.text: ūr eṅkum aṭiyoṟṟi tiriyumiṟē, taṉiyē niṉṟu tayir kaṭaivār uṇṭō? eṉṟu, orutti taṉiyē niṉṟu tayir kaṭaiya kaṇṭavāṟē alabhyalābham peṟṟāṉāy ōṭi ceṉṟu pukkāṉ.
children.translated_text: He would go about stamping His feet all over the town; is there anyone who churns curds standing alone? So, the moment He saw one woman standing alone churning curds, as if having obtained the unobtainable, He ran and entered.

children.text: ollai nāṉum kaṭaivaṉ eṉṟu
children.translated_text: 'I too will churn quickly, saying thus' —

children.text: nī taṉiyē niṉṟu tayir kaṭaiyil orukālum veṇṇey paṭṭatāka māṭṭātu, caṭakk eṉa veṇṇey paṭuvatu nāṉum orutalai paṟṟi kaṭaiyil-āyttu’ eṉṟu.
children.translated_text: 'If you stand alone churning curds, butter will never form; butter forms quickly only when I too grab one end and churn' — thus He said.

children.text: aṉṟu tēvar acurar vāṅka
children.translated_text: 'That day when the <s>Devas</s> and <s>Asuras</s> churned' —

children.text: eṉṟu piṟar kaiviṭṭāl kaṭaivatu piṟar kāryam ākiliṟē; iṅku ivaḷum orutalai paṟṟiliṟē taṉ prayojanam āvatu
children.translated_text: When others let go, the churning was for others' benefit; here, since she too held one end, it became His own gain.

children.text: kaḷḷa
m
children.translated_text: glances

children.text: viḻiyai viḻittu pukku
children.translated_text: 'He cast His deceitful eyes and entered' —
With thieving

children.text: ivaṉ kaḷḷaviḻi; avaḷ keṇṭai oḷ kaṇ maṭavāḷ. nōkkum niṉaivum ceyalum collum orupaṭi paṭṭ’ irukkum avaḷukku; ivaṉukku nōkk’ orupaṭiyum niṉaiv’ orupaṭiyum col orupaṭiyum ceyal vēṟ’ orupaṭiyumāy irukkum. ivaṉ nōkkālē ellām mey eṉṟu avaḷ viśvasittāḷ-āyttu.
children.translated_text: His eyes are thieving; her eyes are bright and innocent like the <s>keṇṭai</s> fish. For her, gaze, thought, action, and speech all accord; for Him, gaze is one way, thought another, speech another, and action yet another. She trusted Him entirely because of His gaze.

children.text: vaṇṭ’ amar ityādi
children.translated_text: 'Bees frequenting' etc. —

children.text: mēl paṇṇiṉa vyāpāraṅkaḷ oru mahābhāratamiṟē
children.translated_text: The activities that followed were a whole <s>Mahābhārata</s> (epic saga)!

children.text: vaṇṭ’ amar pūm kuḻal tāḻnt’ ulāva
children.translated_text: 'While His bee-frequented flower-adorned tresses hung swaying' —

children.text: uṉ kuḻalai viśvasitta vaṇṭukaḷ eṉ paṭṭaṉavō?
children.translated_text: What happened to the bees that trusted Your tresses?

children.text: vāḷ mukam vērppa
children.translated_text: 'His bright face perspiring' —

children.text: tāmaraiyilē muttu paṭintā pōlē oḷiyai uṭaiya mukam vērppa
children.translated_text: Like pearls set upon a lotus — His radiant face perspiring

children.text: ce
m
children.translated_text: beau-

children.text: vāy tuṭippa
children.translated_text: 'tiful lips quivering' —
His red

children.text: adharasphuraṇam piṟakka; ivai ellām puṇarcci kuṟiyiṟē. tamiḻar cuṉai āṭal eṉṟu oru kalaviyai collumā pōlē.
children.translated_text: The quivering of the lips (<s>adharasphuraṇa</s>) arose — all these are signs of union. Just as Tamil poets speak of a type of lovemaking called 'bathing in the spring' (<s>cuṉai āṭal</s>).

children.text: taṇ tayir nī kaṭaint’ iṭṭa vaṇṇam
children.translated_text: 'The manner in which You churned the cool curds' —

children.text: uṉ neñcukku poruntiṉa tayir kaṭainta paṭi; ivaḷ coṉṉavāṟē iṅṅaṉē iruppaṉa cila eṉakk’ uṇṭō eṉṉa
children.translated_text: The manner in which You churned the curds that pleased Your heart — when she spoke thus, He wondered 'do I really have such things?'

children.text: tāmōtarā mey aṟivaṉ nāṉē
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Dāmodara</s>! I know the truth!' —

children.text: uṉ uṭampil taḻumpai maṟaikkalām ākil aṉṟō uṉ ceyalkaḷai maṟaikkal āvatu!
children.translated_text: If only You could hide the marks on Your body, then You could hide Your deeds!
Introduction to the second verse: The words of another consort (<s>pirāṭṭi</s>).

children.text: karu
m
children.translated_text: flower-adorned tresses —

children.text: malar kūntal orutti taṉṉai kaṭaikkaṇitt’ āṅkē orutti taṉ pāl
children.translated_text: casting a sidelong glance at one woman, immediately placing His heart upon another,
A woman with dark

children.text: maruvi maṉam vaittu maṟṟ’ oruttikk’ uraitt’ oru pētaikku poy kuṟittu
children.translated_text: declaring love to yet another, making a false assignation with an innocent girl,

children.text: puri kuḻal maṅkai orutti taṉṉai puṇarti avaḷukkum meyyaṉ allai
children.translated_text: uniting with another maiden of curly tresses — even to her You are not true!

children.text: marut’ iṟuttāy uṉ vaḷartti ūṭē vaḷarkiṉṟatāl uṉ taṉ māyai tāṉē
children.translated_text: O You who broke the <s>Marut</s> (Arjuna) trees! Your deceit grows alongside Your growing up!

children.text: avatārikai - mūṉṟām pāṭṭu. vēṟ’ orutti vārttai.
karu
m
children.translated_text: flower-adorned —

children.text: malar kūntal orutti taṉṉai kaṭaikaṇittu
children.translated_text: 'tresses, casting a sidelong glance at her' —
A woman with dark

children.text: neyttu iruṇṭu pūvai uṭaittāy irukkiṟa mayirmuṭiyai uṭaiyāḷ oruttiyai, tāṉ mayir muṭiyilē tōṟṟamai tōṟṟa ciṟāṅkaṇittu pārttu; nērē pārttāṉ ākiliṟē potu nōkku eṉṟu irukkal-āvatu
children.translated_text: Looking with a sidelong glance that appears as though He appeared in her very hair — at a woman with hair that is dark, dense, and flower-like; had He looked straight, one could dismiss it as a common glance,

children.text: āṅkē orutti taṉ pāl maruvi maṉam vaittu
children.translated_text: 'Immediately placing His heart upon another' —

children.text: ivaḷ pakkalilē kaṇ cellā-niṟka vēṟ’ orutti pakkalilē avaḷai allatu aṟiyēṉ eṉṉumpaṭi manassai aṅkē vaittu
children.translated_text: While His eyes go toward this one, He places His mind upon another woman in such a way that He appears to know none but her

children.text: maṟṟ’ oruttik’ uraittu
children.translated_text: 'Declaring love to yet another' —

children.text: manassu avaḷ pakkalilē irukka ceytē, vēṟē oruttikku aṭiyēṉ eṉṟu colli
children.translated_text: While His mind is with that one, He says 'I am Your servant' to yet another

children.text: oru pētaikku poy kuṟittu
children.translated_text: 'Making a false assignation with an innocent girl' —

children.text: coṉṉa vārttaiyai viśvasittu akavāy aṟiyātāḷ oru mugdhaikku iṉṉa iṭattilē pōy nillu, nāṉ aṅkē varukiṟēṉ eṉṟu iṭam kuṟittu
children.translated_text: To an innocent girl (<s>mugdhai</s>) who believes whatever is said and knows nothing of the inner reality — He assigned a place saying 'go and stand there, I will come'

children.text: puri kuḻal maṅkai orutti taṉṉai puṇarti
children.translated_text: 'Uniting with a maiden of curly tresses' —

children.text: mayirmuṭi alaitikulaitiyāy pēṇātē bhogayogyaiyāy iruppāḷ oruttiyōṭē saṃśleṣittu
children.translated_text: He embraced yet another woman whose disheveled, untended hair showed her readiness for enjoyment

children.text: avaḷukkum meyyaṉ allai
children.translated_text: 'Even to her You are not true!' —

children.text: atuvum mithyāparirambhaṇam - atāvatu poyyē taḻuvukai
children.translated_text: Even that was a false embrace (<s>mithyāparirambhaṇa</s>) — that is, embracing falsely

children.text: marut’ iṟuttāy
children.translated_text: 'O You who broke the <s>Marut</s> trees!' —

children.text: paruvam nirampuvataṟku muṉṉē tīṇṭiṉārai kolla pukkāy.
children.translated_text: Even before reaching maturity, You set about killing those who touched You.

children.text: uṉ vaḷartti ityādi
children.translated_text: 'Your growing up' etc. —

children.text: uṉṉuṭaiya vañcanamum, nī prāyam puka, okka prāyam pukā-niṉṟatiṟē.
children.translated_text: Your deceit too, as You come of age, comes of age alongside.
Introduction to the third verse: The words of yet another woman.

children.text: tāy mulai pālil amut’ irukka tavaḻntu taḷar naṭai iṭṭu ceṉṟu
children.translated_text: While nectar existed in the mother's breast milk, You crawled and toddled and went

children.text: pēy mulai vāy vaittu nañcai uṇṭu pittaṉ eṉṟē piṟar ēca niṉṟāy
children.translated_text: and placed Your mouth on the demoness's breast and drank poison — 'He is mad!' so others mocked, and You stood!

children.text: āy miku kātalōṭ
u
yāṉ iruppa yāṉ viṭa vanta eṉ tūtiyōṭē
children.translated_text: with the messenger-girl I had sent whom I then dismissed —
While I was here with great love, exceedingly

children.text: nī miku pōkattai naṉk’ ukantāy atuvum uṉ kōrampukk’ ēṟkum aṉṟē
children.translated_text: You greatly enjoyed lovemaking with her! And that indeed befits Your mischief!

children.text: avatārikai - nālām pāṭṭu. ukant’ aruḷiṉa deśattai anubhavittār kīḻ; a- anubhavam avatāraṅkaḷai anubhavikka vēṇum eṉṉum apekṣai piṟantu atil tōḷtīṇṭiyatāṉa kṛṣṇāvatārattai anubhavittavarkaḷ pācurattālē anubhavikkiṟār.
tāy mulai pālil amut’ irukka
children.translated_text: 'While nectar existed in the mother's breast milk' —

children.text: uṉṉai peṟukaikku nōṉpu nōṟṟu pattu māsam cumantu nī mulai uṇṇil dharittum, mulai uṇṇāviṭil neṟittum āṟṟāḷāy irukkiṟavaḷuṭaiya, uṉakku dhārakamāy irunta mulaippāl irukka
children.translated_text: While the breast milk that sustained You — of her who performed austerities to obtain You, carried You for ten months, who would sustain herself only if You nursed and would wither if You did not — still existed,

children.text: tavaḻntu taḷar naṭai iṭṭu ceṉṟu
children.translated_text: 'Crawling and toddling, He went' —

children.text: tavaḻntu naṭakka pukku māṭṭātē taḷḷāmpāṟi ceṉṟu
children.translated_text: Crawling, beginning to walk but unable, tottering along

children.text: pēy mulai vāy vaittu nañcai uṇṭu
children.translated_text: 'Placed His mouth on the demoness's breast and drank poison' —

children.text: uṉ pakkal bhāvabandham illāta pūtanaiyuṭaiya mulaiyilē vāyvaittu, vināśattai viḷaippatāṉa nañcai uṇṭu
children.translated_text: Placing His mouth on the breast of <s>Pūtanā</s> who had no emotional bond with Him, and drinking the poison that would cause destruction

children.text: pittaṉ eṉṟē piṟar ēca niṉṟāy
children.translated_text: 'He is mad!' — so others mocked, and He stood' —

children.text: rāgadveṣaṅkaḷukku viṣayavibhāgam paṇṇa māṭṭāta aṭaivukēṭaṉ eṉṟu nāṭṭār ēcumpaṭi niṉṟāy. nāṉ ippōtu viḻukkāṭ’ aṟiyātē ceytat’ eṉ? eṉṉa -
children.translated_text: You stood while the villagers mocked You as one without discrimination who cannot distinguish between objects of love and hatred. 'What have I done now without knowing the proper proportion?' — to this she says:

children.text: āy miku kātalōṭu yāṉ iruppa yāṉ viṭa vanta eṉ tūtiyōṭē
children.translated_text: 'While I was here with exceedingly great love — with the messenger-girl I had sent' —

children.text: eṉ dūtavākhyam koṇṭu vantavaḷōṭē
children.translated_text: With the very one who came bearing my message as an envoy

children.text: nī miku pōkattai naṉk’ ukantāy
children.translated_text: 'You greatly enjoyed lovemaking with her' —

children.text: āy - āyampoṉ.  uṉṉai ācaippaṭṭu vaivarṇyattai uṭaiya nāṉ irukka. āy eṉṟu kaṭaikkuṟaittalāy kiṭakkiṟatu. eṉṉōṭu parimāṟum parimāṟṟattukku a- varukē eṉ niṉaivum uṉ niṉaivum koṇṭu parimāra niṉaittālum, avaḷukku a- niṉaivu illāmaiyālē māntumavaḷiṟē avaḷ.
children.translated_text: '<s>Āy</s>' means gold. While I, who desired You, sat with pallor; '<s>āy</s>' also means to diminish. Even if in the manner of Your dealings with me You thought to deal with her sharing both my intent and Your intent, since she lacks that same intent, she is one who would merely submit.

children.text: atuvum uṉ kōrampukk’ ēṟkum aṉṟē
children.translated_text: 'And that indeed befits Your mischief!' —

children.text: kōramp’ āvatu tīmpu. atāvatu - uṉ tīmpukku ēṟkum ittaṉaiyiṟē eṉkai.
children.translated_text: '<s>Kōrampu</s>' means mischief (<s>tīmpu</s>). That is — this much indeed befits Your mischief, she says.

Introduction to the fourth verse: Below he experienced the chosen land (<s>deśa</s>); that experience gave rise to the desire to experience the incarnations, and among them he experiences the <s>Kṛṣṇāvatāra</s> — the incarnation of direct contact — through the words of those who experienced it.

children.text: miṉ otta nuṇ iṭaiyāḷai koṇṭu vīṅk’ iruḷvāy eṉ taṉ vīti ūṭē
children.translated_text: Taking a woman with a waist slender as lightning, through the dense darkness, through my very street,

children.text: poṉ otta āṭai kukkūṭal iṭṭu pōkiṉṟa pōtu nāṉ kaṇṭu niṉṟēṉ
children.translated_text: wearing a garment golden in hue, rustling as You went — at that moment I stood watching!

children.text: kaṇṇuṟṟavaḷai nī kaṇṇāl iṭṭu kai viḷikkiṉṟatum kaṇṭē niṉṟēṉ
children.translated_text: And I stood watching as You cast Your eyes upon the woman who caught Your eye and beckoned with Your hand!

children.text: eṉṉukk’ avaḷai viṭṭ’ iṅku vantāy iṉṉam aṅkē naṭa nampi nīyē
children.translated_text: Leave her and come to me here? No — go back there, O <s>Nampi</s> (Lord)!

children.text: miṉ otta nuṇ iṭaiyāḷai koṇṭu
children.translated_text: 'Taking a woman with a waist slender as lightning' —

children.text: miṉ pōlē nuṇṇiya iṭaiyai uṭaiyāḷ oruttiyai a- iṭai nuṭaṅkātapaṭi aṇaittukkoṇṭu
children.translated_text: Embracing tightly — so that her lightning-like slender waist would not sway — one woman,

children.text: vīṅk’ iruḷvāy
children.translated_text: 'Through the dense darkness' —

children.text: uṉṉuṭaiya muṉ aṭi tōṟṟātē pōkaikk’ īṭāṉa mikka iruḷum uṇṭāyttiṟē
children.translated_text: There was indeed great darkness, sufficient to conceal Your footsteps so they would not be seen

children.text: eṉ taṉ vīti ūṭē
children.translated_text: 'Through my very street' —

children.text: koṇṭu pōkiṉṟatu tāṉ vēṟ’ oru teruvē aṉṟē koṇṭu pōvatu. itu ār teru eṉṟ’ iruntāy? it’ eṉṉa añcāmai tāṉ!
children.translated_text: Is it some other street through which You take her? Whose street did You think this was? What audacity!

children.text: poṉ otta āṭai kukkūṭal iṭṭu
children.translated_text: 'Wearing a garment golden in hue, rustling' —

children.text: maṟaittukkoṇṭu pōkiṟatu tāṉ iruḷukku prakāśattai iṭṭ’ aṉṟō; pōkiṟatu pōkiṟāy, tāṉ iṉṉāḷai koṇṭu pōkā-niṉṟōm; iṉṉāḷ teruvē pōkā-niṉṟōm; iṉṉa kālattilē pōkā-niṉṟōm eṉṉum tuṇukkum iṉṟiyilē aṉṟō pōyiṟṟu.
children.translated_text: While going concealed, it was the radiance against the darkness that gave You away! Going as You went — without the slightest awareness of 'I am taking such a woman, I am going through such a street, I am going at such a time' — that is how You went.

children.text: pōkiṉṟa pōtu nāṉ kaṇṭu niṉṟēṉ
children.translated_text: 'At that moment I stood watching!' —

children.text: uṉṉai pōlē anyaparai aṉṟē nāṉ; nī pōṉa iṭam eṅkum aṭiyoṟṟumavaḷ-ākaiyālē kaṇṭu niṉṟēṉ.
children.translated_text: Unlike You, I am not one who is occupied elsewhere; since I am one who follows wherever You go, I stood watching.

children.text: kaṇṇuṟṟavaḷai
children.translated_text: 'The woman who caught Your eye' —

children.text: ivaḷai aṇaittukkoṇṭu pōkā-niṟka ceytē vēṟ’orutti kaṇṇukku ilakk’ āṉāḷ.
children.translated_text: Even as He was going along embracing her, another woman caught His eye.

children.text: nī kaṇṇāl iṭṭu
children.translated_text: You cast Your gaze —

children.text: kaṇṇālē ananyārhai āmpaṭi nōkkiṉāy.
children.translated_text: You looked at her with Your eyes in a way that made her exclusively Yours.

children.text: kai viḷikkiṉṟatum kaṇṭē niṉṟēṉ
children.translated_text: I stood there watching You beckon her with Your hand —

children.text: ivaḷai oru kaiyālē aṇaittu maṟṟai kaiyālē etirppaṭṭavaḷai iṉṉa iṭattē vā eṉṟu aḻaittukkoṇṭu pōkiṟapaṭiyaiyum pārttukkoṇṭu niṉṟēṉ.
children.translated_text: I stood watching as He embraced her with one hand and with the other beckoned the woman He encountered, saying 'Come to such and such a place.'

children.text: eṉṉukk’ avaḷai viṭṭ’ iṅku vantāy
children.translated_text: Why did You leave her and come here to me? —

children.text: appāvi uṉṉai aṟiyātavaḷ-ākaiyālē mey eṉṟ’ irukkiṟavaḷ veṟukkumpaṭi avaḷai viṭṭu iṅku eṉ ceyya vantāy? aṅṅaṉē cila uṇṭō eṉakku ananyagati aṉṟō? eṉṟu avaṉ colla
children.translated_text: That innocent one who, not knowing Your ways, believes You to be true — You have come here leaving her in a state that would make her despise You. Why have You come here? 'Are there such things? Are You not my only refuge?' — when He said this,

children.text: iṉṉam aṅkē naṭa nampi nīyē
children.translated_text: Go back there, <s>Nampi</s>! —

children.text: kuṟaivāḷarai pōlē cila vārttai colla kaṭavīrō? nīr pūrṇar allīrō? aṅkē naṭavīr.
children.translated_text: Would You speak words as if You were deficient? Are You not the complete one? Go there.

children.text: mal poru tōḷ uṭai vācutēvā val viṉaiyēṉ tuyil koṇṭavāṟē
children.translated_text: O <s>Vāsudēva</s> with wrestling-hardened shoulders! I, the one of grievous <s>karma</s>, was put to sleep thus —

children.text: iṟṟai irav’ iṭai ēmatt’ eṉṉai iṉ aṇai mēl iṭṭ’ akaṉṟu nī pōy
children.translated_text: In the middle of this night, at the dead of night, having placed me on the sweet bed, You departed,

children.text: aṟṟai iravum ōr piṟṟai nāḷum arivaiyarōṭumaṇaintu vantāy
children.translated_text: and that night and the next day You spent in the embrace of knowing women and returned —

children.text: eṟṟukku nī eṉ maruṅkil vantāy emperumāṉ nī eḻunt’ aruḷē
children.translated_text: Why have You come to my side? My Lord, please leave!

children.text: mal poru tōḷ uṭai vācutēvā
children.translated_text: O <s>Vāsudēva</s> with wrestling-hardened shoulders —

children.text: uṉ ceyalkaḷ nī mūlaiyaṭi naṭantāy eṉṉa oṇṇātapaṭi nivārakar illāta piṟappu
children.translated_text: Your deeds are such that one cannot say You sneaked around corners — a birth where there are no restrainers,

children.text: val viṉaiyēṉ tuyil koṇṭavāṟē
children.translated_text: I, the one of grievous <s>karma</s>, was put to sleep thus —

children.text: appōtu uṟaṅkāt’ irukka-peṟṟilēṉ uṉ mikai ceyalkaḷ ellām kāṇumpaṭi; nidraiyum eṉṉai pakai mīḷumpaṭi pāpattai paṇṇiṉēṉ.
children.translated_text: I failed to stay awake at that time so as to witness all Your excessive deeds; the sleep too — I committed the sin that turned even sleep into my enemy.

children.text: iṟṟai irav’ iṭai ēmatt’ eṉṉai
children.translated_text: In the middle of this night, at the dead of night, me —

children.text: aṟṟai iravil naṭuccāmattilē bhogayogyamāṉa kālattilē aṉṟō eṉṉai viṭṭu pōyttu.
children.translated_text: It was at midnight of that night, at the time suited for enjoyment, that He left me and went.

children.text: iṉ aṇai mēl iṭṭ’ akaṉṟu nī pōy
children.translated_text: Having placed me on the sweet bed, You departed —

children.text: bhogayogyamāṉa kālattilē, paṭukkai vāyppālē ivaḷ uṟaṅkum; uṟaṅkiṉavāṟē pōvōm eṉṟu, akaṉṟu nī pōy
children.translated_text: At the time suited for enjoyment, she would sleep due to the comfort of the bed; the moment she fell asleep, thinking 'let us go,' He departed,

children.text: aṟṟai iravum ōr piṟṟai
children.translated_text: that night and the next day —

children.text: iṅku-niṉṟu niṉaittu pōṉā pōlē ceyya oṇṇātiṟē aṅku; akaṉṟa aṉṟ’ iravum piṟṟai nāḷum
children.translated_text: Having left here, one cannot pretend there as one pretends here; that night of departure and the next day,

children.text: arivaiyarōṭum aṇaintu vantāy
children.translated_text: You spent in the embrace of knowing women and returned —

children.text: pañcalakṣam kuṭiyil peṇkaḷ ellārōṭum saṃśleṣittu vantāy. arivaiyarōṭum aṇaintu vantāy eṉṟavāṟē ivaḷai āṟṟumpōtu aṇaittu āṟṟa vēṇum eṉṟu avaṉ kiṭṭa puka
children.translated_text: You united with all the women of the five hundred thousand households and returned. The moment she said 'You embraced knowing women and returned,' He approached her thinking 'she must be consoled by an embrace,' and

children.text: eṟṟukku nī eṉ maruṅkil vantāy
children.translated_text: Why have You come to my side? —

children.text: ārai tīṇṭi vantāy eṉṟu teriyātu; eṉṉai tīṇṭātē nī kaṭakka nillu
children.translated_text: Who knows whom You have touched and come? Do not touch me — stand at a distance!

children.text: emperumāṉ nī eḻunt’ aruḷē
children.translated_text: My Lord, please leave! —

children.text: pūrvavāsanaiyālē vantāy eṉṟa iṭam tappa coṉṉēṉ; attai poṟuttu, nīr mutalikaḷ aṉṟō? nīr eḻuntaruḷum.
children.translated_text: I spoke wrongly when I said You came out of old habit; forgiving that — are You not the master? Please depart.

children.text: pai araviṉ aṇai paḷḷiyiṉāy paṇṭaiyōm allōm nām nī ukakkum
children.translated_text: O You who recline on the serpent-couch — we are not the same as before; we whom You desire,

children.text: mai ari oḷ kaṇṇiṉārum allōm vaiki em cēri varav’ oḻi nī
children.translated_text: we are not those with bright collyrium-lined eyes either — stop coming to our street at nightfall!

children.text: ceyya uṭaiyum tiru mukamum cem kaṉi vāyum kuḻalum kaṇṭu
children.translated_text: Having seen Your red garment, Your divine face, Your red fruit-like lips, and Your curls,

children.text: poy oru nāḷ paṭṭatē amaiyum puḷḷuvam pēcātē pōku nampī
children.translated_text: the deception we fell for one day is enough — do not speak falsehoods, go, <s>Nampi</s>!

children.text: pai araviṉ aṇai paḷḷiyiṉāy
children.translated_text: O You who recline on the serpent-couch —

children.text: nī eṉakku nallai allai ākilum nāṉ uṉakku nallēṉ. ācaippaṭṭārkku uṭampu koṭukkumavaṉ, etirttalaiyiṉ uṭaiya rakṣaṇacintai paṇṇumavaṉ nāṉ eṉṟu avaṉ colla, pai araviṉ aṇai paḷḷiyiṉāy eṉkiṟāḷ.
children.translated_text: Even if You are not good to me, I am good to You. 'I am one who gives His body to those who desire, one who thinks of the protection of the other' — when He said this, she says 'O You who recline on the hooded serpent-couch.'

children.text: paṇṭaiyōm allōm nām
children.translated_text: We are not the same as before —

children.text: akappaṭuttukaikkāka nī muṉpu ceyyum ceyalkaḷ aṟintavarkaḷ-ākaiyālē paḻaiyavarkaḷ allōm kāṇ nāṅkaḷ.
children.translated_text: Since we have come to know the things You used to do in the past to entrap us, we are not the naive ones of before, know this.

children.text: nāk’ aṇai-micai nampirāṉ caraṇē caraṇ namakku
children.translated_text: "The feet of our Lord who reclines on the serpent-couch are our sole refuge" —

children.text: eṉṟ’ irukkum nilai tavirntōm kāṇ nāṅkaḷ; tañcamāka niṉaitt’ irukkum atilēyum atiśaṅkai paṇṇumpaṭi avagāhittār kāṇum ivar. nīṅkaḷ paṇṭaiyavarkaḷ aṉṟākilum nāṉ tāṉ paḻaiyavaṉ-ākaiyālē ukappēṉ uṅkaḷai eṉṟu avaṉ colla
children.translated_text: know that we have departed from that state of trust; even in the matter of considering Him as our refuge, these women have plunged into such excessive doubt. 'Even if you are not the same as before, since I am the same old one, I will cherish you' — when He said this,

children.text: nī ukakkum mai ari oḷ kaṇṇiṉārum allōm
children.translated_text: We are not those with bright collyrium-lined eyes whom You desire —

children.text: nī ippōtu ukakkiṟavarkaḷum allōm kāṇ nāṅkaḷ. muṉṉaṭi tōṟṟātē uṉṉai mūlaiyaṭiyē naṭakka paṇṇukiṟa avayavaśobhai uṭaiyavarkaḷ allōm kāṇ nāṅkaḷ. āṉāl eṉṉai ceyya collukiṟat’ eṉ? eṉṉa,
children.translated_text: We are not the ones You currently desire either, know this. We are not those possessing such beauty of limbs that makes You unable to see what lies ahead and makes You walk blindly. 'Then what would you have me do?' —

children.text: em cēri varav’ oḻi nī
children.translated_text: Stop coming to our street! —

children.text: eṅkaḷuṭaiya iruppiṭaṅkaḷ eṅkaḷukkē ājñai celluvatu; eṅkaḷ iruppiṭattil vārātē koḷ. ellārum parimāṟukiṟa uṅkaḷ iṭattil nāṉ vārāt’ oḻikiṟat eṉ? eṉṉa -
children.translated_text: Our dwellings are under our own authority; do not come to our dwelling place. 'When I am not coming to your place where everyone else comes and goes, what is the reason?' —

children.text: em cēri varav’ oḻi nī
children.translated_text: Stop coming to our street! —

children.text: ellārum varum pōtil vara vēṇṭā eṉkiṟōm aṉṟu; āḷ aṟṟa pōtāka pōkā-niṉṟāṉ; ivaṉukku oru niṉaiv’ uṇṭu eṉṟu śaṅkikkumpōtu vara vēṇṭā eṉkiṟōm attaṉaiallatu, sarvasādhāraṇamāṉa pōtu vara vēṇṭā eṉṟilōmē eṉṉa; ivarkaḷ vara vēṇṭā eṉṉātapaṭi āciyilē kaivaittāṉ; ivarkaḷ vārttaiyilē tāṉ ceyalaṟṟapaṭiyālē ivarkaḷ vāy māḷumpaṭi brahmāstraprayogam paṇṇa pārttāṉ.
children.translated_text: We are not saying 'do not come' when everyone comes; he comes at times when people are absent; when there is suspicion that 'this one has some intention,' we say 'do not come' — that is all, we did not say 'do not come' at the common time when all come. When they did not say 'do not come,' He placed His hand on the threshold; since He was powerless before their words, He looked to deploy the <s>brahmāstra</s> (supreme weapon) to silence them.

children.text: ceyya uṭaiyum tiru mukamum cem kaṉi vāyum kuḻalum kaṇṭu
children.translated_text: Having seen Your red garment, Your divine face, Your red fruit-like lips, and Your curls —

children.text: tiru pariyaṭṭattai pēṇuvatu, ivarkaḷ mukaṅkaḷilē mukattai kāṭṭuvatu, smitam paṇṇuvatu, tiru kuḻalai pēṇuvatāṉāṉ: ippaṭi ceytavāṟē iṟāyttāḷ. atāvatu - kaṇṇai cempaḷittāḷ. kaṇpaṭaitta lābham kāṇātē kaṇṇai cempaḷikkiṟat’ eṉ eṉṟu colla kaṇṭu
children.translated_text: He adjusted His sacred garment, showed His face to their faces, smiled, and arranged His sacred curls: the moment He did this, she wavered. That is — she blinked her eyes. 'Why are you blinking the eyes that were created for seeing?' he said, and seeing that,

children.text: poy oru nāḷ paṭṭatē amaiyum
children.translated_text: The deception we fell for one day is enough —

children.text: uṉṉuṭaiya ceyalkaḷ ellām mey eṉṟu oru nāḷ paṭṭatē amaiyum kāṇ! eṉkiṟāḷ. aṭiyēṉ kuṭiyēṉ eṉṟu cila vārttaikaḷai colla
children.translated_text: The one day we believed all Your deeds to be true is enough, know this! When He began to say some words like 'I am Your servant, I am Your slave,'

children.text: puḷḷuvam pēcātē pōku nampi
children.translated_text: Do not speak falsehoods, go, <s>Nampi</s>! —

children.text: kāṭcikku muṉṉē kāṇ śravaṇamum, atuvum ellām paṇṭē ceytu aṟṟatu kāṇ; iṉi nī collukiṟavaṟṟukku oru prayojanam illai. puḷḷuvam āvatu - vañcanam. vañcanaṅkaḷ ellām aṟinta eṅkaḷ pakkal prayogiyātē pō. eṉṉai ‘pō’ eṉkiṟat’ eṉ? uṅkaḷai oḻiya pukaliṭam uṇṭō? eṉṉa,
children.translated_text: Before the act of seeing, there was hearing too, and all that was already done and exhausted long ago; henceforth there is no use in what You say. <s>Puḷḷuvam</s> means deception. Do not practice Your deceptions on us who know them all — go! 'Why are you telling me to go? Is there any refuge other than you?' —

children.text: nampī
children.translated_text: <s>Nampi</s>! —

children.text: pūrṇarāy irukkiṟa nīr kuṟaivāḷarai pōlē cila colla kaṭavīrō. collukkum ceyalukkum aṭi illai eṉṉumpaṭi nirapekṣar eṉṟu aṟinta piṉpu cila sāpekṣarai pōlē colla kaṭavīrō? naṭavīr.
children.translated_text: Would You who are complete speak like one who is deficient? Having known that You are one who is independent to the point that there is no basis for either word or deed, would You speak like one who is dependent? Go.

children.translated_text: Having slipped past her, He turned the real fear He had shown into pretense and laughed standing there; if the fear were genuine, then the tryst too would be genuine; in order to make the tryst appear false, he pretended to be falsely afraid.

children.text: pōtiyēlum
children.translated_text: Even as You flee —

children.text: appōtaikku ivaḷai tappa pōmatiṟē uddeśyam. appaṭiyē kaikaḻala pōṉāṉ.
children.translated_text: His immediate purpose was to escape past her. And so He slipped away.

children.text: iṉṉam eṉ kai akatt’ īṅk’ oru nāḷ varutiyēl
children.translated_text: If You come into my hands here one day more —

children.text: nī niyatasvabhāvaṉ allāmaiyālē eṉ kaiyilēyum oru nāḷ vantu akappaṭa kūṭumiṟē; akappaṭṭāy ākil
children.translated_text: Since You are not one of fixed nature, one day You will come and fall into my hands too; if You are caught,

children.text: eṉ ciṉam tīrvaṉ nāṉē
children.translated_text: I myself shall satisfy my anger! —

children.text: uynta piḷḷai pāṭā-niṟka, empār pārtt’ eḻuntaruḷi irukka i- iṭattukku abhinayikkiṟār: kālālē pāyntu taḷḷuvatāka kāṭṭa; attai kaṇṭ’ aruḷi, keṭuvāy! aṅṅaṉē ceytāḷ-ākil avaṉukku pollātō? avaṉukku at’ aṉṟō tēṭṭam? aṅṅaṉ aṉṟu kāṇum eṉṟu kaiyai iṭṭu mukattai maṟaittu tiriya vaitt’ aruḷi kāṭṭiṉār.
children.translated_text: When <s>Uynta Piḷḷai</s> was reciting this, <s>Empār</s> was watching; at this passage he acted it out: he showed kicking and pushing with the feet. Seeing that, <s>Empār</s> said: 'O foolish one! If she did that, would it not be just what he wants? Is that not exactly what he is seeking? That is not how it is, you see' — and covering his face with his hand, he showed the correct interpretation by turning away.

wearing flower

children.text: nekiḻntavarkaḷōṭu oru nīrāka kalantu a- kalaviyāl piṟanta harṣam ellām tōṟṟumpaṭiyāka iṉitāka kuḻalūti vantāy.

children.text: eṅkaḷukkē oru nāḷ vant’ ūta un kuḻal iṉ icai pōtarātē
children.translated_text: Will the sweet music of Your flute never come to play for us alone one day? —

children.text: nī sarvasādhāraṇaṉāṉa piṉpu uṉ kuḻalum sarvasādhāraṇamāy irukka, ōrō iṭaṅkaḷilēyāy nāṅkaḷ kēṭka ūta vēṇum eṉṟāl nī ūtiyēlum icai puṟap-paṭātapaṭiāyttiṟē uṉ kuḻaliṉ svabhāvam. kuḻal ōcai eṉṟum saṃśleṣam eṉṟum paryāyamiṟē. eṅkaḷōṭu saṃśleṣam uṉakku poruntātu eṉkiṟārkaḷ.
children.translated_text: Since You are common to all, Your flute too is common to all; when we say You should come to each of our places and play for us to hear, even if You play, the nature of Your flute is such that the music will not come forth. The flute's sound and union are synonymous. They say that union with them does not suit Him.
Introduction — Ninth verse. They speak in a way that reveals their defeat.

children.translated_text: Desiring <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> who is the supreme beloved,

children.text: iḷa āyccimārkaḷ
children.translated_text: the young cowherd women —

children.text: avaṉai pōlē ēṟi maṟinta paruvam aṉṟiyē pāṭ’ āṟṟamāṭṭāta iḷa āyccimārkaḷ
