children.text: ūṭi attālē īṭupaṭṭu a- īṭupāṭu tāṉ collāy vaḻintu puṟappaṭṭat’ eṉṉalāmpaṭiyāṉa pācurattai
children.translated_text: having quarreled, thereby becoming overwhelmed, that overwhelming itself flowing out as words — the verses that can be described thus,

children.text: kolli nakarkk’ iṟai kūṭal kōmāṉ
children.translated_text: <s>Kulacēkaraṉ</s>, lord of <s>Kolli</s> city, king of <s>Kūṭal</s> —

children.text: kolli eṉṟu cēraṉ paṭaivīṭu; kūṭal eṉṟu pāṇṭiyaṉ paṭaivīṭu; kōḻi kōṉ eṉṟu muṉpē colli-vaittār. mūṉṟu rājyattukkum kaṭavar āṉa śrī kulaśekhara perumāḷ; śrīgopimārkaḷ taṅkaḷ strītvābhimānam ellām aṟṟu coṉṉā pōlē ivarum periya abhimānam ellām aṟuttapaṭi
children.translated_text: <s>Kolli</s> is the military encampment of the Cēra king; <s>Kūṭal</s> is that of the Pāṇṭiya king; 'king of <s>Kōḻi</s>' was already stated before. <s>Śrī Kulaśekhara Perumāḷ</s> who was lord of all three kingdoms; just as the <s>Gopīs</s> spoke having abandoned all their womanly pride, he too, having cut away all his great pride,

children.text: iṉ icaiyil mēvi colliya iṉ tamiḻ mālai pattum
children.translated_text: set them in sweet melody — these ten verses of sweet Tamil garland —

children.text: pāṭhye geye ca madhuram
children.translated_text: "<s>pāṭhye geye ca madhuram</s>" (sweet in recitation and in song) —

children.text: eṉṉumpaṭiyāṉa tamiḻ toṭai pattum
children.translated_text: as described thus, these ten verses of Tamil composition,

children.text: colla vallārkk’ illai tuṉpam tāṉē
children.translated_text: those who can recite them shall have no sorrow!

children.text: ivaruṭaiya bhāvabandham illaiyākilum ivai kaṟṟavarkaḷukku bhaga-vadanubhavattukku vicchedaśaṅkai piṟavātē nirantarānubhavamāy cella peṟuvārkaḷ. saṃbhogamadhyē piṟakkumatiṟē ūṭal āvatu. uṉ talai pattu eṉ talai pattu eṉṟu muṭiya kūṭalāy cellum anubhavattai peṟuvārkaḷ.
children.translated_text: Even if they lack his depth of emotional bond, those who learn these verses will receive uninterrupted experience of the Lord without the fear of cessation of <s>bhagavadanubhava</s> (divine experience). For lovers' quarrel (<s>ūṭal</s>) arises only in the midst of union. They will attain the experience that continues as reconciliation from beginning to end, 'your turn and my turn.'
In the concluding verse —

children.text: avatārikai - pirāṭṭi, tiruvaṭiyai kaṇṭavāṟē praṇayaroṣam talaiyeṭuttu piturvacanaparipālanam paṇṇa pōntār eṉṟiṟē perumāḷ uṅkaḷ goṣṭhiyilē prasiddharāy iruppatu; ippōtu aṅṅaṉ aṉṟu kāṇ; tammai viśvasittu kaikoṭutta eṉṉai viṭukaikkāka kāṇ.
rakṣitā jīvalokasya
children.translated_text: <s>rakṣitā jīvalokasya</s> (the protector of the world of living beings)

children.text:
eṉkiṟattaiyum viṭṭāriṟē eṉṟu kilāyttā pōlē kilāyttār ivarum kīḻil tirumoḻiyilē; sarvātmākkaḷukkum pirāṭṭimār ōpāti prāpti uṇṭ’ eṉṉumpaṭi bhagavadviṣayattilē avagāhittavar-ākaiyālē ivar kilāyttār.
	  ippaṭi kilāykkaikku prāpti uṇṭāy irukkiṟa viṣayattai anādikālam iḻantōm eṉkiṟa iḻavu vantu talaiyeṭuttu, muṉpu kṛṣṇaṉai peṟṟuvaittu bālyāvasthaiyil avaṉ ceyalkaḷai anubhavikka peṟātē iḻant’ iruntu, kaṃsavadha-paryantamāka muṉp’ uḷḷa virodhikaḷai ellām pōkki, taṅkaḷ mukattilē viḻitta kṛṣṇaṉai kaṇṭapōtu kīḻ anubhavikka peṟāta iḻavukaḷai colli kūppiṭṭa devakiyār pācurattālē anādikālam tām iḻanta iḻavai collukiṟār i- tirumoḻiyil.
children.translated_text:
She sulked as if saying 'He has abandoned even that vow' — thus he too sulked in the previous <s>Tirumoḻi</s>; since he, like <s>Pirāṭṭi</s> herself, had immersed himself in the Lord's domain to the point where all souls have the same entitlement as She does, he sulked.
	With this entitlement to sulk, the loss of having lost the worthy object for beginningless time arose and asserted itself — having previously obtained <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> but having lost the enjoyment of His childhood deeds, and after all the previous enemies up to the slaying of <s>Kaṃsa</s> were removed — when they saw <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> looking into their faces, <s>Devakī</s> cried out lamenting the earlier losses she could not enjoy. Through <s>Devakī</s>'s words, he expresses in this <s>Tirumoḻi</s> the loss he himself has suffered since beginningless time.

Introduction — <s>Pirāṭṭi</s> (Sītā), the moment she saw <s>Tiruvadī</s> (<s>Hanumān</s>), her <s>praṇayaroṣa</s> (love-borne anger) arose and she insisted on <s>Perumāḷ</s> (Lord <s>Rāma</s>) upholding His father's command — this is how it is well known in your assembly. But now it is not so — it was in order to abandon me who had trusted Him and offered my hand.

children.text: ālai nīḷ karump’ aṉṉavaṉ tālō ampuya taṭam kaṇṇiṉaṉ tālō
children.translated_text: Lullaby to him who is like tall sugarcane from the mill! Lullaby to the one with lotus-pond eyes!

children.text: vēlai nīr niṟatt’ aṉṉavaṉ tālō vēḻa pōtakam aṉṉavaṉ tālō
children.translated_text: Lullaby to the one whose hue is like the ocean waters! Lullaby to the one who is like a young elephant calf!

children.text: ēla
m
vār kuḻal eṉ makaṉ tālō eṉṟ’ eṉṟ’ uṉṉai eṉ vāyiṭai niṟaiya
children.translated_text: Lullaby to my son with long tresses of flowing hair! — thus to fill my mouth saying again and again to you
fragrant

children.text: tāl olittiṭum tiru viṉai illā tāyaril kaṭai āyiṉa tāyē
children.translated_text: the lullaby-singing fortune I lacked — I became the lowest among mothers, a mother without such blessed deed!

children.text: ālai nīḷ  karump’ aṉṉavaṉ tālō
children.translated_text: Lullaby to him who is like tall sugarcane from the mill!

children.text: camaiya vaḷarnta ālai karumpu pōlē rasanendriyattukku iṉiyaṉ-āṉavaṉē!
children.translated_text: He who is sweet to the sense of taste, like sugarcane grown to full maturity in the mill!

children.text: ampuya taṭam kaṇṇiṉaṉ tālō
children.translated_text: Lullaby to the one with lotus-pond eyes!

children.text: vikāsam, cevvi, kuḷirtti, meṉmaiyai uṭaiya tāmarai pū pōlē irukkiṟa tiru kaṇkaḷai koṇṭu eṉṉai kuḷira nōkkukiṟavaṉē! eṉṟu cakṣurindriyattukku iṉitāy irukkiṟapaṭi collukiṟār.
children.translated_text: With sacred eyes that are like lotus flowers possessing bloom, beauty, coolness, and softness, He gazes upon me with coolness! — thus she speaks of how He is sweet to the sense of sight.

children.text: vēlai nīr niṟatt’ aṉṉavaṉ tālō
children.translated_text: Lullaby to the one whose hue is like the ocean waters!

children.text: avayavaṅkaḷai pirittu colla vēṇumō? avayaviyāṉa tirumēṉiyālum śramaharamāṉa kaṭal pōlē irukkiṟavaṉē!
children.translated_text: Need one describe each limb separately? In His entire sacred form, He is like the fatigue-removing ocean!

children.text: vēḻa pōtakam aṉṉavaṉ tālō
children.translated_text: Lullaby to the one who is like a young elephant calf!

children.text: āṉai kaṉṟu pōlē, vaitta kaṇ vāṅkātē pārttapaṭiyē irukkumpaṭiyāṉa caritaṅkaḷai uṭaiyavaṉē!
children.translated_text: He who has deeds such that one cannot withdraw the gaze once fixed upon Him, like a baby elephant!

children.text: ēla
m
vār kuḻal eṉ makaṉ tālō
children.translated_text: Lullaby to my son with long tresses of flowing hair!
fragrant

children.text: ippaṭi upamānaṅkaḷāl colla oṇṇāmaiyālē eṉ makaṉ eṉṉum ittaṉai.
children.translated_text: Since He cannot be adequately described through comparisons, she simply says 'my son' — that is all.

children.text: eṉṟ’ eṉṟ’ uṉṉai eṉ vāyiṭai niṟaiya tāl olittiṭum tiru viṉai illā
children.translated_text: Saying again and again to you, to fill my mouth with lullabies — the blessed fortune I lacked

children.text: ippaṭi palakālum colli vāyāra tālāṭṭum sampat illāta
children.translated_text: the fortune of singing lullabies many times until my mouth is full, which I lacked

children.text: tāyaril kaṭai āyiṉa tāyē
children.translated_text: I became the lowest among mothers!

children.text: peṟukaikku nōṉpu nōṟṟu peṟṟuvaittu anubhavattil kuṟaiya niṟkaiyālē, piḷḷaikaḷai peṟṟu anubhavikkum tāymār ellārilum kaṭai āṉēṉiṟē nāṉ.
children.translated_text: Having performed austerities to beget, having begotten, yet having fallen short in enjoyment — I became the lowest among all mothers who bear and enjoy their children.

children.text: vaṭi koḷ añcaṉam eḻutu cem malar kaṇ maruvi mēl iṉit’ oṉṟiṉai nōkki
children.translated_text: With beautiful red-lotus eyes traced with sharp collyrium, gazing sweetly at something above

children.text: muṭakki cē aṭi malar ciṟu karum tāḷ poliyum nīr mukil kuḻaviyē pōla
children.translated_text: with curled red lotus-feet, small dark legs — like a baby dark rain-cloud

children.text: aṭakki āra cem ciṟu viral aṉaittum aṅkaiyōṭ’ aṇaint’ āṉaiyil kiṭanta
children.translated_text: tucking all the beautiful small red fingers tightly pressed together with the palm, lying as an elephant lies

children.text: kiṭakkai kaṇṭiṭa peṟṟilaṉ antō kēcavā keṭuvēṉ keṭuvēṉē
children.translated_text: I did not get to see that posture of lying — alas! O <s>Keśava</s>! I am ruined, ruined!

children.text: vaṭi koḷ añcaṉam eḻutu cem malar kaṇ
children.translated_text: With beautiful red-lotus eyes traced with sharp collyrium

children.text: kūrmaiyai uṭaiya cem malar kaṇ eṉṉutal; tiru kaṇṇukku īṭāka vaṭikkappaṭṭa añjanattai uṭaiya kaṇ eṉṉutal. cem malar - civanta tāmarai pōlē iruntuḷḷa
children.translated_text: This means either: eyes of red flowers possessing sharpness; or: eyes with collyrium shaped to match the beauty of the sacred eyes. Red flowers — like red lotuses.

children.text: maruvi mēl iṉit’ oṉṟiṉai nōkki
children.translated_text: gazing sweetly at something above

children.text: piḷḷaiyai toṭṭililē vaḷartti ananyaparaṉāy pārttu kiṭakkaikkāka mēlē oṉṟai tūkki vaippārkaḷiṟē. attai iṉiyaṉāy koṇṭu sadādarśanam paṇṇi kiṭakkumiṟē.
children.translated_text: When raising a child in a cradle, they would hang something above for it to gaze at single-mindedly. It would find that sweet and lie there gazing at it constantly.

children.text: muṭakki cē aṭi malar ciṟu karum tāḷ
children.translated_text: with curled red lotus-feet, small dark legs

children.text: aṅku kiṭakkumpaṭi collukiṟatu mēl. puṟavāy kaṟuttu, akavāy civanta tiruvaṭikaḷai muṭakki
children.translated_text: What follows describes how He lies there. Bending the sacred feet that are dark on the outside and red within

children.text: poliyum nīr mukil kuḻaviyē pōla
children.translated_text: like a baby dark rain-cloud

children.text: kaḻuttē kaṭṭaḷaiyāka nīrai parukiṟṟ’ oru megha kaṉṟu pōlē
children.translated_text: like a cloud-calf that has drunk water up to its neck

children.text: aṭakki āra cem ciṟu viral aṉaittum aṅkaiyōṭ’ aṇaintu
children.translated_text: tucking all the beautiful small red fingers tightly pressed together with the palm

children.text: ceṟintu aḻakiyatāṉa tiru viralkaḷai uḷḷaṅkaiyilē aṭaṅkumpaṭi maṭittu piṭittu
children.translated_text: folding and gripping the delicate, beautiful sacred fingers so that they fit within the palm of the hand

children.text: āṉaiyil kiṭanta kiṭakkai kaṇṭiṭa peṟṟilaṉ antō
children.translated_text: I did not get to see the posture of lying like an elephant — alas!

children.text: āṉai taṉ avayavaṅkaḷai pōkaṭṭu svairamāka kiṭantā pōlē toṭṭililē kiṭakkum pōtu anubhavikka peṟṟilēṉ eṉṟu aiyō eṉkiṟāḷ.
children.translated_text: She cries 'alas!' saying: I did not get to enjoy His lying in the cradle with limbs relaxed, like an elephant lying at ease.

children.text: kēcavā keṭuvēṉ keṭuvēṉē
children.translated_text: O <s>Keśava</s>! I am ruined, ruined!

children.text: appōtai tiru kuḻal aḻakai anubhavikkavum peṟṟilēṉ; muṉpu malaṭu niṉṟu iḻantēṉ. piṉpu peṟṟuvaittē anubhavikka peṟātē iḻantēṉ. iraṇṭālum mahāpāpiyiṟē nāṉ.
children.translated_text: I did not even get to enjoy the beauty of His sacred hair at that time; earlier I lost Him while barren. Later, having borne Him, I lost Him without getting to enjoy Him. By both counts, I am a great sinner.

children.text: muntai nal muṟai aṉp’ uṭai makaḷir muṟai muṟai tam tam kuṟaṅk’ iṭai irutti
children.translated_text: The women of love from the good old noble lineage, in proper succession, would seat Him on their laps

children.text: entaiyē eṉ taṉ kula perum cuṭarē eḻu mukil kaṇatt’ eḻil kavar ēṟē
children.translated_text: 'O my father! O great luminary of my clan! O bull captivating the beauty of seven cloud-masses!'

children.text: untai yāvaṉ eṉṟ’ uraippa niṉ cem kēḻ viraliṉum kaṭai kaṇṇiṉum kāṭṭa
children.translated_text: When they asked 'Who is your father?', with your red-hued finger and sidelong glance you would point —

children.text: nantaṉ peṟṟaṉaṉ nal viṉai illā naṅkaḷ kōṉ vacutēvaṉ peṟṟilaṉē
children.translated_text: <s>Nandaṉ</s> obtained that fortune. Our Lord <s>Vasudeva</s>, who lacked good fortune, did not obtain it!

children.text: muntai nal muṟai aṉp’ uṭai makaḷir
children.translated_text: The women of love from the good old noble lineage

children.text: tāymār, avarkaḷuṭaiya tāymār, pāṭṭimār ellārum
children.translated_text: the mothers, their mothers, and all the grandmothers

children.text: muṟai muṟai tam tam kuṟaṅk’ iṭai irutti
children.translated_text: in proper succession, would seat Him on their laps

children.text: tam tam avvō aṭaivukaḷilē kuṟaṅkukaḷilē vaittu koṇṭu
children.translated_text: each in their respective turns, placing Him on their laps

children.text: entaiyē eṉ taṉ kula perum cuṭarē eḻu mukil kaṇatt’ eḻil kavar ēṟē
children.translated_text: 'O my father! O great luminary of my clan! O bull captivating the beauty of seven cloud-masses!'

children.text: eṉ-taṉ tamappaṉē! eṅkaḷ kulattukku viḷakk’āṉavaṉē! ēḻu vakaippaṭṭa meghasamūhaṅkaḷiṉuṭaiya aḻakai kavarnta siṃham pōlē irukkiṟavaṉē!
children.translated_text: 'O my father! O one who is the lamp of our clan! O one who is like a lion captivating the beauty of the seven kinds of cloud-masses!'

children.text: untai yāvaṉ eṉṟ’ uraippa
children.translated_text: When they asked 'Who is your father?'

children.text: ippaṭi stotraṅkaḷai paṇṇi uṅkaḷ tamappaṉār yār eṉṟu kēṭka
children.translated_text: thus praising Him, when they would ask 'Who is your father?'

children.text: niṉ cem kēḻ viraliṉum kaṭai kaṇṇiṉum kāṭṭa nantaṉ peṟṟaṉaṉ
children.translated_text: with your red-hued finger and sidelong glance you would point — <s>Nandaṉ</s> obtained that

children.text: kēḻ viraliṉum kaṭai kaṇṇiṉālum kāṭṭa śrīnandagopar peṟṟār.
children.translated_text: pointing with His ruddy finger and sidelong glance — <s>Śrī Nandagopa</s> obtained that.

children.text: nal viṉai illā naṅkaḷ kōṉ vacutēvaṉ peṟṟilaṉē
children.translated_text: Our Lord <s>Vasudeva</s>, who lacked good fortune, did not obtain it!

children.text: bhāgyahīnaiyāṉa eṉṉai kaippiṭikkaiyālē śrīvasudevarum iḻantārē.
children.translated_text: Because of taking the hand of unfortunate me, even <s>Śrī Vasudeva</s> lost it all.

children.text: kaḷi nilā eḻil mati purai mukamum kaṇṇaṉē tiṇ kai mārvum tiṇ tōḷum
children.translated_text: a face resembling the joyous, radiant full moon, O <s>Kaṇṇā</s>! the firm hands, chest, and strong shoulders

children.text: taḷir malar karum kuḻal piṟai atuvum taṭam koḷ tāmarai kaṇkaḷum polinta
children.translated_text: the tender-flowered dark curls and that crescent brow, and the wide lotus eyes all resplendent

children.text: iḷamai iṉpattai iṉṟ’ eṉ taṉ kaṇṇāl parukuvēṟk’ ivaḷ tāy eṉa niṉainta
children.translated_text: for me who today drinks in with my own eyes the joy of youth — thinking 'this one is His mother'

children.text: aḷav’ il piḷḷaimai iṉpattai iḻanta pāviyēṉ eṉat’ āvi nillātē
children.translated_text: the sinner who lost the immeasurable joy of infancy — my life does not endure!

children.text: kaḷi nilā eḻil mati purai mukamum
children.translated_text: a face resembling the joyous, radiant full moon

children.text: ceṟinta nilāvai uṭaiya pūrṇacandraṉai pōlē irukkiṟa tiru mukamum
children.translated_text: a sacred face like the full moon with its refined moonlight

children.text: kaṇṇaṉē tiṇ kai mārvum tiṇ tōḷum
children.translated_text: O <s>Kaṇṇā</s>! the firm hands, chest, and strong shoulders

children.text: kṛṣṇaṉē! collukiṟa vilakṣaṇamāy tiṇṇiyatāy irukkiṟa tiru kaiyum tiru mārpum tiru tōḷum
children.translated_text: O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>! the extraordinarily firm sacred hands, sacred chest, and sacred shoulders

children.text: taḷir malar karum kuḻal piṟai-atuvum
children.translated_text: the tender-flowered dark curls and that crescent brow

children.text: taḷiraiyum malaraiyum uṭaittāy iruṇṭ’ irukkiṟa tiru kuḻaliṉ-kīḻē unneyamāṉa piṟai pōlē viḷaṅkukiṟa tiru neṟṟiyum
children.translated_text: beneath the dark sacred hair adorned with tender shoots and flowers, the sacred forehead that shines like a crescent moon smeared with oil

children.text: taṭam koḷ tāmarai kaṇkaḷum
children.translated_text: and the wide lotus eyes

children.text: oru tāmarai pūvē taḍākam ellām viḻuṅkumpaṭi alarntā pōlē tirumēṉi ellām parappumāṟumpaṭi alarnta tiru kaṇkaḷum
children.translated_text: sacred eyes that have bloomed so wide as if a single lotus flower had expanded to swallow an entire pond, spreading across the whole sacred form

children.text: polinta iḷamai iṉpattai iṉṟ’ eṉ taṉ kaṇṇāl parukuvēṟku
children.translated_text: for me who today drinks in with my own eyes the joy of resplendent youth

children.text: i- ayavaśobhaikaḷāl viḷaṅkā-niṉṟuḷḷa yauvanāvasthaiyil aḻakai eṉ kaṇṇālē anubhavikkiṟa eṉakku
children.translated_text: for me who now beholds with my eyes the beauty of the youthful state radiant with the splendor of each limb

children.text: ivaḷ tāy eṉa niṉainta aḷav’ il piḷḷaimai iṉpattai iḻanta pāviyēṉ
children.translated_text: the sinner who, thinking 'this one is His mother,' lost the immeasurable joy of infancy

children.text: tāy oruttiyaiyum allatu vēṟ’ oruttaraiyum aṟiyāta atiśaiśavamāy irukkiṟa paruvattai anubhavikka peṟāmaiyālē ippōtu kiṭṭi anubhavikka ceytēyum iḻavē talaiyeṭukkumpaṭiyāṉa mahāpāpattai paṇṇiṉēṉ.
children.translated_text: being a sinner who committed great sin such that even now, though able to approach and enjoy, the loss still asserts itself — having failed to enjoy the stage of earliest infancy when the child knows no one but its mother.

children.text: eṉat’ āvi
children.translated_text: my life

children.text: eṉ prāṇaṉ dharikkiṟat’ illai.
children.translated_text: my <s>prāṇa</s> (life-breath) cannot endure.

children.text: maruvu niṉ tiru neṟṟiyil cuṭṭi acaitara maṇi vāyiṭai muttam
children.translated_text: the ornament on your beautiful sacred forehead swaying, a kiss on the gem-like mouth

children.text: tarutalum uṉ taṉ tātaiyai pōlum vaṭivu kaṇṭukoṇṭ’ uḷḷam uḷ kuḷira
children.translated_text: and giving that, and seeing the form that resembles your grandfather, with the heart cooling within

children.text: viralai cem ciṟu vāyiṭai cērttu vekuḷi āy niṉṟ’ uraikkum a- uraiyum
children.translated_text: placing the finger in the small red mouth, standing angry and uttering those words

children.text: tiruvilēṉ oṉṟum peṟṟilēṉ ellām teyva
m
naṅkai yacōtai peṟṟāḷē
children.translated_text: the divine lady <s>Yaśodā</s> obtained!
I, the unfortunate one, obtained none of these — all of it

children.text: maruvu niṉ tiru neṟṟiyil cuṭṭi acaitara
children.translated_text: the ornament on your beautiful sacred forehead swaying

children.text: tiru neṟṟiyil kūṭa piṟantā pōlē irukkum tiru cuṭṭiyāṉatu acaiyumpaṭi
children.translated_text: the sacred <s>cuṭṭi</s> (forehead ornament) that appears as if born together with the sacred forehead, swaying thus

children.text: maṇi vāyiṭai muttam tarutalum
children.translated_text: a kiss on the gem-like mouth

children.text: aḻakiya vāyil muttam - adharamuttam koṭuttalum
children.translated_text: giving a kiss — a lip-kiss — on the beautiful mouth

children.text: uṉ taṉ tātaiyai pōlum
children.translated_text: resembling your grandfather

children.text: uṉ tamappaṉai pōlē
children.translated_text: resembling your father

children.text: vaṭivu kaṇṭukoṇṭ’ uḷḷam uḷ kuḷira
children.translated_text: seeing the form and the heart cooling within

children.text: vaṭiv’ aḻakai kaṇṭukoṇṭu neñcamāṉatu uḷ kuḷira
children.translated_text: seeing the beauty of the form, the heart cooling within

children.text: viralai cem ciṟu vāyiṭai cērttu vekuḷi āy niṉṟ’ uraikkum a- uraiyum
children.translated_text: placing the finger in the small red mouth, standing angry and uttering those words

children.text: civantu kuvint’ iruntuḷḷa tiru pavaḷattilē tiru viralai cērttu cīṟṟattōṭē niṉṟu collukiṟa maḻalai coṟkaḷum
children.translated_text: placing the sacred finger in the red, pursed sacred coral lips, standing with anger and uttering those baby words

children.text: tiru ilēṉ, ityādi
children.translated_text: 'I, the unfortunate one,' etc.

children.text: bālyāvasthaiyil anubhavaṅkaḷai anubhavikka bhāgyahīnaiyāṉa nāṉ iḻantēṉ. iḻakkaikku nāṉ orutti uṇṭāṉā pōlē, anubhavikkaikku iṭṭu piṟanta yaśodai pirāṭṭi ellām peṟṟāḷiṟē.
children.translated_text: I, being one bereft of fortune, lost the enjoyments of the childhood state. Just as I alone existed to lose, <s>Yaśodā Pirāṭṭi</s>, born to enjoy, obtained everything.

children.text: taṇ am tāmarai kaṇṇaṉē kaṇṇā tavaḻnt’ eḻuntu taḷarntat’ ōr naṭaiyāl
children.translated_text: O cool-lotus-eyed <s>Kaṇṇā</s>! crawling, rising, and with a tottering, unsteady gait

children.text: maṇṇil cem poṭi āṭi vant’ eṉ taṉ mārvil maṉṉiṭa peṟṟilēṉ antō
children.translated_text: playing in the red dust on the ground, coming and settling on my chest — I did not get that! Alas!

children.text: vaṇṇa cem ciṟu kai viral aṉaittum vāri vāy koṇṭa aṭiciliṉ miccil
children.translated_text: the leftovers of the rice scooped up by all those beautiful, red, small hand-fingers and put into the mouth

children.text: uṇṇa peṟṟilēṉ ō koṭu
m
viṉaiyēṉ eṉṉai eṉ ceyya peṟṟat’ em mōyē
children.translated_text: sinful one that I am! What was the use of my mother bearing me?
I did not get to eat — O cruel

children.text: taṇ am tāmarai kaṇṇaṉē
children.translated_text: O cool-lotus-eyed one!

children.text: kuḷirntu aḻakiyatāṉa tāmarai pū pōlē alarnta tiru kaṇkaḷai uṭaiya kṛṣṇaṉē!
children.translated_text: O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> with sacred eyes blooming like cool, beautiful lotus flowers!

children.text: tavaḻnt’ eḻuntu taḷarntat’ ōr naṭaiyāl
children.translated_text: crawling, rising, and with a tottering, unsteady gait

children.text: tavaḻnt’ eḻunt’ iruntu naṭakka pukuvatu taḷḷampāṟuvatāṉa taḷar-naṭaiyālē
children.translated_text: crawling, rising, and beginning to walk — with the tottering, faltering, unsteady gait

children.text: maṇṇil cem poṭi, ityādi
children.translated_text: 'playing in the red dust on the ground,' etc.

children.text: nila paṇpālē civanta puḻutiyai āṭi vantu a- kōlattōṭē eṉ mārpilē kaṭṭikkoṇṭu kiṭakka peṟṟilēṉ.
children.translated_text: I did not get to have Him come playing in the dust that is red by the nature of the soil, and in that very state cling to my chest and lie there.

children.text: vaṇṇa cem ciṟu, ityādi
children.translated_text: 'the beautiful, red, small,' etc.

children.text: aḻakiyatāy civanta tiru viralkaḷ aṉaittālum vāri amutuceyta śeṣattai uṇṇa peṟāta mahāpāpattai paṇṇiṉēṉ.
children.translated_text: I committed the great sin of not getting to eat the remnants of what He had eaten, scooped up with all His beautiful, red, sacred fingers.

children.text: eṉṉai eṉ ceyya peṟṟat’ em mōyē
children.translated_text: What was the use of my mother bearing me?

children.text: rājamahiṣiyāy piḷḷaikaḷ aḷainta eccil uṇṇāmaikkō eṅkaḷ tāyār eṉṉai peṟṟatu?
children.translated_text: Was it to be a royal queen and not eat the food-remnants from my children's hands that our mother bore me?

children.text: amutiṉum āṟṟa iṉitē tam makkaḷ ciṟu kai aḷāviya kūḻ
children.translated_text: Sweeter even than <s>amṛta</s> (nectar) is the rice that small hands of one's children have scooped.

children.text: makkaḷ mey tīṇṭal uṭaṟk’ iṉpam maṟṟ’ avar tam col kēṭṭal iṉpam cevikku.
children.translated_text: The touch of one's children's bodies is joy to the body; hearing their words is joy to the ears.

children.text: kuḻakaṉē eṉ taṉ kōmaḷa piḷḷāy kōvintā eṉ kuṭaṅkaiyil maṉṉi
children.translated_text: O beautiful boy! O my tender child! O <s>Govinda</s>! Settling in the cup of my hands

children.text: oḻuku pēr eḻil iḷam ciṟu taḷir pōl oru kaiyāl oru mulai mukam neruṭā
children.translated_text: with your overflowing, supremely beautiful, tender young sprout-like form, with one hand pressing one breast to your face

children.text: maḻalai mel nakai iṭai iṭai aruḷā vāyilē mulai irukka eṉ mukattē
children.translated_text: granting baby smiles now and then — while the breast is in the mouth, upon my face

children.text: eḻil koḷ niṉ tiru kaṇ iṇai nōkkam taṉṉaiyum iḻantēṉ iḻantēṉē
children.translated_text: the glance of your beautiful sacred pair of eyes — even that I have lost! I have lost!

children.text: kuḻakaṉē eṉ taṉ kōmaḷa piḷḷāy
children.translated_text: O beautiful boy! O my tender child!

children.text: lokayātraiyilē anyaparaiyāy taṉakku mukam koṭāt’ iruntāl lokayātraiyai kaiviṭṭu uṉṉaiyē pārkka vallēṉ āmpaṭi kalakka vallaiyāy, atutāṉ poṟāta saukumāryattai uṭaiyavaṉē!
children.translated_text: If she, being occupied with worldly affairs, does not turn her face toward Him, He is capable of disrupting her worldly affairs so that she looks only at Him — and yet He has such tenderness (<s>saukumārya</s>) that even that He cannot endure!

children.text: kōvintā eṉ kuṭaṅkaiyil maṉṉi
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Govinda</s>! Staying in the hollow of my hands' —

children.text: gosamṛddhiyai uṭaiyavaṉē! eṉ kaiyilē iruntu
children.translated_text: O You who possess the prosperity of cows (<s>gosamṛddhi</s>)! Remaining in my hands,

children.text: oḻuku pēr eḻil iḷam ciṟu taḷir pōl oru kaiyāl oru mulai mukam neruṭā
children.translated_text: With one hand like a beautiful, tender young sprout from which beauty flows, pressing one breast —

children.text: aḻaku veḷḷam paṭint’ ōṭumpaṭiyāṉa taḷir pōlē irukkiṟa oru tiru kaiyālē ivaḷ iraṅki mulaikoṭukkumpaṭi oru mulaikkaṇṇai neruṭikkoṇṭu
children.translated_text: With one sacred hand, like a sprout from which a flood of beauty flows, pressing one nipple in such a way as to make her yield milk with compassion,

children.text: maḻalai mel nakai iṭai iṭai aruḷā vāyilē mulai irukka eṉ mukattē
children.translated_text: With babbling, soft smiles in between — while the breast is in the mouth, looking at my face —

children.text: vāyilē mulai irukka ceytē mulai curakkumpaṭiyāka eṉ mukattilē iṭaiyiṭaiyē maḻalai cirippāka ciriyā
children.translated_text: While the breast is in His mouth, to make the milk flow, He smiles babbling baby-smiles at my face now and then,

children.text: eḻil koḷ niṉ tiru kaṇ iṇai nōkkam
children.translated_text: The gaze of Your beautiful twin sacred eyes —

children.text: atukkum iraṅkārum iraṅkumpaṭi aḻakiya tiru kaṇkaḷālē pārkkiṟa pārvaiyaiyum, peṟṟa aṉṟē pōkaviṭṭatukku mēlē i- avasthaiyil ceṣṭi-taṅkaḷaiyum anubhavikka peṟṟilēṉ.
children.translated_text: The glance from His beautiful sacred eyes that would melt even one who would not otherwise be moved — I did not get to experience these acts in that stage of infancy, having let Him go the very day He was born.

children.text: muḻutum veṇṇey aḷaintu toṭṭ’ uṇṇum mukiḻ iḷam ciṟu tāmarai kaiyum
children.translated_text: The budding young small lotus hand that scoops up all the butter and eats it by touching,

children.text: eḻil koḷ tāmpu koṇṭ’ aṭippataṟk’ eḷku nilaiyum veḷ tayir tōynta cem vāyum
children.translated_text: The posture of standing still, easy to strike, when beaten with a beautiful rope, and the red mouth smeared with white curds,

children.text: aḻukaiyum añci nōkkum a- nōkkum aṇi koḷ cem ciṟu vāy neḷippatuvum
children.translated_text: The crying, the fearful glance, that look, and the quivering of the beautiful small red lips,

children.text: toḻukaiyum ivai kaṇṭa acōtai tollai iṉpatt’ iṟuti kaṇṭāḷē
children.translated_text: And the joining of palms in supplication — having seen all these, <s>Yaśodā</s> saw the ultimate limit of ancient bliss!

children.text: avatārikai - eṭṭām pāṭṭu.
muḻutum ityādi
children.translated_text: 'All the butter' etc. —

children.text: nāṉ iḻanta iḻavai ellām yaśodai pirāṭṭi peṟṟāḷ eṉkiṟār.
children.translated_text: He says that <s>Yaśodā Pirāṭṭi</s> obtained everything that I lost.

children.text: muḻutum veṇṇey aḷaintu
children.translated_text: 'Scooping up all the butter' —

children.text: veṇṇeyil uṇṭāṉa ādarātiśayattālē tiru kaikaḷai veṇṇey kuṭattilē iṭṭu aḷaiyum āyttu.
children.translated_text: Due to the excess of love for butter, He would plunge His sacred hands into the butter pot and churn.

children.text: toṭṭ’ uṇṇum
children.translated_text: 'Touching and eating' —

children.text: aticāpalattālē māḷum eṉṟu
children.translated_text: Due to excessive eagerness, as if He would die,

children.text: viraloṭu vāy tōynta
children.translated_text: 'The finger touching the mouth' —

children.text: eṉṉumā pōlē toṭṭuṇṇum āyttu
children.translated_text: As it is said, He would touch and eat,

children.text: mukiḻ iḷam ciṟu tāmarai kaiyum
children.translated_text: 'The budding young small lotus hand' —

children.text: iḷantaḷir pōlēyum niṟattukku, vikāsam cevvikku tāmarai pū pōlēyum irukkiṟa tiru kaikaḷum
children.translated_text: The sacred hands that are like young sprouts in color, and like lotus flowers in their bloom and refinement,

children.text: eḻil koḷ tāmpu
children.translated_text: 'The beautiful rope' —

children.text: sparśikkaikku ācaippaṭṭ’ irukkum tirumēṉiyai sparśittatiṟē eṉṟu eḻil koḷ tāmpu eṉkiṟār. rājajanmam vēṇṭā; acetanam āka amaiyum aṅkuttai sparśam peṟil eṉṟ’ irukkumavariṟē.
children.translated_text: He says 'beautiful rope' because it touched the sacred body (<s>tirumēṉi</s>) that one longs to touch. He is one who thinks: 'I don't need a royal birth; being an insentient object would suffice if I could get the touch of that body.'

children.text: koṇṭ’ aṭippataṟk’ eḷku nilaiyum
children.translated_text: 'The posture of standing still, easy to strike' —

children.text: ivar aṅkuttai sparśattai niṉaittu eḻil koḷ tāmpu eṉkiṟār. ākilum kaikk’ eṭṭiṟṟ’ oṉṟai iṭṭu avaḷ aṭikka, atukku īṭupaṭṭu paiyāntu niṟkum nilaiyum
children.translated_text: He says 'beautiful rope' thinking of that body-touch. Nevertheless, when she picks up something within reach and strikes, the posture of standing still, subdued by that, patiently enduring —

children.text: veḷ tayir tōynta cem vāyum
children.translated_text: 'The red mouth smeared with white curds' —

children.text: tayir kaḷavu kaṇṭāy eṉṟu aṭikka pukkavāṟē illai ceykaikkāka mukattilē pūcikkoḷḷumē. veḷutta tayirum civanta tiru pavaḷamumāṉa parabhāgam irukkiṟa paṭi
children.translated_text: The moment she discovers the curd-theft and is about to strike, He smears it on His face to deny it. The beauty of the white curd against the red sacred coral lips!

children.text: aḻukaiyum
children.translated_text: 'The crying' —

children.text: illai eṉṟirukka ceytē kaḷavai nāṭuvatē nammai eṉṟu aḻukaiyum; aḻa pukkavāṟē, vāy vāy eṉṉumē. attālē bhayappaṭṭu accam ellām taṉ nōkkilē tōṟṟumpaṭi pārttukkoṇṭu niṟkum nilaiyum
children.translated_text: Even though He denies it, when she insists on investigating the theft — the crying; the moment He starts to cry, she says 'mouth! mouth!' (meaning 'hush!'). Frightened by that, He stands looking at her with all His fear showing in His gaze —

children.text: aṇi koḷ cem ciṟu vāy neḷippatuvum
children.translated_text: 'The quivering of the beautiful small red lips' —

children.text: piṉṉaiyum aḻāt’ irukkavum māṭṭāṉ. aḻavum māṭṭāṉ. aḻakiya tiruppavaḷattai neḷikkum attaṉaiyiṟē.
children.translated_text: Furthermore, He can neither stop crying nor properly cry. He merely quivers His beautiful coral lips — that is all.

children.text: toḻukaiyum
children.translated_text: 'The joining of palms' —

children.text: pōkk’ aṟṟār ceyyum ceyaliṟē. sāparādhar-āṉārkku aparādham pōkkumatu añjali eṉṉum iṭam tāṉ aṟint’ irukkumat’ākaiyālē añjaliyai paṇṇum āyttu.
children.translated_text: This is what those who have no other recourse do. Since those who have committed offenses know that the <s>añjali</s> (joined palms) removes offenses, He performs the <s>añjali</s>.

children.text: ivai kaṇṭa acōtai
children.translated_text: '<s>Yaśodā</s> who saw all these' —

children.text: ivaṟṟai aṅkē sākṣātkarittu kaṇṭa yaśodai pirāṭṭi
children.translated_text: <s>Yaśodā Pirāṭṭi</s> who directly witnessed all these there,

children.text: tollai iṉpatt’ iṟuti kaṇṭāḷē
children.translated_text: 'Saw the ultimate limit of ancient bliss!' —

children.text: paramapadattil niravadhiyāṉa anubhavattai sāvadhiyākkiṉavaḷiṟē. aṅkē ceṉṟu ellārum toḻa irukkumavaṉ tāṉ toḻukaiyālē aparicchinnamāṉa anubhavam paricchinnamāyttiṟē.
children.translated_text: She made finite the limitless experience of <s>Paramapadam</s> (the supreme abode). The one whom everyone goes there to worship — He Himself joins His palms, so the boundless experience becomes bounded.
Introduction — Eighth verse.

children.text: kuṉṟiṉāl kuṭai kavittatum kōla kuravai kōttatum kuṭam āṭṭum
children.translated_text: Holding the mountain as an umbrella, performing the beautiful <s>kuravai</s> dance, the pot-dance,

children.text: kaṉṟiṉāl viḷav’ eṟintatum kālāl kāḷiyaṉ talai mitittatum mutal ā
children.translated_text: Throwing the wood-apple fruit with the calf, trampling <s>Kāḷiya</s>'s heads with His feet — beginning with these,

children.text: veṉṟi cēr piḷḷai nal viḷaiyāṭṭam aṉaittilum aṅk’ eṉ uḷḷam uḷ kuḷira
children.translated_text: All the victorious child's wonderful play-acts — for my heart to be cooled within by all of them,

children.text: oṉṟum kaṇṭiṭa peṟṟilēṉ aṭiyēṉ kāṇum āṟ’ iṉi uṇṭ’ eṉil aruḷē
children.translated_text: I did not get to see even one! If there is still a way to see, please grant Your grace!

children.text: kuṉṟiṉāl kuṭai kavittatum
children.translated_text: 'Holding the mountain as an umbrella' —

children.text: iṭaiyarum pacukkaḷum tolaiyumpaṭiyāka indraṉ kalvarṣamāka varṣittapaṭiyālē malaiyai eṭuttu kuṭaiyāka dharittatum
children.translated_text: When <s>Indra</s> rained a storm of stones such that the cowherds and cows would perish, He lifted the mountain and held it as an umbrella,

children.text: kōla kuravai kōttatum
children.translated_text: 'Performing the beautiful <s>kuravai</s> dance' —

children.text: darśanīyamāṉa kuravai kūttilē śrīgopimārōṭu okka taṉṉaiyum kōttatum
children.translated_text: In the beautiful <s>kuravai</s> dance, He joined Himself together with the <s>Śrī Gopīs</s> (cowherd women),

children.text: kuṭam āṭṭum kaṉṟiṉāl viḷav’ eṟintatum
children.translated_text: 'The pot-dance, throwing the wood-apple fruit with the calf' —

children.text: oruvaṉ kaṉṟāy oruvaṉ viḷāvāy vanta iruvaraiyum cēra muṭittatuvum
children.translated_text: When one came disguised as a calf and another as a wood-apple tree, He destroyed them both together,

children.text: kālāl kāḷiyaṉ talai mitittatum mutal ā
children.translated_text: 'Trampling <s>Kāḷiya</s>'s heads with His feet' — beginning with these —

children.text: nāṉ ācaippaṭṭu peṟā tiruvaṭikaḷai koṇṭu āsuraprakṛtiyāṉa kāḷiyaṉ talaiyilē mitittatum mutalāka
children.translated_text: With the sacred feet that I longed for but could not obtain, He trampled upon the heads of <s>Kāḷiya</s> of demonic nature — beginning with such deeds,

children.text: veṉṟi cēr piḷḷai nal viḷaiyāṭṭam
children.translated_text: 'The victorious child's wonderful play-acts' —

children.text: vīrappāṭṭukkum mauḍhyattukkum cērnt’ irukkiṟa atimanoharamāṉa
children.translated_text: Exceedingly captivating acts that combine heroism and childish innocence,

children.text: aṉaittilum aṅk’ eṉ uḷḷam uḷ kuḷira oṉṟum kaṇṭiṭa peṟṟilēṉ aṭiyēṉ
children.translated_text: 'I did not get to see even one of them all, for my heart to be cooled within' —

children.text: ivai kāṇkaiyē prayojanamāka irukkiṟa nāṉ oṉṟum kāṇa peṟṟilēṉ.
children.translated_text: I, for whom seeing these is the very purpose of existence, did not get to see even one.

children.text: kāṇum āṟ’ iṉi uṇṭ’ eṉil aruḷē
children.translated_text: 'If there is still a way to see, please grant Your grace!' —

children.text: nī niṉaittāl ceyya oṇṇātat’ illai. nāṉ itai kāṇumpaṭi aruḷa vēṇum.
children.translated_text: There is nothing You cannot do if You will it. Please grant the grace that I may see this.

children.text: vañcam mēviya neñc’ uṭai pēycci varaṇṭu nār naramp’ eḻa karint’ ukka
children.translated_text: The demoness with a deceitful heart — drained, dried to sinew and nerve, charred and fallen —

children.text: nañcam ār taru cuḻi mulai antō cuvaittu nī aruḷ ceytu vaḷarntāy
children.translated_text: Alas! You tasted and sucked the poison-filled, swirling breast, and by Your grace grew up!

children.text: kañcaṉ nāḷ kavar karu
m
mukil entāy kaṭaippaṭṭēṉ veṟitē mulai cumantu
children.translated_text: Cloud-hued Lord! I am reduced to nothing, having carried my breasts in vain!
<s>Kaṃsa</s>'s days You seized — O dark

children.text: tañcam mēl oṉṟ’ ilēṉ uynt’ iruntēṉ takkatē nalla tāyai peṟṟāyē
children.translated_text: I have no refuge beyond this — I survived, and You obtained a fitting good mother!

children.text: vañcam mēviya neñc’ uṭai pēycci
children.translated_text: 'The demoness with a deceitful heart' —

children.text: ivaṉai kaṇṭāl cevviyarāka irukkaviṟē kaṭavatu; kaṇṭuvaittu vañcanattilē poruntiṉa pūtanai
children.translated_text: Upon seeing Him, one ought to be filled with devotion; but <s>Pūtanā</s>, having seen Him, resorted to deceit,

children.text: varaṇṭu nār naramp’ eḻa karint’ ukka
children.translated_text: 'Drained, dried to sinew and nerve, charred and fallen' —

children.text: māṃsamum uḷ uṇṭāṉa utiramum mulaippālōṭē koḻittukkoṇṭu puṟappaṭa, śeṣitta uṭampu nār narampum tōlum āmpaṭi karint’ ukka
children.translated_text: The flesh and the blood within, along with the breast milk, flowed out, and the remaining body became nothing but sinew, nerves, and skin — charred and fallen,

children.text: nañcam ār taru cuḻi mulai antō cuvaittu nī aruḷ ceytu vaḷarntāy
children.translated_text: 'Alas! You tasted the poison-filled, swirling breast, and by Your grace grew up!' —

children.text: kiṭanta āśrayattaiyum iḻakkavaṟṟāy mikka nañcai uṭaittāy, kopattaiyum uṭaittāy irukkiṟa mulaiyai dhārakamāka uṇṭ’ aruḷi vaḷarntāy.
children.translated_text: The breast that was such as to destroy even the body it rested upon, full of great poison and full of rage — You drank it as sustenance and graciously grew up.

children.text: kañcaṉ nāḷ kavar karu
m
mukil entāy
children.translated_text: 'cloud-hued Lord!' —
'<s>Kaṃsa</s>'s days You seized' — the dark

children.text: kaṃsaṉuṭaiya āyussai apaharittu attālē ēṟiṉa pukarai uṭaiya vaṭivai uṭaiyaiyāy, a- ceyalālum vaṭivaḻakālum eṉṉai eḻutikkoṇṭavaṉē!
children.translated_text: O You who seized <s>Kaṃsa</s>'s life and thereby have a form radiant with the resulting glory, and who by that deed and bodily beauty claimed me as Your own!

children.text: kaṭaippaṭṭēṉ veṟitē mulai cumantu
children.translated_text: 'I am reduced to nothing, having carried my breasts in vain' —

children.text: mulai neṟittapōtu uṇpāṉ oru piḷḷaiyai peṟṟuvaittu peṟātē vyarthamā irukkaiyālē ettaṉaiyēṉum taṇṇiyārilum tāḻntēṉ.
children.translated_text: Having given birth to a child to nurse when the breasts swelled, yet not having obtained Him — because of this futility, I have become lower than the lowest.

children.text: tañcam mēl oṉṟ’ ilēṉ uynt’
children.translated_text: 'I have no refuge beyond this — I survived' —

children.text: vēṟu dhārakar illāmaiyālē prāṇaṉkaḷai varunti dharitt’ iruntēṉ.
children.translated_text: Having no other sustainer, I painfully held on to my life-breaths and survived.

children.text: takkatē nalla tāyai peṟṟāyē
children.translated_text: 'You obtained a fitting good mother!' —

children.text: mulaippāl apekṣitam āṉapōtu uṉakku tarukaikku nalla tāyai peṟṟāyē.
children.translated_text: When You desired breast milk, You obtained a good mother to give it to You.

children.text: mallai mā nakarkk’ iṟaiyavaṉ taṉṉai vāṉ celutti vant’ īṅṅaṉam māyatt’
children.translated_text: Having sent the lord of the great prosperous city to heaven, coming here — the boundless

children.text: ellai il piḷḷai ceyvaṉa kāṇā teyva tēvaki pulampiya pulampal
children.translated_text: Childish deeds of the wondrous One she could not see — the lament that divine <s>Devakī</s> lamented,

children.text: kolli kāvalaṉ māl aṭi muṭi mēl kōlam ām kulacēkaraṉ coṉṉa
children.translated_text: The king of <s>Kolli</s>, at the head and crown of <s>Māl</s>'s (the Lord's) feet — the beautiful <s>Kulacēkaraṉ</s> composed,

children.text: nal icai tamiḻ mālai vallārkaḷ naṇṇuvār ollai nāraṇaṉ ulakē
children.translated_text: Those who master this garland of good-sounding Tamil will swiftly attain the world of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>!

children.text: nigamattil
mallai mā nakarkk’ iṟaiyavaṉ taṉṉai
children.translated_text: 'Having sent the lord of the great prosperous city' —

children.text: mikka sampattai uṭaiya śrīmathuraikku nirvāhakaṉāṉa kaṃsaṉai tāṉ kai toṭṭu muṭikkaiyālē vīrasvargattilē pōkaṭṭu
children.translated_text: Having personally destroyed <s>Kaṃsa</s>, the ruler of greatly prosperous <s>Śrī Mathurā</s>, thereby sending him to the heaven of warriors (<s>vīrasvarga</s>),

children.text: vant’ īṅṅaṉam, ityādi
children.translated_text: 'Having come here,' etc. —

children.text: kaṃsavadham paṇṇi iṅkē vantu kiṭṭiṉa āścaryaceṣṭitaṅkaḷukku avadhi iṉṟiyilē irukkiṟa kṛṣṇaṉuṭaiya bālaceṣṭitaṅkaḷai kāṇāmaiyālē
children.translated_text: Having performed the slaying of <s>Kaṃsa</s> and coming here — because she could not see the limitlessly wondrous childhood deeds (<s>bālaceṣṭita</s>) of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,

children.text: teyva tēvaki pulampiya pulampal
children.translated_text: 'The lament that divine <s>Devakī</s> lamented' —

children.text: ivaṉ ceṣṭitaṅkaḷai anubhavikka peṟāta iḻavaiyum uṭaiyaḷāy ivaṉai piḷḷaiyāka peṟukaikk’ īṭāṉa bhāgyattai paṇṇiṉa devakiyār pulampiya pācurattai
children.translated_text: The verses lamented by <s>Devakī</s> who bore the loss of not experiencing His childhood deeds yet had the great fortune (<s>bhāgya</s>) to bear Him as her child,

children.text: kolli kāvalaṉ
children.translated_text: 'The king of <s>Kolli</s>' —

children.text: kolli eṉkiṟa paṭaivīṭṭukku nirvāhakar-āṉavar
children.translated_text: The ruler of the fortress called <s>Kolli</s>,

children.text: māl aṭi muṭi mēl kōlam-ām kulacēkaraṉ
children.translated_text: '<s>Kulacēkaraṉ</s>, beautiful with the Lord's feet upon his crown' —

children.text: sarveśvaraṉ tiruvaṭikaḷai tamakku muṭi-mēl mālaiyāka uṭaiya perumāḷ
children.translated_text: <s>Perumāḷ</s> who has the feet of the Lord of all (<s>Sarveśvara</s>) as a garland upon his crown,

children.text: coṉṉa nal icai tamiḻ mālai vallārkaḷ
children.translated_text: 'The good-sounding Tamil garland he composed — those who master it' —

children.text: aḻakiya icaiyōṭē kūṭiṉa tamiḻ toṭai vallavarkaḷ
children.translated_text: Those who master the Tamil garland composed with beautiful melody,

children.text: naṇṇuvār ollai nāraṇaṉ ulakē
children.translated_text: 'Will swiftly attain the world of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>!' —

children.text: iṅkē iruntu avatārattil ekadeśattai anubhavikka ācaippaṭṭu atu kiṭaiyātē iruntu pulampātē, ubhayavibhūtināyakaṉai paramapadattilē nityānubhavam paṇṇa peṟuvārkaḷ.
children.translated_text: Without remaining here longing to experience a partial aspect of the incarnation and lamenting at not obtaining it, they will attain eternal experience of the Lord of both realms (<s>ubhayavibhūtināyaka</s>) in <s>Paramapadam</s>.
In the concluding verse —

children.text: avatārikai - devakiyār iḻanta iḻavu mātramēyō? śrīkausalaiyārāy tāṉ kāṇa peṟṟēṉō? eṉṟu, a- samakālattil tām iḻakkaiyālē avaḷ anubhavattai tiru kaṇṇapurattilē anubhavikkiṟār.
children.translated_text: Introduction — Is it only the loss that <s>Devakī</s> suffered? Did I, as <s>Śrī Kausalyā</s>, get to see? — Thus, since he too missed it at that same time, he experiences her experience at <s>Tiru Kaṇṇapuram</s>.

children.text: maṉṉu pukaḻ kaucalai taṉ maṇi vayiṟu vāyttavaṉē
children.translated_text: O You who were worthy of the jeweled womb of <s>Kausalyā</s> of enduring fame!

children.text: teṉ ilaṅkai kōṉ muṭikaḷ cintuvittāy cem poṉ cēr
children.translated_text: O You who scattered the crowns of the king of southern <s>Laṅkā</s>! In the fine gold-adorned

children.text: kaṉṉi nal mā matiḷ puṭai cūḻ kaṇapuratt’ eṉ karumaṇiyē
children.translated_text: <s>Kaṇapuram</s> surrounded by beautiful great impregnable walls — O my dark jewel!

children.text: eṉ uṭaiya iṉ amutē irākavaṉē tālēlō
children.translated_text: O my own sweet nectar! O <s>Rāghava</s>! Lullaby!

children.text: maṉṉu pukaḻ kaucalai taṉ maṇi vayiṟu vāyttavaṉē
children.translated_text: 'O You worthy of the jeweled womb of <s>Kausalyā</s> of enduring fame!' —

children.text: sarveśvaraṉai piḷḷaiyāka peṟṟāḷ eṉṟa nilainiṉṟa pukaḻai uṭaiya śrīkausalaiyāruṭaiya aḻakiya vayiṟṟil avaḷukku piḷḷai āka peṟṟavaṉē!
children.translated_text: O You who were born as a child in the beautiful womb of <s>Śrī Kausalyā</s>, who has the enduring fame of having borne the Lord of all as her son!

children.text: teṉ ilaṅkai kōṉ muṭikaḷ cintuvittāy
children.translated_text: 'O You who scattered the crowns of the king of southern <s>Laṅkā</s>!' —

children.text: ilaṅkaikku nirvāhakaṉāṉa irāvaṇaṉuṭaiya muṭikaḷ pattaiyum tiru caraṅkaḷālē citaṟa paṇṇiṉavaṉē! i- tirumoḻiyiṟē rāmāvatārattil mikai; ākaiyālē i- cantai.
children.translated_text: O You who shattered all ten crowns of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, the ruler of <s>Laṅkā</s>, with sacred arrows! This <s>Tirumoḻi</s> itself emphasizes the <s>Rāmāvatāra</s>; hence this theme.

children.text: cem poṉ cēr kaṉṉi nal mā matiḷ puṭai cūḻ kaṇapuratt’ eṉ karumaṇiyē
children.translated_text: 'In <s>Kaṇapuram</s> surrounded by fine gold-adorned, beautiful great impregnable walls — O my dark jewel!' —

children.text: aḻiv’ illāta matiḷālē cūḻnta tiru kaṇṇapurattilē eṉakku dṛṣṭikku nirvāhakaṉāy niṟkiṟavaṉē!
children.translated_text: O You who stand in <s>Tiru Kaṇṇapuram</s> surrounded by indestructible walls, as the sustainer of my vision!

children.text: eṉ uṭaiya iṉ amutē
children.translated_text: 'O my own sweet nectar!' —

children.text: devarkaḷ amṛtam pōl aṉṟiyē eṉakku amṛtam-āṉavaṉē!
children.translated_text: O You who are nectar to me, unlike the nectar of the <s>devas</s>!

children.text: irākavaṉē tālēlō
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Rāghava</s>! Lullaby!' —

children.text: devarkaḷuṭaiya amṛtam uppuccāṟiṟē; at’ aṉṟiṟē ivaruṭaiya amṛtam irukkiṟa paṭi.
children.translated_text: The nectar of the <s>devas</s> is merely salt-water; unlike that is this one's nectar.

children.text: puṇṭarika
m
malar ataṉ mēl puvaṉi ellām paṭaittavaṉē
children.translated_text: O You who created all the worlds upon the lotus flower!
Upon the lotus

children.text: tiṇ tiṟalāḷ tāṭakai taṉ uram uruva cilai vaḷaittāy
children.translated_text: O You who bent the bow piercing the chest of <s>Tāṭakā</s> of firm strength!

children.text: kaṇṭavar tam maṉam vaḻaṅkum kaṇapuratt’ eṉ karumaṇiyē
children.translated_text: In <s>Kaṇapuram</s> that captivates the hearts of all who behold it — O my dark jewel!

children.text: eṇ ticaiyum āḷ uṭaiyāy irākavaṉē tālēlō
children.translated_text: O You who have servants in all eight directions! O <s>Rāghava</s>! Lullaby!

children.text: puṇṭarikam, ityādi
children.translated_text: 'Upon the lotus,' etc. —

children.text: tiru nābhīkamalattilē lokam ellām sṛṣṭittavaṉē!
children.translated_text: O You who created all the worlds upon the sacred lotus of the navel (<s>nābhīkamala</s>)!

children.text: tiṇ tiṟal ityādi
children.translated_text: 'Of firm strength,' etc. —

children.text: sṛṣṭikkumat’ aṉṟiyē, payirai ceytu kaḷai piṭuṅkumā pōlē, āsuravargattai pōkkiṉa paṭi, tiṇṇiya tiṟalai uṭaiyaḷāṉa tāḍakai urattai maṟupāṭ’ uruva villai vaḷaittavaṉē!
children.translated_text: Not only creating but also, like one who cultivates the crop and pulls out the weeds, removing the demonic race — O You who bent the bow so as to pierce through the chest of <s>Tāṭakā</s> of firm strength!

children.text: kaṇṭavar tam maṉam vaḻaṅkum kaṇapuratt’ eṉ karumaṇiyē
children.translated_text: 'In <s>Kaṇapuram</s> that captivates the hearts of all who behold it — O my dark jewel!' —

children.text: kaṇṭavarkaḷ neñcukaḷai tāṅkaḷum icaintu koṭukkumpaṭi tiru kaṇṇapurattilē niṟkiṟavaṉē!
children.translated_text: O You who stand in <s>Tiru Kaṇṇapuram</s> such that those who behold You willingly surrender their hearts!

children.text: eṇ ticaiyum āḷ uṭaiyāy irākavaṉē tālēlō
children.translated_text: 'O You who have servants in all eight directions! O <s>Rāghava</s>! Lullaby!' —

children.text: avatārattil piṟpāṭarāṉa eṭṭu dikkil uḷḷārum vantu vāḻumpaṭi niṉṟavaṉē!
children.translated_text: O You who stood such that those in all eight directions who missed the incarnation come and thrive!

children.text: koṅku mali karum kuḻalāḷ kaucalai taṉ kula
m
matalāy
children.translated_text: Pillar of her clan,
<s>Kausalyā</s> of fragrant, dark tresses — the

children.text: taṅku perum pukaḻ caṉakaṉ tiru marukā tācaratī
children.translated_text: The sacred son-in-law of <s>Janaka</s> of great enduring fame — O <s>Dāśarathi</s>!

children.text: kaṅkaiyilum tīrttam mali kaṇapuratt’ eṉ karumaṇiyē
children.translated_text: In <s>Kaṇapuram</s> richer in sacred waters than the <s>Gaṅgā</s> — O my dark jewel!

children.text: eṅkaḷ kulatt’ iṉ amutē irākavaṉē tālēlō
children.translated_text: O sweet nectar of our clan, O <s>Rāghava</s>! <s>Tālēlō</s> (lullaby)!

children.text: koṅku mali karum kuḻalāḷ kaucalai taṉ kula
m
matalāy
children.translated_text: the one who uplifts—
The scion of the clan of <s>Kausalyā</s> with fragrant dark tresses—

children.text: mikka parimaḷattai puṟappaṭa viṭukiṟa iruṇṭa kuḻalai uṭaiya śrīkausalaiyāruṭaiya kulattukku uddhārakaṉāṉavaṉē!
children.translated_text: O You who are the redeemer of the clan of <s>Śrī Kausalyā</s> who has dark tresses that release abundant fragrance!

children.text: taṅku perum pukaḻ caṉakaṉ tiru marukā
children.translated_text: "the illustrious son-in-law of <s>Janaka</s> of great and enduring fame"—

children.text: pukaḻ eṉṟu piṟantavai ellām taṅkumpaṭi periya pukaḻai uṭaiya śrījanakarājaṉukku marumakaṉ-āṉavaṉē!
children.translated_text: O You who became the son-in-law of <s>Śrī Janaka Rāja</s>, who possesses such great fame that all that is born as fame abides in him!

children.text: tācaratī
children.translated_text: "O son of <s>Daśaratha</s>"—

children.text: avaṉōṭē sadṛśasaṃbandham paṇṇalāmpaṭiyāṉa piṟappai uṭaiyavaṉē!
children.translated_text: O You who have a birth worthy of forming an equal relationship with him!

children.text: kaṅkaiyilum tīrttam mali kaṇapuratt’ eṉ karumaṇiyē
children.translated_text: "O my dark gem of <s>Kaṇapuram</s> (Tirukkaṇṇapuram), more sacred than the <s>Gaṅgā</s>!"—

children.text: kādācitkasambandhattāl varum śuddhiyogamiṟē gaṅgaikk’ uḷḷatu; saṃbandham nityam-ākaiyālē atilum śuddhi mikk’ irukkiṟa tiru poykaiyai uṭaiya tirukkaṇṇapurattilē sulabhaṉāṉavaṉē!
children.translated_text: The <s>Gaṅgā</s> has only the purifying power that comes from an occasional connection; since the connection here is eternal, O You who have made Yourself accessible at <s>Tirukkaṇṇapuram</s> which has a sacred pond surpassing the <s>Gaṅgā</s> in purity!

children.text: eṅkaḷ kulatt’ iṉ amutē irākavaṉē tālēlō
children.translated_text: "O sweet nectar of our clan, O <s>Rāghava</s>! <s>Tālēlō</s>!"—

children.text: rājavaṃśattukkāka bhogyabhūtaṉāṉavaṉē!
children.translated_text: O You who are the object of enjoyment for the royal dynasty!

children.text: tāmarai mēl ayaṉ avaṉai paṭaittavaṉē tayarataṉ taṉ
children.translated_text: "O You who created <s>Ayaṉ</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) upon the lotus, and who created that one! O son of <s>Daśaratha</s>,"

children.text: mā matalāy maitili taṉ maṇavāḷā vaṇṭ’ iṉaṅkaḷ
children.translated_text: "O great scion, O bridegroom of <s>Maithilī</s> (Sītā)! Where swarms of bees"

children.text: kāmaraṅkaḷ icai pāṭum kaṇapuratt’ eṉ karumaṇiyē
children.translated_text: "sing melodies of love in <s>Kaṇapuram</s>, O my dark gem!"

children.text: ē maruvum cilai valavā irākavaṉē tālēlō
children.translated_text: "O wielder of the ever-fitting bow, O <s>Rāghava</s>! <s>Tālēlō</s>!"

children.text: tāmarai mēl ayaṉ avaṉai paṭaittavaṉē
children.translated_text: "O You who created <s>Ayaṉ</s> upon the lotus, and who created that one"—

children.text: kīḻ coṉṉa sṛṣṭi piṉ nāṭṭiṉapaṭi
children.translated_text: as the creation mentioned earlier was subsequently established,

children.text: tayarataṉ taṉ mā matalāy
children.translated_text: "O great scion of <s>Daśaratha</s>"—

children.text: aṟupatiṉāyiram āṇṭu malaṭu niṉṟa cakravartiyiṉ uṭaiya malaṭu tīra piṟantavaṉē!
children.translated_text: O You who were born to end the barrenness of <s>Cakravartī</s> (Emperor Daśaratha) who had stood childless for sixty thousand years!

children.text: maitili taṉ maṇavāḷā
children.translated_text: "O bridegroom of <s>Maithilī</s>"—

children.text: piḷḷaipeṟṟa ēṟṟattiṉ mēlum, piṟappil vanta ēṟṟattukku mēlē, yasya sā janakātmajā eṉṟu pirāṭṭiyai uṉakk’ eṉṟu iṭṭu piṟanta mēṉmaiyai uṭaiyavaṉē!
children.translated_text: Beyond the glory of having a son, beyond the glory that came through birth, He possesses the greatness of being born such that <s>Pirāṭṭi</s> (Sītā) was given to Him, as declared: '<s>yasya sā Janakātmajā</s>' (she, the daughter of <s>Janaka</s>, is his)!

children.text: kāmaraṅkaḷ icai pāṭum kaṇapuratt’ eṉ karumaṇiyē
children.translated_text: "O my dark gem of <s>Kaṇapuram</s> where bees sing melodies of love!"—

children.text: vaṇṭ’ iṉaṅkaḷ kāmaram eṉkiṟa paṇṇilē icai pāṭukiṟa tiru kaṇṇapurattilē sannihitaṉāṉavaṉē!
children.translated_text: O You who are present at <s>Tirukkaṇṇapuram</s> where swarms of bees sing in the <s>kāmara</s> musical mode!

children.text: ē- maruvum cilai valavā irākavaṉē tālēlō
children.translated_text: "O wielder of the ever-fitting bow, O <s>Rāghava</s>! <s>Tālēlō</s>!"—

children.text: ārēṉum piṭikkilum ēvilē mūṭṭum śrīśārṅgattai uṉ niṉaivilē varumpaṭi celutta vallavaṉē!
children.translated_text: O You who can wield the <s>Śrī Śārṅga</s> (divine bow) that strikes its target the moment anyone grasps it, directing it by Your will alone!

children.text: pār āḷum paṭar celvam parata nampikkē aruḷi
children.translated_text: "Having graciously bestowed upon <s>Bharata Nampi</s> (the trustworthy Bharata) the expansive wealth of ruling the earth,"

children.text: ārā aṉp’ iḷaiyavaṉōṭ’ arum kāṉam aṭaintavaṉē
children.translated_text: "with insatiable love, together with the younger prince (<s>Iḷaiyavaṉ</s>, Lakṣmaṇa), He entered the difficult forest,"

children.text: cīr āḷum varai mārpā tirukkaṇṇapuratt’ aracē
children.translated_text: "O You of mountain-like chest ruled by glory! O King of <s>Tirukkaṇṇapuram</s>!"

children.text: tār āḷum nīḷ muṭi eṉ tācaratī tālēlō
children.translated_text: "O my son of <s>Daśaratha</s> with tall crown encircled by garlands! <s>Tālēlō</s>!"

children.text: pār āḷum paṭar celvam parata nampikkē aruḷi
children.translated_text: "Having graciously bestowed upon <s>Bharata Nampi</s> the expansive wealth of ruling the earth"—

children.text: bhūmi parapp’ aṭaiya āḷa kaṭavatāṉa periya sampattai pāratantrya-guṇaṅkaḷāl pūrṇaṉāy irukkiṟa śrībharatāḻvāṉukkē aruḷi
children.translated_text: having graciously given exclusively to <s>Śrī Bharatāḻvāṉ</s> (Bharata), who is full of the qualities of subordination (<s>pāratantrya</s>), the great wealth of ruling the entire expanse of the earth,

children.text: ārā aṉp’ iḷaiyavaṉōṭ’ arum kāṉam aṭaintavaṉē
children.translated_text: "with insatiable love, together with the younger prince, He entered the difficult forest"—

children.text: avaṉai pōlē niyamitta iṭattil pirint’ irukka māṭṭātē
children.translated_text: unlike him (Bharata) who, when commanded, could not bear to remain separated,

children.text: kuruṣva māṃ
children.translated_text: "<s>kuruṣva mām</s>" (make use of me)—

children.text: eṉṉum iḷaiyaperumāḷōṭē kūṭi, oruvarālum iyaṅka oṇṇāta duṣṭasattva-pracuramāṉa kāṭṭilē praveśittavaṉē!
children.translated_text: together with <s>Iḷaiya Perumāḷ</s> (Lakṣmaṇa) who said thus, He entered the forest that was impenetrable for anyone, teeming with fierce creatures!

children.text: cīr āḷum varai mārpā
children.translated_text: "O You of mountain-like chest ruled by glory"—

children.text: vīraśrī nirvāhakaṉ-āṉatuvum
children.translated_text: He who is the bearer of heroic splendor (<s>vīraśrī</s>),

children.text: tār āḷum nīḷ muṭi eṉ tācaratī tālēlō
children.translated_text: "O my son of <s>Daśaratha</s> with tall crown encircled by garlands! <s>Tālēlō</s>!"—

children.text: ādhirājyasūcakamāṉa mālaiyōṭu kūṭiṉa muṭiyai uṭaiya cakravarti tirumakaṉē!
children.translated_text: O son of <s>Cakravartī</s> (the Emperor), possessing the crown joined with the garland that signifies supreme sovereignty (<s>ādhirājya</s>)!

children.text: cuṟṟam ellām piṉ toṭara tol kāṉam aṭaintavaṉē
children.translated_text: "He who entered the ancient forest with all His retinue following behind,"

children.text: aṟṟavarkaṭk’ arum maruntē ayōtti nakarkk’ atipatiyē
children.translated_text: "O rare medicine for those in distress! O Lord of the city of <s>Ayodhyā</s>!"

children.text: kaṟṟavarkaḷ tām vāḻum kaṇapuratt’ eṉ karumaṇiyē
children.translated_text: "O my dark gem of <s>Kaṇapuram</s> where the learned dwell!"

children.text: ciṟṟavai taṉ col koṇṭa cīrāmā tālēlō
children.translated_text: "O <s>Śrī Rāma</s> who accepted the words of His stepmother! <s>Tālēlō</s>!"

children.text: cuṟṟam ellām piṉ toṭara tol kāṉam aṭaintavaṉē
children.translated_text: "He who entered the ancient forest with all His retinue following behind"—

children.text: ellārum pōṉārkaḷō, ciṟit’ iṭam pōy mīṇṭār eṉṟ’ aṉṟō colliṟṟu? eṉṉa -
children.translated_text: Did not everyone go and then turn back after going a short distance? To this—

children.text: ahaṃ sarvaṃ kariṣyāmi
children.translated_text: "<s>ahaṃ sarvaṃ kariṣyāmi</s>" (I shall do everything)—

children.text: eṉṟu coṉṉa ellā aṭimaiyum ceyyum iḷaiyaperumāḷ kūṭa pōkaiyālē ellā bandhukkaḷum kūṭa pōṉārkaḷ-āyttiṟē eṉṟu emperumāṉār aruḷicceytār.
children.translated_text: <s>Iḷaiya Perumāḷ</s> (Lakṣmaṇa) who said thus and would perform all service went along, and so it was as if all kinsmen went along—thus <s>Emperumāṉār</s> (Rāmānuja) graciously declared.

children.text: aṟṟavarkaṭk’ arum maruntē
children.translated_text: "O rare medicine for those in distress"—

children.text: garbhabhūtāstapodhanāḥ
children.translated_text: "<s>garbhabhūtās tapodhanāḥ</s>" (the ascetics who were like His own progeny)—

children.text: eṉṟ’ irukkumavarkaḷukku
children.translated_text: for those who are as described thus,

children.text: arum maruntē
children.translated_text: "rare medicine"—

children.text: api ahaṃ jīvitaṃ jahyām
children.translated_text: "<s>api ahaṃ jīvitaṃ jahyām</s>" (I would even give up My life)—

children.text: eṉṟ’ irukkum aru maruntāṉavaṉē!
children.translated_text: O You who are such a rare medicine as declared thus!

children.text: ayōtti nakarkk’ atipatiyē
children.translated_text: "O Lord of the city of <s>Ayodhyā</s>"—

children.text: paramapadam pōlē ayodhyaiyiṟē itukku pēr; appaṭippaṭṭa paṭaivīṭṭukku adhipatiyāṉavaṉē!
children.translated_text: Just as <s>Paramapadam</s> (the supreme abode) is known by its name, so too <s>Ayodhyā</s> is named thus; O Lord of such a great citadel!

children.text: kaṟṟavarkaḷ tām vāḻum kaṇapuratt’ eṉ karumaṇiyē
children.translated_text: "O my dark gem of <s>Kaṇapuram</s> where the learned dwell!"—

children.text: kaṟpatu oru deśattilē iruntu oru kālattilēyāy. prāpyavastuvai kiṭṭi anubhavippatu oru deśaviśeṣattilē ākāmē, prāpyavastu teṟku dikkilē kāṇalāmpaṭi tiru kaṇṇapurattil niṉṟavaṉē!
children.translated_text: Learning happens in one place at one time. But experiencing the object to be attained need not be limited to a special place—O You who stand at <s>Tirukkaṇṇapuram</s> where the object to be attained can be seen in the southern direction!

children.text: ciṟṟavai taṉ col koṇṭa cīrāmā tālēlō
children.translated_text: "O <s>Śrī Rāma</s> who accepted the words of His stepmother! <s>Tālēlō</s>!"—

children.text: peṟṟa tāyārāṉa nāṉ ummai piriyil dhariyēṉ eṉṟu śrīkausalaiyār piṉ toṭara ceytēyum māṟṟuttāyāṉa kaikeyi collu māṟātē vaṉattē pōntavaṉē!
children.translated_text: even as <s>Śrī Kausalyā</s>, His birth-mother, followed behind saying 'I cannot endure separation from You,' He went to the forest without going against the word of <s>Kaikeyī</s>, the stepmother!

children.text: āliṉ ilai pālakaṉ āy aṉṟ’ ulakam uṇṭavaṉē
children.translated_text: "O You who as an infant on a banyan leaf consumed the worlds long ago!"

children.text: vāliyai koṉṟ’ arac’ iḷaiya vāṉarattukk’ aḷittavaṉē
children.translated_text: "O You who slew <s>Vāli</s> and gave the kingdom to the younger monkey prince!"

children.text: kāliṉ maṇi karai alaikkum kaṇapuratt’ eṉ karumaṇiyē
children.translated_text: "O my dark gem of <s>Kaṇapuram</s> where jeweled anklets of the river wash against the bank!"

children.text: āli nakarkk’ atipatiyē ayōtti maṉē tālēlō
children.translated_text: "O Lord of <s>Āli</s> city! O King of <s>Ayodhyā</s>! <s>Tālēlō</s>!"

children.text: āliṉ ilai pālakaṉ āy aṉṟ’ ulakam uṇṭavaṉē
children.translated_text: "O You who as an infant on a banyan leaf consumed the worlds long ago"—

children.text: lokattai ellām tiru vayiṟṟilē vaittu oru bhavaṉāṉa ālilaiyilē, atu tāṉ viñcum eṉṉumpaṭi kaṇ vaḷarnt’ aruḷiṉa aghaṭitaghaṭanāsāmarthyattai uṭaiyavaṉē!
children.translated_text: O You who possess the power of accomplishing the impossible (<s>aghaṭitaghaṭanāsāmarthya</s>)—having placed all the worlds in Your divine belly, You graciously slept on a single banyan leaf, in a manner that made even that seem insufficient!

children.text: vāliyai koṉṟ’ arac’ iḷaiya vāṉarattukk’ aḷittavaṉē
children.translated_text: "O You who slew <s>Vāli</s> and gave the kingdom to the younger monkey prince"—

children.text: vāli, ārai tuṇaiyāka nī vijayam paṇṇiṉa rāvaṇaṉai vālilē kaṭṭi vaittāṉ? a- vāliyai koṉṟu avaṉukku iṭaintu parvataguhaikaḷilē kiṭakkiṟa mahārājarkku vānararājyattai koṭuttavaṉē!
children.translated_text: <s>Vāli</s>—with whose tail's help did you achieve your victory over <s>Rāvaṇa</s>? He slew that <s>Vāli</s> and gave the monkey kingdom to <s>Mahārāja</s> (Sugrīva) who lay hiding in mountain caves, oppressed by him!

children.text: kāliṉ maṇi, ityādi
children.translated_text: "jeweled anklets of the river" and so forth—

children.text: kāṟṟālē uḷḷu kiṭakkiṟa ratnaṅkaḷai karaiyilē ēṟiṭum eṉṉutal
children.translated_text: it means that the current casts up the gems lying within onto the bank,

children.text: āli nakarkk’ atipatiyē
children.translated_text: "O Lord of <s>Āli</s> city"—

children.text: tiru ālikku nirvāhakaṉ-āṉavaṉē! vāliyai koṉṟu āli-taṉṉai tuṇaiyāka koḷḷa peṟṟatē!
children.translated_text: O You who became the ruler of <s>Tiruvāli</s>! Having slain <s>Vāli</s>, He gained <s>Āli</s> itself as His ally!

children.text: malai ataṉāl aṇai kaṭṭi matiḷ ilaṅkai aḻittavaṉē
children.translated_text: "O You who built a bridge with mountains and destroyed the fortified <s>Laṅkā</s>!"

children.text: alai kaṭalai kaṭaint’ amararkk’ amut’ aruḷi ceytavaṉē
children.translated_text: "O You who churned the surging ocean and graciously bestowed nectar upon the immortals!"

children.text: kalai valavar tām vāḻum kaṇapuratt’ eṉ karumaṇiyē
children.translated_text: "O my dark gem of <s>Kaṇapuram</s> where masters of the arts dwell!"

children.text: cilai valavā cēvakaṉē cīrāmā tālēlō
children.translated_text: "O wielder of the bow! O warrior! O <s>Śrī Rāma</s>! <s>Tālēlō</s>!"

children.text: malai ataṉāl aṇai kaṭṭi matiḷ ilaṅkai aḻittavaṉē
children.translated_text: "O You who built a bridge with mountains and destroyed the fortified <s>Laṅkā</s>"—

children.text: nilattilē vara malaiyai koṇṭu araṇāṉa kaṭalil aṇaiyāka kaṭṭi, nīr tāṉum mikai eṉṉumpaṭiyāka araṇai uṭaittāṉa laṅkaiyai mūlaiyaṭiyē vaḻi pōkkiṉavaṉē!
children.translated_text: O You who brought a mountain onto the land and built it as a bridge across the fortified ocean, and demolished <s>Laṅkā</s> with its defenses from its very foundations, such that even the water seemed inadequate!

children.text: alai kaṭalai kaṭaint’ amararkk’ amut’ aruḷi ceytavaṉē
children.translated_text: "O You who churned the surging ocean and graciously bestowed nectar upon the immortals"—

children.text: agādhamāṉa samudrattai kaṭaintu amṛtattai vāṅki, asurarkaḷ kaiyilē devarkaḷ cāvātapaṭi, avarkaḷukku koṭuttavaṉē!
children.translated_text: O You who churned the fathomless ocean, obtained the <s>amṛta</s> (nectar), and gave it to the <s>deva</s>-s (gods) so that they would not perish at the hands of the <s>asura</s>-s (demons)!

children.text: kalai valavar tām vāḻum kaṇapuratt’ eṉ karumaṇiyē
children.translated_text: "O my dark gem of <s>Kaṇapuram</s> where masters of the arts dwell"—

children.text: sakalavidyāsthalaṅkaḷum kaivantirukkumavarkaḷ uṉṉai anubhavikkum tiru kaṇṇapurattilē sannihitaṉ-āṉavaṉē!
children.translated_text: O You who are present at <s>Tirukkaṇṇapuram</s> where those who have mastered all branches of learning come to experience You!

children.text: cilai valavā
children.translated_text: "O wielder of the bow"—

children.text: śrīśārṅgam kaivantirukkumavaṉē!
children.translated_text: O You in whose hand the <s>Śrī Śārṅga</s> (divine bow) rests!

children.text: cēvakaṉē ityādi
children.translated_text: "O warrior" and so forth—

children.text: atutāṉ mikai eṉṉumpaṭiyāṉa vīrappāṭṭai uṭaiyavaṉē!
children.translated_text: O You who possess such valor that even the bow seems insufficient!

children.text: taḷai aviḻum naṟum kuñci tayarataṉ taṉ kula matalāy
children.translated_text: "O scion of <s>Daśaratha</s>'s clan, with loosening, fragrant baby curls,"

children.text: vaḷaiya oru cilai ataṉāl matiḷ ilaṅkai aḻittavaṉē
children.translated_text: "O You who with a single curved bow destroyed the fortified <s>Laṅkā</s>!"

children.text: kaḷai kaḻunīr maruṅk’ alarum kaṇapuratt’ eṉ karumaṇiyē
children.translated_text: "O my dark gem of <s>Kaṇapuram</s> where water-lilies bloom along the banks among the weeds!"

children.text: iḷaiyavarkaṭk’ aruḷ uṭaiyāy irākavaṉē tālēlō
children.translated_text: "O You who are gracious to the young! O <s>Rāghava</s>! <s>Tālēlō</s>!"

children.text: taḷai aviḻum, ityādi
children.translated_text: "with loosening, fragrant baby curls" and so forth—

children.text: kaṭṭu aviḻumpaṭiyāṉa naṟunāṟṟattai uṭaiya mayirmuṭiyai uṭaiya cakravartikulattukku uddhārakaṉ-āṉavaṉē
children.translated_text: O You who are the redeemer of the clan of the Emperor, who has baby hair with fragrance so intense that its bonds come undone,

children.text: vaḷaiya oru cilai ityādi
children.translated_text: "with a single curved bow" and so forth—

children.text: brahmāstrādikaḷum vāymaṭiyum ūrai manuṣyatvattukku ekāntamāṉa villālē aḻiya ceytavaṉē!
children.translated_text: O You who accomplished the destruction with a mere human bow—the singular weapon—while even <s>brahmāstra</s>-s and the like fell slack and useless!

children.text: kaḷai kaḻunīr ityādi
children.translated_text: "water-lilies among the weeds" and so forth—

children.text: kaḷaiyāka paṟittu karaiyilē pōkaṭṭa ceṅkaḻunīrkaḷ, pōkaṭṭa iṭaṅkaḷilē kiṭantu taṉ nilattil alarumā pōlē cevvi peṟṟu alarum tiru kaṇṇapuram
children.translated_text: the red water-lilies that were plucked as weeds and thrown onto the banks, lying in those cast-off places, bloom beautifully as though in their own soil—such is <s>Tirukkaṇṇapuram</s>,

children.text: iḷaiyavarkaḷ ityādi
children.translated_text: "to the young ones" and so forth—

children.text: tampimārkku uṟupp’ ākātapōtu eṉ prāṇaṉkaḷum eṉakku vēṇṭā eṉṉumavariṟē.
children.translated_text: He is one who says 'when I cannot be of use to My younger brothers, even My life-breaths are unwanted to Me.'

children.text: tēvaraiyum acuraraiyum ticaikaḷaiyum paṭaittavaṉē
children.translated_text: "O You who created the gods and the demons and the directions!"

children.text: yāvarum vant’ aṭi vaṇaṅka araṅka nakar tuyiṉṟavaṉē
children.translated_text: "O You who recline in the city of <s>Araṅkam</s> (Śrīraṅgam) where all come and bow at Your feet!"

children.text: kāviri nal nati pāyum kaṇapuratt’ eṉ karumaṇiyē
children.translated_text: "O my dark gem of <s>Kaṇapuram</s> where the good river <s>Kāviri</s> (Kāvēri) flows!"

children.text: ē- vari vem cilai valavā irākavaṉē tālēlō
children.translated_text: "O wielder of the striped, fierce bow! O <s>Rāghava</s>! <s>Tālēlō</s>!"

children.text: tēvaraiyum acuraraiyum ticaikaḷaiyum paṭaittavaṉē
children.translated_text: "O You who created the gods and the demons and the directions"—

children.text: sahajaśatrukkaḷāṉa devāsurar mutalāṉa padārthaṅkaḷaiyum ivarkaḷukku avakāśapradhānam paṇṇum deśaṅkaḷaiyum sṛṣṭittavaṉē!
children.translated_text: O You who created entities such as the <s>deva</s>-s and <s>asura</s>-s who are natural enemies, and the regions (<s>deśa</s>-s) that provide them their respective spheres!

children.text: yāvarum vant’ aṭi vaṇaṅka araṅka nakar
children.translated_text: "where all come and bow at Your feet, in the city of <s>Araṅkam</s>"—

children.text: sṛṣṭiprayojanam ellām taṉṉai āśrayikkaikkiṟē; itukkāka kōyililē vantu kaṇvaḷarnt’ aruḷiṉavaṉē!
children.translated_text: the purpose of all creation is for beings to take refuge in Him; for this purpose He came and graciously reclines in the temple!

children.text: kāviri nal nati pāyum kaṇapuratt’ eṉ karumaṇiyē
children.translated_text: "O my dark gem of <s>Kaṇapuram</s> where the good river <s>Kāviri</s> flows"—

children.text: oruvar ēṟṟi pāycca vēṇṭātapaṭi tāṉē vantu eṅkum parakkum kāveriyai uṭaiya tiru kaṇṇapurattilē sulabhaṉ-āṉavaṉē!
children.translated_text: O You who have made Yourself accessible at <s>Tirukkaṇṇapuram</s> which has the <s>Kāvēri</s> that comes flowing everywhere of its own accord, without anyone needing to channel it!

children.text: ē- vari vem cilai valavā irākavaṉē
children.translated_text: "O wielder of the striped, fierce bow, O <s>Rāghava</s>"—

children.text: ēvilē mūṭṭa kaṭavatāy darśanīyamāy, piṭitta piṭiyilē śatrukkaḷ maṇṇuṇ-ṇumpaṭiyāṉa śrīśārṅgattai uṉ karuttilē naṭatta vallavaṉē!
children.translated_text: O You who can direct by Your mere will the <s>Śrī Śārṅga</s>, which is fit to be drawn upon the bowstring, which is beautiful to behold, and which in the very grip of the hand makes enemies bite the dust!

children.text: kaṉṉi nal mā matiḷ puṭai cūḻ kaṇapuratt’ eṉ kākuttaṉ
children.translated_text: "O my <s>Kākutstha</s> (descendant of Kakutstha) of <s>Kaṇapuram</s> surrounded by maiden, beautiful, great ramparts,"

children.text: taṉ aṭi mēl tālēlō eṉṟ’ uraitta tamiḻ mālai
children.translated_text: "this garland of Tamil verses composed upon His feet with '<s>Tālēlō</s>,'"

children.text: kol navilum vēl valavaṉ kuṭai kulacēkaraṉ coṉṉa
children.translated_text: "spoken by <s>Kulacēkaraṉ</s> of the royal parasol, wielder of the sharp, deadly spear—"

children.text: paṉṉiya nūl pattum vallār pāṅk’ āya pattarkaḷē
children.translated_text: "those who master all ten of these well-composed verses will become intimate devotees."

children.text: nigamattil
kaṉṉi nal mā matiḷ puṭai cūḻ
children.translated_text: "surrounded by maiden, beautiful, great ramparts"—

children.text: aḻiyāta periya tiru matiḷ cūḻnta tiru kaṇṇapurattilē niṉṟ’ aruḷiṉa kṛṣṇaṉaiaṉṟiyilē cakravarti tiru makaṉaiāyttu kavi pāṭiṟṟu.
children.translated_text: he composed the poem about the son of the Emperor (<s>Cakravartī Tirumakaṉ</s>, Rāma) rather than about <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> who graciously stands at <s>Tirukkaṇṇapuram</s> surrounded by imperishable great ramparts.

children.text: taṉ aṭi-mēl ityādi
children.translated_text: "upon His feet" and so forth—

children.text: cakravarti tiru makaṉuṭaiya bālyāvasthaiyil śrīkausalaiyār coṉṉa pācurattai tiru kaṇṇapurattilē coṉṉa tamiḻ toṭai
children.translated_text: the garland of Tamil verses composed at <s>Tirukkaṇṇapuram</s>, being the lullaby that <s>Śrī Kausalyā</s> sang during the infancy of the son of the Emperor,

children.text: kol navilum vēl valavaṉ kuṭai kulacēkaraṉ coṉṉa
children.translated_text: "spoken by <s>Kulacēkaraṉ</s> of the royal parasol, wielder of the sharp, deadly spear"—

children.text: vēlai piṭitta piṭiyilē ellārum vēliṉ koṭumaiyē eṉṟu collā-niṉṟa vēlaiyum, aiśvaryaprakāśakamāṉa veṇkoṟṟakkuṭaiyum uṭaiya śrīkulaśekhara perumāḷ aruḷicceyta
children.translated_text: composed by <s>Śrī Kulaśekhara Perumāḷ</s> who possesses the spear whose very grip makes all declare only the spear's fierceness, and the white royal parasol that proclaims sovereignty,

children.text: paṉṉiya nūl pattum vallār
children.translated_text: "those who master all ten of these well-composed verses"—

children.text: parampiṉa lakṣaṇattāl kuṟaiv’ aṟṟa i- pattum vallārkaḷ, tiru tāyārāyum aṭiyārāyum anubhavikka peṟuvārkaḷ.
children.translated_text: those who master these flawless ten verses composed in the traditional style will attain the experience of being both the divine mother and devotees.
In the concluding verse—

children.text: avatārikai – śrīkausalaiyār peṟṟa pēṟṟai anubhavittār kīḻil tirumoḻiyil; bālyāvasthai ellām anubhavittu prāptayauvanar āṉavāṟē anubhavikka peṟātē iḻanta cakravarti ōpātiyum tamakku prāpti ottirukkaiyālē, anubhavikka peṟātē iḻantēṉ eṉṟu avaṉ collukiṟa pācurattālē tam iḻavai pēcukiṟār itil.
children.translated_text: Introduction — In the previous <s>Tirumoḻi</s> he experienced the fortune that <s>Śrī Kausalyā</s> obtained; having experienced the entire infancy, when the prince came of age (<s>prāptayauvana</s>), since the Emperor's entitlement to experience was equal to his own, he now speaks of his own loss through the words of the Emperor who says 'I lost without being able to experience.'

children.text: val tāḷiṉ iṇai vaṇaṅki vaḷa
m
nakaram toḻut’ ētta maṉṉaṉ āvāṉ
children.translated_text: "city bowed and praised—You who stood to become king,"
"Bowing at the pair of mighty feet, the prosperous"

children.text: niṉṟāyai ariyaṇai mēl iruntāyai neṭum kāṉam paṭara pōku
children.translated_text: "You who then sat upon the throne—she said 'Go now to the vast forest!'"

children.text: eṉṟāḷ em irāmā ō uṉai payanta kaikēci taṉ col kēṭṭu
children.translated_text: "She said 'O my <s>Rāma</s>!'—hearing the words of <s>Kaikeyī</s> who bore You,"

children.text: naṉṟ’ āka nānilattai āḷvittēṉ nal makaṉē uṉṉai nāṉē
children.translated_text: "'What a fine thing I have done—I have made this good land be ruled well, O my good son!'—thus I, even I"

children.text: vaṉ tāḷiṉ iṇai vaṇaṅki
children.translated_text: "Bowing at the pair of mighty feet"—

children.text: tāṉum rājya parappai ellām āṇṭāṉāyirukka ceytē, a- aḷav’ aṉṟiyē,
children.translated_text: though he himself was ruling the entire expanse of the kingdom, beyond even that,

children.text: vaḷ pukaḻ nāraṇaṉ tiṇ kaḻal
children.translated_text: "the mighty feet of <s>Nāraṇaṉ</s> (Nārāyaṇa) of generous fame"—

children.text: eṉṉumā pōlē, āśritarai ellā avasthaiyilum viṭēṉ eṉṉum tiruvaṭikaḷai vaḻipaṭṭu
children.translated_text: just as that verse says, he worshipped the divine feet that declare 'I will not abandon those who take refuge in Me in any condition,'

children.text: vaḷa
m
nakaram toḻut’ ētta
children.translated_text: "city bowed and praised"—
"the prosperous"

children.text: tiru abhiṣekattukku alaṅkarittirukkiṟa tiru nagariyilē, appaṭi irukkiṟa tiru nagari toḻut’ ētta
children.translated_text: in the sacred city that had been adorned for the consecration (<s>abhiṣeka</s>), such a sacred city bowed and praised—

children.text: maṉṉaṉ āvāṉ niṉṟāyai
children.translated_text: "You who stood to become king"—

children.text: tiru abhiṣekattukku muṉp’ uḷḷa kartavyaṅkaḷ ellām talaikkaṭṭi tiru abhiṣekam paṇṇukaikku tiru kāppunāṇ cātti niṟkiṟa uṉṉai
children.translated_text: Having completed all the duties prior to the sacred coronation (<s>abhiṣeka</s>), You who stood with the sacred protective thread (<s>kāppunāṇ</s>) tied, ready for the coronation —

children.text: ariyaṇai mēl iruntāyai
children.translated_text: 'You who sat upon the royal throne' —

children.text: siṃhāsanattilē padasthaṉāy iruntāṉ eṉṉumpaṭi tōṟṟa camaint’ irukkiṟa uṉṉai
children.translated_text: You who sat so magnificently upon the lion-throne (<s>siṃhāsana</s>) that one would say 'He is installed in His position' —

children.text: neṭum kāṉam paṭara pōku eṉṟāḷ
children.translated_text: 'She told You to go to the vast forest' —

children.text: ippaṭi rājākkaḷ allātārum puka māṭṭāta kāṭṭai.
children.translated_text: To a forest that even non-royals would not enter.

children.text: te vanena vanaṃ gatvā
children.translated_text: <s>te vanena vanaṃ gatvā</s> (Having gone by that path to the forest)

children.text: eṉṉumā pōlē i- ūril niṉṟum puṟappaṭṭu vaḻiyē pōy kāṭṭilē pukumat’ aṉṟiyē kāṭṭil niṉṟum kāṭṭilēyē pōmpaṭiyāy, neṭiya kāṭṭilēyiṟē pōka colliṟṟu.
children.translated_text: As it is said — not just departing from this city, going along the way and entering the forest, but going from forest to forest endlessly; she commanded Him to go to a vast, endless forest.

children.text: em irāmā ō
children.translated_text: 'O my <s>Rāma</s>!' —

children.text: niṉaikkavum collavum kāṇavum tāpam pōmpaṭiyāṉa ummaiyiṟē pōka colliṟṟu
children.translated_text: It was You — the mere thought, mention, and sight of whom removes all anguish — whom she commanded to go!

children.text: uṉai payanta kaikēci taṉ col kēṭṭu
children.translated_text: 'Having heard the words of <s>Kaikēyī</s> who bore You' —

children.text: tiru abhiṣekakalyāṇavārtai śrīkausalaiyārilum kāṭṭil taṉakku nāṉ ceṉṟu colli prīti kāṇa vēṇum eṉṉumpaṭi peṟṟa tāyāy pōnta kaikeyi vārttai kēṭṭu

children.translated_text: 'In the vast forest, beneath the shade of a tree' —

children.translated_text: The moment she cannot see Him for a little while, she sends <s>Sumantra</s> to bring Him back to see Him. Then she says 'Go!' to see His back and departure once more; and the moment He disappears from sight, she says 'Come!' again.
