children.translated_text: His fragrant flower-adorned beautiful locks now matted into ascetic braids, His waist that befits flower-draped garments

children.text: kāmar eḻil viḻal uṭuttu kalaṉ aṇiyāt’ aṅkaṅkaḷ aḻaku māṟi
children.translated_text: now clothed in lovely bark garments, His limbs bereft of ornaments, His beauty altered —

children.text: ēmaru tōḷ eṉ putalvaṉ yāṉ iṉṟu cela takka vaṉam tāṉ cērtal
children.translated_text: My mighty-shouldered son today goes to the forest that I should have gone to!

children.text: tū maṟaiyīr itu takavō cumantiraṉē vaciṭṭaṉē collīr nīrē
children.translated_text: O pure Vedic scholars! Is this just? O <s>Sumantra</s>! O <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>! Speak, you yourselves!

children.text: pūm maruvu naṟum kuñci puṉ caṭai āy puṉaintu
children.translated_text: 'His fragrant flower-adorned beautiful locks now matted into ascetic braids' —

children.text: pū māṟātē iruppatāy, parimaḷattai puṟappaṭaviṭā-niṟkum tiru kuḻalai, manuṣyarkku pārkka oṇṇātapaṭi jaṭhaiyākki
children.translated_text: His sacred tresses that were ever adorned with flowers and emanated fragrance — now turned into matted locks (<s>jaṭā</s>) that people could not bear to look upon,

children.text: pūntukil cēr alkul kāmar eḻil viḻal uṭuttu
children.translated_text: 'His waist clothed in lovely bark garments instead of flower-draped cloth' —

children.text: aṟupatiṉāyiram āṇṭu tēṭiṉa tiru pariyaṭṭaṅkaḷil nallavai ellām cātta kaṭava tiru araiyilē, kaṇṭār virumpumpaṭi viśvāmitrattai kayiṟāka muṟukki cātti
children.translated_text: Upon the sacred waist that should be draped with the finest of garments sought over sixty thousand years — now wrapping <s>viśvāmitra</s> grass twisted into cord, in a way that makes onlookers weep,

children.text: kalaṉ aṇiyāt’ aṅkaṅkaḷ aḻaku māṟi
children.translated_text: 'His limbs bereft of ornaments, His beauty altered' —

children.text: svābhāvikamāṉa aḻak’ oḻiya tiru ābharaṇaṅkaḷ cāttāmaiyālē attāl varum aḻakiṉṟiyē
children.translated_text: Apart from His natural beauty, the beauty that comes from sacred ornaments being absent — being without that adornment,

children.text: ēmaru tōḷ eṉ putalvaṉ
children.translated_text: 'My mighty-shouldered son' —

children.text: vighnam paṇṇiṉārai aḻiyacceytu abhiṣekam paṇṇa valla eṉ makaṉ
children.translated_text: My son who is capable of destroying those who create obstacles and performing the coronation (<s>abhiṣeka</s>)

children.text: yāṉ iṉṟu cela takka vaṉam tāṉ cērtal
children.translated_text: 'Today goes to the forest that I should have gone to!' —

children.text: aṟupatiṉāyiram āṇṭu bhogaṅkaḷai bhujittu vītarāgaṉāṉa nāṉ pōka kaṭava kāṭṭilē, sukumārarāy bhogayogyarāṉa tām pōkai
children.translated_text: That I — who having enjoyed pleasures for sixty thousand years became dispassionate — should go to the forest; instead, He who is delicate and worthy of enjoyment goes there!

children.text: tū maṟaiyīr itu takavō
children.translated_text: 'O pure Vedic scholars! Is this just?' —

children.text: patiṃ viśvasya
children.translated_text: <s>patiṃ viśvasya</s> (the lord of the universe)

children.text: eṉṟu ōtiyirukkiṟa brāhmaṇarē! nīṅkaḷ itu collikōḷ; itu dharmamō?
children.translated_text: O <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who recite thus in the <s>Vedas</s>! Tell me: is this <s>dharma</s>?

children.text: cumantiraṉē vaciṭṭaṉē collīr nīrē
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Sumantra</s>! O <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>! Speak, you yourselves!' —

children.text: rājadharmattai paḻacu aṟintu naṭatti pōnta sumantraṉē! collāy! i- vamśattukku guruvāy rājadharmaṅkaḷai upadeśittu pōrukiṟa śrīvasiṣṭha-bhagavānē! collāy.
children.translated_text: O <s>Sumantra</s> who has long known and administered royal <s>dharma</s> (<s>rājadharma</s>)! Speak! O <s>Śrī Vasiṣṭha Bhagavān</s> who is the preceptor of this dynasty and has been teaching royal duties! Speak!

children.text: poṉ peṟṟār eḻil vēta putalvaṉaiyum tampiyaiyum pūvai pōlum
children.translated_text: Those blessed teachers' beautiful, Veda-learned son and His younger brother, along with the flower-like

children.text: miṉ paṟṟā nuṇ maruṅkul melliyal eṉ marukiyaiyum vaṉattil pōkki
children.translated_text: lightning-waisted, tender maiden, my daughter-in-law — having sent them all to the forest,

children.text: niṉ paṟṟ’ ām niṉ makaṉ mēl paḻi viḷaittiṭṭ’ eṉṉaiyum nīḷ vāṉil pōkka
children.translated_text: having heaped blame upon Your own son who is Your refuge, and having sent me too to the vast heavens —

children.text: eṉ peṟṟāy kaikēcī iru
m
children.translated_text: land,

children.text: nilattil iṉit’ āka irukkiṉṟāyē
children.translated_text: you sit here happily!
what have you gained, O <s>Kaikēyī</s>? In this vast

children.text: poṉ peṟṟār eḻil vēta putalvaṉaiyum tampiyaiyum
children.translated_text: 'Those blessed teachers' beautiful, Veda-learned son and His younger brother' —

children.text: dhanyar eṉṟu ellārum collumpaṭi irukkiṟa upādhyāyarkaḷ kīḻē iruntu aḻakiya sakalavedaśāstraṅkaḷaiyum ōti irukkiṟa perumāḷaiyum, avarai allatu aṟiyāta tampiyāraiyum
children.translated_text: <s>Perumāḷ</s> (the Lord), who sat under teachers whom all call 'blessed' and studied all the beautiful <s>Vedas</s> and <s>śāstras</s> — and His younger brother who knows none but Him —

children.text: pūvai pōlummiṉ paṟṟā nuṇ maruṅkul melliyal eṉ marukiyaiyum
children.translated_text: my daughter-in-law, of delicate nature, with a waist slender as lightning and like a <s>pūvai</s> flower

children.text: pūvai pōlē iruppāḷumāy, miṉṉukku opp’ āṉa iṭaiyai uṭaiyāḷumāy mṛdusvabhāvaiyumāṉa eṉ marumakaḷāṉa eṉ pirāṭṭiyaiyum
children.translated_text: my daughter-in-law, my <s>Pirāṭṭi</s> (princess), who is like a <s>pūvai</s> flower, who has a waist matching lightning in slenderness, and who is of soft nature

children.text: vaṉattil pōkki
children.translated_text: sending her to the forest

children.text: kāṭṭilē pōkaviṭṭu
children.translated_text: sending her away to the forest

children.text: niṉ paṟṟ’ ām niṉ makaṉ mēl paḻi viḷaittiṭṭu
children.translated_text: bringing blame upon your own son, who is your sole support

children.text: uṉṉai allatu vēṟ’ oruvarai tāy eṉṟ’ irāta perumāḷaiyum iḷaiya-perumāḷaiyum vanattilē pōkaviṭṭu śrībharatāḻvāṉ-mēlē bhrātṛdrohi eṉkiṟa paḻiyai ēṟiṭṭu
children.translated_text: sending <s>Perumāḷ</s> and <s>Iḷaiya Perumāḷ</s> (<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>), who knew no mother other than you, to the forest, and heaping upon <s>Śrī Bharatāḻvāṉ</s> the blame of being a 'fratricide'

children.text: eṉṉaiyum nīḷ vāṉil pōkka eṉ peṟṟāy
children.translated_text: and sending me too to the vast heavens — what did you gain, O my begetter?

children.text: i- ceyalkaḷ ellām ceytu nī peṟṟa prayojanam eṉ?
children.translated_text: having done all these deeds, what benefit did you obtain?

children.text: iru
m
nilattil iṉit’ āka irukkiṉṟāyē
children.translated_text: on this great earth, comfortably!
sitting

children.text: saṃsārasukham-ākiṟatu putrarkaḷōṭum bhartāvōṭum kūṭiyirukkaiāyttu; uṉakku putrarāṉa perumāḷai kāṭṭilē pōkki eṉṉaiyum svargattilē pōkkukaiyālē saṃsārasukham aḻakiyatāka anubhavikka kaṭavaiyiṟē!
children.translated_text: The happiness of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) consists of living together with one's sons and husband; since you sent <s>Perumāḷ</s>, who is your son, to the forest and sent me too to heaven, you can beautifully enjoy the happiness of <s>saṃsāra</s>!

children.text: muṉ oru nāḷ maḻu āḷi cilai vāṅki avaṉ tavattai muṟṟum ceṟṟāy
children.translated_text: Once long ago, you wrested the axe-wielding one's bow and completely destroyed his <s>tapas</s> (penance)

children.text: uṉṉaiyum uṉ arumaiyaiyum uṉ mōyiṉ varuttamum oṉṟ’ āka koḷḷātu
children.translated_text: without regarding yourself, your own greatness, or your mother's distress as anything

children.text: eṉṉaiyum eṉ mey uraiyum mey āka koṇṭu vaṉam pukka entāy
children.translated_text: taking me and my truthful words as true, O my lord who entered the forest!

children.text: niṉṉaiyē makaṉ āka peṟa peṟuvēṉ ēḻ piṟappum neṭum tōḷ vēntē
children.translated_text: May I obtain you as my son in all seven births, O king of long arms!

children.text: muṉ oru nāḷ maḻu āḷi cilai vāṅki
children.translated_text: Once long ago, wresting the bow from the axe-wielder

children.text: muṉ oru kālattilē maḻuvai āyudhamāka uṭaiya śrī paraśurāmaṉ kaiyil śrī śārṅga tiru villai vāṅki
children.translated_text: Once in a former time, from <s>Śrī Paraśurāma</s> who had the axe as his weapon, wresting the sacred bow <s>Śrī Śārṅga</s>

children.text: avaṉ tavattai muṟṟum ceṟṟāy
children.translated_text: you completely destroyed his <s>tapas</s>

children.text: avaṉ lokāntaraṅkaḷai prāpikka kaṭavatāka ārjitatapassai a- ampālē aḻittu pōkaṭṭāy
children.translated_text: with that very arrow, you destroyed the <s>tapas</s> he had accumulated for attaining the higher worlds

children.text: uṉṉaiyum uṉ arumaiyaiyum
children.translated_text: without regarding yourself or your own greatness

children.text: uṉ ślāghyataiyaiyum,
children.translated_text: or your praiseworthiness,

children.text: mahatā tapasā rāma
children.translated_text: <s>mahatā tapasā rāma</s> (O <s>Rāma</s>, obtained through great austerity)

children.text: eṉṟu nāṉ uṉṉai peṟa paṭṭa arumaiyaiyum
children.translated_text: or the great effort I underwent to obtain you,

children.text: uṉ mōyiṉ varuttamum oṉṟ’ āka koḷḷātu
children.translated_text: or your mother's distress as anything

children.text: uṉṉai piriyil dhariyēṉ eṉṟu piṉ toṭarnta śrīkausalaiyār vyasanattaiyum oṉṟ’ āka koḷḷātu
children.translated_text: or the anguish of <s>Śrī Kausalyā</s> who followed you saying 'I cannot bear separation from you' — regarding none of these as anything

children.text: eṉṉaiyum eṉ mey uraiyum mey āka koṇṭu vaṉam pukka
children.translated_text: taking me and my truthful words as true, O my lord who entered the forest!

children.text: uṉ pakkal eṉakk’ uṇṭāṉa bhāvabandhattai mey āka aṟiyātē, eṉṉai pitā eṉṟē niṉaittu, neṭu nāḷ satyam colli pōntavaṉai nāṉ tōṉṟi asatyapratijñaṉ ākka oṇṇātu eṉṟu eṉ asatyattai satyam ākka vēṇum eṉṟu neñcilē koṇṭu kāṭēṟa pōṉa eṉ nāyaṉē!
children.translated_text: without truly knowing the emotional bond I have toward you, merely thinking of me as 'father,' and thinking 'I who have spoken truth for so long must not appear to be one of false vows — my falsehood must be made truth' — with that resolve entering the forest, O my master!

children.text: niṉṉaiyē makaṉ āka peṟa peṟuvēṉ ēḻ piṟappum neṭum tōḷ vēntē
children.translated_text: May I obtain you as my son in all seven births, O king of long arms!

children.text: anekajanmaṅkaḷ piṟantu, piṟanta janmam tōṟum nī eṉakku piḷḷaiyāy piṟakkumpaṭi peṟṟ’ uṭaiyēṉ āvēṉē.
children.translated_text: Being born through many births, in each birth so born, may I be blessed to have you born as my son!

children.text: neṭum tōḷ vēntē
children.translated_text: O king of long arms!

children.text: rakṣyavargattiṉ aḷav’ allāta kāval tuṭipp’ uṭaiya tōḷai uṭaiyavaṉē!
children.translated_text: O one who has shoulders with a resolve for protection that exceeds the measure of those to be protected!

children.text: tēṉ naku mā malar kūntal kaucalaiyum cumittiraiyum cintai nōva
children.translated_text: <s>Kausalyā</s> and <s>Sumitrā</s> with honey-dripping, great flower-adorned tresses — with their hearts grieving

children.text: kūṉ uruviṉ koṭum toḻuttai col kēṭṭa koṭiyavaḷ taṉ col koṇṭ’ iṉṟu
children.translated_text: having heeded the words of the cruel woman who listened to the words of the hunchback of crooked form

children.translated_text: city — renouncing it, I too
you who greatly desired the forest and renounced the prosperous

children.translated_text: greatly desiring heaven, I depart! O king of the <s>Manu</s> dynasty!

children.text: tēṉ naku mā malar kūntal ityādi
children.translated_text: '<s>Kausalyā</s> and <s>Sumitrā</s> with honey-dripping, great flower-adorned tresses,' etc.

children.text: tēṉai puṟappaṭuvikkiṟa malarōṭē kūṭiṉa mayirmuṭiyai uṭaiya śrīkau-salaiyārum sumitraiyārum neñcu nōva
children.translated_text: causing grief to the hearts of <s>Śrī Kausalyā</s> and <s>Sumitrā</s> who have hair adorned with flowers that exude honey

children.text: kūṉ uru ityādi
children.translated_text: 'the hunchback of crooked form,' etc.

children.text: vaṭivil vakram pōlē neñcum vakramāy tiṇṇitāṉa kūṉiyuṭaiya vārttaiyai kēṭṭa kaikeyiyuṭaiya vārttaiyilē akappaṭṭu
children.translated_text: ensnared by the words of <s>Kaikeyī</s> who listened to the words of the hunchback whose heart was as crooked as her form

children.text: kāṉakamē mika virumpi nī tuṟanta vaḷa
m
nakarai tuṟantu

you who greatly desired the forest and renounced the prosperous

children.text: nāṉ pōka coṉṉēṉ eṉṉumattaiyē koṇṭu oruvarukkum sañcarikka aritāṉa kāṭṭai virumpi, tiru abhiṣekattukku alaṅkaritt’ irukkiṟa ūrai nī kaiviṭṭāy eṉṟu nāṉum tiru ayodhyaiyai tuṟantu
children.translated_text: taking merely the fact that I commanded your departure, desiring the forest that is difficult for anyone to traverse, you abandoned the city that was adorned for the coronation — thus I too renounce sacred <s>Ayodhyā</s>

children.text: vāṉakamē mika virumpi pōkiṉṟēṉ
children.translated_text: greatly desiring heaven, I depart

children.text: nī illāta nagariyiṟē; attālē svargamē ākilum nī illāta ūrai viṭṭu pōkiṉṟēṉ
children.translated_text: since it is a city without you; therefore, even if it be heaven itself, I depart from a city without you

the beautiful, dark

varai tōḷ tayarataṉ tāṉ pulampiya a- pulampal taṉṉai

the one with garland-adorned, broad

children.translated_text: spoken in verse by <s>Kulacēkaraṉ</s>, the king of <s>Kōḻi</s> (Uṟaiyūr), wielder of the keen, sharp spear

the beautiful, dark

children.translated_text: the Supreme Lord, complete in every way and superior to all, incarnated as one of the same kind as those subject to <s>karma</s>, and entered the forest where even those subject to <s>karma</s> would not go — unable to bear that

children.translated_text: 'the one with garland-adorned,' etc.

children.translated_text: the lamentation uttered by the <s>Cakravarti</s> (<s>Daśaratha</s>) who, having ruled for sixty thousand years, had garlands that never left him, and had firm, mountain-like shoulders

children.text: kūr ārnta ityādi
children.translated_text: 'of the keen, sharp,' etc.

children.text: kūrmai mikka vēlai uṭaiyarumāy, uṟaiyūrkku niyāmakarumāy, aiśvarya-prakāśakamāṉa veṇkoṟṟakkuṭaiyai uṭaiyarumāṉa kulaśekhara perumāḷ aruḷicceyta
children.translated_text: graciously composed by <s>Kulaśekhara Perumāḷ</s>, who possessed a most keen spear, who was the ruler of <s>Uṟaiyūr</s>, and who possessed the white royal parasol that manifests sovereignty

children.translated_text: as stated thus, those who master this complete Tamil composition

children.text: tī neṟi kaṇ cellār tāmē
children.translated_text: will never walk the evil path!

children.text: bhagavadviṣayattai kāṟkaṭaikkoṇṭu viṣayapravaṇar ākārkaḷ.
children.translated_text: they will not abandon the Lord's domain and become attached to sense objects.
In the concluding verse —

children.text: avatārikai - anādikālam tām iḻanta iḻavai, devaki deviyār peṟṟuvaittum kṛṣṇaṉuṭaiya bālaceṣṭitaṅkaḷai anubhavikka peṟātē iḻantavaḷ pācurattālē pēciṉār ālai nīḷ karumpil; maṉṉu pukaḻil śrīkausalaiyār peṟṟa pēṟṟai anubhavittār; bālyāvasthaiyilē ellām anubhavittu prāptayauvanar āṉavāṟē anubhavikka peṟātē iḻanta cakravarti ōpāti tamakku prāpti uṇṭākaiyālē avaṉ pācurattālē tam iḻavai pēciṉār vaḷ tāḷil; i- tirumoḻiyil kīḻ piṟanta iḻavukaḷ ellām tīra, cakravarti tiru makaṉ nityavāsam paṇṇukiṟa tiruccitrakūṭam-ākiṟa tiru patiyilē tiru avatāram toṭaṅki anta avatāravṛttāntattai śrīvālmīkibhagavān pēci anubhavittā pōlē, tammuṭaiya jñānavaiśadyattālē samakālattil pōlē anubhavikkiṟār.
children.translated_text: Introduction — Having expressed through <s>Devakī Devī</s>'s words in 'ālai nīḷ karumpu' the loss they had endured since beginningless time — she who had borne <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> but lost the enjoyment of His childhood play; in 'maṉṉu pukaḻ' he enjoyed the fortune that <s>Śrī Kausalyā</s> obtained; just as <s>Cakravarti</s> (<s>Daśaratha</s>) who had enjoyed everything during the childhood and then lost the enjoyment once the youth was attained — since he too has such entitlement, he expressed his own loss through <s>Daśaratha</s>'s words in 'vaḷ tāḷ'; in this <s>Tirumoḻi</s>, to remedy all the losses born in the previous ones, at the sacred place of <s>Tiruccitrakūṭam</s> where the Son of the Emperor (<s>Rāma</s>) eternally dwells, beginning from the sacred incarnation and that incarnation-narrative, just as <s>Śrī Vālmīki Bhagavān</s> spoke and experienced it, he too, through the clarity of his spiritual knowledge, experiences it as if he were a contemporary.

children.text: am kaṇ neṭu
m
matiḷ puṭai cūḻ ayōtti eṉṉum aṇi nakaratt’ ulak’ aṉaittum viḷakkum cōti
children.translated_text: in the city called <s>Ayodhyā</s>, surrounded by tall walls on all sides, the light that illuminates all worlds
beautiful-eyed, long

children.text: vem katirōṉ kulattukk’ ōr viḷakku āy tōṉṟi viṇ muḻutum uyakkoṇṭa vīraṉ taṉṉai
children.translated_text: appearing as a lamp to the dynasty of the fierce-rayed sun, the hero who uplifted all of heaven

children.text: cem kaṇ neṭum karu mukilai irāmaṉ taṉṉai tillai nakar tiruccitrakūṭam taṉ uḷ
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> himself, the red-eyed, great dark cloud — in <s>Tiruccitrakūṭam</s> in the city of <s>Tillai</s>

children.text: eṅkaḷ taṉi mutalvaṉai emperumāṉ taṉṉai eṉṟu-kolō kaṇ kuḷira kāṇum nāḷē
children.translated_text: our peerless primal Lord, our <s>Emperumāṉ</s> — when, oh when, will be the day I behold Him to my eyes' content?

children.text: avatārikai – mutal pāṭṭu. devarkaḷ ellārum kṛtārthar āmpaṭi vantu tiru avatāram paṇṇiṉapaṭi collukiṟatu.
am kaṇ ityādi
children.translated_text: 'beautiful-eyed,' etc.

children.text: bhogyabhogopakaraṇabhogasthānaṅkaḷai uṭaittāy, ākāśāvakāśam ellām tāṉē āmpaṭi nimirnta matiḷālē cūḻappaṭṭa ayodhyai. ayodhyā eṉṟum, aparājitā eṉṟum collappaṭukiṟa paramapadam pōlē śatrukkaḷukku kaṇicikka oṇṇāta ūr.
children.translated_text: possessing objects of enjoyment, instruments of enjoyment, and places of enjoyment, with walls that rose so high as to fill the entire expanse of the sky, surrounded by them — <s>Ayodhyā</s>. A city impregnable to enemies, like <s>Paramapadam</s> (the supreme abode) which is called both <s>Ayodhyā</s> (unconquerable) and <s>Aparājitā</s> (undefeated).

children.text: eṉṉum
children.translated_text: called

children.text: paramapadam pōlē cilar aṟintu cilar aṟiyāt’ irukkai aṉṟikkē, sarvalokaprasiddhamāy irukkai
children.translated_text: unlike <s>Paramapadam</s> where some know it and some do not, this is universally renowned

children.text: aṇi nakarattu
children.translated_text: the ornamental city

children.text: alaṅkāraṅkaḷāl kuṟaiv’ aṟṟa ūr eṉṉutal
children.translated_text: meaning: a city lacking nothing in adornments

children.text: ulak’ aṉaittum viḷakkum cōti
children.translated_text: the light that illuminates all worlds

children.text: sarvalokaṅkaḷaiyum taṉ tejassālē
children.translated_text: with His own <s>tejas</s> (radiance), all the worlds

children.text: nārāyaṇa paro jyotiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>nārāyaṇa paro jyotiḥ</s> (<s>Nārāyaṇa</s> is the supreme light)

children.text: eṉkiṟapaṭiyē, parañjyotissāy uḷḷatu
children.translated_text: as stated thus, He is the supreme light

children.text: vem katirōṉ ityādi
children.translated_text: 'of the fierce-rayed sun,' etc.

children.text: jagattil andhakāram ellām nīkka kaṭava ādityaṉ vaṃśattilē, avaṉai pōlē iravu kalacātē advitīyamāṉa tejassāy vant’ utittu
children.translated_text: in the dynasty of the sun who removes all darkness in the world, appearing like the sun itself as an unrivaled radiance that does not mix with night

children.text: viṇ muḻutum uyakkoṇṭa vīraṉ taṉṉai
children.translated_text: the hero who uplifted all of heaven

children.text: taṉ vīryaguṇattālē devajātiyai aṭaiya ujjīvippittavaṉai
children.translated_text: He who, through the quality of His valor, uplifted the entire race of celestials

children.text: cem kaṇ neṭum karum mukilai
children.translated_text: the red-eyed, great dark cloud

children.text: devajātiyē aṉṟikkē jagattai aṭaiya rakṣippatāka, kaṭalil maṇalē śeṣamāka parukiṉa kāḷameghattiṉ uṭaiya vaṭivaiyum sarveśvaratva-lakṣaṇamāṉa puṇḍarīkākṣatvattaiyum uṭaiyavaṉē
children.translated_text: He who possesses the form of a dark cloud that has drunk the ocean leaving only the sand, and who possesses the <s>puṇḍarīkākṣatva</s> (lotus-eyedness) that is the mark of <s>sarveśvaratva</s> (universal sovereignty), for the protection not only of the celestial race but of the entire world

children.text: irāmaṉ taṉṉai
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> himself

children.text: vaṭiv’ aḻakālum kaṇ aḻakālum abhirāmataiyālum anukūlapratikūla-vibhāgam iṉṟiyē tōṟpikkumavaṉai. kīḻil vīraṉ eṉkiṟatai iṅkum anvayikka kaṭavatu.
children.translated_text: He who conquers all without distinction of friend or foe through the beauty of His form, the beauty of His eyes, and His captivating charm. The word 'hero' stated earlier should be connected here as well.

children.text: satyena
children.translated_text: <s>satyena</s> (by truth)

children.text: ityādivat.
children.translated_text: and so forth.

children.text: tillai nakar tiruccitrakūṭam taṉ uḷ
children.translated_text: in <s>Tiruccitrakūṭam</s> in the city of <s>Tillai</s>

children.text: a- avatārattil samakālattil anubhavikka peṟāta iḻavu tīra, piṟpaṭṭa kālattil uḷḷārkkum utavalāmpaṭi sannihitaṉ-āṉavaṉai
children.translated_text: He who became present so that even those of later times may readily approach — to remedy the loss of not being able to experience during that incarnation

children.text: eṅkaḷ taṉi mutalvaṉai
children.translated_text: our peerless primal Lord

children.text: a- kālattil anubhavikka peṟāta eṅkaḷai ujjīvippikkaikku opp’ illāta kāraṇabhūtaṉ-āṉavaṉai
children.translated_text: He who is the incomparable cause for the salvation of us who could not experience during that time

children.text: emperumāṉ taṉṉai
children.translated_text: our <s>Emperumāṉ</s> (Lord)

children.text: vakutta śeṣiāṉavaṉai
children.translated_text: He who is the appointed Master

children.text: eṉṟu-kolō kaṇ kuḷira kāṇum nāḷē
children.translated_text: when, oh when, will be the day I behold Him to my eyes' content?

children.text: inta rājyadhurandharataiyilē akappaṭṭirukkiṟa nāṉ, aṉṟu avaṉai kāṇa peṟātē viṭāytta kaṇkaḷ-āṉavai kaṇṭu, viṭāy tīrntu kaṇ paṭaitta prayojanam peṟal āvatu eṉṟō? eṉkiṟār, eṉṟu kolō eṉṟu kālattiṟku oru avadhi peṟṟār-ākil, iṉṟu kaṇṭatōṭu okkum kiṭīr.
children.translated_text: I who am trapped in this burden of rulership — when will my eyes, which have been thirsting from not seeing Him then, behold Him and have their thirst quenched and attain the purpose for which eyes were created? — he says. If he could fix even a time-limit by saying 'when, oh when,' it would be as good as having seen Him today.
Introduction — First verse. It speaks of how He incarnated so that all the celestials became fulfilled.

children.text: vant’ etirnta tāṭakai taṉ urattai kīṟi varu kuruti poḻitara val kaṇai oṉṟ’ ēvi
children.translated_text: Tearing open the chest of <s>Tāṭakā</s> (Tāḍakā) who came charging forward, dispatching a powerful arrow that made the flowing blood pour forth

children.text: mantiram koḷ maṟai muṉivaṉ vēḷvi kāttu val arakkar uyir uṇṭa maintaṉ kāṇmiṉ
children.translated_text: Behold the young hero who protected the sacrifice of the sage of sacred mantras and Vedas, and consumed the lives of the mighty demons!

children.text: cem taḷirvāy malar nakai cēr ceḻum taṇ cōlai tillai nakar tiruccitrakūṭam taṉ uḷ
children.translated_text: in <s>Tiruccitrakūṭam</s> in the city of <s>Tillai</s>, amidst cool, luxuriant groves where flower-smiles bloom amid red tender sprouts

children.text: antaṇarkaḷ oru mū āyiravar ētta aṇi maṇi ācaṉatt’ irunta ammāṉ tāṉē
children.translated_text: seated on a jeweled throne as three thousand <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> sing His praise — that is the Lord Himself!

children.text: avatārikai - iraṇṭām pāṭṭu. vant’ etirnta - rākṣasavadhattukk’ ellām aṭiyākavum, ṛṣiyuṭaiya abhimatam talaikkaṭṭukaikkum tāḍakātāḍakeyarai nirasittapaṭi collukiṟatu.
vant’ etirnta tāṭakai
children.translated_text: the <s>Tāḍakā</s> who came charging forward

children.text: tāṉ mikaittu vantu mēliṭṭa tāḍakai; nikṛtikku opp’ illātavaḷ.
children.translated_text: <s>Tāḍakā</s> who came surging and overwhelming; she who was unmatched in treachery.

children.text: taṉ nikar oṉṟ’ illāta’ tāṭakai
children.translated_text: '<s>Tāḍakā</s> who has no equal'

children.text: iṟē.
children.translated_text: indeed.

children.text: taṉ urattai kīṟi
children.translated_text: tearing open her chest

children.text: perumāḷ pakkal pollāṅku niṉaitta neñcai malai piḷantā pōlē piḷantu
children.translated_text: splitting the heart that had thought evil toward <s>Perumāḷ</s>, as if splitting a mountain

children.text: varu kuruti poḻi-tara
children.translated_text: the flowing blood pouring forth

children.text: cempāṭṭu taraiyilē malaiyaruvi viḻuntā pōlē rudhiram vantu koḻikka
children.translated_text: blood flowing down like a mountain waterfall cascading on copper-colored ground

children.text: val kaṇai oṉṟ’ ēvi
children.translated_text: dispatching a powerful arrow

children.text: valikku opp’ illāta tiru carattai naṭatti
children.translated_text: directing a sacred arrow of unmatched power

children.text: mantiram koḷ maṟai muṉivaṉ
children.translated_text: the sage of sacred mantras and Vedas

children.text: ṛṣi tuṇukku tuṇukk’ eṉṉātapaṭi nirbhayaṉāy taṉṉuṭaiya anuṣṭhānaṅkaḷ ellām aṭaivē anuṣṭhittu yāgattai talaikkaṭṭumpaṭi paṇṇi
children.translated_text: making the sage perform all his rituals in succession without trembling, becoming fearless, and bringing the sacrifice (<s>yāga</s>) to completion

children.text: val arakkar uyir uṇṭa
children.translated_text: who consumed the lives of the mighty demons

children.text: yajñavighnarāṉa mārīcasubāhukkaḷai muṭitta piḷḷaittaṉattai uṭaiyavaṉē. mārīcaṉ paṭṭāṉō? eṉṉil - piṉṉai irunta iruppu mṛtaprāyam eṉṟu karuttu.
children.translated_text: possessing the youthful prowess of having finished off <s>Mārīca</s> and <s>Subāhu</s> who were obstructing the sacrifice. Did <s>Mārīca</s> die? — The idea is that his subsequent existence was as good as dead.

children.text: cem taḷir vāy malar nakai cēr
children.translated_text: amidst red tender sprouts and blooming flower-smiles

children.text: civanta taḷirkaḷ naṭuvē vikasiyā-niṉṟuḷḷa puṣpaṅkaḷai uṭaittāy darśanīyamāy śramaharamāṉa cōlaiyālē alaṅkṛtamāṉa ūrilē
children.translated_text: in the city adorned with visually delightful and fatigue-removing groves that have flowers blooming amidst red tender sprouts

children.text: antaṇarkaḷ oru mū āyiravar
children.translated_text: three thousand <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>

children.text: ananyaprayojanarāṉa brāhmaṇar mū āyiram pēr
children.translated_text: three thousand <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who seek no other purpose

children.text: ētta
children.translated_text: singing His praise

children.text: tiraṇṭu maṅgaḷāśāsanam paṇṇa
children.translated_text: assembling together to perform <s>maṅgalāśāsana</s> (auspicious benediction)

children.text: aṇi maṇi ācaṉatt’ irunta
children.translated_text: seated on the jeweled throne

children.text: kōpp’ uṭaiya cīriya ciṅkācaṉam
children.translated_text: a magnificent lion-throne befitting royalty

children.text: eṉṉumpaṭiyē mahārghaṅkaḷāṉa ratnaṅkaḷai uṭaittāṉa simhāsanattilē taṉ mēṉmai tōṟṟa irunta sarveśvaraṉ kiṭīr eṉkiṟār.
children.translated_text: as described thus, he says 'come see' <s>Sarveśvara</s> (the Lord of all) who was seated displaying His greatness upon a throne studded with precious gems.

Introduction — Second verse. 'Who came charging forward' — it tells how He slew <s>Tāḍakā</s> and <s>Tāḍakeya</s> (her sons), which became the foundation for all the <s>Rākṣasa</s> slayings and the fulfillment of the sage's desire.

children.text: ce
m
children.translated_text: -streaked,

children.text: vari nal karu
children.translated_text: beautiful, dark,

children.text: m
children.translated_text: large

children.text: neṭum kaṇ cītaikk’ āki ciṉa viṭaiyōṉ cilai iṟuttu maḻu vāḷēnti
children.translated_text: eyes — for <s>Sītā</s>'s sake, He broke the bow of the angry bull-rider, and wielding the battle-axe,
The red

children.text: ve
m
children.translated_text: the fierce,

children.text: vari nal cilai vāṅki veṉṟi koṇṭu vēl vēntar pakai taṭinta vīraṉ taṉṉai
children.translated_text: striped, great bow and, having conquered, the hero who ended the enmity of the lance-bearing kings —
He took

children.text: tevvar añca neṭum puricai uyarnta pāṅkar tillai nakar tiruccitrakūṭam taṉ uḷ
children.translated_text: in <s>Tillai</s> city with tall fortifications that make enemies tremble, within <s>Tiruccitrakūṭam</s>,

children.text: evv’ ari vem cilai taṭa kai irāmaṉ taṉṉai iṟaiñcuvār iṇai aṭiyē iṟaiñciṉēṉē
children.translated_text: I worshipped the pair of feet of those who worship <s>Rāma</s> who holds the fierce, invincible bow in His mighty hand!

children.text: avatārikai - mūṉṟām pāṭṭu. ce vari nal - pirāṭṭiyārōṭṭai kalavikku virodhiyai pōkkiṉa paṭi collukiṟatu.
cem vari ityādi
children.translated_text: "<s>Cem vari</s>" etc.

children.text: asitekṣaṇā
children.translated_text: "<s>asitekṣaṇā</s>" (dark-eyed one) —

children.text: eṉkiṟapaṭiyē kaṇ aḻakilē tōṟṟu, ciṉattai uṭaiya ṛṣabhattai taṉakku vāhanamāka uṭaiya rudraṉuṭaiya villāy oruvarāl kiṭṭa oṇṇātē irukkiṟa villai anāyāsena muṟittu, a- ceyalālē tōṟṟa pirāṭṭiyai tirumaṇam puṇarntu eḻuntaruḷā-niṟka, vaḻiyilē vantu tōṟṟiṉa taṉ krauryattukku takka maḻuv’ ākiya āyudhattai uṭaiya śrīparaśurāmāḻvāṉuṭaiya vemmaiyai uṭaittāy darśanīyamāṉa villai vāṅki, avaṉai veṉṟu, tāṉ tiru avatāram paṇṇiṉa kṣatriyakulattukku pakai tīrtta vīrattai uṭaiyavaṉai
children.translated_text: as described thus, having been captivated by the beauty of Her eyes, He effortlessly broke the bow of <s>Rudra</s> who has the angry bull as his mount — a bow unapproachable by anyone — and having thereby won and married <s>Pirāṭṭi</s>, as He was proceeding, <s>Śrī Paraśurāma Āḻvāṉ</s> who appeared on the way, possessing the axe as weapon befitting his ferocity — He took his fierce and beautiful bow, conquered him, and thus the hero who avenged the enmity against the <s>kṣatriya</s> clan into which He had incarnated,

children.text: tevvar añca neṭum puricai ityādi
children.translated_text: "<s>Tevvar añca neṭum puricai</s>" etc. —

children.text: śatrukkaḷ añcumpaṭiyāṉa uyarnta matiḷaiyum aṭṭālaikaḷaiyum uṭaittāṉa ūrilē vartikkiṟa
children.translated_text: in the city that has tall walls and watchtowers that make enemies tremble,

children.text: evv’ ari ityādi
children.translated_text: "<s>Evv' ari</s>" etc. —

children.text: avaṣṭabhya mahaddhanuḥ
children.translated_text: "<s>avaṣṭabhya mahaddhanuḥ</s>" (having grasped the great bow) —

children.text: eṉṟu, vēṟ’ oruttarāl aṭakki āḷa oṇṇātē kāṇavē pratipakṣam muṭiyumpaṭiyāṉa śrīśārṅgattai uṭaiya cakravarti tiru makaṉai
children.translated_text: as stated, the son of the emperor (<s>Cakravarti Tiru Makaṉ</s>) who possesses the <s>Śrī Śārṅga</s> bow, which cannot be subdued by anyone else and which by mere sight destroys the adversary,

children.text: iṟaiñcuvār iṇai aṭiyē
children.translated_text: the pair of feet of those who worship Him —

children.text: cakravarti tiru makaṉuṭaiya vīrattukkum aḻakukkum tōṟṟirukkum śrīvaiṣṇavarkaḷukku tōṟṟu avarkaḷ tiruvaṭikaḷilē
children.translated_text: being captivated by the beauty and valor of the son of the emperor, I fell at the feet of the <s>Śrīvaiṣṇavas</s> who are thus captivated,

children.text: iṟaiñciṉēṉē
children.translated_text: I worshipped! —

children.text: śrībharatāḻvāṉ guṇaṅkaḷukku tōṟṟa śrīśatrughnāḻvāṉai pōlē.
children.translated_text: just like <s>Śrī Śatrughna Āḻvāṉ</s> who was captivated by the qualities of <s>Śrī Bharata Āḻvāṉ</s>.
Introduction — Third verse. '<s>Cem vari nal</s>' — this describes how the obstacle to union with <s>Pirāṭṭi</s> (Sītā) was removed.

children.text: tott’ alar pūm curi kuḻal kaikēci collāl tol nakaram tuṟantu tuṟai kaṅkai taṉṉai
children.translated_text: By the words of <s>Kaikeyī</s> with her curly tresses adorned with flowers in clusters, He left the ancient city, crossed the <s>Gaṅgā</s> at its ford,

children.text: patti uṭai kukaṉ kaṭatta vaṉam pōy pukku parataṉukku pātukamum aracum īntu
children.translated_text: <s>Guha</s>, full of devotion, ferried Him across; He went and entered the forest, gave <s>Bharata</s> His sandals and the kingdom,

children.text: cittirakūṭatt’ iruntāṉ taṉṉai iṉṟu tillai nakar tiruccitrakūṭam taṉ uḷ
children.translated_text: He who resided at <s>Citrakūṭa</s> — today in <s>Tillai</s> city, within <s>Tiruccitrakūṭam</s>,

children.text: ettaṉaiyum kaṇ kuḷira kāṇa peṟṟa iru
m
children.translated_text: are

children.text: nilattārkk’ imaiyavar nēr ovvār tāmē
children.translated_text: equal to — nay, surpass — the celestials themselves!
those on this great earth who obtained the fortune of seeing Him to their eyes' full delight

children.text: tott’ alar
children.translated_text: Flowers in clusters adorning her curly tresses —

children.text: kottu kottāka alarukiṟa pūkkaḷai uṭaiya curuṇṭu aḻakiyatāṉa kuḻalai uṭaiya kaikeyi; ittāl taṉ oppaṉaiyālum aḻakālum cakravartiyai tāṉ iṭṭa vaḻakkāmpaṭi paṇṇi bhramippikka vallaḷāṉa
children.translated_text: <s>Kaikeyī</s> who had curly, beautiful tresses adorned with flowers blooming cluster upon cluster; by this it is indicated that she was one who could, by her beauty and coquetry, make the emperor dance to her tune and delude him,

children.text: kaikēci collāl
children.translated_text: By the words of <s>Kaikeyī</s> —

children.text: cakravarti vāy tiṟakka māṭṭāt’ irukka, piḷḷāy! uṅkaḷ aiyar, uṉṉai kāṭṭēṟa pōka collā-niṉṟār eṉṟu kaikeyi coṉṉa vārttaiyālē
children.translated_text: When the emperor could not bring himself to speak, <s>Kaikeyī</s> said 'Son! Your father is commanding you to go to the forest' — by those words of <s>Kaikeyī</s>,

children.text: tol ṉakaram tuṟantu
children.translated_text: He left the ancient city —

children.text: tol nakaram tuṟantu kulakramāgatamāy varukiṟa paṭaivīṭṭai sanyasittu; ivaḷ coṉṉāḷ eṉṟu pōkaikku prāpti illāmaiyai kāṭṭukiṟatu
children.translated_text: He renounced the hereditary capital that had been passed down through the dynasty; that He went because she said so shows that there was no entitlement for His departure otherwise,

children.text: tuṟai kaṅkai taṉṉai
children.translated_text: At the ford of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> —

children.text: gaṅgaiyiṉ tuṟai taṉṉai
children.translated_text: at the ford of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,

children.text: patti uṭai kukaṉ kaṭatta
children.translated_text: <s>Guha</s>, full of devotion, ferried Him across —

children.text: tampimārai kāṭṭilum snehattai uṭaiyaṉāy, piriyil dhariyātapaṭiyāy, perumāḷ niyamikkaiyālē niṉṟavaṉumāy, śrībharatāḻvāṉaiyum kūṭa acirkkumpaṭiyāṉa śrīguha perumāḷ gaṅgaiyai kaṭatta
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī Guha Perumāḷ</s>, who had more affection than even His own brothers, who could not bear separation, who stood because <s>Perumāḷ</s> commanded him, and who was such that even <s>Śrī Bharata Āḻvāṉ</s> would be envious of him — he ferried them across the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,

children.text: vaṉam pōy pukku
children.translated_text: He went and entered the forest —

children.text: manuṣyasañcāram iṉṟikkē duṣṭamṛgaṅkaḷēyāṉa kāṭṭilē pōy pukku
children.translated_text: He went and entered the forest devoid of human habitation, inhabited only by wild beasts,

children.text: parataṉukku pātukamum aracum īntu cittirakūṭatt’ iruntāṉ taṉṉai
children.translated_text: He gave <s>Bharata</s> His sandals and the kingdom and resided at <s>Citrakūṭa</s> —

children.text: citrakūṭattilē eḻuntaruḷi irukkiṟa iruppu tāṉ kāṇa peṟātē piṟpaṭṭārkkum iḻavu tīra, sarvakālattilum anubhavikkaikkāka tiruccittirakūṭattilē vartik-kiṟavaṉai
children.translated_text: So that even those who came later and missed seeing His residence at <s>Citrakūṭa</s> could have their loss made good, He dwells at <s>Tiruccitrakūṭam</s> for all time to be experienced,

children.text: ettaṉaiyum kaṇ kuḷira
children.translated_text: to their eyes' full delight —

children.text: ivaṉai kāṇa peṟātē viṭāytta kaṇ kuḷirumpaṭi
children.translated_text: so that the eyes that had been thirsting from not seeing Him are fully cooled,

children.text: kāṇa peṟṟa
children.translated_text: who obtained the fortune of seeing —

children.text: kēṭṭē pōkai aṉṟikkē kaṇṭu anubhavikka peṟṟa
children.translated_text: not merely hearing about Him, but obtaining the fortune of seeing and experiencing Him directly,

children.text: iru nilattārkku
children.translated_text: those on this great earth —

children.text: ukant’ aruḷiṉa deśaṅkaḷai uṭaiya ślāghyamāṉa bhūmiyil uḷḷārkku
children.translated_text: those on this praiseworthy earth that contains the places He graciously chose,

children.text: imaiyavar nēr ovvār
children.translated_text: surpass the celestials —

children.text: sadā paśyanti
children.translated_text: "<s>sadā paśyanti</s>" (they always behold) —

children.text: paṇṇi irukkaiyē svabhāvamāṉa nityasūrikaḷum ovvār. iṅku, kaṇṇukku viṣayam puṟampē uṇṭāyirukka ceytē, attai tyajittu kāṇkiṟavarkaḷ; avarkaḷ yātraiyāka irukkiṟavarkaḷiṟē.
children.translated_text: even the <s>Nityasūris</s> (eternal attendants) whose very nature is to always behold cannot equal them. For here, though the object for the eyes exists externally, those who abandon everything else and choose to see are greater; the <s>Nityasūris</s> are merely following their nature.

children.text: vali vaṇakku varai neṭum tōḷ virātai koṉṟu vaṇ ṭamiḻ mā muṉi koṭutta vari vil vāṅki
children.translated_text: Having slain <s>Virāta</s> (Virādha) of mountain-like mighty shoulders, having taken the striped bow given by the great sage of beautiful Tamil,

children.text: kalai vaṇakku nōkk’ arakki mūkkai nīkki karaṉōṭu tūṭaṇaṉ taṉ uyirai vāṅki
children.translated_text: having cut off the nose of the demoness whose glance surpasses that of a deer, having taken the lives of <s>Khara</s> and <s>Dūṣaṇa</s>,

children.text: cilai vaṇakki māṉ mariya eytāṉ taṉṉai tillai nakar tiruccitrakūṭam taṉ uḷ
children.translated_text: He who bent His bow and shot the deer to death — in <s>Tillai</s> city, within <s>Tiruccitrakūṭam</s>,

children.text: talai vaṇakki kai kūppi ētta vallār tiritalāl tavam uṭaitt’ itaraṇi tāṉē
children.translated_text: because those who can bow their heads and fold their hands and praise Him walk upon it, this earth possesses great merit!

children.text: vali vaṇakku
children.translated_text: Subduing the mighty —

children.text: etirikaḷ valimaiyai tōṟpikka kaṭavatāy, malai pōlē tiṇṇiyatāṉa tōḷkaḷai uṭaiya virādhaṉai koṉṟu
children.translated_text: He who killed <s>Virādha</s> who had mountain-like sturdy shoulders, whose power was destined to subdue enemies,

children.text: vaḷ ṭamiḻ mā muṉi koṭutta
children.translated_text: Given by the great sage of beautiful Tamil —

children.text: agastyaṉ koṭutta darśanīyamāṉa villai vāṅki
children.translated_text: He took the beautiful bow given by <s>Agastya</s>,

children.text: kalai vaṇakku nōkk’ arakki
children.translated_text: The demoness whose glance surpasses that of a deer —

children.text: kalai nōkkai tōṟpikkumpaṭiyāṉa nōkkai uṭaiya śūrpaṇakhiyuṭaiya mūkkai vāṅki
children.translated_text: <s>Śūrpaṇakhā</s> whose gaze was such as to defeat the sidelong glance of a deer — He took her nose,

children.text: nīkki karaṉōṭu tūṭaṇaṉ taṉ uyirai vāṅki
children.translated_text: Having taken the lives of <s>Khara</s> and <s>Dūṣaṇa</s> —

children.text: ivaḷuṭaiya rūpavairūpyam kaṇṭu poṟukka māṭṭātē vanta kharadūṣaṇarkaḷ prāṇaṉkaḷ harittu
children.translated_text: Unable to bear the disfigurement of her beauty, <s>Khara</s> and <s>Dūṣaṇa</s> who came — He took their lives,

children.text: cilai vaṇakki māṉ mariya
children.translated_text: He bent His bow and shot the deer to death —

children.text: atu kēṭṭu poṟāta rāvaṇaṉālē preritaṉāy vanta mārīcaṉāṉa māyāmṛgattai eytu koṉṟavaṉai
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Rāvaṇa</s> who could not bear it sent <s>Mārīca</s> as a magical deer — He who shot and killed that one,

children.text: tillai nakar ityādi
children.translated_text: "<s>Tillai nakar</s>" etc. —

children.text: akkālattil kāṇa peṟāta iḻav’ ellām tīra talai uṇṭāṉa prayojanam peṟa toḻutu, vāy uṇṭāṉa prayojanam peṟa ētta vallār tiritalāl
children.translated_text: To make good the loss of not having seen Him in that era, those who can bow and obtain the fruit of having a head, and praise and obtain the fruit of having a mouth,

children.text: tavam uṭaitt’ i- taraṇi tāṉē
children.translated_text: because of them, this earth possesses great merit! —

children.text: ivarkaḷuṭaiya sañcārattukku viṣayam-ākaiyālē bhūmiyāṉatu bhāgyattai uṭaiyatu.
children.translated_text: Because the earth is the field of their travels, it is blessed.

children.text: taṉam maruvu vaitēki piriyal uṟṟu taḷarv’ eyti caṭāyuvai vaikuntatt’ ēṟṟi
children.translated_text: Grieving over separation from <s>Vaidēhi</s> (Sītā) who clings to wealth, becoming weak, having sent <s>Jaṭāyu</s> to <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>,

children.text: vaṉam maruvu kavi aracaṉ kātal koṇṭu vāliyai koṉṟ’ ilaṅkai nakar arakkar kōmāṉ
children.translated_text: having accepted the love of <s>Sugrīva</s>, the monkey-king dwelling in the forest, having killed <s>Vāli</s>, through <s>Māruti</s> (Hanumān) He had the city of <s>Laṅkā</s>, of the demon king,

children.text: ciṉam aṭaṅka mārutiyāl cuṭuvittāṉai tillai nakar tiruccitrakūṭam taṉ uḷ
children.translated_text: burned until his fury subsided — in <s>Tillai</s> city, within <s>Tiruccitrakūṭam</s>,

children.text: iṉit’ amarnta ammāṉai irāmaṉ taṉṉai ēttuvār iṇai aṭiyē ēttiṉēṉē
children.translated_text: the Lord who joyfully abides there, <s>Rāma</s> Himself — I praised the pair of feet of those who praise Him!

children.text: taṉam maruvu
children.translated_text: Wealth-loving —

children.text: tirumulai taṭattiṉ aḻakālum ābhijātyattālum piriya takāta pirāṭṭi pirivālē perumāḷ tam aḷavil nōvuppaṭṭu, pirāṭṭikkāka rāvaṇaṉōṭē yuddham paṇṇi prāṇaṉaiviṭṭa periyavuṭaiyārai paramapadatt’ ēṟa pōkaviṭṭu. taṉa maruvu vaitēki eṉṟu
children.translated_text: <s>Perumāḷ</s> (Rāma) suffered grief at the separation from <s>Pirāṭṭi</s> (Sītā) who was inseparable by virtue of the beauty of Her form and Her noble birth; for Her sake He fought with <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, and <s>Periya Uṭaiyār</s> (Jaṭāyu) who gave his life — He sent him to <s>Paramapadam</s>. '<s>Taṉam maruvu Vaidēhi</s>' means

children.text: viṣṇoḥ śrīḥ
children.translated_text: "<s>Viṣṇoḥ Śrīḥ</s>" (the Śrī of Viṣṇu) —

children.text: eṉkiṟapaṭiyē, perumāḷukku dhanamāṉa pirāṭṭi eṉṟumām.
children.translated_text: as stated thus, <s>Pirāṭṭi</s> who is the wealth of <s>Perumāḷ</s>.

children.text: vaṉam maruvu kavi aracaṉ
children.translated_text: The monkey-king dwelling in the forest —

children.text: vālikku añci kāṭṭilē maṟaintu kiṭakkiṟa kuraṅkukaḷukku rājāvāṉa sugrīvaṉai snehapūrvakamāka kāṭcikoṇṭu, avarkkāka atibalaparākramaṉāṉa vāliyai nirasittu
children.translated_text: Having graciously received <s>Sugrīva</s>, the king of the monkeys who were hiding in the forest out of fear of <s>Vāli</s>, with love, and for his sake having destroyed <s>Vāli</s> who was of great strength and valor,

children.text: ilaṅkai nakar
children.translated_text: The city of <s>Laṅkā</s> —

children.text: laṅkaikku nirvāhakaṉ eṉṟum rākṣaseśvaraṉ eṉṟum mohitt’ irukkiṟavaṉuṭaiya abhimānamum, cīṟṟamum aṭaṅkumpaṭi, tiruvaṭi vālilē neruppai iṭṭu cuṭuvittāṉai
children.translated_text: He who was deluded thinking 'I am the ruler of <s>Laṅkā</s>' and 'I am the lord of the <s>Rākṣasas</s>' — to subdue both his pride and his fury, <s>Tiruvaṭi</s> (Hanumān) set fire with his tail and had it burned,

children.text: tillai nakar ityādi
children.translated_text: "<s>Tillai nakar</s>" etc. —

children.text: a- kālattil anubhavikka peṟṟilōm eṉṉum iḻavu tīra iṅkē nityasannihitaṉāy vartikkiṟa sarveśvaraṉāṉa cakravarti tiru makaṉai
children.translated_text: To make good the loss of not having experienced Him at that time, the Lord of all who is the son of the emperor, ever-present here,

children.text: ēttuvār
children.translated_text: those who praise Him —

children.text: avaṉuṭaiya vaṭiv’ aḻakilum saulabhyattilum īṭupaṭṭu ēttumavarkaḷ tiruvaṭikaḷai ēttiṉēṉē.
children.translated_text: I praised the feet of those who, being captivated by His beauty of form and <s>saulabhya</s> (accessibility), praise Him.

children.text: kurai kaṭalai aṭal ampāl maṟuka eytu kulai kaṭṭi maṟu karaiyai ataṉāl ēṟi
children.translated_text: Having shot the roaring ocean with fierce arrows to make it retreat, having built a bridge and crossed to the other shore by means of it,

children.text: eri neṭu
m
children.translated_text: spear

children.text: vēl arakkaroṭum ilaṅkai vēntaṉ iṉ uyir koṇṭ’ avaṉ tampikk’ aracum īntu
children.translated_text: — having taken the dear life of the <s>Laṅkā</s> king along with his fire-spear-bearing <s>Rākṣasas</s>, having given the kingdom to his brother,
the blazing, long

children.text: tirumakaḷōṭ’ iṉit’ amarnta celvaṉ taṉṉai tillai nakar tiruccitrakūṭam taṉ uḷ
children.translated_text: the prosperous one who joyfully united with <s>Tirumakaḷ</s> (Śrī/Sītā) — in <s>Tillai</s> city, within <s>Tiruccitrakūṭam</s>,

children.text: arac’ amarntāṉ aṭi cūṭum aracai allāl arac’ āka eṇṇēṉ maṟṟ’ aracu tāṉē
children.translated_text: I shall consider no kingship to be kingship other than the kingship of wearing on one's head the feet of Him who reigns there!

children.text: kurai kaṭalai
children.translated_text: The roaring ocean —

children.text: ghoṣattai uṭaittāṉa kaṭalai, śatrukkaḷ eṉṟāl eppōtō eṉṟu mēlviḻa kaṭavatāṉa ampaiviṭṭu maṟukumpaṭiyāka eytu
children.translated_text: The ocean that was roaring — He shot arrows that were eager to rush at anything called an enemy, making it retreat in fear,

children.text: kulai kaṭṭi
children.translated_text: Having built a bridge —

children.text: añciṉa kaṭal-āṉatu eṉ mēlē tūrttu koḷvīr eṉṉa, atiṉ-mēlē malaikaḷai iṭṭu tūrttu vaḻi ceytu anta karaiyilē pōy
children.translated_text: The frightened ocean said 'fill me up' — upon it He piled mountains, built a causeway, made a path, and went to the other shore,

children.text: eri neṭu vēl
children.translated_text: The blazing, long spear —

children.text: śatrukkaḷai erikka kaṭavatāy neṭitāṉa vēlai uṭaiya rākṣasarōṭē, laṅkādhipatiyāṉa rāvaṇaṉai avaṉ ukanta prāṇaṉai harittu, avaṉ tampikku rājyattai koṭuttu, pirāṭṭiyōṭē kūṭa, pirinta piriv’ ellām maṟakkumpaṭi iṉitu amarnt’ aruḷiya aiśvaryam uṭaiyavaṉ taṉṉai
children.translated_text: Along with the <s>Rākṣasas</s> bearing long spears destined to burn enemies, He took from <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, the lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, the life he held dear, gave the kingdom to his younger brother, and united with <s>Pirāṭṭi</s> — so joyfully that all the sorrow of separation was forgotten — the one possessing such <s>aiśvarya</s> (sovereignty),

children.text: tillai nakar ityādi
children.translated_text: "<s>Tillai nakar</s>" etc. —

children.text: rājyam paṇṇiyirukkiṟavaṉ tiruvaṭikaḷai cūṭukaiākiṟa rājyam oḻiya atukk’ etir taṭṭāka svātantryattai pārkkum rājyattai rājyamāka eṇṇēṉ.
children.translated_text: Except the kingship that consists of wearing on one's head the feet of Him who reigns, I shall not consider as kingship any kingdom that looks to independence as its counterpart.

children.text: am poṉ neṭu
m
children.translated_text: gem-studded

children.text: maṇi māṭa
children.translated_text: mansions

children.text: m
ayōtti eyti arac’ eyti akattiyaṉ vāy tāṉ muṉ koṉṟāṉ
children.translated_text: having reached <s>Ayodhyā</s>, having regained the kingdom, He heard from <s>Agastya</s>'s mouth the full story of the one He had previously slain,
The beautiful, golden, tall,

children.text: taṉ perum tol katai kēṭṭu mitilai celvi ulak’ uyya tiru vayiṟu vāytta makkaḷ
children.translated_text: and the daughter of <s>Mithilā</s> — the children born of her blessed womb for the world's salvation,

children.text: cem pavaḷa tiraḷ vāy taṉ caritai kēṭṭāṉ tillai nakar tiruccitrakūṭam taṉ uḷ
children.translated_text: with coral-red rounded lips, heard their own story — in <s>Tillai</s> city, within <s>Tiruccitrakūṭam</s>,

children.text: emperumāṉ taṉ caritai ceviyāl kaṇṇāl parukuvōm iṉ amutam matiyōm aṉṟē
children.translated_text: we shall drink in with our ears and eyes the story of our Lord as sweet nectar — we shall not undervalue it!

children.text: am poṉ
children.translated_text: The beautiful, golden —

children.text: tiru abhiṣekattukku īṭāka alaṅkarittu darśanīyamāy, ōkkattai uṭaittāy, nalla ratnaṅkaḷālē camaikkappaṭṭa māṭaṅkaḷai uṭaiya tiru ayodhyaiyilē jagat ellām ukakkumpaṭi mīṇṭu eḻuntaruḷi pukuntu
children.translated_text: Adorned fittingly for the sacred coronation, beautiful to behold, lofty, having mansions built of fine gems — having returned to sacred <s>Ayodhyā</s> and entered it to the joy of the entire world,

children.text: arac’ eyti
children.translated_text: Having regained the kingdom —

children.text: rājyaṃ punaravāptavān
children.translated_text: "<s>rājyaṃ punaravāptavān</s>" (he regained the kingdom) —

children.text: eṉṉumpaṭiyē jagat ellām vāḻumpaṭi sāmrājyattilē adhikarittu
children.translated_text: as stated, He was established in the imperial sovereignty so that the entire world could flourish,

children.text: akattiyaṉ
children.translated_text: <s>Agastya</s> —

children.text: vēṟu kṛtyāṃśam illāmaiyālē pōtupōkkāka tāṉ muṉ koṉṟa rāvaṇaṉuṭaiya pūrvavṛttāntaṅkaḷai aṭaiya agastyabhagavān viṇṇappam ceyya kēṭṭu
children.translated_text: Since there were no other duties, as a way of passing time, <s>Agastya Bhagavān</s> presented to Him the entire past history of <s>Rāvaṇa</s> whom He had previously slain, and He listened,

children.text: mitilai celvi ityādi
children.translated_text: "the daughter of <s>Mithilā</s>" etc. —

children.text: śrījanakarājaṉ tirumakaḷ, jagattai aṭaiya ujjīvikkumpaṭi peṟṟa kuśalavarkaḷ pēca, tammuṭaiya vṛttamāṉa śrīrāmāyaṇakathaiyai kēṭṭ’ aruḷiṉavar. iṉṟu tiruccitrakūṭattilē nityavāsam paṇṇukiṟa, eṉṉuṭaiya nāthaṉuṭaiya vṛttāntattai tiruvaṭiyai pōlē sarvendriyaṅkaḷālum anubhavikka peṟṟa nām, devajāti anubhavikkiṟa amṛtattai oṉṟ’ āka matiyōmē.
children.translated_text: The daughter of <s>Śrī Janaka Rāja</s> — when <s>Kuśa</s> and <s>Lava</s>, born for the salvation of the entire world, recited, He graciously heard the <s>Śrī Rāmāyaṇa</s> story which was His own history. Today, we who have obtained the fortune of experiencing with all our senses, like <s>Tiruvaṭi</s> (Hanumān), the history of my Lord who eternally dwells at <s>Tiruccitrakūṭam</s> — we shall not regard as equal the <s>amṛta</s> (nectar) enjoyed by the divine race.

children.text: ceṟi tava campukaṉ taṉṉai ceṉṟu koṉṟu ceḻum maṟaiyōṉ uyir mīṭṭu tavattōṉ īnta
children.translated_text: Having gone and slain <s>Śambuka</s> of rigorous austerities, having restored the life of the eminent Brahmin, having accepted the gem-studded ornament offered by the ascetic,

children.text: niṟai maṇi pūṇ aṇiyum koṇṭ’ ilavaṇaṉ taṉṉai tampiyāl vāṉ ēṟṟi muṉivaṉ vēṇṭa
children.translated_text: having slain <s>Lavaṇa</s> through His younger brother and sent him heavenward, at the sage's request,

children.text: tiṟal viḷaṅkum ilakkumaṉai pirintāṉ taṉṉai tillai nakar tiruccitrakūṭam taṉ uḷ
children.translated_text: He who was separated from the valorous <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> — in <s>Tillai</s> city, within <s>Tiruccitrakūṭam</s>,

children.text: uṟaivāṉai maṟavāta uḷḷam taṉṉai uṭaiyōm maṟṟ’ uṟu tuyaram aṭaiyōm aṉṟē
children.translated_text: we who possess a heart that never forgets Him who dwells there — we shall never be afflicted by any sorrow!

children.text: ceṟi tava campukaṉ
children.translated_text: <s>Śambuka</s> of rigorous austerities —

children.text: mikka tapassai uṭaiyavaṉāy śūdraṉāṉa jaṃbukaṉai talai aṟuttu
children.translated_text: He cut off the head of <s>Jambuka</s> (Śambuka) who, though a <s>Śūdra</s>, possessed great austerity,

children.text: ceḻum maṟaiyōṉ uyir mīṭṭu
children.translated_text: and restored the life of the eminent Brahmin —

children.text: vilakṣaṇaṉāṉa brāhmaṇaṉuṭaiya putraṉ prāṇaṉai mīṭṭu, agastyabhagavān koṭutta peru vilaiyāṉa hārattaiyum cātti aruḷi, tiru ayodhyaiyilē pukuntu, lavaṇāsuraṉai śrīśatrughnāḻvāṉai iṭuvittu vīrasvargattilē kuṭiyēṟṟuvittu
children.translated_text: Having restored the life of the son of the distinguished <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, having adorned Himself with the precious necklace given by <s>Agastya Bhagavān</s>, entering <s>Tiru Ayodhyā</s>, and sending <s>Lavaṇāsura</s> to the warriors' heaven (<s>vīrasvarga</s>) through <s>Śrī Śatrughna Āḻvāṉ</s>,

children.text: muṉivaṉ ityādi
children.translated_text: 'The sage,' etc. —

children.text: dūrvāsāviṉuṭaiya śāpattālē
children.translated_text: Due to the curse of <s>Durvāsā</s>,

children.text: dvitīyaṃ me’ntarātmānam
children.translated_text: '<s>Dvitīyaṃ me'ntarātmānam</s>' (the second, my inner self) —

children.text: eṉkiṟapaṭiyē, tammuṭaiya prāṇabhūtarāṉa iḷaiyaperumāḷukku viṭai koṭuttu, appaṭippaṭṭa taṉṉai piṉpuḷḷār kāṇa peṟāta iḻavu tīra tiruccitrakūṭattilē nityavāsam paṇṇukiṟavaṉai
children.translated_text: As stated, having bid farewell to <s>Iḷaiya Perumāḷ</s> (<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>) who was His very life-breath, He who is such that later generations could not bear the loss of not seeing Him — now eternally resides at <s>Tiruccitrakūṭam</s>,

children.text: maṟavāta uḷḷam taṉṉai uṭaiyōm
children.translated_text: 'We who possess a heart that never forgets' —

children.text: ippaṭippaṭṭa saulabhyattai anavaratabhāvanai paṇṇi irukkiṟa namakku emperumāṉai anubhavikka peṟṟilōm eṉkiṟa iḻavu iṉi illai.
children.translated_text: For us who constantly contemplate such accessibility (<s>saulabhya</s>), there is no longer any loss of not having experienced the Lord.

children.text: aṉṟu carācaraṅkaḷai vaikuntatt’ ēṟṟi aṭal arava pakai ēṟi acurar tammai
children.translated_text: On that day, having sent all moving and unmoving beings to <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, mounting the fierce serpent's enemy,

children.text: veṉṟ’ ilaṅku maṇi neṭum tōḷ nāṉkum tōṉṟa viṇ muḻutum etir vara taṉ tāmam mēvi
children.translated_text: Having conquered the <s>asuras</s>, with four long arms adorned with shining jewels appearing resplendent, as all of heaven came forth to receive Him, wearing His own garland,

children.text: ceṉṟ’ iṉitu vīṟṟirunta ammāṉ taṉṉai tillai nakar tiruccitrakūṭam taṉ uḷ
children.translated_text: He went and seated Himself in bliss — that Lord, within <s>Tiruccitrakūṭam</s> in the city of <s>Tillai</s>,

children.text: eṉṟum niṉṟāṉ avaṉ ivaṉ eṉṟ’ ētti nāḷum iṟaiñcumiṉō eppoḻutum toṇṭīr nīrē
children.translated_text: He who stands there forever — He is this one here! Praising thus, O devotees, worship Him daily at all times!

children.text: aṉṟu carācaraṅkaḷai
children.translated_text: 'On that day, all moving and unmoving beings' —

children.text: api vṛkṣāḥ parimlānāḥ
children.translated_text: '<s>Api vṛkṣāḥ parimlānāḥ</s>' (even the trees withered) —

children.text: eṉṟu vyatirekattilē avai paṭṭatu aṟint’ aruḷukaiyālē,
children.translated_text: Since He knew through their separation what even they suffered,

children.text: nocchvasat tad ayodhyāyāṃ susūkṣmam api dṛśyate tiryagyonigatāś cānye sarve rāmam anuvratāḥ
children.translated_text: '<s>Nocchvasat tad ayodhyāyāṃ susūkṣmam api dṛśyate / tiryagyonigatāś cānye sarve rāmam anuvratāḥ</s>' (Nothing in <s>Ayodhyā</s> even breathed to the slightest degree; all creatures even in animal births followed <s>Rāma</s>'s vow) —

children.text: eṉkiṟapaṭiyē, iḷaiyaperumāḷ ōpāti paramapadattukku pōkaviṭṭu
children.translated_text: As stated, just as <s>Iḷaiya Perumāḷ</s> (<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>), He sent them all equally to <s>Paramapadam</s>,

children.text: aṭal arava pakai ēṟi
children.translated_text: 'Mounting the fierce serpent's enemy' —

children.text: sarpajātikku janmaśatruvāṉa periyatiruvaṭiyai mēṟkoṇṭu, asuravargattai veṉṟu anta vīraśrī viḷaṅkukiṟa tiru tōḷkaḷ nālōṭumkūṭa aṅk’ uḷḷār ukakkumpaṭi eḻuntaruḷi, paramapadattilē pōy pukku, taṉ mēṉmai ellām tōṟṟumpaṭiyāṉa īśvaraṉai
children.translated_text: Mounting <s>Periyatiruvaṭi</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>), who is the natural enemy of the serpent race, having conquered the demonic host, with the four sacred shoulders resplendent with that heroic glory, He graciously proceeded such that all those there rejoiced, entered <s>Paramapadam</s> — this Lord whose full majesty is thus manifest,

children.text: tillai nakar ityādi
children.translated_text: 'The city of <s>Tillai</s>,' etc. —

children.text: a- iruppil oṉṟum kuṟaiyāmē kālatattvam uḷḷataṉaiyum iṅkē namakkāka nityavāsam paṇṇumavaṉai. ananyaprayojanarāṉa nīṅkaḷ avaṉai āśrayittu kṛtārthar ākuṅkōḷ.
children.translated_text: He who, without any diminishment of that state, eternally resides here for our sake as long as time endures. You who seek no other purpose — take refuge in Him and become fulfilled!

children.text: tillai nakar tiruccitrakūṭam taṉ uḷ tiṟal viḷaṅku mārutiyōṭ’ amarntāṉ taṉṉai
children.translated_text: He who is seated in <s>Tiruccitrakūṭam</s> in the city of <s>Tillai</s> together with the mighty <s>Māruti</s> (<s>Hanumān</s>),

children.text: ellai il cīr tayarataṉ taṉ makaṉ āy tōṉṟiṟṟ’ atu mutal ā taṉ ulakam pukkat’ īṟ’ ā
children.translated_text: Beginning from His appearing as the son of <s>Daśaratha</s> of boundless glory, up to His entering His own world,

children.text: kol iyalum paṭai tāṉai koṟṟa
m
oḷ vāḷ kōḻiyar kōṉ kuṭai kulacēkaraṉ col ceyta
children.translated_text: Bright sword — <s>Kulacēkaraṉ</s> of the parasol, king of the <s>Kōḻiyar</s> (Cōḻas), composed these words,
With a spear-wielding army and victorious

children.text: nal iyal iṉ tamiḻ mālai pattum vallār nalam tikaḻ nāraṇaṉ aṭi kīḻ naṇṇuvārē
children.translated_text: Those who master this garland of ten in good, sweet Tamil will attain the feet of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> who shines with all goodness!

children.text: nigamattil
tillai nakar ityādi
children.translated_text: 'The city of <s>Tillai</s>,' etc. —

children.text: bhāvo nānyatra gacchati
children.translated_text: '<s>Bhāvo nānyatra gacchati</s>' (the mind goes nowhere else) —

children.text: eṉṟu aṅku pōkēṉ eṉṟa tiruvaṭiyai viṭa māṭṭāmē iṅkē vantu nityavāsam paṇṇukiṟavaṉai
children.translated_text: He who, unable to abandon <s>Tiruvaṭi</s> (<s>Hanumān</s>) who said 'I will not go elsewhere,' came here and eternally resides,

children.text: ellai il cīr ityādi
children.translated_text: 'Of boundless glory,' etc. —

children.text: bahuguṇaṉāṉa cakravartikku,
children.translated_text: For <s>Cakravartti</s> (<s>Daśaratha</s>) who was endowed with many virtues,

children.text: pitaraṃ rocayāmāsa
children.translated_text: '<s>Pitaraṃ rocayāmāsa</s>' (He delighted His father) —

children.text: eṉṟu piḷḷaiyāy piṟantatu toṭakkamāka paramapadam pukkatu muṭivāka uṇṭāṉa śrīrāmāyaṇakathaiyai
children.translated_text: Beginning from His being born as a son and ending with His entering <s>Paramapadam</s> — the story of <s>Śrī Rāmāyaṇa</s>,

children.text: kol iyalum paṭai tāṉai
children.translated_text: 'With a spear-wielding army' —

children.text: kolaiyai muyalā-niṉṟa vēlai uṭaiya paṭaiyai uṭaiyarāy
children.translated_text: Possessing an army equipped with spears ever ready for battle,

children.text: koṟṟa oḷ vāḷ
children.translated_text: 'Victorious bright sword' —

children.text: veṟṟiyaiyum aḻakaiyum uṭaiya vāḷai uṭaiya
children.translated_text: Possessing a sword of victory and beauty,

children.text: kōḻiyar kōṉ
children.translated_text: 'King of the <s>Kōḻiyar</s>' —

children.text: kōḻiyarkku kōṉ. kōḻi - uṟaiyūr. cōḻarkku rājāāṉavar
children.translated_text: King of the <s>Kōḻiyar</s>. <s>Kōḻi</s> means <s>Uṟaiyūr</s>. The ruler of the <s>Cōḻas</s>,

children.text: kuṭai kulacēkaraṉ col ceyta
children.translated_text: '<s>Kulacēkaraṉ</s> of the parasol composed these' —

children.text: veṇkoṟṟakkuṭaiyai uṭaiyarāṉa śrīkulaśekhara perumāḷ aruḷicceyta
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī Kulaśekhara Perumāḷ</s> who possesses the white royal parasol graciously composed these,

children.text: nal iyaliṉ tamiḻ mālai pattum vallār
children.translated_text: 'Those who master these ten in good Tamil' —

children.text: aḻakiya iyalai uṭaiya tamiḻ mālai pattum vallār
children.translated_text: Those who master the ten verses of the Tamil garland with beautiful meter,

children.text: nalam tikaḻ nāraṇaṉ aṭi kīḻ naṇṇuvārē
children.translated_text: 'Will attain the feet of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> who shines with all goodness!' —

children.text: paramapadattilē viḷaṅkā-niṉṟuḷḷa sarveśvaraṉ tiruvaṭikaḷai kiṭṭa peṟuvārkaḷ.
children.translated_text: They will attain the sacred feet of <s>Sarveśvara</s> (the Lord of all) who shines resplendent in <s>Paramapadam</s>.
In the concluding verse —
